If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is seeking a Sr. Manager, Communications to lead storytelling for the front lines of our business: the teams that site, power, and build Crusoe's AI factories — for ourselves and our partners — at massive scale. This role sits at the center of our Digital Infrastructure Group (DIG), Energy, and Real Estate organizations, driving the narrative around how and where we build the physical backbone of AI.

This is a fast-moving, high-stakes environment. You'll dive deep into the AI infrastructure buildout — from gigawatt-scale power and site development to construction and community partnerships — and translate it into compelling stories that elevate Crusoe's work while protecting our brand. You'll partner closely with our Public Affairs and Government Affairs teams on community engagement, ensuring the places we build see Crusoe as a good neighbor and a serious partner.

This role requires mastery of messaging and storytelling, a "roll-up-your-sleeves" approach to execution, and a meticulous eye for detail. We are an AI-first company and are looking for a practitioner who views generative AI as a core part of their toolkit — someone who leverages modern AI agents and tools to scale their impact and sharpen their output.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • News Engine: Drive a strategic news program that demonstrates momentum across Crusoe's data center development, energy, and real estate work — turning our buildout into a consistent cadence of high-impact moments.

  • Media and Influencer Relations: Build and maintain direct relationships with journalists across infrastructure, energy, real estate, technology, and financial media. You must be able to pitch and place stories independently; we need a practitioner who can "hunt" and isn't solely reliant on agencies.

  • Community & Stakeholder Engagement: Partner closely with our Public Affairs and Government Affairs teams to support community engagement in the markets where we build — ensuring local audiences, officials, and stakeholders understand Crusoe's investment and impact.

  • Narrative Development: Partner with subject matter experts across DIG, Energy, and Real Estate to sharpen messaging — translating complex topics across site development, power, construction, and data center operations into compelling stories for a range of audiences.

  • Thought Leadership: Work with Crusoe's bench of spokespeople to develop and place high-impact op-eds, keynote scripts, and social content that secures Crusoe's position as a leader in AI infrastructure development.

  • Issues Management: Monitor the media and community landscape closely and coordinate timely, strategic responses to industry shifts, local dynamics, and challenges — protecting Crusoe's brand and reputation in a quickly shifting environment.

  • Agency Management: Help manage our PR agency relationships day-to-day focused on your line of business — setting clear priorities, holding teams accountable to outcomes, and ensuring resources are deployed against the highest-value opportunities.

  • Measurement: Own communications reporting. You will track coverage, share of voice, and program outcomes, using data to continuously improve strategy and demonstrate impact.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: 7+ years in communications or public relations, with a demonstrated track record of securing press results at top-tier outlets.

  • AI-First Mindset: You don't just talk about AI; you use it daily. You have integrated AI into your workflows — from deploying agents to automate tasks to using LLMs for research and drafting — and you adopt new tools as they emerge.

  • Domain Expertise: Experience working in data center construction/development, energy, infrastructure, real estate, or AI industries is strongly preferred.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Senior Staff Applications Engineer to own how Spark answers the question of technical fit. You will build and maintain the evaluation framework that determines whether a site, partnership, or commercial opportunity is viable for the Spark modular data center (MDC) and Spark-Liquid (DLC) product lines, and you will support the Energy Development Group (EDG), business development, and partner teams as they apply it. When an opportunity is undefined, unconventional, or contested, you are the Spark team's point of contact, the person who answers the hard product questions and delivers the technical verdict.

Spark is on a path to deploy hundreds of megawatts of modular capacity, and every megawatt of it begins as an unqualified site on a map. Your judgment about where this product can be applied, not the design of the product itself, is what converts that pipeline into deployable capacity.

What You'll Be Working On:

Product Authority & Opportunity Qualification

  • Qualification Framework: Build and maintain the standardized screening criteria, scoring model, decision thresholds, and report format that define what makes a site or opportunity viable for Spark deployments. Keep it current as the product roadmap evolves, and keep a record of past calls and their rationale.

  • Team Enablement: Equip EDG, business development, and partner teams to apply the framework themselves on standard opportunities. Train, document, and iterate so routine qualification does not depend on a single point of failure, you.

  • Escalated Technical Judgment: Serve as the Spark team's point of contact for opportunities the framework cannot resolve, including undefined sites, non-standard configurations, and contested calls. Deliver a clear fit, conditional fit, or no-fit verdict with the engineering rationale behind it.

  • Speed Discipline: Turn around escalated feasibility assessments in days, not weeks. Frame the problem tightly enough that deeper analysis, when required, lands on the respective engineering discipline ready to be worked.

  • Deviation & Exception Management: Identify where an opportunity requires deviation from the standard Spark configuration, quantify the engineering cost and schedule impact, and route it to the responsible engineering discipline for disposition.

  • New Application Assessment: Evaluate technical fit for non-standard applications such as edge deployments, distributed energy assets, co-located industrial sites, and third-party colocation and shell-rent arrangements, and define what the product would need to change to serve them.

  • Roadmap Feedback Loop: Feed recurring field constraints back to Spark design engineering and R&D as prioritized product requirements. You are the closed loop between what the market presents and what the product can absorb.

Site & Partner Engagement

  • EDG Partnership: Serve as Spark's dedicated technical counterpart to the Energy Development Group across the full site pipeline, from initial screen through definitive agreement.

  • Spark Fit Assessment: Evaluate candidate sites and opportunities against Spark module requirements, covering power, thermal, civil, and physical interface, and define what the site must deliver at the module boundary.

  • Field Validation: Conduct site walks alongside EDG, developers, and utility counterparties, converting observations into Spark product requirements and a maintained risk register.

Technical Communication & Diligence

  • Diligence Support: Provide the technical inputs that Finance requires to model an opportunity, including module configuration, power and cooling assumptions, and site-specific efficiency and derate factors.

  • Executive Communication: Translate multi-discipline engineering tradeoffs into clear go/no-go decision frameworks for commercial and executive stakeholders.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Professional Experience: 10+ years of progressive engineering experience spanning data center infrastructure, power generation or utility interconnection, industrial capital projects, or modular and containerized systems.

  • Broad Engineering Fluency: Working fluency across data center infrastructure disciplines including electrical (MV/LV distribution, switchgear, transformers), mechanical/thermal (DLC, CDUs, heat rejection), and civil/structural (foundations, seismic/wind loading, rigging).

  • First-Principles Decision Making: Track record of making feasibility calls from first principles under incomplete information, with direct accountability for recommendations carrying real capital consequences.

  • Technical Counterparty Credibility: Proven ability to hold technical credibility with external developers, utilities, enterprise customers, and executives while keeping opportunities moving rapidly.

  • Unit Economics Command: Ability to connect engineering decisions directly to $/MW, capex, PUE, and deployment schedules.

  • Product Authority Track Record: Demonstrated depth on a specific engineered product or platform, where you were the person others relied on for an authoritative answer on capabilities and limits.

  • Mountaineer Spirit: Relentless technical rigor, comfort with ambiguity, a safety-first culture, the judgment to say no early, and the discipline to make calls when perfect information is unavailable.

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with modular, containerized, or prefabricated infrastructure product lines.

  • Familiarity with agency certification and AHJ coordination for modular electrical equipment across varied jurisdictions.

  • Deep familiarity with energy development, interconnection processes/queues, and behind-the-meter site configurations.

This Role Is Not a Good Fit If:

  • You prefer purely theoretical design work over applied, rapid feasibility assessments.

  • You require complete data and fully finalized engineering designs before making a technical recommendation.

  • You struggle to communicate complex engineering tradeoffs to commercial partners or executive stakeholders.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $190,000-$215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDCORP)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Staff Instrumentation & Controls Engineer, Deployment
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

 

As Staff Instrumentation and Controls Engineer, Deployment - you will be a deployment and execution lead for the "nervous system" of Crusoe’s hyperscale data centers. You will spearhead the installation and integration of the sophisticated BMS/EPMS and SCADA solutions that allow us to monitor and control our high-performance computing environments with surgical precision. This role is fundamental to Crusoe’s mission: by successfully bringing online and integrating field-level HVAC, electrical, and monitoring infrastructure into a seamless, operational fabric, you ensure our AI-optimized cloud remains resilient, efficient, and scalable from day one.

This leadership position demands a technical authority who can bridge the gap between engineering design and on-site field execution. You won't just be maintaining systems; you will be driving complex rollouts, overseeing contractor integration, and implementing the deployment standards and commissioning frameworks that scale our global footprint. We are seeking a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced, hands-on environment and is passionate about bringing automated systems to life, working with others, and driving consistency and efficiencies across our startup through operational handover. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • System Deployment & Execution: Lead the field deployment, integration, and startup of automation solutions for BMS/EPMS systems, ensuring seamless integration and monitor with electrical, and cooling infrastructure.

  • Standardization & Implementation: Enforce system standards, frameworks, and deployment patterns for controls, BMS, and EPMS rollouts across multiple projects and sites.

  • SCADA & Graphics Configuration: Deploy and configure dashboards, HMIs, and operator workstations, ensuring site personnel have clear, functional visibility and control over complex building and power systems.

  • Startup Governance & Escalation Resolution: Oversee system integrators during standard deployments and point-to-point checkouts to ensure strict compliance with design standards, and operate as the controls escalation point to troubleshoot complex automation integration, system inconsistencies, and network integration issues.

  • Protocol Integration & Troubleshooting: Collaborate with design engineers, contractors, and OEM partners in the field to configure, integrate, and troubleshoot networks utilizing BACnet, Modbus, OPC-UA, and MQTT protocols.

  • Site Validation & Handover: Conduct system testing, simulation, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) to validate functionality, sequencing, and data accuracy prior to operational handover.

  • System Optimization & Turnover: Ensure controls platforms correctly collect and push real-time and historical data, enabling performance insight and analysis.

  • Site Support & Training: Mentor and train other controls engineers, on control system operation, troubleshooting best practices, and execution methodology.

 

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Deployment & Integration Mastery: Extensive professional experience in the physical deployment, integration, and startup of PLC, SCADA, BMS, and EPMS platforms.

  • Mission-Critical Execution: Proven ability to successfully execute, deploy, and startup automation systems in data center or other high-availability environments.

  • Protocol & Networking Proficiency: Deep hands-on familiarity with configuring and troubleshooting control protocols such as BACnet, Modbus, OPC-UA, and MQTT, integrating diverse field devices into unified platforms.

  • Industrial Systems Literacy: Strong practical knowledge of HVAC, electrical systems, PLC/DDC logic, and industrial automation equipment operations.

  • Project & Field Leadership: Demonstrated ability to translate engineering designs into physical installations, driving deployment timelines, and navigating a fast paced construction environment.

  • On-Site Problem Solving: A track record of solving complex automation challenges, quickly diagnosing integration issues, and ensuring systems operate exactly as designed.

  • Mandatory Education: A Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Advanced Academic Credentials: A Master’s degree in a relevant engineering or technical field.

  • Industry Certifications: Relevant professional certifications in specific PLC or SCADA platforms. Ignition and Rockwell preferred.

  • Cybersecurity Focus: Experience ensuring controls implementations comply with industrial cybersecurity best practices.

  • Sustainability Alignment: A passion for leveraging automation to meet company-wide energy efficiency and sustainability goals.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $148,000 - $170,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

 

As Staff Instrumentation and Controls Engineer, Deployment - you will be a deployment and execution lead for the "nervous system" of Crusoe’s hyperscale data centers. You will spearhead the installation and integration of the sophisticated BMS/EPMS and SCADA solutions that allow us to monitor and control our high-performance computing environments with surgical precision. This role is fundamental to Crusoe’s mission: by successfully bringing online and integrating field-level HVAC, electrical, and monitoring infrastructure into a seamless, operational fabric, you ensure our AI-optimized cloud remains resilient, efficient, and scalable from day one.

This leadership position demands a technical authority who can bridge the gap between engineering design and on-site field execution. You won't just be maintaining systems; you will be driving complex rollouts, overseeing contractor integration, and implementing the deployment standards and commissioning frameworks that scale our global footprint. We are seeking a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced, hands-on environment and is passionate about bringing automated systems to life, working with others, and driving consistency and efficiencies across our startup through operational handover. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • System Deployment & Execution: Lead the field deployment, integration, and startup of automation solutions for BMS/EPMS systems, ensuring seamless integration and monitor with electrical, and cooling infrastructure.

  • Standardization & Implementation: Enforce system standards, frameworks, and deployment patterns for controls, BMS, and EPMS rollouts across multiple projects and sites.

  • SCADA & Graphics Configuration: Deploy and configure dashboards, HMIs, and operator workstations, ensuring site personnel have clear, functional visibility and control over complex building and power systems.

  • Startup Governance & Escalation Resolution: Oversee system integrators during standard deployments and point-to-point checkouts to ensure strict compliance with design standards, and operate as the controls escalation point to troubleshoot complex automation integration, system inconsistencies, and network integration issues.

  • Protocol Integration & Troubleshooting: Collaborate with design engineers, contractors, and OEM partners in the field to configure, integrate, and troubleshoot networks utilizing BACnet, Modbus, OPC-UA, and MQTT protocols.

  • Site Validation & Handover: Conduct system testing, simulation, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) to validate functionality, sequencing, and data accuracy prior to operational handover.

  • System Optimization & Turnover: Ensure controls platforms correctly collect and push real-time and historical data, enabling performance insight and analysis.

  • Site Support & Training: Mentor and train other controls engineers, on control system operation, troubleshooting best practices, and execution methodology.

 

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Deployment & Integration Mastery: Extensive professional experience in the physical deployment, integration, and startup of PLC, SCADA, BMS, and EPMS platforms.

  • Mission-Critical Execution: Proven ability to successfully execute, deploy, and startup automation systems in data center or other high-availability environments.

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role

As a Staff Commissioning Engineer, you will serve as the primary point of accountability for commissioning activities across your assigned data center projects. You will own the full commissioning lifecycle — from factory witness testing through integrated systems testing and formal turnover — ensuring all electrical, and EPMS systems are delivered in alignment with design intent, Owner Project Requirements, and Crusoe's operational readiness standards. This role requires deep technical expertise, strong cross-functional coordination, and the ability to manage third-party commissioning agents and vendors with minimal oversight.

 
 

What You'll Be Working On

  • Serve as the on-site electrical subject matter expert for all commissioning activities, serving as the primary escalation point for technical issues across all project phases.

  • Review contractor submittals, shop drawings, and O&M documentation to ensure alignment with design intent and project specifications.

  • Ensure Owner Project Requirements (OPR) remain aligned with commissioning scope throughout the project lifecycle, tracking changes and maintaining traceability to project objectives.

  • Oversee third-party commissioning agents (CxA), including scope development, performance management, deliverable tracking, and activity oversight such as factory witness testing and startup validation.

  • Identify equipment requiring factory testing and coordinate with the procurement team to schedule vendor testing activities.

  • Review and validate factory test procedures for compliance with project specifications prior to execution; oversee Factory Witness Testing (FWT) for off-site manufactured equipment.

  • Review and approve commissioning documentation including the Cx Plan, L2–L5 test scripts, reports, and turnover packages.

  • Oversee quality control processes including first-of-kind inspections and installation validation.

  • Drive issue identification, troubleshooting, remediation, and formal closure across all commissioning phases.

  • Ensure all commissioning activities — both static and dynamic testing — align with approved plans and performance standards.

  • Facilitate cross-functional collaboration between construction, engineering, controls, and operations teams throughout all project phases.

  • Manage stakeholder expectations by clearly defining commissioning processes, roles, and levels of engagement.

  • Ensure all commissioning documentation is complete, accurate, and supports a clean project turnover.

  • Support transition to operations by providing technical guidance, training coordination, and post-handover support as required.

  • Enforce safety, compliance, and regulatory requirements across all commissioning activities.

 
 

What You'll Bring

  • 7+ years of experience in data center commissioning, construction, or critical infrastructure delivery.

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, or a related field; equivalent commissioning experience considered (CxA certification a plus).

  • Deep knowledge of commissioning levels L1 through L5 and the associated documentation and testing requirements at each phase.

  • Hands-on experience with data center systems including power distribution and EPMS infrastructure.

  • Proven experience managing third-party commissioning agents and holding vendors accountable to scope, schedule, and quality.

  • Ability to review and interpret technical documentation including construction drawings, single-line diagrams, submittals, and test procedures.

  • Strong cross-functional coordination skills with the ability to align construction, engineering, controls, and operations teams around commissioning objectives.

  • Experience with issue tracking, risk management, and project reporting across multiple concurrent workstreams.

  • Solid understanding of safety and compliance requirements within active construction and commissioning environments.

  • Willingness to travel to project sites as required (75% travel).

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $136,000 - $165,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDDIG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Network Engineer, Deployment
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About this Role

Crusoe Cloud is seeking a Senior Staff Network Deployment Engineer to serve as the technical owner of how we deploy network infrastructure across our global fleet. As we rapidly scale our footprint of high-performance compute (HPC) and GPU-based AI infrastructure, you will define the deployment strategy, set the standards, and architect the automation platform that brings new data centers and edge sites online — at a pace and scale few companies have ever attempted.

This is a senior technical leadership role at the intersection of Network Engineering, Data Center Operations, and Infrastructure Strategy. You will partner with Network Architecture to shape designs for deployability, mentor a team of Staff and Senior engineers executing your vision, and represent the deployment org in cross-functional planning with Supply Chain, Data Center Ops, and Site Reliability leadership. You're not refining a runbook — you're authoring the playbook that defines how the world's most innovative AI cloud comes online.

What You'll Be Working On

  • Own Global Deployment Strategy: Define the multi-quarter technical roadmap for how Crusoe deploys network infrastructure across new and existing data centers, edge sites, and backbone interconnects.

  • Set the Standards: Author and ratify internal RFCs and technical standards for physical and logical network deployment — cabling, optics, fabric provisioning, validation, and handoff — that the broader engineering org executes against.

  • Influence Architecture for Deployability: Partner closely with Network Architecture to shape designs that scale operationally; serve as the senior voice ensuring what gets designed can actually be built and validated at hyperscale pace.

  • Architect the Deployment Automation Platform: Set the technical direction for Crusoe's ZTP, IaC, and validation tooling stack. Drive the strategy for Python-, Ansible-, and CI/CD-based systems that stage and validate hundreds of devices simultaneously.

  • Define the Validation Framework: Establish the burn-in, site acceptance testing (SAT), and commissioning criteria used across the fleet to ensure zero-defect handovers to Operations.

  • Lead Vendor and Partner Strategy: Establish standards, SLAs, and qualification programs for structured cabling vendors, remote hands partners, and data center providers globally. Influence hardware vendor roadmaps (Arista, Juniper, NVIDIA/Mellanox) based on Crusoe's operational needs.

  • Drive Capacity and Asset Strategy: Partner with Supply Chain and Infrastructure leadership on capacity planning, hardware lifecycle, and the turn-up cadence for new backbone capacity and edge interconnects.

  • Mentor and Multiply: Provide technical guidance to Staff and Senior network deployment engineers. Lead design reviews, post-incident reviews, and drive systemic improvements to deployment quality across the org.

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • 12+ years of network engineering experience with a heavy focus on large-scale data center deployments and infrastructure programs, including significant time in hyperscale, large cloud, or ISP environments.

  • Python

  • Demonstrated Technical Leadership: Proven track record of authoring standards, mentoring engineers, and driving multi-quarter technical initiatives that span teams. You've operated as a senior technical voice in an organization where decisions you've made are still in production.

  • Hyperscale Operational Experience: Comfort operating at scale — 10K+ network devices, multi-region fabric deployments, and the realities of building when the supply chain, the timeline, and the physics are all working against you.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

About the Role:

Crusoe's Compute supply chain runs around the clock and across continents. As we scale GPU and CPU server deployments globally, we need a sourcing specialist who can act as the connective tissue between deployment, procurement, and vendor operations for our global Compute category.

This is a hands-on execution role and you will report to the Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager, Compute and work as part of a globally distributed team supporting GPU/CPU server programs across all Crusoe data centers. Your scope covers BOM management, supplier onboarding, RFQ execution, and procurement operations for Crusoe Cloud's compute infrastructure. This role is ideal for someone with deep hardware fluency and proven procurement execution who is ready to step into a strategic sourcing track.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • BOM and Hardware Sourcing Execution: Support BOM planning, hardware requisitions, and procurement execution for GPU and CPU server deployments across all Crusoe data centers, partnering with deployment engineering and cloud operations teams.

  • Global Supplier Coordination: Serve as a key point of contact for global Compute suppliers (OEMs, ODMs, and component vendors), driving timely responses on quotes, lead times, and shipment status.

  • RFQ and Quote Management: Lead RFQ cycles for compute hardware in partnership with the Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager, including quote analysis, supplier comparison, and recommendation packages.

  • Purchase Order Lifecycle: Own end-to-end PO creation, change orders, invoice reconciliation, and payment follow-up in Coupa for the Compute category.

  • Supplier Onboarding and Compliance: Drive supplier onboarding, NDA coordination, and vendor compliance documentation for new and existing Compute suppliers.

  • DCIM and Asset Accuracy: Maintain accurate hardware tracking in NetBox/DCIM systems for deployments and ensure data integrity across procurement and asset records.

  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner with Deployment, Cloud Operations, Finance, Legal, and Logistics to unblock procurement issues and keep deployments on schedule.

  • Urgent Deployment Support: Provide rapid-response procurement support for critical data center deployments, including expedites and emergency sourcing.

  • Reporting and Visibility: Prepare procurement status reports, PO trackers, and supplier performance updates for the Compute leadership team.

  • Process Improvement: Identify and implement workflow improvements across procurement operations, with particular focus on automation opportunities using modern tools.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: 5+ years of progressive experience in procurement, sourcing, or hardware deployment operations, preferably for data center, cloud, or hardware supply chains.

  • Hardware Fluency: Strong working knowledge of compute server hardware (GPU servers, CPU servers, components) and ability to read BOMs, specs, and vendor quotes at the component level.

  • Procurement Operations: Hands-on experience with Coupa or a comparable ERP/procurement platform, including PO management, supplier onboarding, and invoice reconciliation.

  • DCIM / Asset Tracking: Working experience with NetBox, ServiceNow, or similar DCIM/asset management tools.

  • Vendor Coordination: Track record of managing OEM, ODM, distributor, or VAR relationships at an operational level.

  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to operate effectively across time zones with a globally distributed team.

  • Process Orientation: Highly organized, with a track record of building or improving procurement and operations workflows.

  • Compliance: Must be able to pass a background check.

  • Authorization: Authorized to work in Ireland, or eligible for Crusoe-sponsored relocation and work authorization.

Bonus Points:

  • Hands-on experience with HPE, Dell, Supermicro, or major ODMs (Quanta, Wiwynn, Foxconn, Inventec, Hon Hai).

  • Experience supporting GPU server programs (NVIDIA H100/H200/B200/GB200 generations or equivalent).

  • Automation and scripting exposure (Python, SQL, Power Automate, or comparable).

  • Active use of modern AI tools (Claude, Gemini, Copilot, NotebookLM) for procurement workflows, vendor communication, or analysis.

  • Prior experience in a hyperscaler, cloud, or large-scale data center procurement environment.

  • Familiarity with international import/export, customs, and trade compliance for hardware (US, EU, APAC).

  • Must be able to pass a background check

  • Embody the Company values

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $110,000 - $135,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Data Scientist, Analytics
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Join Crusoe as a Data Scientist, a dedicated hire on our central Data Science and Engineering team. This full-time position offers you the opportunity to own the data and analytics function for key parts of the business, starting with the Data Center Infrastructure Group (DIG) -- the arm of Crusoe that builds and operates data centers, spanning real estate, energy, construction, and parts lifecycle management. As part of a central team, you will also have the opportunity to partner with other groups across the company as needs arise.

You will partner directly with business stakeholders, translate their needs into analytical work, and own the reporting and data quality that leadership depends on for high-stakes decisions.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Own Reporting & Dashboards: Build and maintain the weekly and monthly reports and dashboards that business leaders rely on for operational decision-making. You are the DRI for accuracy and timeliness.

  • Partner with Business Stakeholders: Work directly with leaders across construction, real estate, energy, procurement, and other functions to gather requirements and translate business questions into analytical deliverables.

  • Drive New Data Integrations: Work with data engineering to identify and onboard data from third-party enterprise systems (ERP, procurement, asset management, etc.) into the data lake, defining requirements and validating data quality as new sources come online.

  • Track Complex Projects: The infrastructure side of Crusoe runs large, multi-year construction projects with long lead times and many vendors. You will build and maintain tracking for project progress, cost burn-down, timelines, and financial performance.

  • Translate Business to Technical: Take business requirements and produce technical or techno-functional specifications that data engineers can execute on. Bridge the gap between what the business needs and how the data platform delivers it.

  • Support Master Data Management: As the company matures its MDM and ERP practices, you will help ensure master data (vendors, parts, projects, cost centers, sites) is consistent and accurate across systems.

  • Champion Data Quality: Identify gaps and inconsistencies in data, investigate root causes, and work with data engineers to implement fixes. When a number is wrong, you own the resolution.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Business Acumen: You understand why you are building something, not just what. You ask questions until the business context is clear and you can explain your work to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Technical Fluency: Possess strong SQL skills -- you will query BigQuery daily. Comfort working with large, complex datasets across multiple source systems.

  • Modern Data Stack Experience: Experience with a modern data stack (BigQuery, dbt, Airflow, or equivalents).

  • Reporting Expertise: Experience building and maintaining dashboards and reports for operational use. Familiarity with BI tools (e.g., Sigma, Looker, Power BI, Tableau).

  • Stakeholder Management: Proven experience working directly with business partners to gather requirements and deliver data products. You are credible in a room with construction project managers and equally comfortable reviewing a data model with an engineer.

  • Ownership: Track record of being the go-to person for "is this number right?" You take accountability for data accuracy and do not wait to be told when something is off.

Bonus Points

  • Background in construction, manufacturing, supply chain, or other operationally complex industries.

  • Experience with ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, Sage Intacct, or similar) and the data that flows from them.

  • Familiarity with master data management concepts and cross-system entity resolution.

  • Experience working in a fast-growing company where processes are still being built.

  • Python for data analysis is a plus but not required.

  • Experience with AI-assisted coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot) to accelerate analytical work.

Our Data Stack

  • Cloud: Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

  • Data Lake: Google Cloud Storage (GCS)

  • Data Warehouse: BigQuery

  • Orchestration: Apache Airflow

  • Transformation: dbt (SQL-based)

  • BI Tools: Sigma (primary), Grafana (operational)

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $136,850 -$161,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role

As an Assembly Technician, you’ll help us build modular data centers right here in our manufacturing facility. This is a heavy-duty, hands-on role where you’ll work with a tight-knit production team to assemble modular buildings. You’ll be working with equipment to attach large parts to metal frames (up to 60 feet long), weatherproofing and sealing, and bolting components together using nuts, bolts, and fasteners. Check out what our final products look like here.

No data center experience required – if you have a strong work ethic, mechanical aptitude, and want to build a career with a rapidly expanding company, we’d love to hear from you.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Building & Assembly: Bolt together wall panels, steel columns, roof racks, light fixtures, and cable trays using nuts, bolts, and fasteners. Use wrenches, bridge/overhead cranes, forklifts, and power tools to finish assembling units.

  • Weatherproofing & Sealing: Apply final touches like gaskets, caulking, and metal panel joints to make sure the modular units are sealed tight.

  • Structural Work: Work with large equipment to attach parts to metal frames (up to 60 ft long), and help install metal siding and roofing.

  • Modular Data Center Build-Outs: Work as part of a team to install equipment like GPU racks and electrical components inside modular buildings.

  • Kitting & Pre-Work: Gather, count, and prep all the small parts and hardware (the "kits") needed for a specific assembly step before the work begins.

  • Materials & Work Orders: Review work orders to make sure your team has the right parts and materials before starting each job.

  • Labeling & Compliance: Help apply company logos, labels, and safety ratings to finished products.

  • Inventory & Organization: Keep your workspace clean and parts organized to avoid production slowdowns.

  • Team Support: Pitch in as needed to keep production moving.

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • Hand & Power Tool Experience: Comfortable using basic shop tools like wrenches, impact guns, tape measures, and drills.

  • Mechanical Aptitude: A mechanical mindset — you enjoy figuring out how things work and go together. Ability to assemble large parts with nuts and bolts.

  • Physical Requirements: Ability to lift, lower, and push materials up to 50 lbs. Ability to be on your feet for your full shift as it requires standing, walking, stooping, and bending.

  • Basic Computer Skills

  • Drawing Interpretation: Ability to accurately read and following drawings and schematics for assembly requirements.

  • Team Player: A positive attitude, eagerness to learn, great communication skills, and ability to work well with your team.

  • Problem Solving: Lots of patience to problem-solve, troubleshoot equipment, and see complex projects through to the end.

  • Coachability & Growth Mindset: You listen to tips and guidance from supervisors and senior team members, and you use that feedback to make your work better. Share ideas to make your team’s work safer, faster, and/or better.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required. Must be able to pass a background check.

Bonus Points

  • Manufacturing Experience Preferred: Background working in a heavy manufacturing facility, industrial shop, or assembly line environment that dealt with large-scale components and products – especially metal and/or environments involving heavy equipment such as overhead cranes and forklifts.

  • Bridge/Overhead Crane Operation Experience

  • Forklift Certification

  • ERP: Familiarity with ERP software, such as Infor Visual, Acumatica, or similar programs

  • MS Office or Google Workspace

  • ISO 9001

  • Electro-Mechanical Experience

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $23 -$31 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.descriptionHtml:

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role

At Crusoe, the Capacity Planning & Efficiency team operates at the critical intersection of all Crusoe products, services, and underlying physical infrastructure. As the Senior GPU Capacity and Optimization Planner, you will own the day-to-day management, allocation, and strategic bin-packing optimization of Crusoe Cloud’s high-performance GPU fleet. This is a highly cross-functional, high-impact role that bridges the gap between our technical infrastructure and our Go-To-Market (GTM) engine.

You will work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and Fleet Management to translate commercial customer pipelines into requirements within the datacenter. Your mission will be to maximize resource utilization, eliminate fragmentation across accelerated computing clusters, and ensure our AI/ML customers receive seamless performance, directly supporting Crusoe’s mission to align the future of computing with environmental sustainability.

What You'll Be Working On

  • GPU Fleet Bin-Packing & Optimization: Develop and execute advanced bin-packing strategies to optimize GPU resource allocations within our data centers, minimizing fragmentation and maximizing cluster utilization.

  • GTM & Pipeline Alignment: Act as the primary technical capacity partner to Sales, Customer Success, and Solutions Engineering, reviewing upcoming pipeline demands and mapping them to physical hardware constraints.

  • Cross-Functional Capacity Execution: Collaborate tightly with Fleet Management, Infrastructure Engineering, and Data Center Operations to ensure maximum uptime of our customer workloads.

  • Utilization Modeling & Metrics: Design and implement models to track real-time GPU cluster headroom, workload densities, and allocation velocities to prevent supply bottlenecks.

  • Strategic Demand Forecasting: Synthesize commercial demand signals and large-scale AI training/inference architectural trends to inform hardware placement and scheduling.

  • Automation Requirements: Partner with Core Software Engineering to translate manual allocation processes into scalable, automated programmatic scheduling and visualization tools.

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • Proven Capacity & Scheduling Domain Expertise: 3+ years of direct experience in Infrastructure Capacity Planning, Technical Product Management, or Systems Engineering with heavy exposure to machine-level resource scaling.

  • Hyperscaler Experience: Experience working within a hyperscaler cloud environment (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure, Oracle Cloud) or a specialized, large-scale AI/accelerated compute cloud fabric.

  • GPU & Accelerated Compute Knowledge: Solid foundational understanding of GPU topologies (e.g., NVIDIA H100/B200 ecosystems).

  • Strong Cross-Functional Navigation: Proven ability to communicate complex infrastructure and physical layout constraints clearly to business stakeholders like Sales and Customer Success, while translating commercial requirements back to hardware engineers.

  • Education: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Data Science, or an equivalent quantitative field.

Bonus Points

  • Deep technical familiarity with distributed AI training frameworks and multi-tenant cloud storage dynamics.

  • A passion for green energy and aligning massive computing scales with environmental sustainability initiatives.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000 - $195,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Load Integration & Model Development
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

As a Senior Engineer for Load Interconnection & Model Development you will play a critical role in expanding our energy infrastructure and integrating our large-load facilities into the electric grid. You will be a key individual contributor, focusing on the complex challenges of connecting and optimizing our operations within the MISO and SPP RTOs.

This position requires deep technical expertise in power systems and a proactive approach to problem-solving. You will navigate the regulatory and technical hurdles of load deliverability to ensure our data centers have the high-capacity, reliable power required for AI and high-performance computing.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Perform and support comprehensive grid integration studies for large-load facilities within MISO and SPP..

  • Manage transmission injection processes and perform load deliverability studies to ensure grid stability and capacity.

  • Strategize Points of Interconnection (POIs) based on evolving business needs and changing regulatory requirements.

  • Contribute to the technical development of the team, sharing expertise and best practices in grid integration and ISO/RTO navigation.

  • Work with internal teams to draft technical specifications and support Business Development on the technical aspects of project proposals.

  • Identify POIs that best suit our business development needs while staying ahead of grid code compliance and transmission topology changes.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Master’s degree in Power Systems with 3+ years of experience, or a Bachelor’s degree with 7+ years of experience in Power Systems.

  • Deep experience in grid planning, system modeling, and grid code compliance studies.

  • Strong working knowledge of MISO/SPP transmission topology and load interconnection methodologies.

  • Ability to think outside the box to identify POIs that offer the best path to interconnection for large-scale loads.

  • Excellent technical report writing and verbal communication skills.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with other ISO/RTO markets (e.g., CAISO, ERCOT, WECC, SERC).

  • Proficiency with power system simulation tools: PowerWorld Simulator, ETAP, TSAT, or ASPEN OneLiner.

  • Working knowledge of scripting languages such as R or Python for data analysis and automation.

Benefits:

  • Industry competitive pay

  • Restricted Stock Units in a fast growing, well-funded technology company

  • Health insurance package options that include HDHP and PPO, vision, and dental for you and your dependents

  • Employer contributions to HSA accounts

  • Paid Parental Leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Teladoc

  • 401(k) with a 100% match up to 4% of salary

  • Generous paid time off and holiday schedule

  • Cell phone reimbursement

  • Tuition reimbursement

  • Subscription to the Calm app

  • MetLife Legal

  • Company paid commuter benefit; $300 per month


Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $175,000 - $210,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Principal Sustaining Engineering Manager - Spark
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI Factory company accelerating energy and compute infrastructure. We believe that “speed is the only moat” and our vertical integration allows us to design, manufacture, and deploy modular power and compute infrastructure at market leading speed and cost.

 

We are seeking a Sustaining Engineering Leader to own how Spark physical modules perform post-deployment and drive continuous improvement. While Product Management defines future generations and NPI delivers them for production, you own each generation once it ramps: fleet reliability, field failures, configuration, component obsolescence, and the design modifications required for full service life performance.

 

In this role, “hardware” and “product” refers to the physical infrastructure of the Spark module: structural steel modules, RPPs, DLC cooling loops, CDUs, chillers, piping headers, electrical and mechanical systems, and power distribution gear. Compute hardware (servers, GPUs, storage, networking, and rack specifications) is owned by Cloud Product. Sitting on the Spark design engineering team, you capture how deployed Spark modules perform in service and aggregate the lessons learned and required changes into the design process, so the next version is more reliable, serviceable, and cost-effective. Working with Data Center Facility Operations and Field Operations, you are the definitive evidence source for Product Management and NPI, turning field data into design requirements and acceptance criteria. You start as the single-threaded leader of this function and build the team as the fleet expands.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

I. Fleet Ownership, Facility Ops Interface & Field Issues

  • Year 1 Ramp & Handover: Participate in production release and ramp readiness reviews for deploying generations as the receiving organization. Establish as-built baselines, spares strategies, service intervals, and repair-vs-replace policies prior to initial fleet launch.

  • Facility Operations Feedback Loop: Serve as the primary engineering interface with the Data Center Facility Operations team. Gather site-level field feedback across broader facility power, thermal, and environmental systems to analyze how site-wide operational dynamics impact individual Spark modules.

  • Fleet Reliability: Own subsystem failure rates, mean time between failures (MTBF), and repeat failure metrics. Define the required telemetry every deployed unit must report to ensure operational visibility.

  • Closed-Loop Corrective Action: Stand up and run the Failure Reporting, Analysis, and Corrective Action System (FRACAS) function. Drive root-cause analysis to closure with verified fixes, containing safety or fleet-wide risks immediately when issues arise.

II. Change, Configuration & Obsolescence

  • Post-Release Change Control: Own engineering change orders (ECOs) for fielded generations, quantifying cost and fleet impacts prior to approval.

  • Configuration Baseline: Maintain as-built and as-maintained configuration baselines, ensuring field retrofits precisely target affected units.

  • Proactive Component Obsolescence: Manage component lifecycles using Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) practices - modeling last-time buys against fleet demand and qualifying alternate parts before component shortages occur.

  • Retrofits & Maintenance: Issue change packages, preventive maintenance schedules, and acceptance criteria for Field Operations execution.

III. Feedback Loop to Product Management & NPI

  • Requirements into Product: Convert fleet and facility operations data into quantified design requirements for future Product Requirement Document (PRD) iterations.

  • Qualification into NPI: Supply field-derived acceptance criteria to NPI, ensuring historical failure modes are designed out of future module generations before release.

  • Total Cost of Ownership (TCO): Own reliability, serviceability, and maintenance inputs driving Spark unit economics and long-term TCO.

  • Serviceability Advocacy: Represent maintainability and serviceability in design reviews, using field data to influence future hardware architecture.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Education

  • Required: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Reliability, or a closely related engineering discipline.

Experience

  • 10 to 15 years in sustaining, reliability, or product support engineering for deployed capital hardware or infrastructure assets.

  • Track record of converting field performance data into design changes that measurably reduce failure rates and service costs.

  • Experience building sustaining engineering processes (root-cause analysis frameworks, review boards, spares policies) from the ground up.

  • Hands-on management of component obsolescence and supplier end-of-life transitions for long-lifecycle hardware.

Technical Depth

  • Reliability Engineering: Failure Reporting, Analysis, and Corrective Action Systems (FRACAS), structured root-cause analysis (8D, 5-Why), MTBF modeling, and population failure rate analysis.

  • Configuration Management: PLM workflows, serial-level effectivity, change order management, and as-built control.

  • Obsolescence & Service Economics: Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) practices, last-time buy modeling, spares planning, and unit service cost drivers.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with modular, containerized, or prefabricated infrastructure products in the field.

  • Direct familiarity with liquid-cooled data center hardware.

  • The persistence to chase root causes past obvious answers, paired with the practical judgment needed to manage fleet disruptions.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $225,000 -$255,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

 

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About This Role:

At Crusoe, we move fast and build things. We are seeking a dedicated and detail-oriented Material Handler to ensure the smooth and accurate flow of materials from our manufacturing shops to job sites. This full-time role is critical to our production process. You will be responsible for the preparation, packaging, and continuous improvement of all shipping activities for the products and parts we manufacture. The ideal candidate has proven experience in shipping and logistics, exceptional attention to detail, and a commitment to safety and teamwork. You will play a vital role in our daily operations, ensuring that the right materials arrive at the right place, on time.

 

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Shipping & Logistics: Collaborate with the transportation coordinator to follow the shipping schedule, identify opportunities for efficiency, and prepare and process all required documentation, including shipping invoices and packing slips. You will also coordinate and perform the loading of outgoing shipments, ensuring proper packaging to prevent damage.

  • Material Handling & Inventory: Inspect all incoming and outgoing inventory for accuracy and quality. You will be responsible for tagging all materials with the required information and using a pallet jack or forklift to move materials throughout the shop and load/unload delivery trucks.

  • Quality & Continuous Improvement: Ensure all quality check sheets are completed to company standards before final packaging. You will photograph projects to create a quality history and document any damages, overages, or shortages. Your contributions will help the team update the status board and identify areas for improvement.

  • Leadership & Safety: Uphold Crusoe's relentless commitment to safety and adhere to all company policies and procedures. You will provide input to management regarding staffing and hiring decisions and actively participate in training new team members to foster a positive, team-oriented culture.

 

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: Proven experience in a shipping, receiving, or related role.

  • Technical Skills: Required forklift experience and the ability to use basic hand tools.

  • Personal Attributes: Exceptional attention to detail and a strong commitment to accuracy. You must also be a collaborative team player with a good attitude and a willingness to learn and improve.

  • Physical Requirements: The ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs. You must also be able to stand, walk, stoop, bend, and use your arms and hands for a full workday.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and is located within a safety-sensitive facility. Active drug and alcohol program participation is required. Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Proficiency with ERP software (e.g., Infor Visual, Acumatica).

  • Experience with ISO 9001:2015 standards.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $21 -$26/HR + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

About This Role:

The Inventory Control Coordinator is responsible for maintaining optimal inventory levels, managing materials within the ERP system, overseeing finished goods inventories, and conducting annual physical inventories. This role is crucial for ensuring smooth production operations by providing timely access to necessary materials and maintaining inventory accuracy. The ideal candidate has 3-5 years of inventory control experience in a manufacturing environment and is proficient with MRP systems. This is a full-time position.

 

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Inventory Transaction Management: Transacting the movement of inventory for multiple projects, ensuring proper documentation (i.e., material requisition) is completed and procedures are followed before and after any inventory movement. Managing transactions within the WMS/ERP to match the physical movement of goods. Identifying discrepancies and performing root cause analysis.

  • Inventory Control and Accuracy: Conducting cycle counts to control inventory accuracy and minimize variances. Performing monthly cycle counts of material. Ensuring adequate inventory of materials and products in accordance with inventory cycles and organizational philosophy. Double-checking the Bill of Materials for projects taken to production to ensure all parts are present.

  • Production Floor Support: Running parts to the production floor. Issuing parts to jobs per specifications. Kitting jobs for production. Unboxing all parts and grouping like materials on the job cart together. Pulling sheet metal for the CNC operators to speed up production times.

  • ERP System Management: Using the ERP system to accurately track materials.

  • Inventory Planning and Management: Assisting in planning the full inventory annually. Assisting with managing and disposing of surplus materials and scrap.

  • Warehouse Assistance: Providing assistance to the warehouse where needed, including receiving, unloading trucks, cleaning, and picking up the lot.

 

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Inventory Control Experience: 3-5 years of inventory control experience in a manufacturing environment.

  • Physical Requirements: Ability to meet the physical demands of the role, including lifting, lowering, pushing, and pulling materials.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with an MRP system.

  • Metrics & Dashboards: Build metrics engines, real-time dashboards, and automated insights pipelines that provide continuous visibility into technical risk posture and emerging infrastructure risks.
