jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Crusoe Container Registry
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We're looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help make Crusoe Cloud's container registry fast and reliable as the platform grows. The registry sits on the critical path of every deployment and job launch on our platform, and its performance directly affects how quickly customer workloads come online. You'll own the evolution of the registry, drive its scaling roadmap, and be accountable for how it performs, degrades, and recovers in production. This is a full-time position.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Own the technical direction: Set the architecture and scaling roadmap for Crusoe Cloud's container registry. Establish the patterns and standards the team builds against, and stay accountable for scalability, reliability, and maintainability over the long haul.

  • Ship end-to-end: Drive high impact changes from design through production, and stay accountable for their scalability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Push performance limits: Drive performance strategy across the system and get ahead of demand curves before they reach customers. Make the architecture tradeoffs that keep the registry dependable as it grows.

  • Multiply the team: Raise the team's technical bar through architecture, design, and code review, and through mentorship, while staying hands-on on complex challenges. Make the engineers around you more effective, not just yourself.

  • Drive technical strategy across teams: Influence designs across adjacent teams, align with product and other partners on priorities and tradeoffs, and lead the technical response when things break.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Distributed systems at scale: You have proven success designing, scaling, and hardening distributed systems, all while keeping them reliable under high-load production environments.

  • A performance-driven mindset: You set performance strategy and have deep, practical experience profiling, benchmarking, and optimizing distributed systems, with sound judgment about latency, throughput, caching, and resource tradeoffs at scale.

  • Thrive in ambiguity: You thrive on transforming ambiguous performance problems into measured action and durable fixes. You work ahead of demand, identifying constraints before they reach customers.

  • A track record of system level ownership: You've owned critical systems from design through production and carried them through operational pressure. You've made difficult calls under conflicting requirements and visible risk, and stood behind them.

  • A customer-centric mindset: You keep the customers top of mind, and you can translate their needs into actionable changes in the codebase.

  • Technical & infrastructure proficiency: You have strong fundamentals in microservices and cloud-native infrastructure technologies (Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform) alongside languages like Go, Rust, Java, or C++.

  • Collaboration and communication: You are comfortable working across functions to align on priorities and to explain technical tradeoffs clearly to technical and non-technical partners alike.

  • Mentorship and force multiplication: You’ve grown other engineers. You’ve mentored teammates on the team's systems, helped newer engineers find their footing, raised the team’s technical bar, and contributed to hiring.

  • Experience: You have 8+ years of professional software development experience, including time spent building and operating distributed systems but we care more about what you've built than the exact number.

We know great engineers come from many different paths. If you're excited about this work but don't match every point below, we'd still love to hear from you. What you've built and how you think matters more to us than a perfect checklist.

Bonus Points

  • Familiarity with the OCI image and distribution specs

  • Experience building container registry products

  • Experience with storage or caching systems at scale

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Strong interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills.

  • Team player who can work well independently and with limited direction.

  • Working knowledge of accounting principles and financial statements.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

As Senior Manager, Utility Contracts, you will sit within the Energy Development Group (EDG) and own the full lifecycle of Crusoe's utility infrastructure agreements: negotiating new agreements and amendments with serving utilities, and managing the obligations under executed agreements across our data center portfolio. You will be the person who knows every deadline, every deliverable, and every counterparty commitment. You will work hand-in-hand with our real estate, power engineering, legal, and finance teams, and help shape the obligation-management platform we are building to scale this function across every future project.

This is a role for someone who has lived inside the utility world - who reads tariffs and connection requirements fluently, understands how utilities think about interconnection, cost recovery, and reliability obligations, and can lead negotiations with utility commercial and legal teams.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Utility Agreement Negotiation: Lead the negotiation of utility infrastructure agreements for new and existing data center campuses - construction agreements, operating agreements, transfer agreements, and amendments - in coordination with EDG commercial leads, outside counsel, and utility counterparties.

  • Obligation Management: Own the responsibility matrix for each project's agreement stack: every obligation tracked with its contractual cite, deadline, owner, and status. Run the monthly deadline review, drive early escalation of at-risk items, and make sure recurring obligations (reports, forecasts, certifications, payments) never slip.

  • Utility Requirements & Compliance: Serve as EDG's authority on utility requirements - tariff provisions, end-user connection requirements, metering and interconnection specifications, Good Utility Practice, and NERC / RTO reliability obligations for large loads (load ride-through, UFLS, emergency operations, ramp rates) and translate them into actionable requirements for our engineering and operations teams.

  • Construction agreements: Manage the contractual side of customer-build programs - design package submittals, procurement compliance against utility approved lists, commissioning and title transfer sequencing, easement and land-rights deliverables, and closeout obligations with enough EPC fluency to engage credibly with project and construction teams.

  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Act as the connective tissue between EDG, Real Estate, Power Engineering, Legal, Finance, and our data center tenants on everything touching the utility agreements - from milestone payments and collateral postings to easement deliveries and operating protocols.

  • Executive Reporting: Provide leadership with clear, current visibility into obligation status, upcoming deadlines, counterparty performance, and contract risks across the portfolio.

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • Deep Utility Experience: 8+ years in the electric utility sector, at a utility, or negotiating and managing utility agreements on behalf of large customers or developers - with direct experience in large-load interconnection, energy service / electric service agreements, and utility construction agreements.

  • Utility Requirements Fluency: Strong working command of utility tariffs, end-user connection requirements, interconnection processes, metering standards, and reliability obligations (NERC standards, RTO/ISO requirements such as MISO, ERCOT, or CAISO large-load rules). You know how utilities operate, what they will and won't agree to, and why.

  • EPC Exposure: Hands-on familiarity with the engineering, procurement, and construction lifecycle - design reviews, procurement standards, commissioning, and project closeout - sufficient to manage customer-build and transfer obligations credibly alongside project teams.

  • Negotiation Track Record: Demonstrated success negotiating complex infrastructure agreements with utility counterparties, balancing commercial outcomes, schedule protection, and long-term relationships.

  • Contract Management Rigor: Exceptional organization and attention to detail. You are the person who reads the footnotes, catches the cross-reference, and builds the system so nothing depends on memory.

  • Cross-Functional Communication: Ability to translate contract language into clear actions for engineers, real estate teams, finance, and executives - and to communicate credibly with utility commercial, legal, and operations staff.

  • Location: Based in, or willing to relocate to, Dallas, TX or San Francisco, CA.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center, large industrial, or other large-load development projects.

  • Familiarity with behind-the-meter / bring-your-own-capacity structures, customer-build lead lines, or asset transfer agreements with utilities.

  • Experience implementing contract lifecycle management or obligation-tracking tools.

  • Utility regulatory exposure (state commission proceedings, tariff filings)

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000 - $200,000+ Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role

Crusoe is scaling hyperscale AI data center campuses across the country, and we're looking for a seasoned construction leader to own delivery across a major program or geography. As Senior Director of Construction, you'll set the strategy and operating model for a portfolio of our most critical builds, own the budgets and schedules that make them successful, and build and shape the construction organization that delivers them - including developing the next generation of senior construction leaders.

This is a role that spans hands-on delivery and organizational leadership: you're close enough to the work to solve real problems on real job sites, and senior enough to partner with Executive leadership on workforce strategy, capital priorities, and succession planning as Crusoe's construction program scales.

What You'll Own

  • Own the strategy and operating model for construction delivery across a defined geography or major program, partnering with DIG (Digital Infrastructure Group) leadership to set 12-month delivery targets and capital investment priorities.

  • Lead a portfolio of complex, hyperscale AI Data Center construction programs, accountable for on-time, on-budget delivery and for the organizational investments that improve delivery velocity and quality.

  • Oversee multiple simultaneous data center construction programs where decisions carry division-level risk and directly affect Crusoe's ability to meet regional compute capacity commitments.

  • Solve problems that cross site, contractor, and functional boundaries by designing scalable delivery frameworks and program management methodologies - navigating contractor market constraints, regulatory complexity, and capital allocation decisions at the same time.

  • Build, mentor, and lead a team of construction management professionals and specialists - hiring well, developing talent, and creating a culture where people do their best work.

  • Lead with strong emotional intelligence; read team dynamics, navigate conflict constructively so you can build high-performing construction management teams that stay together.

  • Partner with DIG and Executive leadership on organizational structure, workforce strategy, and succession planning as Crusoe's construction program scales, and develop the next generation of senior construction leaders within the function.

  • Manage executive stakeholder relationships and drive organizational performance through effective leadership and accountability, partnering with GCs, subcontractors, and internal teams to align on project plans and long-range build strategy.

  • Drive cross-functional coordination with Engineering, Operations, Finance, and Real Estate to keep projects aligned with company-wide objectives.

  • Stay current on construction best practices, methodologies, and industry trends, and apply that knowledge to raise the bar across your portfolio.

  • Travel as needed (up to 40%) to oversee multiple project sites.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • 15+ years of experience in construction management of mission-critical projects, including direct experience delivering hyperscale data centers, large hospitals, or highly complex infrastructure projects.

  • A proven track record of managing and delivering challenging, large-budget project portfolios on time and on budget, at the scale of multiple concurrent programs.

  • Experience building organizational capability, not just delivering projects - you've built, led, or grown construction management or project teams and developed managers and directors within them.

  • Comfort making consequential decisions with incomplete information and competing priorities, and balancing technical and resource tradeoffs across teams and programs.

  • High EQ and strong people leadership instincts, you know how to get the best out of a team under pressure and tight deadlines.

  • Deep understanding of construction best practices, budgeting, scheduling and quality management, with the judgment to apply them across multiple projects at once.

  • Ability to operate across multiple stakeholders; internal leadership, GCs, subcontractors, cross-functional and executive partners in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.

About This Role:

The Senior Contract Specialist (IT, Network & Cloud) plays a pivotal role as the bridge between technical requirements and legal/financial compliance. In this position, you will oversee complex procurement, SLA negotiations, and licensing models tailored to modern data centers, cloud infrastructure, and enterprise software. Your expertise will directly impact company goals by optimizing cloud spending, mitigating vendor risk, and building a scalable procurement framework across our IT and Cloud footprint.

The ideal candidate possesses a strong grasp of SaaS, IaaS, and modern virtualization technologies, alongside a proven track record of contract lifecycle management. You thrive in a dynamic environment, excel at translating technical jargon into clear business terms, and know how to partner with cross-functional technical, legal, and financial leaders to protect company interests.

This role will be 100% onsite at our San Francisco office.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Contract Negotiation & Drafting: Define and negotiate complex Service Level Agreements (SLAs), focusing on critical uptime metrics, latency, and mean time to repair (MTTR).

  • Licensing & Model Transitions: Manage the transition from legacy perpetual licenses to subscription-based cloud models across platforms like Azure, AWS, and GCP.

  • Data Privacy & Compliance: Ensure all vendor agreements adhere to GDPR, CCPA, SOC2, and internal security standards in coordination with the CISO.

  • Financial & Cost Optimization: Monitor cloud consumption to eliminate unused licenses or inactive instances, driving cost savings across the organization.

  • Lifecycle & Renewal Management: Oversee contract timelines and co-terminous renewal structures to maximize bargaining power and streamline renewals.

  • Dispute Resolution & Vendor Oversight: Enforce SLA compliance and negotiate credit claims when vendors fail to meet performance and uptime commitments.

  • Asset & Security Tracking: Work with cross-functional teams to maintain an accurate inventory of physical hardware assets (routers, switches, servers) and software licenses.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: 3-5 years of dedicated experience in IT procurement, technology vendor management, or legal contract administration.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Law, Information Technology, or a related field.

  • Technical Knowledge: Deep understanding of cloud hierarchy (Public vs. Private), virtualization, and network security concepts.

  • Software Proficiency: Hands-on experience with Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) platforms and enterprise ERP tools like SAP or Oracle.

  • Legal & Compliance Acumen: Solid understanding of Intellectual Property (IP) rights, liability limitations, and Data Processing Agreements (DPAs).

  • Cross-Functional Communication: Demonstrated ability to translate complex technical concepts from engineering teams into clear, business-driven terms for executives.

Bonus Points:

  • Certified Professional Contract Manager (CCCM) certification.

  • Foundational cloud certifications (e.g., AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner).

  • Experience managing data center hardware procurement alongside cloud software contracts.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $110,000 - $135,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

(#INDCORP)

About This Role:

Crusoe is seeking an experienced and proactive Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) Specialist to join our expanding team and champion safety across our power operations. Based at our data center power plant in Abilene, TX, with potential travel to additional locations, you'll be an integral member of the Power Operations Team. Your deep technical safety knowledge, especially in rotating equipment, electrical safety, process safety, and/or large-scale turbine operations, will be crucial. We're looking for someone who can effectively communicate across all levels of the organization, continuously assess and mitigate risks, and foster a robust safety culture. This is a full-time position where your expertise will directly contribute to the efficiency and well-being of our critical power infrastructure.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Risk Partnership & Action Planning: Partner closely with the Power Operations Team to understand operational risks and develop concrete action plans to effectively address them.

  • HSE Culture Development: Cultivate a high level of HSE awareness and a strong safety culture through consistent communications, targeted training, and promotion of active involvement in all HSE programs.

  • Risk Assessment & Mitigation: Conduct thorough assessments of worker risks and provide actionable recommendations to reduce exposure and enhance safety.

  • Procedure & Process Implementation: Develop and implement various HSE processes, procedures, work instructions, and checklists, ensuring clear guidelines for safe operations.

  • Compliance Monitoring & Reporting: Actively monitor compliance with all relevant regulations, internal policies, and established procedures, and regularly report on HSE objectives and key metrics.

  • Stakeholder Engagement: Liaise effectively with contractors, clients, and regulatory agencies regarding HSE issues, ensuring transparent and constructive communication.

  • Audit & Assessment Support: Plan and actively assist with compliance audits and assessments, contributing to a culture of continuous improvement.

  • Incident Investigation & Analysis: Facilitate thorough incident investigations and lead root cause analysis efforts following any failures, incidents, or accidents to prevent recurrence.

  • Corrective Action Follow-Up: Actively monitor and follow up on the status of corrective actions, reports, and audit findings, ensuring timely completion and effectiveness.

  • HSE Training & Development: Coordinate and actively participate in the HSE training of all personnel, enhancing their safety knowledge and practices.

  • Regulatory Awareness: Maintain continuous awareness of new HSE requirements and manage their integration into existing systems and practices accordingly.

  • Documentation Management: Ensure that all relevant HSE documentation is meticulously maintained and readily available at all worksites.

  • Operational Group Support: Provide HSE support to other operational groups and projects as necessary, demonstrating flexibility and a broad commitment to safety.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Industry Experience: Minimum of 5+ years of relevant industry experience, with a strong preference for backgrounds in Oil and Gas, Plants, Refineries, Power Generation, or other heavy industrial operations.

  • HSE Regulatory Knowledge: Possess deep technical knowledge of various HSE rules and regulations at both the Federal and State levels, ensuring comprehensive compliance.

  • Direct Implementation Experience: Proven direct experience with the practical implementation of HSE rules, regulations, policies, and procedures in an operational environment.

  • Strong Communication Skills: Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, enabling effective interaction across all levels of the organization and with external stakeholders.

  • Excellent Computer Skills: Proficient computer skills for documentation, reporting, and utilizing HSE management systems.

  • Legal Work Authorization: Must be able to legally work and reside in the US without requiring sponsorship.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • University degree in a related field (e.g., Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering).

  • Specific expertise in rotating equipment safety, electrical safety (NFPA 70E), or process safety management (PSM).

  • Certifications such as CSP (Certified Safety Professional), ASP (Associate Safety Professional), or OHST (Occupational Health and Safety Technologist).

  • Experience in a fast-paced, high-growth company environment.

  • Proven ability to drive cultural change related to safety.

jobs.title: Senior Incident Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

As a Senior Incident Manager at Crusoe, you'll lead the response when things go wrong, coordinating the right people across teams, driving urgency, and keeping everyone focused until customer-impacting issues are resolved. You'll own communication throughout that process, including internal updates that keep responders coordinated and leadership informed, and status page decisions that keep customers informed. Once an incident is resolved, you'll drive the post-incident review process, ensuring postmortems are written and debriefs are held on time, then translate those findings into a clear, customer-facing root cause analysis (RCA) that builds lasting trust with enterprise customers and executives. You'll also maintain the incident metrics and reporting that show how we're performing, and ensure preventative actions coming out of incidents are properly documented and tracked.

In this full-time position, you'll have the opportunity to shape and enhance our incident management processes as the team and company scale, improving how we detect, respond to, and learn from incidents. The ideal candidate combines strong incident coordination fundamentals with real experience writing customer-facing root cause analysis to enterprise customers, plus the analytical rigor to track and report on incident data, and basic technical fluency to engage credibly with infrastructure teams, without needing to be the one troubleshooting.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Incident Response Leadership: Lead end-to-end management of high-visibility technical incidents and enterprise customer escalations, ensuring rapid restoration of services and effective communication throughout the lifecycle.

  • Incident Coordination: Coordinate the response effort across teams during an incident — you won't be troubleshooting the technical issue yourself, but you'll work closely with responders to determine which teams are needed and ensure everyone stays focused in the right direction.

  • Strategic Collaboration: Act as a critical bridge between Customer Success and internal engineering/product teams, translating frontline feedback into actionable incident response steps.

  • Customer Communication & Judgment: Own status page communications — determining the right level of detail and the best way to frame updates so customers get clear, useful information. This requires more judgment at a startup, where communication practices are still being defined, versus larger, more established companies.

  • RCA Ownership: Own end-to-end production of customer-facing root cause analyses — translating incident data into clear, structured writing for enterprise customers and executives.

  • Corrective Action Documentation: Ensure proper documentation of internal corrective actions coming out of incidents, driving improvements to the reliability of our products and platform.

  • Incident Metrics & Reporting: Maintain and report on core incident metrics (response time, resolution time, time to RCA delivery), ensuring incident data is accurate and complete.

  • Knowledge Empowerment: Develop and deliver training materials, internal documentation, and knowledge base articles for teammates and customers.

  • Process Innovation: Design and implement incident response strategies and self-serve support processes to scale the function as the team grows.

  • On-Call Participation: Participate in on-call rotation, 10am–10pm coverage, 5 days per week, providing a reliable safety net for critical service interruptions.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Background on an enterprise customer support team, or direct experience working with enterprise customers

  • Strong written communication — able to turn technical, ambiguous incident detail into clear, structured narratives for a non-technical audience

  • Understands the nuances of what can and cannot be communicated to customers, including what needs to be documented in writing

  • Strong judgment on communication level — knowing what to filter out when reporting bad news, since each incident case is different

  • Sound judgment on transparency — knowing when to stay high-level vs. go into detail

  • Logical, structured thinker with a solid grounding in incident management process and best practices

  • Comfortable working with data to track and report on trends, not just handling incidents in the moment

  • Working familiarity with Linux, virtualization, and Kubernetes — comfortable enough to engage credibly with infrastructure and technical responders during an incident, without needing to be the one troubleshooting

Bonus Points:

  • Experience working with customers in a startup environment, with an understanding of the complexities that come with it

  • Background in cloud infrastructure or AI-focused environments

  • Understanding of Virtualization and orchestration/scheduling technologies (Slurm or Kubernetes)

  • Hands-on experience with Linux, virtualization, or Kubernetes

  • Understanding of the TCP/IP stack

  • Understanding of Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) practices

What Makes This Role Compelling:

  • Builder mentality welcome: the opportunity to create and refine incident management processes, leave a lasting imprint on the function, and grow alongside the team as it scales

  • Real scaling story: the team has grown from 2 people covering 24x7 to a team of 5, with continued growth ahead — a chance to help scale the function without sacrificing quality

  • Exposure to cutting-edge AI infrastructure across the full stack: compute, networking (SDN), storage (VAST), Kubernetes, and Slurm

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $145,000 – $175,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

Crusoe is building the AI infrastructure that powers the next generation of intelligence, and we empower our own engineers to operate at the same frontier. The Storage engineering team is the backbone of Crusoe’s AI cloud platform.

You’ll have real latitude here. You’ll build AI powered tools that make storage operations and engineering workflows faster and smarter, and you’ll shape how an entire engineering team works by driving adoption of tools like Claude Code, Codex; mentoring engineers one on one, and removing the friction that keeps great tools from getting used.

If you love building and using AI tools, and love getting others just as excited about them, please apply.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

About This Role:

Crusoe is seeking a visionary and hands-on Senior Manager of Accounts Payable to join our dynamic finance team. In this critical leadership role, you will be the strategic architect responsible for building and scaling our entire procure-to-pay process for the future. As we experience rapid growth, you will drive process automation, implement best-in-class systems, and ensure our financial operations are as innovative as our technology. This is a unique opportunity to make a significant impact on Crusoe's foundation, ensuring efficiency and accuracy to support our aggressive expansion trajectory. This is a full-time position.

 

What You’ll Be Working On

  • Strategic Leadership & Vision: Develop and execute the long-term vision for the Accounts Payable function, focusing on scalability, efficiency, and accuracy to support rapid growth.

  • Operational Excellence & Oversight: Oversee the entire, full-cycle accounts payable process, including vendor onboarding, invoice processing, payment runs (ACH, wire, virtual card), and employee expense reporting (T&E). Ensure the accurate and timely processing of all invoices and payments.

  • Team Building & Management: Recruit, mentor, and lead a high-performing AP team. Foster a culture of excellence, collaboration, and continuous professional development.

  • Process Automation: Drive continuous improvement by proactively identifying and eliminating manual processes, integrating modern financial technology for peak efficiency.

  • Stakeholder Collaboration: Build strong cross-functional relationships with Procurement, Engineering, and other departments to ensure a seamless and efficient procure-to-pay experience across the entire organization.

  • Financial Controls & Compliance: Design, implement, and maintain robust internal controls to ensure strict compliance with GAAP, SOX, and company policies. Serve as the primary contact for AP-related audits.

  • Cash Management & Reporting: Partner with the Treasury and FP&A teams on critical cash flow forecasting. Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to track departmental performance, such as Days Payable Outstanding (DPO) and on-time payment metrics.

What You’ll Bring to the Team

  • Education & Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field. You have 8+ years of progressive experience in accounts payable, with at least 4 years in a leadership role managing a team.

  • Growth Environment Success: Demonstrated success in a fast-paced, high-volume tech, SaaS, or startup environment is essential. You thrive in ambiguity and possess the proven ability to build processes from the ground up.

  • Systems & Automation Expertise: Deep, hands-on experience with ERP systems and AP platforms.

  • Leadership & Mentorship: A proven ability to lead, mentor, and effectively scale a team. You inspire your team and lead by example.

  • Analytical & Project Management Skills: Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and project management skills. You are data-driven and can translate insights into actionable process improvements.

  • Communication: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to effectively collaborate with vendors and internal stakeholders at all levels.

Bonus Points

  • Direct experience with Sage Intacct and Coupa ERP and AP platforms.

  • Experience scaling the AP function for SOX compliance or IPO readiness.

  • Professional certifications such as CPA or CTP.

Benefits

  • Industry competitive pay

  • Restricted Stock Units in a fast growing, well-funded technology company

  • Health insurance package options that include HDHP and PPO, vision, and dental for you and your dependents

  • Employer contributions to HSA accounts

  • Paid Parental Leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Teladoc

  • 401(k) with a 100% match up to 4% of salary

  • Generous paid time off and holiday schedule

  • Cell phone reimbursement

  • Tuition reimbursement

  • Subscription to the Calm app

  • MetLife Legal

  • Company paid commuter benefit; $300 per month

Compensation

Compensation will be paid in the range of $145,000 - $175,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

Location: San Francisco, Denver or Dallas (50% Travel)

 

About This Role

As a Senior Staff Commissioning Engineer, you will serve as a campus and multi-campus technical authority for commissioning across Crusoe's data center portfolio. You own outcomes across projects — setting technical direction for the electrical discipline, governing the commissioning program itself, and serving as the trusted resource for the highest-impact, most technically complex decisions that shape site outcomes. You operate as a "Master of Discipline": the escalation point of last resort, the standard-setter for trade partner and CxA performance, and a force multiplier who elevates every engineer around you. This role blends deep technical mastery with programmatic ownership, commercial fluency, and executive-level communication that builds client and stakeholder confidence in Crusoe.

 
 

What You'll Be Working On

 

Multi-Campus Strategic Leadership

  • Provide high-level commissioning oversight and direction across multiple campuses, ensuring operational alignment, cohesive strategy, and exceptional client relations across the portfolio.

  • Drive consistency in commissioning execution across sites, identifying cross-project patterns, recurring issues, and systemic risks, and translating lessons learned into program-level change.

  • Represent Crusoe Commissioning (CCx) in cross-functional governance forums, leadership reviews, and client-facing engagements, translating technical complexity into clear business impact.

Technical Authority & Decision-Making

  • Serve as the "Master of Discipline" for electrical systems — responsible for high-impact, technically complex decisions that shape site outcomes, including energization readiness, acceptance testing, and risk-based deviations.

  • Act as the recognized escalation authority for complex technical issues across all project phases, rapidly resolving problems that span disciplines, vendors, and project boundaries.

  • Own technical sign-offs across project boundaries, and maintain exceptional customer communication that builds confidence in Crusoe's delivery.

  • Maintain comprehensive understanding of building systems — power distribution, EPMS, controls, and mechanical interfaces — including power generation systems and how they interact with the data center.

 

Programmatic Process Ownership

  • Own the development and continuous improvement of the commissioning program: create, pilot, deploy, and validate new and improved processes, standards, and governance documents (e.g., FWT program, deficiency management, script library governance).

  • Conduct QA audits and drive root cause analysis on systemic issues; establish the frameworks by which program quality is measured and improved.

  • Define what "good" looks like across the L0–L6 lifecycle and drive adoption of improvements across Crusoe portfolio.

 

Quoting & Financial Oversight

  • Support CCx with all quoting activities, taking a lead role in financial accuracy, bid leveling, and the strategic pursuit of new business.

  • Manage program-level CxA and vendor commercial outcomes — scope development, change order review, and performance-based accountability.

  • Bring deep contractual and risk understanding to protect the business in vendor negotiations and commissioning scope decisions.

 

Trade Partner & CxA Performance

  • Manage and analyze trade partner and third-party commissioning agent execution to ensure high standards, accountability, and continuous improvement in external collaborations.

  • Set the performance bar for CxAs across the program, driving accountability across vendors through structured performance management, deliverable tracking, and data-driven scorecards.

  • Build long-term, trust-based partnerships with key external partners (clients, vendors, OEMs) at senior level.

 

Mentorship & Team Elevation

  • Actively coach and develop team members across the organization, bridging the gap between current performance and exceptional.

  • Mentor engineers across all levels, develop next-level talent, and elevate the team around you to your own performance standard.

  • Anchor calibration and growth conversations in specific, observable behaviors, building the technical bench that scales with Crusoe's growth.

 

What You'll Bring

  • 10+ years of experience in data center commissioning, construction, or critical infrastructure delivery, including demonstrated ownership at the campus, region and program level.

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field; equivalent commissioning experience considered (CxA certification a plus).

  • Mastery of the full commissioning lifecycle (L0 through L6), including the documentation, testing, and governance requirements at each phase.

  • Recognized subject matter expertise in electrical systems — power distribution, EPMS, protection and controls — with complete understanding of design, construction, and testing principles within the discipline, including power generation systems and their interaction with data center loads.

  • Proven track record developing, deploying, and governing commissioning programs, standards, and processes adopted across multiple projects or an organization.

  • Demonstrated commercial and contractual fluency: quoting, bid leveling, vendor scope and change order management, and program-level CxA performance management.

  • Experience managing and holding trade partners, CxAs, OEMs, and general/electrical/mechanical contractors accountable to scope, schedule, and quality across concurrent projects.

  • Strong executive communication skills — able to present independently to senior leadership and clients, and translate technical complexity into clear, data-driven business narratives.

  • A track record of mentoring and developing engineers, with measurable elevation of team performance.

  • Solid understanding of safety, compliance, and regulatory requirements within active construction and commissioning environments.

  • Willingness to travel to project sites as required (50% travel).

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $175,000 -$215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

Crusoe’s Data Center Infrastructure Engineering (DCIE) team is fundamental to our mission of providing AI hardware and infrastructure as a service. The team provides infrastructure for Crusoe’s fleet GPU’s and data center. The team sits at the nexus of high performance computing and AI infrastructure as a service.

The DCIE team owns, deployment maintenance, observability, critical environment, and automation. The team builds, and maintains GPU clusters, develops automation for logical and physical maintenance, provision systems, and observability tooling.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Software Engineer to join Crusoe’s Data Center Infrastructure Engineering team. This position is focused on the development of software for the management of a fleet of GPU servers as well as the data centers that house those systems. The role focuses on the developing and implementing advanced diagnostic, observability, automation and repair tooling for high-performance GPU compute clusters.

The ideal new team member will be a hands-on problem solver who is comfortable working independently. The new team member will play a critical role in maintaining the health and scalability of Crusoe’s rapidly growing GPU fleet.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Developing and implementing deep-level diagnostics and troubleshooting of hardware faults within GPU racks and high-density compute systems.

  • Developing troubleshooting and automation tooling for GPU platforms including NVIDIA A100, H200, GB200, B200 and AMD 350X / 355X.

  • Developing automation and AI agents for executing component-level diagnosis and remediation for failed or degraded hardware.

  • In conjunction with data center operations develop innovative tooling and AI agents for managing the critical environment.

  • Developing tooling for post-repair validation and testing tools such as burn-in, Pytorch, and NVIDIA NCCL to ensure system stability and performance.

  • Own the deployment, monitoring, and operational support of developed tooling, ensuring solutions maximize GPU fleet availability and performance to drive customer success.

  • Developing automation and operational tooling for facilities management power as well as direct liquid cooling hardware systems

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Software engineering experience.

  • The ability to identify a problem, rapidly develop a scalable solution and ship it.

  • Ability to lean in and assist team members working on critical or complex technical initiatives.

  • Ability to set the technical direction for a specific project and execute.

  • Expertise in distributed systems, reliability, and cloud platforms (Kubernetes, IaC, GCP etc.)

  • Strength in at least one programming language - Go, Python, Java, Rust.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

  • Ability to work independently and within a team

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with Temporal and Kubernetes.

  • Experience working directly with hardware vendors.

  • Background in large-scale GPU fleet operations or hyperscale data center environments.

Benefits:

  • Industry competitive pay

  • Restricted Stock Units in a fast growing, well-funded technology company

  • Health insurance package options that include HDHP and PPO, vision, and dental for you and your dependents

  • Employer contributions to HSA accounts

  • Paid Parental Leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Teladoc

  • 401(k) with a 100% match up to 4% of salary

  • Generous paid time off and holiday schedule

  • Cell phone reimbursement

  • Tuition reimbursement

  • Subscription to the Calm app

  • MetLife Legal

  • Company paid commuter benefit; $300 per month

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $250,000 - $300,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

About the Role:

As a Senior Staff Automation Engineer for the Compute Team, you will be responsible for deployment and testing automation of large-scale, multi-node GPU clusters. You will own the CI/CD infrastructure, including both deployment and integration testing, for a rapidly scaling fleet of virtualized GPU and CPU hosts across our AI Cloud. Your role is critical in ensuring the stability of the low-level infrastructure and enabling teams across our Cloud Infrastructure organization to quickly and reliably release, test, and deploy their artifacts across our datacenters.

San Francisco, Sunnyvale, Bellevue (Onsite)

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Deployment and Integration Testing Ownership: Completely own deployment and integration testing automation for all bare-metal, on-premise systems across Crusoe’s AI Cloud Stack.

  • CI/CD Automation and Tooling: Build CI/CD platforms that enable developers to quickly test, iterate, and deploy critical, low-level systems and applications.

  • Multi-Node Scaling Validation: Design and execute large-scale validation tests across multi-node virtualized clusters to ensure linear scaling and stability of GPU workloads.

  • Configuration Management and Observability: Maintain and scale bare-metal Linux configurations using a mix of custom and off the shelf tooling such as Gitlab, Ansible, AWX, osquery, etc.

  • Deployment Orchestration: Create control applications to coordinate canary deployments on live production systems, run Blue/Green testing, and perform automatic rollback where necessary.

  • Cluster Orchestration: Develop and maintain automation frameworks in Python or Go to dynamically provision, configure, and stress-test multi-node virtualized environments.

  • Create automated test suites leveraging tools like fio, stress-ng, and iperf to ensure performance and multi-tenant isolation of CPU and GPU hosts.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education & Experience: 12+ YOE demonstrated ability to competently and independently perform responsibilities plus Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.

  • Experience building and deploying automated integration testing for an AI Cloud Environment, ranging from low-level Linux Systems up to Distributed Control Planes.

  • Working knowledge of the modern infrastructure stack, including Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, and Postgres.

  • CI/CD & Gitlab: Intimate knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and Gitlab Tooling to enable stable infrastructure releases across multiple datacenters.

  • Configuration Management: Previous experience with at least 1-2 configuration management systems, including Ansible, Puppet, Chef, or SaltStack.

  • Automation & Scripting: Advanced proficiency in Python and/or Bash for automating complex cluster-wide test scenarios.

  • System Internals: Knowledge of Linux kernel internals, specifically PCIe topology, VFIO, and memory management (HugePages, IOMMU).

  • Distributed GPU Ecosystems: Familiarity with NVIDIA (CUDA/NCCL) and/or AMD (ROCm/RCCL) stacks in a multi-node context.

  • Networking Knowledge: Strong understanding of RDMA, RoCE, and InfiniBand protocols and their implementation in virtualized systems.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with MNNVL (Multi-Node NVLink) or specialized AI fabric architectures.

  • Familiarity with hardware-level debugging tools and performance profilers (e.g., NVIDIA Nsight, AMD Omniperf).

  • Knowledge of containerized orchestration for GPUs (e.g., Kubernetes with specialized device plugins).

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $250,000 -$300,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the role

You will set the technical direction for Crusoe's Linux kernel team, owning the roadmap and architecting critical development projects. This role requires a balance of high-level architectural design and hands-on kernel coding. You will tackle the most complex kernel problems while mentoring and growing the engineers around you to deliver production-ready infrastructure at scale.


What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Perform deep-dive root-cause analysis of issues across the OS and hardware layers. You will lead the triage and backporting for kernel CVEs while building automated tooling for vulnerability analysis.

  • Architect and lead critical projects — new kernel features, security patching infrastructure, deployment systems — from design through production and upstream.

  • Develop kernel code with an upstream-first mindset — we aim to contribute all changes to the Linux kernel community and keep our downstream patches zero; this is a core part of how the team works, not an afterthought

  • Develop and review kernel code: memory management, scheduler, networking, storage, and GPU-related subsystems

  • Design and implement advanced virtualization technologies tailored for GPU-accelerated AI and HPC workloads. You will optimize the stack for low latency and high scalability across hypervisors and device emulation.

  • Find and develop kernel efficiency improvements proactively (e.g., DAMON-based memory management, hugepage optimization, memory overcommit)

  • Mentor and review work from mid-level and junior engineers

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Deep knowledge of Linux kernel internals — memory management, scheduler, networking, storage subsystems and/or device drivers

  • Strong C programming skills; fluency in kernel development workflow (patch submission, mailing lists, Lore)

  • Experience evaluating kernel security vulnerabilities: CVE analysis, exploitability assessment, backporting fixes

  • Demonstrated ability to set technical direction and drive projects end-to-end

  • Track record of upstream Linux kernel contributions is a strong plus

  • Deep knowledge of Linux kernel internals (memory management, scheduler, I/O) and virtualization technologies (KVM, Xen, or QEMU)

  • 10+ years of experience in systems software engineering working on low-level systems or infrastructure teams.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About Crusoe

Crusoe is building the energy and infrastructure foundation for the AI era. We design, build, and operate purpose-built, AI-optimized data centers — from gigawatt-scale campuses like Stargate in Abilene, Texas, to modular and distributed deployments — powered by an energy-first approach that pairs compute with reliable, low-cost power. Our Facility Remote Operations Center is the nerve center for this footprint: a 24/7 command function that provides centralized visibility, monitoring, and rapid response across Crusoe's critical infrastructure nationwide.

Position Summary

Crusoe is seeking a Senior Manager to lead the Facility Remote Operations Center (ROC) based in Dallas, Texas. This role owns the people, processes, and technology behind 24/7/365 remote monitoring of critical facility infrastructure — electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety, and building automation systems — across Crusoe's national data center portfolio.

The Senior Manager will build and lead a team of shift supervisors and operations specialists who serve as the first line of detection, triage, and escalation for facility events, working in close coordination with on-site Data Center Operations, Engineering, and Critical Facilities teams. This is a highly visible role that blends operational leadership, technical fluency in MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) systems, and program-building responsibility, as the ROC scales alongside Crusoe's rapidly growing AI infrastructure footprint.

Key Responsibilities

Remote Operations Center Leadership

  • Lead 24/7/365 ROC operations, including staffing, scheduling, shift coverage, and performance management for a team of remote operations supervisors and specialists.

  • Establish and continuously improve monitoring protocols, escalation procedures, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for facility alarms, events, and anomalies across the fleet.

  • Serve as the senior escalation point for critical facility events outside of normal parameters, coordinating real-time response with on-site teams, vendors, and leadership.

  • Drive a culture of accountability, urgency, and continuous improvement within the ROC team.

MEP Systems Oversight & Technical Fluency

  • Maintain deep working knowledge of MEP systems within AI data centers, including electrical distribution (utility feeds, switchgear, generators, UPS, PDUs, busway), mechanical/cooling systems (CRAH/CRAC units, chillers, cooling towers, liquid cooling/CDUs, air handling), fire detection/suppression, and building management systems (BMS/DCIM/EPMS).

About This Role:

As the Senior Manager, Material & Production Planning, you will lead and unify the Material Planning and Production Planning functions for Crusoe's Manufacturing organization. In this high-visibility operational leadership role, you will ensure raw materials and critical components are available while driving Master Production Schedules (MPS) and capacity models that maximize throughput for Crusoe’s AI infrastructure products.

You will manage a team of Material Planners and Production Planners responsible for balancing customer demand, supplier performance, shop-floor capacity, material readiness, and inventory strategy. Sitting at the intersection of Supply Chain, Procurement, Manufacturing, Engineering, Logistics, Quality, and Program Management, you will design scalable, integrated planning processes and drive S&OP execution to support rapid scaling. This is a full-time, onsite leadership position supporting Crusoe's advanced manufacturing operations in Arvada, Colorado.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Lead & Scale the Integrated Planning Team: Hire, mentor, coach, and develop a high-performing team of Material Planners and Production Planners while fostering a culture of operational excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.

  • Drive S&OP & Master Production Scheduling (MPS): Lead cross-functional S&OP alignment and develop production plans that balance demand forecasts with shop-floor capacity, labor availability, tooling, and component readiness.

  • Own Material Readiness & Shortage Mitigation: Establish material planning processes to guarantee line availability. Lead Clear-to-Build (CTB) forums to proactively identify supplier constraints, part shortages, and long-lead risks before they impact shop-floor schedules.

  • Manage Capacity Planning & Throughput: Evaluate shop-floor capacity, labor constraints, and manufacturing resources to optimize production flow, eliminate bottlenecks, improve schedule attainment, and support rapid footprint expansion.

  • Optimize Total Inventory Health: Oversee safety stock policies, reorder points, buffer stock, excess & obsolete (E&O) risk, cycle counting, and Just-in-Time (JIT) material delivery to balance supply continuity with working capital optimization.

  • Cross-Functional Executive Alignment: Partner closely with Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, Manufacturing Operations, Engineering, Logistics, Quality, and Program Management to align material availability, production schedules, and shipping targets with business priorities.

  • Support New Product Introductions (NPI): Coordinate material and production readiness for new hardware revisions and modular product launches, partnering with NPI teams to ensure smooth prototype-to-production transitions, BOM audits, and ramp schedules.

  • Leverage ERP/MRP & Advanced Systems: Drive demand planning, automated replenishment, work order creation, and shop-floor scheduling using ERP/MRP enterprise platforms (Oracle, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, NetSuite), identifying opportunities for system automation and master data integrity.

  • Monitor & Drive Key Operational Metrics: Establish and track key performance indicators including Schedule Attainment, On-Time In-Full (OTIF) delivery, Material Availability, Inventory Turnover, WIP levels, and Planning Accuracy while driving corrective actions.

  • Lean & Continuous Improvement: Spearhead Lean Manufacturing practices (Kaizen, Standard Work, 5S, Visual Management) across material flow and shop-floor scheduling to reduce lead times and improve delivery performance.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Business, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field.

  • Experience: 10+ years of experience across material planning, production planning, supply chain operations, master scheduling, or capacity planning within a complex manufacturing environment.

  • Leadership: 5+ years of direct people management experience leading material planners, production schedulers, or multi-disciplinary supply chain teams.

  • Dual Discipline Mastery: Proven track record running both Material Requirements Planning (MRP) and Master Production Scheduling (MPS) inside a fast-paced hardware manufacturing facility.

  • Systems Expertise: Advanced proficiency with enterprise ERP/MRP platforms (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, NetSuite) and advanced supply chain planning modules.

  • Analytical Capability: Strong quantitative skills using Excel and data visualization tools (Power BI or Tableau) to analyze inventory health, model shop-floor capacity, and build operational dashboards.

  • Problem Solving & Lean: Demonstrated ability to manage supplier-related risks, resolve floor bottlenecks, lead cross-functional initiatives, and apply Lean tools to optimize end-to-end material flow.

Bonus Points:

  • Master’s degree in Supply Chain or an MBA

  • APICS/ASCM certifications (CPIM, CSCP) or Lean Six Sigma Green/Black Belt.

  • Experience supporting high-growth, rapidly scaling advanced manufacturing or highly configurable modular hardware (electrical systems, data center equipment, power/cooling infrastructure, aerospace).

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $155,000 - $185,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDCORP)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Director, International Project Management - Spark
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We are seeking a seasoned Technical Project Manager to own Crusoe's international modular data center deployments . You will lead modular data center projects from powered land to “Available to Customer” in markets with different regulatory regimes, different construction norms, different utility interconnection standards, and no existing in-country playbook. This is a builder's role in every sense: you're writing the playbook on how Crusoe deploys modular compute in new geographies while executing projects in parallel.

This role will require travel up to 50% of the time, including international travel, with extended trip durations when needed to support first-of-a-kind builds.

What You'll Be Working On:

Deployment Lifecycle Management

  • Project Execution Ownership: Manage the project schedule, budget, and scope for Crusoe's international and other special project modular deployments.

  • Site Readiness: Coordinate with Crusoe and in-country subject matter experts on site preparation, permitting, and utility interconnection timelines, adapted to local codes and standards.

  • Risk Mitigation: Proactively identify bottlenecks in procurement, construction, networking, and power readiness — with an extra layer of risk for cross-border logistics, customs, and in-country political/regulatory shifts. Always have a “Plan B.”

International & Cross-Border Complexity

  • Trade Compliance Partnership: Work with Crusoe Legal and Trade Compliance to navigate customs and import/export requirements for shipping GPUs, networking gear, and Spark modules across borders. Partner with Government Affairs to engage financing entities (e.g. EXIM Bank)

  • In-Country Partner Coordination: Collaborate with in-country partners to bring Crusoe’s level of execution rigor and speedo regions where Crusoe doesn't yet have an established presence.

  • Mobility & Staffing Coordination: Partner with HR on work authorization, visas, and any temporary relocation needed to keep a Crusoe presence on the ground during critical build phases.

Cross-Functional Orchestration

  • Product Management Interface: Feed region-specific requirements to the Spark Product Manager to inform the Spark Product Roadmap

  • Internal Connectivity: Serve as the air traffic controller between Real Estate, Legal, Finance, Manufacturing Planning, Cloud Product & Procurement, Site Design & Engineering, Construction, and the Spark Business Unit for each international or special project.

  • External Partner Coordination: Manage relationships with international contractors, suppliers, customs brokers, and local authorities.

  • Reporting: Provide high-fidelity project status updates for executives, calling out the risks unique to operating outside the US, and coordinate with the Lead Technical Project Manager to keep these projects visible on the Spark deployments dashboard.

Process Standardization — Writing the Playbook

  • The International Playbook: Build the first version of a “Spark International Deployment Playbook,” capturing what's different (and what isn't) about deploying Spark outside the US, so future international sites can move faster.

  • Lessons Learned: Meticulously record lessons learned from each first-of-a-kind or international build and identify opportunities for continuous process improvement.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Safety & Readiness: A relentless commitment to safety and a “Mountaineer” level focus on operational readiness.

  • Technical Project Leadership: 10-15+ years of experience managing complex, capital-intensive infrastructure or first-of-a-kind projects (data centers, energy, advanced manufacturing) with budgets exceeding $500M.

  • International Project Experience: Demonstrated experience delivering capital projects outside the United States, ideally across more than one country or regulatory regime.

  • Trade Compliance Literacy: Working familiarity with export controls, customs, and import/export processes for high-value technical equipment (prior partnership with Legal/Trade Compliance teams a plus).

  • Schedule Mastery: Demonstrated expertise in scheduling software; you leverage schedules as a proactive decision-making tool.

  • Technical Acumen: Evidence of technical breadth and curiosity to manage engineering requirements, evaluate trade-offs, and surface risks across electrical, mechanical, civil, cloud, and network engineering.

  • Cross-Cultural Fluency: Experience managing distributed, multicultural teams and in-country partners; comfortable being the only Crusoe person in the room.

  • International Regulatory Exposure: Experience navigating construction codes, labor law, utility interconnection standards, and permitting processes in foreign countries.

  • Comfort with Ambiguity: Willing and able to build a process from scratch where no playbook yet exists, rather than execute against an established one.

  • Travel Readiness: Able to travel up to 50% of the time, including international travel, with extended trip durations when needed to support first-of-a-kind builds

  • Exceptional Communication: Knows how to adjust communication styles accordingly, across cultures and contexts. Offers a steady hand at the wheel during periods of ambiguity or change.

  • Resilience: Proven ability to drive projects to completion despite global supply chain headwinds, cross-border logistics friction, or technical uncertainty. A “no surprise” mentality on timelines, schedules, and budgets, with alternatives identified so projects stay on track.

  • Education: Bachelor’s Degree in related field or equivalent experience.

This Role Is Not a Good Fit If:

  • You need a fixed home-base routine and can't support extensive international travel.

  • You've only operated within standard US regulatory and construction frameworks.

Bonus Points

  • Spanish Language Proficiency: Professional or business-level proficiency.

  • Fluency in an additional language (beyond Spanish).

  • Prior expatriate or extended-relocation work experience.

  • Experience standing up a joint-venture or government-partnership project structure abroad.
