You will lead modular data center projects from powered land to “Available to Customer” in markets with different regulatory regimes, different construction norms, different utility interconnection standards, and no existing in-country playbook. This is a builder's role in every sense: you're writing the playbook on how Crusoe deploys modular compute in new geographies while executing  projects in parallel.



This role will require travel up to 50% of the time, including international travel, with extended trip durations when needed to support first-of-a-kind builds.



What You'll Be Working On:

Deployment Lifecycle Management

 - Project Execution Ownership: Manage the project schedule, budget, and scope for Crusoe's international and other special project modular deployments.

 - Site Readiness: Coordinate with Crusoe and in-country subject matter experts on site preparation, permitting, and utility interconnection timelines, adapted to local codes and standards.

 - Risk Mitigation: Proactively identify bottlenecks in procurement, construction, networking, and power readiness — with an extra layer of risk for cross-border logistics, customs, and in-country political/regulatory shifts. Always have a “Plan B.”

International & Cross-Border Complexity

 - Trade Compliance Partnership: Work with Crusoe Legal and Trade Compliance to navigate customs and import/export requirements for shipping GPUs, networking gear, and Spark modules across borders. Partner with Government Affairs to engage financing entities (e.g. EXIM Bank)

 - In-Country Partner Coordination: Collaborate with in-country partners to bring Crusoe’s level of execution rigor and speedo regions where Crusoe doesn't yet have an established presence.

 - Mobility & Staffing Coordination: Partner with HR on work authorization, visas, and any temporary relocation needed to keep a Crusoe presence on the ground during critical build phases.

Cross-Functional Orchestration

 - Product Management Interface: Feed region-specific requirements to the Spark Product Manager to inform the Spark Product Roadmap

 - Internal Connectivity: Serve as the air traffic controller between Real Estate, Legal, Finance, Manufacturing Planning, Cloud Product & Procurement, Site Design & Engineering, Construction, and the Spark Business Unit for each international or special project.

 - External Partner Coordination: Manage relationships with international contractors, suppliers, customs brokers, and local authorities.

 - Reporting: Provide high-fidelity project status updates for executives, calling out the risks unique to operating outside the US, and coordinate with the Lead Technical Project Manager to keep these projects visible on the Spark deployments dashboard.

 - The International Playbook: Build the first version of a “Spark International Deployment Playbook,” capturing what's different (and what isn't) about deploying Spark outside the US, so future international sites can move faster.

 - Technical Project Leadership: 10-15+ years of experience managing complex, capital-intensive infrastructure or first-of-a-kind projects (data centers, energy, advanced manufacturing) with budgets exceeding $500M.

Crusoe is looking for a Mechanical Engineering Manager to own the day-to-day technical execution of our mechanical engineering team. Reporting to the Sr. Engineering Manager, you will bridge the gap between strategic design direction and efficient project delivery, transforming complex customer requirements into production-ready 3D models and detailed drawings for modular buildings and power distribution equipment.

While primarily an execution and people leadership role focused on managing the engineering queue and reviewing mechanical deliverables, you must also be a capable and willing expert technical individual contributor. The ideal candidate is a highly analytical, seasoned engineer who leads from the front, eagerly tackles advanced IC work when needed, removes team blockers, and takes ownership of quality from the first schematic to production release.

 

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Team Leadership & People Management: Directly manage a team of mechanical design engineers. Conduct regular 1-on-1s, performance reviews, and growth conversations while providing expert technical guidance, mentorship, and professional development.

  • Engineering Queue & Resource Execution: Own the mechanical engineering workqueue, assigning engineers to projects based on expertise, availability, and production schedule priorities while pro-actively surfacing schedule risks.

  • Technical Design Leadership & Execution: Step in to execute individual contributor work at an advanced level, utilizing expert 3D modeling skills to tackle complex design challenges when the team requires additional bandwidth.

  • Deliverable & Model Review: Serve as a technical reviewer for mechanical deliverables, including specification sheets, bills of materials (BOMs), structural/thermal analysis, and detailed assembly instructions.

  • Lifecycle & Change Management: Independently lead and manage Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) as a key part of product release and ongoing lifecycle management.

  • Compliance & Standards Execution: Champion and ensure strict compliance of all product designs with regulatory requirements, commercial codes, and engineering standards (e.g., UL, IEC, IBC, ISO), while maintaining PDM/PLM/ERP data integrity.

  • Design-to-Manufacturing Handoff: Partner closely with Manufacturing Engineering and the shop floor to resolve design questions, leading Design for Manufacturability and Assembly (DFMA/DFx) reviews and driving cost-reduction strategies.

 

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering.

  • Professional Experience: 7+ years of hands-on experience in mechanical design.

  • Leadership Track Record: Proven success in a supervisory or management role for at least 1-2 years leading engineering teams.

  • Technical Depth: Expert proficiency with 3D modeling software, specifically SolidWorks and SolidWorks PDM, with deep knowledge of metals, fabrication materials, and manufacturing methods.

  • First-Principles Problem Solving: Proven track record of solving complex engineering problems utilizing a first-principles approach to design and analysis.

  • Regulatory & Code Knowledge: Proficient knowledge of a wide range of building codes, energy codes, and UL listings applicable to engineered infrastructure.

  • Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts across cross-functional teams.

  • Safety & Physical Capabilities: Ability to lift/move up to 50 lbs and meet physical operational demands on site. This position is designated safety-sensitive and located in a safety-sensitive facility; drug and alcohol program participation is required.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license.

  • Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or related post-graduate discipline.

  • Experience serving as a SolidWorks PDM Vault Administrator.

  • Experience with advanced simulation and analysis software (e.g., FEA/FDM).

  • Lean or continuous improvement experience applied to an engineering design workflow.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $160,000 - $195,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

About This Role:

The Strategic Sourcing Manager owns the strategic sourcing function as a unified, coherent system rather than a collection of siloed commodities. In this leadership role, you will be responsible for building the team, setting contract and negotiation governance, establishing rigorous process standards, and managing the consolidated cross-category risk view. While individual Category Managers own specific spend areas end-to-end, you will ensure their work is consistently high-caliber, defensible, and aligned with Crusoe’s broader strategic objectives.

This is a pivotal people leadership and strategy role designed to scale our sourcing organization. The ideal candidate brings extensive experience designing sourcing playbooks, coaching talent through complex vendor negotiations, and translating portfolio-level supply chain risks into actionable leadership insights. If you thrive on developing high-performing teams, enforcing strategic discipline under schedule pressure, and building scalable procurement frameworks in an industrial manufacturing environment, this position offers high-impact visibility. This is a Full-Time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Team Leadership & Talent Development: Hire, coach, and evaluate the Category Manager team, implementing structured development projects to elevate capability across commodity areas.

  • Cross-Category Risk Rollup: Maintain a consolidated, portfolio-wide risk register identifying top single-source exposures, lead-time bottlenecks, and supplier financial concerns across all categories.

  • Process Standardization: Own and continuously improve core sourcing playbooks, including the RFI/RFQ/AVL qualification sequence, Kraljic category frameworks, and standardized supplier scorecards.

  • Negotiation Governance: Establish deal sign-off thresholds, escalation paths, and redline standards, providing direct coaching to Category Managers on high-stakes, complex supplier contracts.

  • Capacity & Resource Prioritization: Prioritize team bandwidth across spend categories to ensure sourcing efforts align with critical business demands and schedule constraints.

  • Functional Boundary Enforcement: Enforce clean operational boundaries between Strategic Sourcing and Material Planning so Category Managers remain focused on commercial strategy rather than tactical execution.

  • Executive Reporting & S&OP Representation: Synthesize all category strategies, cost savings/avoidance metrics, and supply constraints into a single, cohesive view for executive leadership and monthly S&OP reconciliations.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: 8–12+ years of dedicated experience in strategic sourcing or category management, including direct people management of a sourcing or procurement team within manufacturing, industrial hardware, or electrical equipment sectors.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • Organizational Scaling: Proven track record of designing, implementing, and scaling sourcing governance, process playbooks, and team development structures from the ground up.

  • Negotiation Coaching: Demonstrated expertise in contract negotiation with the ability to review, redline, and coach team members on complex commercial terms (e.g., liability caps, force majeure, delivery commitments).

  • Strategic & Financial Acumen: Fluency in portfolio risk management, category segmentation models (e.g., Kraljic Matrix), and financial modeling to defend cost savings and cost avoidance at the leadership level.

Bonus Points:

  • Master of Business Administration (MBA) or relevant advanced degree.

  • Prior experience scaling sourcing teams within high-tech infrastructure, power systems, data centers, or modular manufacturing environments.

  • Hands-on ERP experience with Acumatica or similar enterprise systems.

  • Professional certifications such as CPSM (Certified Professional in Supply Management).

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $155,000 - $185,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDCORP)

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Network State Management: Design and develop the systems that manage network state for Crusoe Cloud, including network provisioning, configuration management, topology/routing state, and control plane APIs that other teams and systems rely on.

  • Scaling the Control Plane: Contribute to and help drive engineering efforts to scale control plane systems reliably as Crusoe Cloud grows, handling increasing network scale, device counts, and infrastructure complexity.

  • Engineering Best Practices: Advocate for modern software development, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code (IaC) practices to improve engineering velocity and control plane reliability.

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, building backend systems in production.

  • Proficiency in at least one modern backend language such as Go, Rust, C++, Java, or Python.

  • Solid understanding of distributed systems concepts: consensus, state reconciliation, fault tolerance, and high availability design.

  • Track record of designing and building scalable, reliable APIs or services used by multiple teams.

  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code tooling (e.g., Terraform, Ansible).

  • Strong communication skills and experience collaborating cross functionally with product, operations, and other engineering teams.

  • Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers and contribute to technical direction.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with networking software, protocols, or control plane systems (e.g., routing, switching, BGP, SDN).

  • Experience at a cloud provider, hyperscaler, or large scale data center operator.

  • Familiarity with network telemetry/management protocols such as gNMI, gRPC, or NETCONF.

  • Experience with Kubernetes based orchestration or building custom controllers/operators.

  • Contributions to open source infrastructure or networking projects.

Benefits:

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $170,000 - $205,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

The Senior Category Manager, Strategic Sourcing owns any electrical/mechanical spend —including switchgear, PDC components, cable/wire, and specialized electrical hardware, enclosures, structural fabrication, doors, sheet metal—end-to-end at the strategic layer. In this role, you will lead market intelligence, supplier qualification, commercial negotiations, and proactive risk management across Crusoe’s key site locations. This category skews toward Strategic and Bottleneck profiles, making your technical credibility central to driving success alongside your negotiation skills.

Unlike tactical procurement, this role is accountable for the why behind our supply chain strategy—setting up the frameworks, agreements, and Approved Vendor Lists (AVL) rather than processing daily purchase orders. The ideal candidate brings a deep understanding of industrial electrical equipment, excels at drafting defensible category strategies, and proactively mitigates single-source and lead-time risks before they impact build schedules. This is a Full-Time position at our Arvada & Brighton locations.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Market & Spend Intelligence: Maintain deep intelligence across electrical categories, tracking supply base capabilities, pricing benchmarks, actual lead times, and capacity constraints with a heavy focus on long-lead items like switchgear.

  • AVL Qualification & Management: Own the electrical Approved Vendor List (AVL), conducting rigorous vetting and maintaining a defensible, scored qualification rationale for every entry, including NEC/UL compliance verification.

  • Category Strategy & Segmentation: Apply framework models (e.g., Kraljic Matrix) to classify electrical categories, balancing technical capability, quality, and lead-time reliability to build a 12–24 month category roadmap with dual-sourcing options.

  • Commercial Negotiations & Contracting: Structure and negotiate MSAs, pricing, terms, and SLAs while redlining buyer-adverse clauses (e.g., delivery commitments, force majeure, liability caps) to protect schedule integrity.

  • Proactive Risk Mitigation: Manage single-source exposures and lead-time risks on specialized electrical components, maintaining a live category risk register with clear mitigation paths.

  • Supplier Performance Tracking: Establish and maintain quarterly supplier scorecards evaluating on-time delivery, quality, responsiveness, and cost trends.

  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Create clean, robust commercial frameworks that allow operational teams (such as Material Planners and PO Specialists) to execute seamlessly against established terms.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: 4–7+ years of dedicated experience in strategic sourcing or category management specifically focused in manufacturing of electrical & mechanical components.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • Technical Compliance Knowledge: Working familiarity with NEC/UL compliance requirements and electrical component specifications sufficient to evaluate supplier technical claims.

  • Contracting & Negotiation Skills: Demonstrated hands-on experience reading, structuring, and redlining complex commercial terms and contracts.

  • Strategic Sourcing Frameworks: Proficiency with supplier qualification frameworks, RFI/RFQ processes, scorecarding, and category segmentation methodologies.

Bonus Points:

  • Hands-on ERP experience with platforms like Acumatica or similar enterprise systems.

  • Experience in high-power compute, data center infrastructure, or energy/industrial equipment environments.

  • Proven track record of building dual-sourcing strategies for long-lead industrial hardware.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $120,000 - $145,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

(#INDCORP)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Director, Portfolio Product Marketing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Sales can't sell what they can't explain. As we ship faster across datacenter, infrastructure, training, and inference, our field needs someone who can take a dense technical roadmap and turn it into a story a seller can tell.

Our product-line PMMs own the messaging for their individual products. This role sits above and across them. You take the positioning each product PMM produces and synthesize it into a coherent portfolio story, then translate that story into the plays, training, and competitive frameworks the field actually runs on. You are the connective tissue between the product-marketing bench and Revenue Enablement.

You own the sales narrative, the competitive intelligence, and the go-to-market motion across the whole portfolio. You own the first-call deck and the story arc that follows it through the customer journey, and you arm the field with the objections they'll hit and the plays to overcome them.

What You'll Be Working On:

Sales Plays

  • Serve as the primary SME for building sales plays for new products and features, synthesizing across product lines into a single motion the field can run

  • Translate product-line MRDs into sales-facing playbook components and launch guidance: what we're building, why, for whom, and what it displaces, framed for the questions sales will actually ask

  • Partner with Product and product-line PMMs on launch calendars, ensuring Revenue Enablement gets months of lead time, not days

  • Translate early-access and preview learnings into targeting guidance and field-ready talk tracks

Messaging & Narrative

  • Synthesize product-line messaging into a portfolio-level sales narrative using Command of the Message (Force Management), keeping the cross-product story coherent and differentiated

  • Own the sales narrative for the First Call Deck: conversational up front

  • Build modular slide libraries so reps can tailor by persona, segment, and use case without going off-message

Training & Field Readiness

  • Build curriculum components for new-hire onboarding and ongoing field education

  • Build and deliver training with Product for Field Forum; help plan the calendar around launches

  • Run train-the-trainer sessions with the Revenue Enablement team so enablement can scale delivery

  • Review enablement-created content for technical accuracy before it reaches the field

Competitive & Market Intelligence

  • Maintain competitive battlecards using one consistent framework, so reps learn the structure once and can recall it under pressure

  • Keep the competitive matrix current across hyperscalers, neoclouds, and managed inference providers

  • Publish digestible analyst and industry updates with FAQs and "what to say" guidance, drawing on sources like SemiAnalysis and Gartner

  • Keep ICP definitions current and help sellers identify and qualify new ICP targets

Customer-Facing Content

  • Product one-pagers and datasheets for every product, ready to send

  • Customer stories, each with a single business-impact slide reps can drop into any deck

  • Infographics, top-ten lists, and short attention-grabbing assets for outreach and LinkedIn

  • Build ROI/TCO calculators and other decision-support tools for sales

Operations

  • Restructure and maintain content repositories so blogs, ungated content, and decks are discoverable, and so AI assistants and Field Guide can reliably pull the latest version

  • Enforce version hygiene: one source of truth per asset, visible last-updated dates

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Required

  • 10+ years in product marketing, ideally in cloud infrastructure, AI, or machine learning

  • Technical depth in AI/ML infrastructure: you understand the real differences between training and inference workloads, what makes an inference stack fast or cheap, and how customers actually evaluate compute

  • Working knowledge of the competitive landscape: hyperscalers, neoclouds, managed inference providers, and the buy-vs-build calculus

  • Fluency with sales messaging frameworks; Command of the Message strongly preferred

  • Proven storytelling: you can take a technical concept and make a non-technical seller feel confident repeating it

  • Real understanding of how enterprise sales works: pipeline stages, MEDDIC-style qualification, what a rep is actually doing in a first call, and why most enablement content goes unused

  • Ability to work across a bench of product-line PMMs: synthesizing their work, not duplicating it, and holding the portfolio view none of them own individually

  • Experience building content that sellers voluntarily reuse

Strong Plus

  • Prior experience at an infrastructure, semiconductor, or AI platform company

  • Background as a sales engineer, solutions architect, or technical seller

  • Comfort with data tooling to build TCO models that survive customer scrutiny

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $240,000 - $270,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About This Role:

The Production Planner is responsible for ensuring the production schedule is both achievable and executed across Crusoe’s manufacturing footprint. In this role, you will convert the reconciled Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) plan into a real, capacity-constrained Master Production Schedule (MPS) and drive it through to floor execution—operating either at the network level (cross-site MPS, time fences, master scheduling) or across a specific site cluster.

Serving as the operational architect of manufacturing cadence, this role sits at the intersection of demand, capacity, and floor execution. The ideal candidate brings a strong grasp of MPS logic, enforces schedule discipline through planning time fences, and provides independent, data-driven capacity insights to protect production timelines across single or multi-site operations. This is a Full-Time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Master Production Scheduling: Convert the reconciled S&OP plan into a time-phased MPS by SKU, site, and work center.

  • Capacity Planning & Feasibility: Assess and represent true capacity feasibility (lines, shifts, work centers) during S&OP supply and capacity reviews.

  • Time Fence Governance: Set and enforce planning time fences (Frozen / Firm / Free) consistently, maintaining a clear approval process for schedule exceptions.

  • Multi-Site Handoff Tracking: For network-scoped assignments, track inter-site handoff timing for dependent site pairs (e.g., Arvada fabrication output feeding Brighton assembly) to ensure cross-site alignment.

  • Site Target Translation: For cluster-scoped assignments, translate network MPS into site-level targets, overseeing Site Schedulers who release work orders and manage floor sequencing.

  • Schedule Adherence & Root Cause Analysis: Track schedule adherence (planned vs. actual by work order), logging deviations and feeding root-cause analysis back into the S&OP cycle.

  • S&OP Forum Representation: Deliver credible capacity assessments, inter-site constraint views, and schedule adherence metrics in monthly S&OP reconciliations.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: 3–5+ years of dedicated experience in production planning, detailed scheduling, or master scheduling within a manufacturing environment.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Operations, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • System & Technical Knowledge: Solid working knowledge of MPS/MRP logic, finite capacity planning, and ERP scheduling modules (e.g., Acumatica or similar systems).

  • Cross-Functional Communication: Comfort presenting capacity constraints, trade-offs, and adherence metrics in cross-functional forums and leadership reviews.

Bonus Points:

  • APICS / ASCM certification, such as CPIM (Certified in Planning and Inventory Management).

  • Prior experience in multi-site or network-level production planning across dependent manufacturing facilities.

  • Hands-on experience using Acumatica ERP.

  • Background in high-tech manufacturing, modular data center production, or complex assembly environments.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $95,000 - $115,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDCORP)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. About This Role:

The Material Planner is responsible for ensuring the production schedule is materially feasible across assigned commodities. Working directly from the Master Production Schedule (MPS) and released Manufacturing Bill of Materials (MBOM), you will run MRP, maintain Clear-to-Build (CTB) status, manage shortages proactively, and own the day-to-day supplier forecast and commitment cadence to keep supply and demand in sync.

This role serves as the operational engine connecting production planning, physical inventory, and strategic sourcing. The ideal candidate brings a strong grasp of MRP logic, thrives on data accuracy, and proactively identifies material constraints weeks ahead of floor execution so that shortages are resolved before they ever impact production schedules. This is a Full-Time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • MRP Execution & Requirements Netting: Run MRP and BOM explosions against the MPS, netting gross requirements against on-hand, on-order, and in-transit material.

  • Clear-to-Build (CTB) Coverage: Maintain and refresh CTB coverage status by SKU and work center for assigned commodity areas on a standing cadence.

  • Proactive Shortage Escalation: Identify potential material shortages well ahead of floor execution, escalating to Strategic Sourcing/Procurement for expedite or dual-sourcing actions while tracking mitigation status.

  • Supplier Forecast & Commitment Cadence: Share rolling forecasts with suppliers, secure lead-time and capacity commitments, and feed commits back into MRP within negotiated commercial frameworks.

  • Planning Parameter Management: Set and maintain item-level ERP planning parameters (order policy, lot sizing, lead times, safety stock, make/buy flags, and time fences) at MBOM release.

  • Inventory Accuracy & ABC Classification: Partner with Materials Management to reconcile ERP balances against physical stock, maintaining ABC usage classification data by part number.

  • S&OP Forum Representation: Represent the material and CTB constraint view during monthly Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) reconciliations.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: 2–5+ years of dedicated experience in material planning, MRP execution, or supply/demand planning within a manufacturing environment.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

  • System & Technical Knowledge: Working knowledge of MRP logic, complex BOM structures, and ERP planning modules (e.g., Acumatica or similar systems).

  • Supplier Coordination: Comfort working directly with suppliers to communicate rolling forecasts and secure firm delivery/capacity commitments.

  • Data & Analytical Skills: Strong Excel and data manipulation skills to manage shortage tracking, CTB models, and net-requirement feeds for Procurement.

Bonus Points:

  • APICS / ASCM certification, such as CPIM (Certified in Planning and Inventory Management).

  • Experience in hardware manufacturing, data center infrastructure, or complex equipment assemblies.

  • Hands-on experience using Acumatica ERP.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation will be paid in the range of $95,0000 - $115,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDCORP)

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

As a GPU-cloud provider, Crusoe’s infrastructure is our product. Infrastructure Security Engineering is a critical executive domain in our security organization. Unlike traditional enterprise cloud security functions that act as passive auditors asking other teams to fix bugs, this is a strategic platform engineering organization. As Director of Infrastructure Security, you will define organizational strategy, scale leadership structures, and lead an expanding organization responsible for foundational security strategy across our hyper-scale fleet.

Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Security Engineering, you will own the long-term strategic vision, organizational architecture, and executive execution across two core pillars: Platform Security Services and Cloud Security Access and Posture Governance. Leveraging extensive executive leadership experience, you will establish multi-year roadmaps, empower engineering managers, and build out high-performing organizational structures required to scale with Crusoe’s growth.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

1. Strategic Leadership, Organizational Architecture & Executive Oversight

  • Organizational Strategy & Manager Leadership: Design and scale dedicated engineering domains across both pillars. Hire, mentor, and empower engineering managers and senior leaders, establishing clear organizational accountability, career paths, and leadership governance as Crusoe scales.

  • Executive Alignment & Resource Allocation: Own multi-year strategic roadmaps, high-level domain metrics, and organizational risk reduction goals. Translate complex technical infrastructure risks into strategic business priorities and resource investments for executive stakeholders.

  • Technical Vision & Governance: Set long-term architectural vision, applying first-principles strategy to guide engineering leadership, challenge legacy norms, and ensure all security initiatives align with Crusoe’s overarching mission.

2. Strategy & Team Building for Platform Security Services

  • Identity, Secrets & PKI Strategy: Define the multi-year identity and access roadmap, ensuring the organization delivers scalable, secure-by-default primitives across the hyper-scale GPU fleet.

  • Fleet Security & Sensor Strategy: Drive strategic planning and organizational alignment for fleet-wide runtime visibility, empowering engineering teams to deploy security sensors and kernel-level protections at scale.

  • Hardware, Firmware & Supply Chain Governance: Establish organizational standards, risk policies, and oversight frameworks for hardware roots of trust, secure boot, firmware update validation, and software supply chain verification across custom GPU nodes and networks.

3. Infrastructure Security Posture and Access Governance

  • Organizational Strategy & Growth: Formally establish the long-term vision, leadership structure, and operational roadmap for this function, driving sustainable organizational scale across Crusoe's infrastructure security domain.

  • Control Plane & Cloud Security Governance: Establish high-level security architecture frameworks and governance for Crusoe’s control plane across public cloud environments and multi-gigawatt on-premise AI data center infrastructure.

  • Zero-Trust & IAM Strategy: Champion executive initiatives to eliminate standing admin privileges and long-lived secrets, enabling leadership teams to deliver automated, just-in-time access engines and least-privilege models.

  • Systemic Risk & Isolation Governance: Oversee the identification and mitigation of architectural risks, driving cross-functional alignment on tenant control plane isolation, decoupling execution environments, and enforcing structural blast-radius boundaries natively through Infrastructure-as-Code strategy.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Executive Security Leadership: 10+ years of progressive security engineering experience, including 5+ years leading second-line management structures or multi-team security organizations at hyper-scale cloud providers or infrastructure-intensive platforms.

  • Organizational Design & Manager Leadership: Proven success in organizational architecture, hiring, developing, and mentoring engineering managers, and building scalable team structures aligned with broader business objectives.

  • Strategic Vision & First-Principles Thinking: Demonstrated track record of evaluating complex technical challenges from foundational principles, guiding engineering leaders to solve systemic architectural bottlenecks without defaulting to off-the-shelf vendor playbooks.

  • Executive Stakeholder Management: Excellence in partnering with cross-functional executive leaders, setting multi-year talent and resource allocation strategies, and translating high-level infrastructure security risk into business context.

  • Technical Credibility: Broad architectural depth across Linux, hypervisors, container orchestration, IAM frameworks, PKI, workload identity, and hardware or network primitives, sufficient to guide senior leaders and evaluate high-level system design.

  • Location: In-person presence in the San Francisco Bay Area to partner closely with senior engineering and operational leadership.

 

Benefits:

Competitive compensation and equity packages

Restricted Stock Units

Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

Employer contributions to HSA account

Paid parental leave

Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

Professional development & tuition reimbursement

Mental health & wellness support

Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

Cell phone stipend

401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

Volunteer time off

Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

Daily meals allowance

Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $285,000 - $335,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

  • Vendor management strategy: Own Crusoe's long-term vendor management strategy for the network, including defining our cost structure and capital allocation.

  • Platform targets: Set the performance, reliability, scalability, and cost targets the network must hit, including network cost per GPU and per server.

  • Connectivity architecture: Own cross-DC and multi-site connectivity strategy, network topology, and failure-domain design.

  • Technology strategy: Drive NIC, DPU, switch, and networking technology strategy, including evaluating new hardware generations and vendors.

  • Structural investment: Identify structural limitations in the current architecture and prioritize the long-term investments that resolve them.

  • Engineering partnership: Partner with Infrastructure Engineering and Architecture on major technical tradeoffs, and define the product requirements and business rationale behind foundational investments.

  • Executive communication: Represent networking foundations in leadership reviews, translating architecture and vendor tradeoffs into clear decision docs.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field.

  • 8+ years of technical product management experience, or product-minded infrastructure engineering experience, with a track record of owning architecture-level outcomes at Principal or equivalent scope.

  • Subject matter expertise in networking, with the credibility to operate as a peer to senior infrastructure engineers and architects.

  • Direct experience with fleet-wide network architecture, topology design, and failure-domain strategy at scale.

  • Experience managing long-term vendor strategy and vetting in-house software engineering investment for core networking infrastructure.

  • A strong grasp of infrastructure economics at scale, including cost per unit and capacity planning.

  • Analytical mindset with the ability to use data to inform multi-year infrastructure decisions.

  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to translate technical tradeoffs into clear narratives for engineering leadership and executives.

  • Direct experience with RDMA fabrics such as InfiniBand or RoCE, and with GPU cluster networking for AI training or inference.

 

Bonus Points

  • Experience with data center network design, including cross-DC and multi-site connectivity.

  • Familiarity with the current landscape of networking silicon, NICs, and switch vendors serving AI infrastructure.

  • Experience managing or mentoring other product managers.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

Crusoe is building the infrastructure layer that powers the most demanding AI workloads on the planet. Our storage stack is what keeps tens of thousands of GPUs fed with data, whether that means block volumes for fast bootups, a shared file system for a training cluster, or the object storage tier a physical AI customer depends on. As a Principal Product Manager on our AI Infrastructure team, you will own the long-term architecture and technology strategy for Crusoe's storage foundation: how we build our storage stack at scale, from hardware and vendor selection to fleet-wide deployment architecture.

This is a foundations role. What You'll Be Working On

  • Long-term vision: Define the 2-4 year vision and roadmap for Crusoe's storage foundation, across block, file, object, local NVMe, and archival tiers.

  • Architecture and hierarchy: Own the long-term storage architecture and hierarchy

  • Vendor management and technology strategy: Own Crusoe's long-term vendor management strategy for the storage stack, and shapes our cost structure, capital allocation, and competitive position.

  • Platform targets: Set the performance and durability targets the platform must hit, including storage cost per usable TB and capacity efficiency.

  • Scale for AI: Own the future architecture required to support significantly larger AI clusters and fleet scale.

  • Structural investment: Identify structural limitations in the current architecture and prioritize the long-term investments that resolve them.

  • Engineering partnership: Partner with Infrastructure Engineering and Architecture on major technical tradeoffs, and define the product requirements and business rationale behind foundational investments.

  • Industry scouting: Actively scout the industry for emerging storage technologies and vendors, and represent storage foundations in leadership reviews.

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field.

  • 8+ years of technical product management experience, or product-minded infrastructure engineering experience, with a track record of owning architecture-level outcomes at Principal or equivalent scope, specifically focused on cloud storage or related infrastructure.

  • Subject matter expertise in storage, with the credibility to operate as a peer to senior infrastructure engineers and architects.

  • Strong technical understanding of cloud storage architectures, including block, file, and object storage, at hyperscale.

  • Experience managing long-term vendor strategy and vetting in-house software engineering investment for storage hardware and software.

  • A strong grasp of infrastructure economics at scale, including cost per usable TB and capacity efficiency.

  • Analytical mindset with the ability to use data to inform multi-year infrastructure decisions.

  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to translate technical tradeoffs into clear narratives for engineering leadership and executives.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with AI/ML infrastructure, including training and inference workloads in the cloud.

  • Direct experience with high-performance storage networking, such as RDMA or GPUDirect Storage.

  • Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, Azure, GCP) and their storage services, or a deep understanding of cloud-native storage principles at hyperscale.

  • Experience managing or mentoring other product managers

jobs.descriptionHtml:

About This Role:

Crusoe is seeking a strategic and results-driven Senior Technical Sourcing Manager, Fiber to lead category strategy, sourcing, and supplier management across Crusoe Cloud’s data center categories. This role is critical for driving cost efficiency, supply resiliency, and partnerships across regions, directly contributing to the overall success of Crusoe's expansion. We are looking for a strong operator and strategic thinker who can serve as the single-threaded leader for global category strategy, bringing a strong background in global sourcing, supplier relationship management, contract negotiation, and cross-functional leadership. This is a full-time position with flexibility to be based in Bellevue (WA).

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Global Category Strategy: Develop and implement global sourcing and category strategies that are innovative, cost-effective, and consistently aligned with company objectives.

  • Supplier Relationship Management: Evaluate, develop, and actively manage relationships with key global suppliers, ensuring they consistently meet Crusoe's quality standards and critical delivery deadlines.

  • Contract Negotiation: Lead negotiation of global supplier contracts and commercial terms to secure favorable pricing, payment terms, and conditions.

  • Risk Management & Contingency: Conduct comprehensive risk management across the global supply base, including proactive contingency planning to ensure business continuity.

  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Lead cross-functional teams and coordinate activities with internal and external stakeholders to accurately plan for category needs across the business.

  • Spend Analysis & Cost Optimization: Analyze global spend, market conditions, and supplier performance to identify cost savings opportunities and negotiation leverage.

  • Business Review Coordination: Lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and ongoing performance reviews with strategic global suppliers.

  • Sustainability Integration: Implement and champion sustainability practices in procurement and sourcing operations, ensuring alignment with Crusoe's environmental goals.

  • Industry Trend Monitoring: Stay current with industry trends, global market conditions, and category innovations to maintain Crusoe's competitive edge.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain/Logistics, International Trade, or a related field.

  • Experience & Leadership: Approximately 5-7+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, category management, or procurement, preferably for Data Center Infrastructure, Cloud, or Hardware supply chains.

  • Operational Track Record: Proven track record of managing global supply chains, complex supplier relationships, ensuring vendor compliance, and implementing process improvements at scale.

  • Core Skills: Strong communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.

  • Analytical Prowess: Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational abilities.

  • Strategic Supply Management: Proven experience working with global manufacturers and suppliers, owning contract negotiation, supplier qualification, documentation, and performance management.

  • Supply Chain Experience: Background working with hyperscalers, OEM/ODMs, or infrastructure providers.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience managing global categories across multiple regions or geographies.

  • Experience managing Data Center Fiber infrastructure specifically Indoor Plant Fiber, Outdoor Plant Fiber, In-the-row fiber connectivity, and cabling

  • Professional certification such as CPSM, CSCP, or CPIM.

  • Experience with AI/data center infrastructure supply chains.

Benefits:

  • Opportunity for career growth in a high-impact organization and industry.

  • Industry competitive pay.

  • Restricted Stock Units in a fast growing, well-funded technology company.

  • Health insurance package options that include HDHP and PPO, vision, and dental for you and your dependents.

  • Employer contributions to HSA accounts.

  • Paid Parental Leave.

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability.

  • Teladoc.

  • 401(k) with a 100% match up to 4% of salary.

  • Generous paid time off and holiday schedule.

  • Cell phone reimbursement.

  • Tuition reimbursement.

  • Subscription to the Calm app.

  • MetLife Legal.

  • Company paid commuter benefits; $300 per month.

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $140,000 – $170,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.descriptionHtml:

About the Role:
Crusoe is seeking a Chief of Staff to serve as a strategic and operational partner to our Chief People Officer (CPO), helping build the operating discipline, alignment, and execution capabilities required as we scale globally.

This leader will shape how the People organization operates, connecting strategic priorities to planning, decision-making, execution, and communication. They will establish the rhythms and mechanisms that enable our leaders to work as one cohesive team, deliver major People initiatives effectively, and make well-informed decisions.

The ideal candidate combines strong strategic judgment with hands-on execution. They bring experience building effective operating practices, ideally across both high-growth and mature organizations, and know how to introduce structure without bureaucracy. This is a highly influential role for someone who can anticipate challenges, navigate complexity, and turn strategy into coordinated action.


What You'll Be Working On:

  • Lead the People Operating Rhythm

    • Design and lead the People organization's operating cadence, including annual and quarterly planning, OKRs, operating reviews, leadership meetings, and decision forums.

    • Establish clear expectations for planning, executive materials, decision-making, accountability, and follow-through.

    • Track progress against strategic priorities, surfacing risks, dependencies, tradeoffs, and decisions requiring leadership attention.

    • Partner with functional leaders to maintain a coordinated enterprise calendar of major People programs, including performance, compensation, talent reviews, and employee listening.

    • Ensure programs are thoughtfully sequenced, business-ready, and designed to minimize competing demands on leaders, managers, and employees.

  • Orchestrate Cross-Functional Priorities and Execution

    • Integrate priorities and initiatives across the People leadership team, ensuring functional strategies contribute to a cohesive enterprise agenda.

    • Maintain visibility into major initiatives, milestones, dependencies, resource constraints, and execution risks.

    • Partner with functional leaders and program managers to identify interdependencies, coordinate priorities, and escalate execution risks, while preserving functional ownership of strategy and delivery.

    • Establish lightweight governance and execution mechanisms that reinforce accountability, transparency, and results.

  • Elevate Executive Communications and Business Readiness

    • Partner with the CPO, People leadership team, and Internal Communications to shape a cohesive narrative and communication strategy for People priorities and initiatives.

    • Develop and refine executive presentations, board materials, leadership updates, and strategic communications, ensuring clarity, analytical rigor, and actionable recommendations.

    • Establish high standards for executive materials, including clear narratives, decision points, and stakeholder expectations.

    • Coordinate communications and leadership readiness for major People initiatives, ensuring messages, timing, and required actions are aligned across the business.

  • Serve as a Strategic Partner to the CPO

    • Act as a trusted advisor and thought partner to the CPO on organizational priorities, operating effectiveness, and leadership alignment.

    • Support the CPO and People leadership team in translating organizational priorities into an integrated People operating plan, with clear milestones, decision points, and accountability.

    • Prepare the CPO for critical discussions and decisions, synthesizing information, stakeholder perspectives, risks, and recommendations.

    • Lead select special projects on behalf of the CPO, particularly those that span the People leadership team or fall outside established functional ownership.

    • Foster a culture of operating excellence, thoughtful prioritization, and consistent follow-through across the People organization.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 10+ years in business operations, strategy, management consulting, Chief of Staff, or related roles, with experience partnering directly with senior executives.

  • Experience navigating rapid organizational growth and complexity, ideally complemented by experience in a mature, publicly traded company with strong operating and governance practices.

  • Proven ability to establish operating rhythms, lead planning processes, manage complex cross-functional priorities, and translate strategy into execution.

  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret complex data, identify meaningful insights, evaluate tradeoffs, and develop evidence-based recommendations.

  • Exceptional ability to personally develop polished, data-driven presentations, strategic narratives, and decision materials for executive leadership. Board-level experience is a plus.

  • Understands how organizations operate, anticipates dependencies and downstream impacts, and brings clarity to ambiguous or complex situations.

  • Builds trust across senior stakeholders, drives alignment without formal authority, and combines strategic perspective with hands-on execution and exceptional attention to detail.

  • Understanding of People/HR functions, talent programs, and employee lifecycle processes preferred, though strong business operators from other disciplines will be considered.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $195,000 - $230,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

The Mechanical Quality Inspector is a quality professional responsible for safeguarding product integrity across the entire manufacturing lifecycle—spanning Incoming Quality Control (IQC), In-Process Quality Control (IPQC), and Outgoing Quality Control (OQC).

Supporting both Modular Data Center (Spark) and Power Distribution Center (PDC) product lines, this role executes end-to-end inspections for mechanical and structural systems. From validating incoming raw components and structural assemblies, to performing in-process inspections and authorizing final ship release, the Quality Inspector ensures every product meets strict engineering specifications, safety codes, and customer requirements.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Incoming Quality Control (IQC): Inspect raw materials, structural steel, and sub-assemblies upon arrival against purchase orders, engineering specs, drawings, supplier CoCs (Certificate of Compliance), and supplier OQC reports to prevent non-conforming materials from entering production.

  • In-Process Quality Control (IPQC): Perform designated hold-point inspections during structural fabrication and enclosure assembly. Ensure alignment and structural fit-up before downstream work continues.

  • Outgoing Quality Control (OQC): Conduct comprehensive pre-shipment inspections on completed modular units including traceability & genealogy requirements.   • Technical & Precision Proficiency: Demonstrated experience using precision mechanical measuring tools (calipers, micrometers, protractors, laser levels, feeler gauges, calibrated torque wrenches).

About This Role:

The Quality Technician - Electrical Inspector serves as a critical stakeholder in Crusoe's manufacturing operations. This role is responsible for ensuring that all modular data centers, medium-voltage (MV) power distribution systems, and complex electrical sub-assemblies meet rigid technical specifications, regulatory standards, and corporate quality benchmarks.

Operating on a fast-paced production floor, the Quality Technician cross-functionally collaborates with Engineering, Safety, and Production teams to mitigate risk, drive continuous improvement, and safeguard product reliability.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • End-to-End Quality Inspection & Testing: Conduct rigorous inspections and hands-on functional testing across a diverse equipment portfolio, ranging from component-level sub-assemblies to fully integrated systems.

  • Component-Level Scope: Verify compliance for enclosures, breaker panels, switchboards, MV switchgear, load centers, HVAC units, surge protection devices, and PLC/control wiring.

  • System-Level Scope: Validate structural and electrical integrity for modular data center units, Power Distribution Centers (PDCs), and electrical houses (E-Houses).

  • Live Power Testing & Commissioning: Perform operational commissioning, live power validation, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), and preliminary commissioning for complex electrical and control infrastructure.

  • Functional System Validation: Confirm total operational integrity across all system levels (including 24VDC, 415VAC, HMI, and ATS) to guarantee zero-defect delivery to the end user.

  • Documentation & Technical Output: Author comprehensive testing reports, compliance certificates, and maintain audit-ready documentation for both component and system-level builds.

  • Process Audits & Standardization: Conduct routine process audits of electrical assembly, control wiring, power distribution integration, and final installation methodologies. Own and continuously optimize quality standard operating procedures (SOPs), testing matrixes, and training materials.

  • Compliance & Engineering Alignment: Verify that all manufacturing execution adheres strictly to approved engineering drawings, schematics, NFPA 70E regulatory frameworks, LOTO protocols, and industry regulations.

  • Defect Management & CAPA: Lead the identification, tagging, and resolution of material non-conformances and engineering deviations. Partner with Engineering and Manufacturing teams (DFM) to analyze defects, implement robust Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA), and eliminate recurring bottlenecks.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Electrical Systems Expertise: Robust, hands-on experience with low-voltage (LV) and medium-voltage (MV) electrical installations, including PDCs, E-houses, and industrial control panels.

  • Regulatory & Industry Standards: Working knowledge of IEC, NEC, NFPA 70B, IEEE, and NETA testing specifications.

  • Advanced Component Familiarity: Strong working knowledge of PLCs, Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs), HMI systems, Motor Control Centers (MCC), and Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPS).

  • Schematic & Drawing Literacy: Advanced proficiency in reading, interpreting, and tracing complex electrical schematics, one-line diagrams, and detailed engineering drawings.

  • Objective Quality Decision-Making: Proven ability to maintain strict quality standards and firmly enforce compliance guidelines within high-throughput manufacturing environments.

  • Analytical Precision & Detail Orientation: Exceptional detail orientation with a proven track record of identifying micro-level anomalies in complex, macro-level assemblies.

  • Digital Literacy: Proficiency in Google Workspace, Microsoft Office (Excel, Word), and standard digital quality logging and QMS tools.

  • Operational Agility & Physical Demands: Ability to stand, walk, stoop, and bend for extended periods on an active manufacturing floor, maneuver through modular units, and safely lift up to 50 lbs.

  • Professional Communication: Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to articulate technical defects clearly to cross-functional stakeholders and floor leadership.

  • Safety & Screening Compliance: Position is designated as safety-sensitive. Must pass a comprehensive background check and drug/alcohol screening in accordance with company safety regulations.

Bonus Points:

  • Licensure & Relevant Experience: 4+ years of hands-on electrical experience with a valid Journeyman license, OR 3+ years of dedicated electrical quality inspection experience in an industrial manufacturing setting.

  • UL Certification & Methodologies: Practical experience with UL inspection methodologies and UL listing certification processes.

  • Precision Assemblies & Torquing: Demonstrated experience with documented industrial torquing procedures and torque specification verification.

  • Quality Frameworks: Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, 5S principles, or ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems.

  • Professional Certifications: Project Management Professional (PMP) or Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) designation.

  • Systems Infrastructure: Operational experience with Manufacturing Resource Planning (MRP) or Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems, specifically Acumatica.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $29.00 - $33.00 / HR + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads.
