We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Crusoe is seeking a Manufacturing Quality Manager to oversee Manufacturing Quality across multiple AI data center infrastructure production sites. Reporting directly to the Director of Quality, this role leads team management, quality assurance, process controls, electrical/mechanical product quality, QMS execution, regulatory compliance, testing, and continuous improvement across our facilities.

Crusoe Quality Org Leadership Philosophy: The ideal candidate does not view Manufacturing Quality as simply an inspection organization. We are looking for a leader who can build a culture where Quality is designed into the product → engineered into the manufacturing process → verified through robust testing → controlled through Statistical Process Controls (SPC) → measured through data → continuously improved with QMS discipline.

The successful candidate will demonstrate equal proficiency in conducting shop-floor oversight, evaluating electrical testing procedures, reviewing weld integrity with Certified Welding Inspectors, and collaborating with Engineering on Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) initiatives. Furthermore, this leader must maintain rigorous audit readiness across UL compliance, QMS, ISO, and safety standards, perform thorough quality data analytics, and effectively communicate manufacturing and quality risks to executive leadership.

This strategic role demands deep expertise in electromechanical assembly, production processes, and QMS. Operating across Manufacturing, QMS, Engineering, and Regulatory Compliance, the Manager will build and guide high-performing Quality teams to foster a rigorous Quality mindset across all Crusoe sites. This position requires approximately 30% to 40% travel among manufacturing facilities, vendor sites, and client locations.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Multi-Site Manufacturing Quality Leadership: Direct quality operations across multiple Crusoe facilities. Define inspection standards and acceptance criteria, lead multi-site containment efforts with urgency, establish staffing requirements, partner with production leadership, coach quality staff, and build scalable quality systems to support rapid growth while owning QMS compliance and discipline.

  • Mechanical Quality Assurance: Provide technical oversight for mechanical fabrication, structural assemblies, sheet metal, welding/welded structures, CWI requirements, dimensional inspection, GD&T, surface coatings/paints, fastening/torque control, and enclosure assembly quality.

  • Electrical Quality Assurance: Direct technical oversight for switchgear, switchboards, breakers, electrical cabinets, busbars, industrial control equipment, wiring/harnessing, electrical safety testing, insulation/dielectric testing, hi-pot testing, continuity/grounding, and electrical IPQC.

  • Product Requirements Compliance & Traceability: Lead QA activities to ensure full compliance with UL 891, UL 508, NRTL, NETA ATS-2025, customer, regulatory, and product certification standards across electrical equipment, assemblies, and infrastructure.

  • Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) & Factory Witness Testing (FWT): Lead Quality oversight for factory testing and customer/certification witness activities, including pre-FAT readiness reviews, test procedure approvals, calibration verification, test result traceability, defect resolution, and witness inspections. Ensure manufacturing sites are fully prepared prior to customer/certification execution.

  • Product Change Management: Ensure all modifications to product designs and Bills of Materials (BOM) are formally communicated to Quality Assurance teams, systematically updating corresponding inspection protocols and acceptance criteria.

  • Manufacturing Process Quality & Quality Engineering: Partner with Manufacturing and Engineering to implement robust process controls (PFMEA, Control Plans, Process Flow Diagrams, SPC, MSA/Gage R&R, Poka-Yoke, standardized work, FAI, layered audits) to drive first-pass yield, reduce scrap/rework, and minimize process variation.

  • QMS Compliance & Audit Readiness: Oversee manufacturing quality problem-solving initiatives across teams. Maintain constant audit readiness for internal, customer, ISO 9001:2026, and certification audits. Oversee corrective actions from audit findings, manage quality records, and serve as the liaison between Manufacturing Quality and the enterprise QMS organization.

  • Structured Problem Solving & CAPA: Lead and coach personnel through core quality and risk management methodologies, including CAPA, NCR, RCA, 8D, SCAR, containment, deviation management, and effectiveness verification to eliminate repeat issues.

  • Quality Assurance Data Management: Establish cross-site quality metrics and dashboards tracking First Pass Yield, Defect PPM, NCR/Rework/Scrap rates, escapes, COPQ, FAT/FWT performance, and audit findings to pinpoint systemic trends and execute targeted operational improvements.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration (Engineering & Supply Chain): Partner with Design, Manufacturing Engineering, and NPI teams on DFM/Quality reviews, CTQ identification, GD&T, change control, and converting compliance rules into factory controls. Collaborate with Supplier Quality and Procurement on supplier qualification, subcontractor quality, incoming requirements, and risk escalation.

  • People Leadership & Team Development: Build and direct high-performing multi-site Quality teams. Align staffing plans with manufacturing volume, define competencies and career paths, enable cross-training between mechanical and electrical teams, cultivate technical SMEs, and foster an organizational culture centered on accountability and continuous improvement.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Professional Experience: 15+ years of progressive experience in Manufacturing Quality, Quality Engineering, Quality Assurance, Electrical Quality, Mechanical Quality, or related disciplines, including significant experience leading Quality organizations in complex manufacturing environments.

  • Multi-Site Leadership Track Record: Demonstrated people-management experience leading cross-functional Quality teams across multiple manufacturing facilities.

  • Dual-Domain Expertise (Electrical & Mechanical): Proven experience supporting both electrical hardware (switchboards, switchgear, breakers, industrial controls) and mechanical hardware (sheet metal fabrication, structural welding, enclosures, coatings).

  • Testing & Inspection Mastery: Strong experience with FAT, FWT, electrical testing (hi-pot, dielectric, continuity), and end-to-end manufacturing inspection (IQC, IPQC, OQC).

  • Regulatory & Compliance Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of UL compliance and certification requirements, with experience working with external auditors, certification bodies, customers, and regulatory organizations.

  • Welding Process Oversight: Working knowledge of welding inspection and CWI-controlled process management.

  • Root Cause & RCA Methodologies: Demonstrated mastery of CAPA, RCA, SCAR, 8D, NCR, and structured problem-solving methodologies.

  • Quality Management Systems: Deep knowledge of QMS principles, ISO auditing, quality data management, and manufacturing quality controls.

This strategic role demands deep expertise in electromechanical assembly, production processes, and QMS. Operating across Manufacturing, QMS, Engineering, and Regulatory Compliance, the Manager will build and guide high-performing Quality teams to foster a rigorous Quality mindset across all Crusoe sites. This position requires approximately 30% to 40% travel among manufacturing facilities, vendor sites, and client locations.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Multi-Site Manufacturing Quality Leadership: Direct quality operations across multiple Crusoe facilities. Define inspection standards and acceptance criteria, lead multi-site containment efforts with urgency, establish staffing requirements, partner with production leadership, coach quality staff, and build scalable quality systems to support rapid growth while owning QMS compliance and discipline.

 - Mechanical Quality Assurance: Provide technical oversight for mechanical fabrication, structural assemblies, sheet metal, welding/welded structures, CWI requirements, dimensional inspection, GD&T, surface coatings/paints, fastening/torque control, and enclosure assembly quality.

 - Electrical Quality Assurance: Direct technical oversight for switchgear, switchboards, breakers, electrical cabinets, busbars, industrial control equipment, wiring/harnessing, electrical safety testing, insulation/dielectric testing, hi-pot testing, continuity/grounding, and electrical IPQC.

 - Product Requirements Compliance & Traceability: Lead QA activities to ensure full compliance with UL 891, UL 508, NRTL, NETA ATS-2025, customer, regulatory, and product certification standards across electrical equipment, assemblies, and infrastructure.

 - Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) & Factory Witness Testing (FWT): Lead Quality oversight for factory testing and customer/certification witness activities, including pre-FAT readiness reviews, test procedure approvals, calibration verification, test result traceability, defect resolution, and witness inspections. Ensure manufacturing sites are fully prepared prior to customer/certification execution.

 - Product Change Management: Ensure all modifications to product designs and Bills of Materials (BOM) are formally communicated to Quality Assurance teams, systematically updating corresponding inspection protocols and acceptance criteria.

 - Manufacturing Process Quality & Quality Engineering: Partner with Manufacturing and Engineering to implement robust process controls (PFMEA, Control Plans, Process Flow Diagrams, SPC, MSA/Gage R&R, Poka-Yoke, standardized work, FAI, layered audits) to drive first-pass yield, reduce scrap/rework, and minimize process variation.

 - QMS Compliance & Audit Readiness: Oversee manufacturing quality problem-solving initiatives across teams. Maintain constant audit readiness for internal, customer, ISO 9001:2026, and certification audits. Oversee corrective actions from audit findings, manage quality records, and serve as the liaison between Manufacturing Quality and the enterprise QMS organization.

 - Structured Problem Solving & CAPA: Lead and coach personnel through core quality and risk management methodologies, including CAPA, NCR, RCA, 8D, SCAR, containment, deviation management, and effectiveness verification to eliminate repeat issues.

 - Quality Assurance Data Management: Establish cross-site quality metrics and dashboards tracking First Pass Yield, Defect PPM, NCR/Rework/Scrap rates, escapes, COPQ, FAT/FWT performance, and audit findings to pinpoint systemic trends and execute targeted operational improvements.

Collaborate with Supplier Quality and Procurement on supplier qualification, subcontractor quality, incoming requirements, and risk escalation.

Align staffing plans with manufacturing volume, define competencies and career paths, enable cross-training between mechanical and electrical teams, cultivate technical SMEs, and foster an organizational culture centered on accountability and continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, AI Infrastructure (Storage)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role

Crusoe is building the infrastructure layer that powers the most demanding AI workloads on the planet. Our storage stack is what keeps tens of thousands of GPUs fed with data, whether that means block volumes for fast bootups, a shared file system for a training cluster, or the object storage tier a physical AI customer depends on. As a Staff Product Manager on our Cloud Infrastructure team, you will own the storage product roadmap and shape how customers experience capacity, durability, and ease of use.

 

This is a customer-obsessed role. You will spend real time with the engineers and infrastructure teams building on Crusoe Cloud, understand what is slowing them down or holding them back, and translate that into a product strategy that wins more of our business. You will work closely with Infrastructure Engineering, Cloud Software Engineering, SRE, Finance, and our executive team to turn customer insight into a storage platform that is easier to build on and better matched to how our customers actually use it.

 

What You'll Be Working On

  • Customer discovery and advocacy: Build deep relationships with customers to understand their storage needs, pain points, and growth plans, and act as their voice inside Crusoe.

  • Roadmap ownership: Own and prioritize the storage product roadmap across block, file, and object, balancing customer requests, technical feasibility, and business impact.

  • Product strategy: Define the roadmap for customer-facing storage capabilities, including tiering, versioning, backup and restore, and lifecycle management.

  • Cross-functional leadership: Partner with Infrastructure Engineering, Cloud Software Engineering, and SRE to define technical specifications, execution timelines, and economics.

  • Executive communication: Distill complex technical tradeoffs into clear, compelling narratives and decision docs for company leadership.

  • Market and competitive analysis: Track industry trends in cloud storage and translate them into concrete opportunities for Crusoe to differentiate.

  • Go-to-market support: Work with sales and marketing to position storage capabilities in a way that resonates with customers and drives new business.

  • Product documentation: Create and maintain documentation that helps customers understand and get the most out of Crusoe's storage capabilities.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer science, or a related field.

  • 5+ years of technical product management experience, or product-minded engineering experience, with a track record of owning outcomes at Staff or Group PM scope.

  • Strong customer orientation, with experience gathering and synthesizing customer feedback into product decisions that grow revenue and retention.

  • In-depth understanding of cloud technologies, platforms, and services (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS).

  • Experience building and launching storage products, such as block volumes, file-systems, or object storage.

  • Proven ability to define and scope ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives with minimal guidance.

  • Analytical mindset with the ability to use data to inform decision-making.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders across engineering, finance, and executive teams.

  • Direct technical experience working with storage hardware, protocols, or file systems.

 

Bonus Points

  • Familiarity with object storage access patterns, including public access and multi-tenant permissions.

  • Familiarity with backup, replication, and disaster recovery product design.

  • Familiarity with cloud storage economics and tiering strategy across hot, warm, and cold tiers.

  • Experience managing or mentoring other product managers.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 - $260,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

The Supplier Quality Engineer (SQE) is responsible for developing, managing, and continuously improving supplier quality performance to ensure purchased components, materials, and subcontracted processes consistently meet defined quality, reliability, delivery, and regulatory requirements.

Serving as the primary Quality interface between the company, suppliers, subcontractors, Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, and Operations, this role drives supplier qualification, New Product Introduction (NPI), process validation, corrective actions, supplier performance improvement, and continuous improvement across the supply base.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Supplier Quality Management: Own quality performance for assigned suppliers and commodities. Establish and maintain supplier quality requirements, specifications, and quality agreements. Monitor performance using defined KPIs, scorecards, and metrics while identifying risks and mitigation plans. Partner with Procurement and Engineering on supplier selection, development, and exit decisions.

  • Supplier Qualification & Development: Participate in supplier qualification and selection. Conduct quality assessments, process audits, capability evaluations, and evaluate manufacturing processes, quality systems, and controls. Develop targeted improvement plans to bridge capability, capacity, and maturity gaps.

  • New Product Introduction (NPI): Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, and suppliers during NPI. Review drawings, specifications, GD&T, CTQs, PFMEAs, Control Plans, Process Flow Diagrams, MSA, SPC, and inspection plans. Drive DFM/DFA/DFR reviews, lead process validation, approve FAI/FAIR and PPAP submissions, and ensure production ramp readiness.

  • Supplier Process & Product Quality: Perform process audits and manufacturing evaluations. Establish inspection and testing requirements based on product risk. Drive implementation of SPC, mistake-proofing, standardized work, and robust process controls, shifting suppliers from inspection-based quality toward prevention-focused quality.

  • Nonconformance & Corrective Action: Lead supplier-related nonconformance investigations. Drive containment, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and preventive action (8D, CAPA, RCCA). Verify effectiveness of corrective actions to prevent recurrence and track issues through closure.

  • Supplier Audits: Plan and execute risk-based supplier quality audits (process, product, system, special-process). Develop audit findings, oversee corrective-action plans, verify closure, and support internal, customer, and regulatory audits involving suppliers.

  • Supplier Performance & Metrics: Develop and maintain quality metrics including incoming defect rates/PPM, NCR rates, FPY, CAPA closure, process capability ($C_p$/$C_{pk}$), COPQ, escape rates, and audit performance. Leverage data to identify systemic trends and continuous improvement opportunities.

  • Incoming Quality & Manufacturing Support: Partner with Receiving and Incoming Inspection to establish risk-based inspection requirements, acceptance criteria, and disposition nonconforming materials. Work with Manufacturing Quality to resolve supplier-originating defects and reduce incoming inspection burdens through demonstrated supplier process capability.

  • Supplier Change Management: Review and approve supplier process, material, equipment, tooling, location, and sub-tier supplier changes. Ensure appropriate qualification, validation, risk assessment, change control documentation, and traceability before implementation.

  • Continuous Improvement: Lead supplier quality improvement projects using Lean Six Sigma and structured problem-solving methodologies. Reduce defects, scrap, rework, and supplier-related COPQ while promoting prevention-focused quality.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Educational Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Quality Engineering, or related field.

  • Professional Experience: 3+ years of experience in Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Quality Engineering, or a related field, with direct experience working with manufacturing suppliers and subcontractors.

  • Core Quality Tool Mastery: Strong knowledge of quality tools and problem-solving methodologies including PFMEA, Control Plans, SPC, MSA, 8D/RCCA, CAPA, and process audits.

  • Engineering & Drawing Literacy: Proven ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, GD&T, technical specifications, and inspection requirements.

  • Analytical & Technical Problem Solving: Strong analytical capabilities to evaluate process capability, statistical data, and complex manufacturing defects.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work effectively across Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, Operations, and external supply partners.

  • Communication & Influence: Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and external executives.

  • Travel Flexibility: Willingness and ability to travel to supplier facilities as required.

  • Safety & Compliance: Position is designated a safety-sensitive position located in safety-sensitive facilities. Mandatory participation in company safety, background check, drug, and alcohol programs is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Professional Certifications: ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Supplier Quality Professional (CSQP), or similar designation.

  • Process Excellence: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.

  • Frameworks & Methodologies: Experience with PPAP/APQP and structured automotive or aerospace quality methodologies.

  • Specialized Manufacturing Processes: Experience with special processes such as welding, machining, fabrication, casting, forging, sheet metal, coating, or electrical assembly.

  • Systems & Data: Experience with ERP/QMS software platforms and supplier quality dashboards.

  • Operational Environment: Experience scaling supplier quality in high-growth manufacturing, NPI/ramp environments, or managing strategic subcontractors.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $130,000 - $150,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

 - New Product Introduction (NPI): Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, and suppliers during NPI. Review drawings, specifications, GD&T, CTQs, PFMEAs, Control Plans, Process Flow Diagrams, MSA, SPC, and inspection plans. Drive DFM/DFA/DFR reviews, lead process validation, approve FAI/FAIR and PPAP submissions, and ensure production ramp readiness.

 - Supplier Process & Product Quality: Perform process audits and manufacturing evaluations. Establish inspection and testing requirements based on product risk. Drive implementation of SPC, mistake-proofing, standardized work, and robust process controls, shifting suppliers from inspection-based quality toward prevention-focused quality.

 - Nonconformance & Corrective Action: Lead supplier-related nonconformance investigations. Drive containment, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and preventive action (8D, CAPA, RCCA). Verify effectiveness of corrective actions to prevent recurrence and track issues through closure.

 - Supplier Audits: Plan and execute risk-based supplier quality audits (process, product, system, special-process). Develop audit findings, oversee corrective-action plans, verify closure, and support internal, customer, and regulatory audits involving suppliers.

 - Supplier Performance & Metrics: Develop and maintain quality metrics including incoming defect rates/PPM, NCR rates, FPY, CAPA closure, process capability ($C_p$/$C_{pk}$), COPQ, escape rates, and audit performance. Leverage data to identify systemic trends and continuous improvement opportunities.

 - Incoming Quality & Manufacturing Support: Partner with Receiving and Incoming Inspection to establish risk-based inspection requirements, acceptance criteria, and disposition nonconforming materials. Work with Manufacturing Quality to resolve supplier-originating defects and reduce incoming inspection burdens through demonstrated supplier process capability.

 - Supplier Change Management: Review and approve supplier process, material, equipment, tooling, location, and sub-tier supplier changes. Ensure appropriate qualification, validation, risk assessment, change control documentation, and traceability before implementation.

 - Continuous Improvement: Lead supplier quality improvement projects using Lean Six Sigma and structured problem-solving methodologies. Reduce defects, scrap, rework, and supplier-related COPQ while promoting prevention-focused quality.



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - Educational Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Quality Engineering, or related field.

 - Professional Experience: 3+ years of experience in Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Quality Engineering, or a related field, with direct experience working with manufacturing suppliers and subcontractors.

 - Core Quality Tool Mastery: Strong knowledge of quality tools and problem-solving methodologies including PFMEA, Control Plans, SPC, MSA, 8D/RCCA, CAPA, and process audits.

 - Engineering & Drawing Literacy: Proven ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, GD&T, technical specifications, and inspection requirements.

 - Analytical & Technical Problem Solving: Strong analytical capabilities to evaluate process capability, statistical data, and complex manufacturing defects.

 - Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work effectively across Engineering, Manufacturing, Procurement, Operations, and external supply partners.

 - Communication & Influence: Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and external executives.

 - Travel Flexibility: Willingness and ability to travel to supplier facilities as required.

 - Safety & Compliance: Position is designated a safety-sensitive position located in safety-sensitive facilities. Mandatory participation in company safety, background check, drug, and alcohol programs is required.



Bonus Points:

 - Professional Certifications: ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Supplier Quality Professional (CSQP), or similar designation.

 - Process Excellence: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.

 - Frameworks & Methodologies: Experience with PPAP/APQP and structured automotive or aerospace quality methodologies.

 - Specialized Manufacturing Processes: Experience with special processes such as welding, machining, fabrication, casting, forging, sheet metal, coating, or electrical assembly.

 - Systems & Data: Experience with ERP/QMS software platforms and supplier quality dashboards.

 - Operational Environment: Experience scaling supplier quality in high-growth manufacturing, NPI/ramp environments, or managing strategic subcontractors.

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

jobs.title: Senior Manager, QMS - Manufacturing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Our Senior QMS Manager, Manufacturing is responsible for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continuously improving Crusoe's Quality Management System (QMS) across all manufacturing and operational facilities. Owning the enterprise QMS framework, this role ensures quality processes, controls, records, procedures, and compliance activities are effectively executed and scaled across the organization.

Reporting into our Director of Quality, the QMS Manager partners closely with Product Quality, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and EHS to transition the organization from site-specific, paper-focused processes to a data-driven, risk-based, and preventive Quality Operating System. From leading internal and external audits to governing CAPA/NCR workflows, document control, and new site QMS launches, this role is pivotal in building an agile quality system that enables rapid business growth.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • QMS Framework & Governance: Own and maintain the overall Quality Management System. Establish QMS policies, standards, and governance mechanisms that bridge operational gaps and scale with manufacturing expansion.

  • Standards & Regulatory Compliance: Maintain organizational compliance with ISO 9001, customer standards, and applicable regulatory requirements. Monitor evolving standards and translate compliance requirements into practical operational controls.

  • Audit Program Leadership: Direct the enterprise audit program—including internal, customer, supplier, certification, and regulatory audits. Oversee audit planning, execution, finding closure, and transition the company toward a proactive quality culture.

  • CAPA & NCR Governance: Own enterprise nonconformance (NCR) and Corrective/Preventive Action (CAPA) processes. Standardize root-cause analysis (RCA), containment, and effectiveness verification while tracking systemic trends to prevent issue recurrence.

  • Document & Change Control: Manage the Quality Document Management System and change-control governance. Ensure current procedures, specs, and records are accessible at points of use and prevent the use of obsolete documentation.

  • Quality Records & Systems Integration: Establish quality record data governance. Partner with IT/Business Systems to integrate QMS data across ERP, MES, and inspection tools to drive enterprise-wide quality visibility.

  • Quality Metrics & Management Reviews: Establish cross-site quality dashboards tracking NCR/CAPA aging, audit findings, COPQ, and training compliance. Lead periodic Quality Management Reviews with executive leadership to convert quality data into strategic decisions.

  • Training & Quality Culture: Define role-based QMS training requirements, maintain competency records, and deploy quality awareness initiatives that foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.

  • Continuous Improvement & Process Maturity: Eliminate non-value-added quality steps, lead Lean Six Sigma projects, and establish closed-loop feedback between operational performance and QMS enhancements.

  • Enterprise Quality Risk Management: Institute risk-based QMS governance. Maintain quality risk registers and ensure high-risk processes receive appropriate controls, audits, and management oversight.

  • New Site Expansion: Lead QMS readiness activities for greenfield manufacturing sites, ensuring required procedures, forms, training, and controls are operational prior to production launch.

  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Serve as the primary QMS subject-matter expert, partnering with Product Quality, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing Quality, Engineering, and Supply Chain to drive systemic issue resolution.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Educational Foundation: Bachelor's degree in Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Operations, or a related field.

  • Professional Experience: 7+ years of experience in Quality, QMS, Quality Engineering, or Manufacturing Quality, with demonstrated success developing and scaling QMS frameworks.

  • Quality Standards Expertise: Deep working knowledge of ISO 9001 standards, quality management principles, and regulatory compliance.

  • Audit Management: Proven track record of planning, executing, and managing internal, customer, regulatory, and third-party certification audits.

  • Root Cause & CAPA Mastery: Strong expertise in CAPA, NCR, 8D, 5-Why, Fishbone, and structured problem-solving methodologies.

  • Document & Change Control Governance: Demonstrated experience managing quality document control systems, record retention, and engineering/operational change management processes.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Strong ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive accountability without relying solely on direct authority.

  • Analytical & Communication Skills: Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills with the ability to translate complex quality data into actionable business strategies.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Professional Certifications: ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE).

  • Process Excellence: Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.

  • ISO Implementation: Direct experience leading ISO 9001 implementation, recertification, or multi-site expansion.

  • Systems & Digital Transformation: Experience implementing enterprise QMS software platforms (e.g., MasterControl, ETQ, Veeva) and integrating QMS with ERP/MES systems.

  • Scaling Environment: Experience establishing QMS frameworks within fast-growing manufacturing organizations or greenfield facility launches.

  • Advanced Quality Technologies: Experience leveraging AI, predictive analytics, or digital transformation tools in quality management.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $190,000 - $215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Internal Tools & Automation
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

As a Forward-Deployed Engineer, you will embed with another Crusoe team, such as SRE, Finance, Sales, People Ops, or a product group. You will learn how they operate and build software that helps them take the next action, not just describe the problem. This is a forward-deployed engineering role serving internal teams. Your customer is a Crusoe team. Your product is the application, automation, or agent that makes their work faster, clearer, and more dependable. Success is measured by adoption and by the time and effort you return to the team. This is also a new function. You will be one of its first engineers and will help shape how it operates.

Several capabilities have matured recently. Modern BI tools now support write-back, so dashboards can update real records instead of only displaying them. Company data and operational context are reachable by AI agents through governed interfaces. Automation platforms and a shared library of reusable skills let you connect actions across many source systems, including CRM, support, infrastructure inventory, and the data warehouse.

Together, these capabilities allow an embedded engineer to deliver interactive tooling in days instead of quarters. We are looking for engineers who want to use that leverage to help internal teams move faster with confidence.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Embed with a stakeholder team. Participate in their rituals, observe manual workflows, and identify high-leverage work that software can remove.

  • Build applications. Build interactive tools that take action: read data, apply decisions, and write results back to systems of record.

  • Automate real workflows. Replace repetitive work with pipelines and agents that run independently and involve a person when judgment is required.

  • Own the work end to end. Scope problems with stakeholders, then build, deploy, measure adoption, and iterate. You are accountable for outcomes, with support from partner teams.

  • Contribute to the platform. Turn reusable parts of your work, such as skills, integrations, or UI patterns, into shared building blocks that accelerate future engagements.

  • Keep it correct. Build on sources of truth, respect governance and access controls, and make tooling reliable enough for daily operational use.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 8+ years building and owning production software. You write clean code, ship it, and remain accountable for it in production.

  • Staff-level scope and judgment. You can take an ambiguous, greenfield charter and turn it into a plan and shipped software with limited direction. You raise technical standards and help engineers around you grow.

  • Full-stack engineering skill. You can build user-facing interfaces, backend services and APIs, and the supporting data layer.

  • Strong SQL and data modeling. You can navigate a data warehouse, reason about pipelines, and validate numbers before relying on them.

  • Product mindset and stakeholder fluency. You collaborate well with non-engineers, translate manual processes into clear tools, and push back when a request is not the right solution.

  • Fast delivery with attention to correctness. You get a useful version in front of users quickly, then harden it thoughtfully. You maintain a clear standard for completion.

  • Comfort with AI-assisted development. You use LLM agents and automation platforms effectively, and understand where guardrails are required.

  • Strong ownership. You measure success by whether stakeholder work becomes easier, faster, and more reliable.

Bonus Points

  • Experience as a forward-deployed, solutions, or embedded engineer.

  • Prior BI or analytics engineering work with tools such as Sigma, Looker, dbt, or Tableau.

  • Familiarity with automation platforms such as Workato or n8n.

  • Experience building on MCP, agent frameworks, or LLM tool use.

  • Comfort in an early-stage environment with a high degree of ambiguity.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 -$260,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

You will own the technology strategy across PLM and adjacent engineering platforms, including the multi-year platform roadmap, build-vs-buy decisions, and integration architecture, working in close partnership with stakeholders across Engineering, Production, Procurement, Inventory, and Quality, and in tight coordination with the ERP team to keep the PLM-to-ERP data handoff reliable. The ideal candidate brings deep engineering-systems domain expertise, a strategic and process-oriented mindset, and the communication skills to translate engineering and manufacturing requirements into reliable, well-documented system solutions and to represent the platform to senior stakeholders.

You will join at a meaningful moment: as Crusoe stands up its PLM capability and scales manufacturing operations, this role will help build a well-governed foundation across engineering systems (product data, BOM accuracy, CAD integration, and change control) that supports that growth.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Administer the PLM platform end-to-end, including configuration, lifecycle and workflow states, user and license management, and access controls, maintaining availability, performance, and security for engineering and operations teams.

  • Own the item/part master and part-numbering framework within PLM (classification, attributes, and revision control) to ensure consistent, high-quality product data.

  • Configure and govern engineering and manufacturing bills of materials (EBOM/MBOM), including the EBOM-to-MBOM transformation and the structures that feed downstream ERP and production processes.

  • Administer engineering change management (ECR/ECN/ECO) workflows, configuring routing, approvals, and business rules to enforce disciplined, auditable change control.

  • Own and maintain the PLM-to-ERP integration for item, BOM, and change data, monitoring sync health, troubleshooting failures, and partnering with the ERP team on data-model alignment.

  • Own CAD data management and integration (mechanical and electrical) as part of the broader Engineering Systems domain, including CAD-to-PLM check-in/check-out, file relationships, and released-data control.

  • Manage release upgrades and patches per change management process, including feature impact assessment, regression testing coordination, and sandbox-to-production promotion.

  • Serve as the senior technology partner to Engineering, Production, Procurement, Inventory, Quality, and Accounting leadership, translating business and manufacturing strategy into Engineering Systems technology direction, and representing the platform in investment and prioritization discussions.

  • Own the PLM ticket queue within the ET team's Jira environment, tracking and resolving system issues, bugs, access requests, and change requests per established SLAs.

  • Own and drive the multi-year technology roadmap for the Engineering Systems domain, including build-vs-buy evaluations and platform modernization initiatives, and shape the Enterprise Technology team's broader project roadmap in Jira.

  • Develop and maintain system documentation for the PLM platform, capturing configurations, customizations, workflows, and integration designs.

  • Design and deliver training content and sessions for engineering and manufacturing users to foster adoption and proficiency.

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

jobs.title: Director, Finance - Real Estate Finance
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is the AI factory company, on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. Crusoe designs, builds, and operates vertically integrated AI infrastructure — from energy generation and land acquisition to AI-optimized data center campuses and Crusoe Cloud, its AI cloud platform. With a development pipeline exceeding tens of GWs across multiple U.S. campuses, real estate, land, and power siting decisions sit at the foundation of every project Crusoe brings to market.

What You'll Be Working On:

Crusoe is looking for a Director of Real Estate, Land & Leases Finance to own the financial due diligence, commercial structuring, and lifecycle management of land and real estate transactions underpinning Crusoe's data center campuses. This role is the finance owner for every site from initial acquisition or lease negotiation, ensuring each land or lease deal is financeable with corp dev, appropriately structured, and tracked against its underlying economics over time.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role suited to someone who can move fluidly between deal due diligence, financial modeling, negotiation support, and long-term asset tracking, in a company where land and power access are often the binding constraint on how fast infrastructure gets built.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Due Diligence

  • Lead financial due diligence on prospective land acquisitions, ground leases, and site control agreements — evaluating cost basis, tax implications, entitlement risk, and site-level economics.

  • Partner with Legal, Real Estate, and Power teams to assess title, easements, zoning, utility access, and environmental factors that affect deal viability and financing.

  • Build site-level financial models (acquisition cost, ground lease economics, property tax, incentive/abatement value) to support go/no-go TCO investment decisions.

  • Partner with Real Estate, Legal, HR and others on our international strategy.

Commercial Structure Support

  • Advise on and help negotiate land purchase agreements, ground leases, option agreements, and related real estate instruments, ensuring terms align with Crusoe's financing strategy and return requirements.

  • Structure deals to optimize for financeability — working with capital markets/project finance teams on how land ownership vs. lease structures affect debt sizing, credit packages, and investor requirements.

  • Support negotiation of economic development incentives, tax abatements, and PILOT (payment in lieu of taxes) agreements with local and state governments.

Lifecycle & Asset Management

  • Own ongoing financial tracking of each land/real estate asset across its lifecycle — from acquisition through construction, operations, and any eventual disposition or refinancing.

  • Maintain a portfolio-level view of land and lease obligations (payment schedules, escalators, renewal options, purchase options) and ensure accurate reflection in forecasts and reporting.

  • Partner with Accounting on proper treatment of land, leases (ASC 842), and related capital costs.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Serve as the finance point of contact for Real Estate, Development, Power, Legal, and Project Finance teams on all land- and lease-related matters.

  • Provide financial analysis and materials for board, investor, and lender due diligence related to real estate holdings and site pipeline.

  • Build scalable processes and tools as Crusoe's land portfolio grows across multiple simultaneous campus developments.

What We're Looking For:

  • 8+ years of experience in real estate finance, land acquisition, project finance, or corporate development, ideally within data centers, energy, industrial, or infrastructure sectors.

  • Demonstrated experience leading financial due diligence on land or real estate transactions, including modeling acquisition and lease economics.

  • Working knowledge of ground leases, purchase options, easements, and real estate/economic development incentive structures (tax abatements, PILOTs).

  • Understanding of how real estate/land structures interact with project financing (debt sizing, financeability, credit requirements) — ability to partner effectively with capital markets and structured finance teams.

  • Strong financial modeling and analytical skills; comfort building models from scratch under time pressure.

  • Experience managing a portfolio of assets over a multi-year lifecycle, not just single-transaction execution.

  • Excellent cross-functional collaboration and negotiation skills; able to work directly with Legal, Development, and external counterparties (landowners, utilities, municipalities).

  • Bachelor's degree required; MBA, JD, or equivalent a plus.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $235,000-$275,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

We're looking for a skilled Facilities Engineer to join our team at our Snyder, TX data center. In this role, you'll own the physical infrastructure that keeps our AI compute environment running at peak performance — from mechanical and electrical systems to HVAC, cooling, and building management. You'll partner closely with data center operations, construction, and energy teams to ensure our facility meets the demanding uptime and efficiency standards our customers depend on.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment and wants to be on the front lines of AI infrastructure.

What You'll Do

  • Own day-to-day operations, maintenance, and performance of all facility systems including electrical distribution (UPS, PDUs, switchgear, generators), HVAC, cooling/chiller plants, and building management systems (BMS)

  • Lead preventive and corrective maintenance programs; track and resolve facility work orders through completion

  • Monitor facility health via DCIM and BMS platforms; identify anomalies and respond rapidly to minimize downtime

  • Partner with construction and capital projects teams on facility expansions, retrofits, and equipment upgrades — including scope development, vendor coordination, and commissioning

  • Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal codes including NEC, OSHA, and applicable fire/life safety regulations

  • Maintain critical documentation including single-line diagrams, equipment logs, maintenance records, and SOPs

  • Coordinate with third-party contractors and vendors for specialized maintenance, inspections, and emergency response

  • Support capacity planning efforts by tracking power, cooling, and space utilization

  • Participate in the on-call rotation to support 24/7 critical facility operations

  • Champion a culture of safety by enforcing lock-out/tag-out (LOTO) procedures and other electrical safety protocols


What We're Looking For
Required

  • 3+ years of experience in facilities engineering, data center operations, or critical infrastructure environments

  • Hands-on knowledge of electrical systems (medium and low voltage), UPS/PDU systems, backup generators, and automatic transfer switches (ATS)

  • Experience with mechanical/cooling systems including CRAC/CRAH units, chilled water plants, cooling towers, and precision air systems

  • Familiarity with BMS/DCIM platforms for monitoring and control

  • Working knowledge of relevant codes and standards (NEC, NFPA, ASHRAE, OSHA)

  • Ability to read and interpret electrical and mechanical drawings, P&IDs, and equipment documentation

  • Strong troubleshooting skills and sound judgment under pressure

  • Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills


Preferred

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Facilities Management, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience)

  • Experience in hyperscale or colocation data center environments

  • Familiarity with DCIM tools (e.g., Sunbird, Nlyte, or similar)

  • OSHA 30 certification or equivalent safety training

  • Experience with commissioning (Cx) and integrated systems testing (IST)

  • Knowledge of energy efficiency practices in data center environments (PUE optimization, free cooling, etc.)

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

About the Role:

Crusoe's Recruiting and People Operations teams move fast - and pre-employment programs sit at the critical handoff point between an accepted offer and a confirmed start date. As the People Operations Manager, Pre-Employment Programs, you will own the orchestration of our pre-employment checks - including background checks, drug and alcohol tests, immigration checks, etc - ensuring each candidate moves smoothly and compliantly from offer to Day 1.

You will manage the vendor relationship with our pre-employment check vendor and act as the connective tissue between Recruiting and Onboarding Programs, translating today's ad hoc handoffs into a documented, auditable process with clear roles and responsibilities. This role also owns the administration of Crusoe's background screening and drug and alcohol testing programs, including DOT and non-DOT populations, ensuring programs are compliant, well-governed, and consistently executed as the company scales. This is a full-time, onsite position based in San Francisco, CA, for someone who wants to build the operational backbone behind a high-stakes, high-visibility process.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Vendor Relationship Management: Own the end-to-end relationship with Crusoe's background check and drug/alcohol testing vendor(s) - service performance, escalations, contract renewals, and issue resolution.

  • Pre-Employment Screening Orchestration: Serve as the operational owner of every pre-employment check, coordinating with Recruiting Operations on package selection, Immigration Operations for work authorization checks, and Onboarding Operations when start dates shift, and resolving exceptions before they delay a start date.

  • Drug & Alcohol Testing Program Administration: Oversee the administration of our pre-employment and support the administration of the random, post-accident, reasonable suspicion, and return-to-duty testing programs, including maintaining appropriate testing pools for DOT and non-DOT populations.

  • Process Design & Documentation: Design and document the end-to-end pre-employment process, including a clear RACI that defines roles and responsibilities across Recruiting, People Operations, and Onboarding.

  • Compliance & Adjudication Partnership: Partner with Compliance, Legal, and Employee Relations on adjudication decisions, job profile designation (safety-sensitive, DOT, PHMSA), and FCRA-compliant recordkeeping.

  • Cross-Functional Bridge: Serve as the connective tissue between Recruiting and Onboarding, ensuring handoffs are seamless and no candidate falls through the cracks.

  • Training & Enablement: Build training, documentation, and communications for Recruiting, People Operations, Onboarding, and hiring managers on pre-employment requirements and processes.

  • Continuous Improvement: Monitor turnaround times, error rates, and candidate experience data; identify opportunities to improve efficiency, compliance, and consistency as volume grows.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Pre-Employment Program Expertise: Experience administering background check and/or drug and alcohol testing programs, ideally within a high-growth or regulated environment.

  • Vendor Management: Proven ability to manage external vendor relationships, holding partners accountable to SLAs and resolving service issues.

  • Process Design: A track record of designing and documenting end-to-end processes, including defining roles and responsibilities across cross-functional teams.

  • Regulatory Fluency: Working knowledge of FCRA and DOT/PHMSA screening and testing requirements, and how they apply to job profile designation.

  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Experience partnering with Recruiting, Onboarding, Compliance, Legal, and Employee Relations to deliver a consistent candidate and employee experience.

  • Systems Proficiency: Comfort working within an ATS and HRIS (e.g. Ashby, Rippling) to track and manage screening statuses.

  • Operational Rigor: Meticulous attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple candidates and cases simultaneously without missing a deadline.

  • Education & Experience: Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience, with 5+ years of experience in People Operations, Recruiting Operations, or a related compliance function.

 

Bonus Points

  • Prior experience supporting a DOT-regulated workforce or other safety-sensitive population.

  • Experience building or significantly overhauling a pre-employment or background screening program from the ground up.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

     

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $130,000 - $160,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

 

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About This Role:

The Contracts Coordinator (IT, Network, & Cloud) serves as the vital bridge between technical engineering requirements and legal/financial compliance across Crusoe's rapidly scaling digital infrastructure. As we expand our high-performance cloud platforms and data center footprint, this role plays a pivotal purpose in structuring technology agreements, mitigating operational risk, and driving speed in vendor execution. You will act as the primary owner for technology contract workflows, ensuring our SaaS, IaaS, and network engagements align with Crusoe’s business goals and security standards.

The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented procurement or legal operations professional who thrives in a fast-paced technology environment and comfortably translates technical jargon from engineers into structured legal vehicles. Operating as a super-user of our Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) platform, Ironclad, you will manage end-to-end deal intake, draft crucial sub-agreements, and partner cross-functionally with Legal, IT, Security, and Strategic Sourcing.

This is a full-time & fully onsite at our Denver (Cherry Creek) office.


What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Contract Workflow & Ironclad Administration: Own the daily administration of Ironclad (CLM) and DocuSign, managing request creation, approval routings, parent-child document linking, naming conventions, signature execution, and dashboard reporting.

  • Contract Drafting & Negotiation: Structure and negotiate key transactional vehicles including Master Services Agreements (MSAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), Service Orders, Amendments, NDAs, Data Protection Addendums (DPAs), and SLAs across SaaS, IaaS, and Network categories.

  • Deal Assessment & Framework Selection: Act as the first checkpoint for technology procurement requests, evaluating deal scope, data exposure, and commercial risk to bucket transactions into the appropriate legal frameworks.

  • Security & Data Compliance Alignment: Partner directly with Information Security and Legal teams to ensure vendor contracts meet strict cybersecurity standards and comply with GDPR, CCPA, and SOC 2 Type II requirements.

  • Contractual Hierarchy & Metadata Governance: Maintain meticulous version control and parent-child document relationships across all agreement types in Ironclad to guarantee audit readiness and renewal visibility.

  • Procurement Enablement & Training: Drive adoption of intake tools (Ironclad, Jira, Coupa), providing guidance and training to internal procurement and business teams on contracting processes.

  • Vendor Consolidation & Optimization: Support category strategies by identifying overlapping software tools and working with sourcing leads to consolidate enterprise vendor bases.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Required Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Law, Information Technology, Supply Chain Management, or a related field.

  • Required Experience: 2 to 4 years of dedicated experience specifically in IT procurement, technology contract administration, or enterprise legal operations.

  • Technical Domain Knowledge: Solid understanding of SaaS, IaaS, Cloud hierarchy (Public vs. Private), virtualization, and data center network security protocols.

  • Contractual & Commercial Acumen: Direct experience negotiating and reviewing MSAs, SOWs, DPAs, and SLAs, with a firm grasp of Intellectual Property (IP) rights, indemnification, and liability limits.

  • CLM & Procurement Systems Mastery: Hands-on proficiency using contract lifecycle management tools like Ironclad and DocuSign, alongside familiarity with Jira, Coupa, or modern ERP platforms.

  • Cross-Functional Communication: Proven ability to translate complex engineering and IT requirements into structured, executive-ready business and contract terms.

Bonus Points:

  • Professional Certifications: Certified Commercial Contracts Manager (CCCM), Certified Professional Contract Manager (CPCM), or foundational cloud certifications such as AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner.

  • Hyperscale / Infrastructure Background: Prior experience in data center operations, semiconductor, hyperscale cloud, or high-growth hardware/tech manufacturing environments.

  • Process Optimization Experience: Track record of driving measurable contract cycle time reductions or building custom Ironclad workflow templates.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $75,000 - $90,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

(#INDCORP)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.
