jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Crusoe is seeking a Manufacturing Quality Manager to oversee Manufacturing Quality across multiple AI data center infrastructure production sites. Reporting directly to the Director of Quality, this role leads team management, quality assurance, process controls, electrical/mechanical product quality, QMS execution, regulatory compliance, testing, and continuous improvement across our facilities.

Crusoe Quality Org Leadership Philosophy: The ideal candidate does not view Manufacturing Quality as simply an inspection organization. We are looking for a leader who can build a culture where Quality is designed into the product → engineered into the manufacturing process → verified through robust testing → controlled through Statistical Process Controls (SPC) → measured through data → continuously improved with QMS discipline.

The successful candidate will demonstrate equal proficiency in conducting shop-floor oversight, evaluating electrical testing procedures, reviewing weld integrity with Certified Welding Inspectors, and collaborating with Engineering on Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) initiatives. Furthermore, this leader must maintain rigorous audit readiness across UL compliance, QMS, ISO, and safety standards, perform thorough quality data analytics, and effectively communicate manufacturing and quality risks to executive leadership.

This strategic role demands deep expertise in electromechanical assembly, production processes, and QMS. Operating across Manufacturing, QMS, Engineering, and Regulatory Compliance, the Manager will build and guide high-performing Quality teams to foster a rigorous Quality mindset across all Crusoe sites. This position requires approximately 30% to 40% travel among manufacturing facilities, vendor sites, and client locations.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Multi-Site Manufacturing Quality Leadership: Direct quality operations across multiple Crusoe facilities. Define inspection standards and acceptance criteria, lead multi-site containment efforts with urgency, establish staffing requirements, partner with production leadership, coach quality staff, and build scalable quality systems to support rapid growth while owning QMS compliance and discipline.

  • Mechanical Quality Assurance: Provide technical oversight for mechanical fabrication, structural assemblies, sheet metal, welding/welded structures, CWI requirements, dimensional inspection, GD&T, surface coatings/paints, fastening/torque control, and enclosure assembly quality.

  • Electrical Quality Assurance: Direct technical oversight for switchgear, switchboards, breakers, electrical cabinets, busbars, industrial control equipment, wiring/harnessing, electrical safety testing, insulation/dielectric testing, hi-pot testing, continuity/grounding, and electrical IPQC.

  • Product Requirements Compliance & Traceability: Lead QA activities to ensure full compliance with UL 891, UL 508, NRTL, NETA ATS-2025, customer, regulatory, and product certification standards across electrical equipment, assemblies, and infrastructure.

  • Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) & Factory Witness Testing (FWT): Lead Quality oversight for factory testing and customer/certification witness activities, including pre-FAT readiness reviews, test procedure approvals, calibration verification, test result traceability, defect resolution, and witness inspections. Ensure manufacturing sites are fully prepared prior to customer/certification execution.

  • Product Change Management: Ensure all modifications to product designs and Bills of Materials (BOM) are formally communicated to Quality Assurance teams, systematically updating corresponding inspection protocols and acceptance criteria.

  • Manufacturing Process Quality & Quality Engineering: Partner with Manufacturing and Engineering to implement robust process controls (PFMEA, Control Plans, Process Flow Diagrams, SPC, MSA/Gage R&R, Poka-Yoke, standardized work, FAI, layered audits) to drive first-pass yield, reduce scrap/rework, and minimize process variation.

  • QMS Compliance & Audit Readiness: Oversee manufacturing quality problem-solving initiatives across teams. Maintain constant audit readiness for internal, customer, ISO 9001:2026, and certification audits. Oversee corrective actions from audit findings, manage quality records, and serve as the liaison between Manufacturing Quality and the enterprise QMS organization.

  • Structured Problem Solving & CAPA: Lead and coach personnel through core quality and risk management methodologies, including CAPA, NCR, RCA, 8D, SCAR, containment, deviation management, and effectiveness verification to eliminate repeat issues.

  • Quality Assurance Data Management: Establish cross-site quality metrics and dashboards tracking First Pass Yield, Defect PPM, NCR/Rework/Scrap rates, escapes, COPQ, FAT/FWT performance, and audit findings to pinpoint systemic trends and execute targeted operational improvements.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration (Engineering & Supply Chain): Partner with Design, Manufacturing Engineering, and NPI teams on DFM/Quality reviews, CTQ identification, GD&T, change control, and converting compliance rules into factory controls. Collaborate with Supplier Quality and Procurement on supplier qualification, subcontractor quality, incoming requirements, and risk escalation.

  • People Leadership & Team Development: Build and direct high-performing multi-site Quality teams. Align staffing plans with manufacturing volume, define competencies and career paths, enable cross-training between mechanical and electrical teams, cultivate technical SMEs, and foster an organizational culture centered on accountability and continuous improvement.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Professional Experience: 6-10 years of progressive experience in Manufacturing Quality, Quality Engineering, Quality Assurance, Electrical Quality, Mechanical Quality, or related disciplines. In addition, 2+ years experience leading Quality organizations in complex manufacturing environments.

  • Multi-Site Leadership Track Record: Demonstrated people-management experience leading cross-functional Quality teams across multiple manufacturing facilities.

  • Dual-Domain Expertise (Electrical & Mechanical): Proven experience supporting both electrical hardware (switchboards, switchgear, breakers, industrial controls) and mechanical hardware (sheet metal fabrication, structural welding, enclosures, coatings).

  • Testing & Inspection Mastery: Strong experience with FAT, FWT, electrical testing (hi-pot, dielectric, continuity), and end-to-end manufacturing inspection (IQC, IPQC, OQC).

  • Regulatory & Compliance Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of UL compliance and certification requirements, with experience working with external auditors, certification bodies, customers, and regulatory organizations.

  • Welding Process Oversight: Working knowledge of welding inspection and CWI-controlled process management.

  • Root Cause & RCA Methodologies: Demonstrated mastery of CAPA, RCA, SCAR, 8D, NCR, and structured problem-solving methodologies.

  • Quality Management Systems: Deep knowledge of QMS principles, ISO auditing, quality data management, and manufacturing quality controls.

  • Cross-Functional Influence: Proven track record of influencing and collaborating across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Executive leadership.

  • Travel Flexibility: Ability and willingness to travel 30% to 40% across manufacturing facilities, vendor locations, and client sites.

  • Safety and Compliance: Position is designated a safety-sensitive position located in safety-sensitive facilities. Mandatory participation in company safety, background check, drug, and alcohol programs is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Quality Engineering, or related technical discipline; Master's degree preferred.

  • Professional Certifications: ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or Certified Quality Manager (CQM).

  • Process Excellence: Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt certification.

  • Welding Credentials: AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) designation or formal NDE training.

  • Standards & Certifications Expertise: Specific exposure to UL 891, UL 508, NRTL certification programs, or NETA ATS specifications.

  • Data & Software Systems: Experience with enterprise QMS software platforms, QMS/ERP/MES integrations, and advanced quality data analytics.

  • Industry Experience: Experience scaling quality organizations within mission-critical infrastructure, data centers, power distribution, switchgear, or industrial controls industries.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $160,000 - $180,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Staff Applied AI Inference Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role

You will spend your time making large language models run faster, cheaper, and more reliably in production. That means owning the inference stack end to end: profiling where time and cost go, bringing modern optimization techniques into real deployments, and getting deep into the serving code when the defaults are not good enough. This is core systems and performance work on some of the most demanding models in use today.

 

The work is applied, not academic. The optimizations you build land in real customer deployments, each with its own models, traffic patterns, latency targets, and cost constraints. So while performance is the heart of the role, you will also work directly with customer engineering teams to tailor deployments to their needs, take a workload from an early proof of concept to a fully monitored production service, and make sure the gains you engineer actually show up for the people running the workload.

 

To set expectations clearly, this is a hands-on engineering role built around coding, profiling, and low-level optimization. It also carries a customer-facing side, along with elements of product and technical solutions work, because that is where the performance work gets proven.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Bring current inference techniques into production and refine them.

  • Design and optimize serving architectures, including prefill and decode disaggregation, request routing, and related approaches.

  • Work down into the serving stack, from frameworks like vLLM and SGLang to the CUDA kernels underneath, profiling and running in-depth analysis to find and fix performance problems.

  • Adapt and scale optimization methods across many kinds of ML models, with an emphasis on large language models.

  • Profile and tune deployments against clear targets for latency, throughput, and cost, and keep them dependable under real traffic.

  • Tailor deployments to each customer's models and constraints, partnering with their engineering teams to move a workload from an early proof of concept through to a live, well-monitored production service.

  • Build and support the software and product features around the inference stack in a production setting, using one or more general-purpose languages, with Python preferred given how central it is to ML work.

  • Experiment quickly: take fuzzy goals, shape them into clear specs and focused proofs of concept, run fast experiments to find what works, and ship well-tested results without delay.

  • Own delivery end to end, from the first experiment through to the optimization running in production, keeping the underlying performance goals, clear specs, and follow-through front of mind, and drafting features and product requirement documents together with other engineering and product teams.

  • Work through ambiguity and make sound calls on tradeoffs and tooling, steering away from complexity that is not needed.

  • Take real pride and ownership in your work, hold yourself accountable, and look for the same from the people around you.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • A Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.

  • Hands-on experience shipping code in production with one or more general-purpose languages, such as Python or C++, with a strong preference for Python.

  • Familiarity with methods for optimizing LLMs for high throughput / low latency inference.

  • Comfort with modern LLM serving frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang, and with profiling and analyzing performance down to the kernel level.

  • A firm grasp of how GPUs are built and how they behave.

  • Clear interest and hands-on experience with large language models.

  • A working knowledge of AI/ML pipelines and the full path of developing and deploying ML models.

  • Strong communication skills, particularly when explaining hard technical topics to customers and teammates.

 

Bonus points:

  • A track record of making software systems run faster, especially for large language models.

  • Experience with CUDA or comparable technologies.

  • A strong command of software engineering fundamentals, with a record of building and shipping AI/ML inference systems.

  • Experience with Docker and Kubernetes.

  • Prior work building or tuning AI/ML projects, particularly in a customer-facing setting.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 - $260,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

Crusoe's Managed AI Services portfolio launched in late 2025 and is scaling fast: We have already secured triple-digit $M ARR commitments from customers. The portfolio spans Managed Inference (Serverless, Self-Deployed and Tailored Deployment), Serverless Fine Tuning, with Serverless Reinforcement Learning and Agent Sandbox GA landing in H2 2026. As VP of Product Management, you will own the vision, strategy, execution and roadmap for this business, reporting to the SVP of Product Management and partnering directly with the VP Engineering for Managed AI Services. You will lead the portfolio as a business and via strong cross-functional partnerships, anchored in the rise of open models and Crusoe's vertically integrated cloud strategy from electrons to tokens.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Define the long-term vision, strategy and roadmap for the Managed AI Services portfolio, aligned to customer needs, company goals, market trends and GTM strategy

  • Build, lead and mentor a team of product managers, owning their performance and development

  • Partner with engineering, technical program management, product partnerships, marketing, customer success and sales to define requirements, prioritize features and drive the lifecycle from concept through launch and adoption at scale

  • Own the business metrics for the portfolio, including usage, reliability and production KPIs, pipeline, revenue, gross margin and customer satisfaction, and use that data to drive decisions

  • Shape go-to-market with sales, marketing and customer success, including positioning, messaging, pricing, routes-to-market and partnerships

  • Build relationships with key customers, ecosystem partners and GTM partners, translating their feedback into product improvements and working alongside the Director of Product Partnerships on partnership and M&A opportunities

  • Track the Managed AI competitive landscape and emerging technologies to inform strategy and surface new opportunities

  • Proactively identify and resolve technical and commercial risks, infrastructure bottlenecks and scaling challenges, and manage product budgets and resources against business goals

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Proven product management track record with AI/ML services, including experience building AI managed services and scaling them from scratch

  • First-hand experience with AI managed services such as inference, tuning, reinforcement learning and agent sandboxes, along with the observability and evaluation practices that support them

  • Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure technologies and trends, ideally as a builder of planet-scale cloud products at a hyperscaler, neocloud or specialized inference provider

  • Experience managing and launching technical products and features for AI-native, digital-native and enterprise customers

  • Proven experience building, leading and mentoring product management teams

  • Strategic leadership: the ability to set a clear vision, make informed decisions with incomplete information, and guide a cross-functional team toward market awareness, adoption, revenue and gross margin goals

  • Analytical rigor: comfort interpreting complex market, customer and production data to drive product strategy

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to present technical concepts, connect them to business outcomes and build consensus across diverse stakeholders

  • Hands-on use of AI tools to accelerate the product management craft

 

Bonus Points

  • Experience leading a technical customer-facing team or operating an AI managed service from the customer or user side

  • Engineering background prior to moving into product management

  • Experience with open model ecosystems and the fine-tuning and inference optimization workflows enterprises use to adapt models to their data

  • Familiarity with Agile and Lean product management methodologies

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $345,000 – $385,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

About This Role:

Reporting to the Chief Accounting Officer, the Head of Internal Audit will play a critical role in building a best-in-class internal audit function that directly supports Crusoe’s strategic objectives. This role serves as the strategic architect of our risk management framework.

We are looking for a high-integrity leader who can balance rigorous compliance with a forward-thinking, consultative approach to business processes. You will lead the internal audit function to ensure our financial, operational, and IT controls are robust, while providing the Executive Team and the Board with the insights needed to navigate a complex regulatory landscape.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Strategic Oversight: Lead the execution of the annual audit plan across corporate shared services, ensuring alignment with business priorities.

  • Audit Lifecycle Management: Oversee all phases of the audit lifecycle, including risk assessment, planning, fieldwork, reporting, and follow-up.

  • Advisory & Assurance: Guide teams delivering assurance and advisory engagements; review and approve audit planning, testing, and documentation for quality and consistency.

  • Risk Mitigation: Assess enterprise and business risks and recommend practical, effective mitigation strategies to senior leadership.

  • Stakeholder Partnership: Partner with leaders across the organization to develop action plans and drive the timely closure of audit findings.

  • Compliance & External Support: Oversee external audit assist testing, including conclusions and remediation support when required.

  • Operational Evolution: Provide ongoing audit and risk advisory guidance as Crusoe’s products, operations, and regulations evolve.

  • Resource Management: Manage budgets, timelines, and resource allocation to meet all audit commitments.

  • Team Development: Coach, mentor, and develop audit leaders and team members while fostering a culture of trust and professional growth.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or equivalent experience.

  • Experience: 10+ years of accounting and/or audit experience, with a proven track record of leading complex audit engagements from planning through closure.

  • Methodological Expertise: Strong knowledge of risk management frameworks and internal audit methodologies.

  • Relationship Building: Proven ability to build collaborative relationships across functions and influence change through audit insights.

  • Communication: Clear and effective written and verbal communication skills; comfort delivering complex or difficult messages to senior leaders.

  • Leadership: Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities under tight timelines.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • CPA, CIA, or similar professional certification.

  • Public accounting experience (Big 4 or similar).

  • Experience leading assurance and advisory work at the enterprise level.

  • Proven experience managing and developing other managers.

  • Ability to translate technical risk into clear, actionable business guidance.

What You’ll Be Working On:

 - Audit Lifecycle Management: Oversee all phases of the audit lifecycle, including risk assessment, planning, fieldwork, reporting, and follow-up.

 - Advisory & Assurance: Guide teams delivering assurance and advisory engagements; review and approve audit planning, testing, and documentation for quality and consistency.

 - Experience: 10+ years of accounting and/or audit experience, with a proven track record of leading complex audit engagements from planning through closure.

 - Relationship Building: Proven ability to build collaborative relationships across functions and influence change through audit insights.

 - Communication: Clear and effective written and verbal communication skills; comfort delivering complex or difficult messages to senior leaders.

 - Leadership: Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities under tight timelines.

 - Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

 - CPA, CIA, or similar professional certification.

 - Public accounting experience (Big 4 or similar).

 - Experience leading assurance and advisory work at the enterprise level.

 - Proven experience managing and developing other managers.

 - Ability to translate technical risk into clear, actionable business guidance.



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off & paid holidays

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

jobs.title: Manager, Modular Building Programs
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Join our team as the Manager of Modular Building Programs and take ownership of the project management function for our entire modular product sector including Spark Modular Data Center units and Power Distribution Center (PDC) buildings. You will own the portfolio schedule, the delivery commitment to hyperscale customers, and the growth of the project managers executing the work.

This is a working leadership role. You'll manage a small team of project managers while personally carrying the hardest programs, the toughest customer conversations, and the cross-functional escalations your team cannot resolve on their own. You are the connective tissue between the PMO, the plant floor, Engineering, and Supply Chain for everything modular.

Your work directly impacts our ability to deploy modular data center buildings to compute from sustainable, renewable and/or stranded energy sources. Success here is measured in throughput and predictability: more units out the door, on the date we committed, at the margin we quoted.

We are seeking an experienced people leader with a proven background in construction, engineering, and/or manufacturing, a strategic mindset, and the operational discipline to scale a product line through rapid growth. This is a full-time position. (#INDMFG)

 

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Modular Portfolio Ownership: Own the consolidated schedule across Spark MDC and PDC building programs, including capacity with Production planning and plant operations.

  • Team Leadership and Mentorship: Lead, coach, and develop a team of project managers. Set the standard for schedule quality, change discipline, cost accuracy, and customer communication — and hold the team to it.

  • Customer Relationship Management and Development: Serve as the senior escalation point for modular customers, including executive-level schedule impact and change negotiation discussions. Become the go-to solution for customer needs and build strong, repeatable relationships that outlast any single program.

  • Capacity and Production Planning: Partner with Manufacturing Operations & Production Planning on line loading, takt-time alignment, labor forecasting, and bottleneck resolution across the modular build area.

  • Strategic Change & Risk Management: Govern the engineering change process for modular products. Enforce impact analysis, pricing discipline, and customer approval before anything reaches the floor. Maintain the portfolio risk register and drive mitigation across engineering, supply chain, and production constraints.

  • Program Economics and Target Accountability: Set the margin and cost targets for each modular program at baseline, and own delivery against them through close-out. Partner with Project Controls in a standing monthly economics review where you jointly validate the cost-to-complete position — Project Controls owns the model, you own the operational assumptions inside it: hours remaining, change order capture, schedule position, and material exposure. Sign the forecast you submit. When a program drifts off target, bring the variance, the root cause, and a recovery plan to the same review rather than waiting for it to surface in the roll-up.

  • Process Improvement & Standardization: Drive standardization across configurations — build repeatable schedule templates, WBS structures, budget templates and close-out packages that reduce per-unit PM overhead.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Sales and Estimating during pursuit and handoff to validate schedule feasibility, scope delineation, and manufacturability before commitments are made.

  • Executive Reporting and Dashboard Ownership: Own the modular executive dashboard — throughput, on-time delivery, backlog, and margin across Spark MDC and PDC programs. Your project managers complete the project-level inputs; you own the dashboard’s accuracy, its cadence, and the story it tells to leadership. Represent modular products in PMO-wide governance including stage gates and post-mortem review, and enable the team to represent individual projects reporting upwards to senior and executive leadership.

  • Schedule Quality Assurance: Perform logic checks, float analysis, critical path validation, and baseline change control on program schedules — audit and correct, not merely report.

 

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Industry Experience — Modular Building Manufacturing or Data Center Construction: Experience delivering multi-disciplinary products (electrical, HVAC, structural, enclosure/building envelope). Modular Building Manufacturing and/or Data Center Construction experience is strongly preferred.

  • Project Management Experience: Minimum of 8+ years managing projects within the electrical equipment, construction, engineering and/or manufacturing industry, including ETO or highly engineered production.

  • People Leadership: 3+ years of direct leadership of project managers or equivalent technical staff, with a track record of developing them.

  • Engineering & Constructability Competency: Ability to interpret electrical, mechanical, and structural engineering design drawings, and to lead a team that does the same. We are looking for a leader who can review a design package from a “we have to build this” perspective and give our engineering group productive, risk-based feedback before release.

  • Bachelor of Science: BS in Business, Engineering, Construction Management. Closely related fields will be considered.

  • Portfolio Accountability: Demonstrated ownership of a multi-project manufacturing or construction portfolio with accountability for on-time delivery and margin performance.

  • Complex Change Leadership & Process Ownership: Proven ability to lead the adoption of dynamic change management practices across Engineering, Manufacturing, and Procurement.

  • Schedule Development & Management: Proficient in scheduling using waterfall methodologies. Proficient with programs such as Smartsheet, MS Project, Monday.com or Primavera P6.

  • Cost Management: Ability to forecast and build cost budgets across a portfolio, and manage those budgets through completion.

  • Technical Proficiency: Proficiency in Google Suite and Microsoft Office. Experience with manufacturing ERP systems like SAP or Visual; experience with Acumatica is preferred.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Direct expertise in managing change on first-of-a-kind (FOAK) manufacturing programs or highly complex projects, maintaining positive client relationships throughout periods of significant project evolution.

  • Experience scaling a modular or prefabricated product line through rapid volume growth.

  • Background spanning both field construction and factory manufacturing.

  • Familiarity with industrialized building regulatory programs and third-party inspection regimes.

  • Experience implementing PMO standards, SOPs, or stage-gate governance in a manufacturing organization.

  • PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000 -$180,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Associate Construction Engineer - Power Infrastructure
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Crusoe is seeking an Associate Construction Engineer to join our Project Execution team, supporting the field execution of large-scale power generation projects for AI data center infrastructure. This role works alongside and under the direction of a senior Construction Engineer, developing the field engineering skills, construction knowledge, and technical judgment required to independently own a project's field execution scope.

You will be an active presence on construction sites — supporting inspection activities, managing field documentation, tracking RFIs and submittals, and building the cross-discipline construction knowledge that defines this career path. During construction and commissioning phases, this position requires significant site presence, requiring resident assignment. During engineering and procurement phases, site travel is limited to vendor and site visits.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Field Engineering & Site Coordination: Support the field engineering team on active power generation construction sites, assisting with day-to-day inspection, documentation, and construction coordination activities under the direction of a senior Construction Engineer.

  • Technical Submittals & RFI Management: Assist with the review of contractor and vendor submittals, RFIs, and Field Engineering Directives (FEDs); learn to coordinate engineering responses with the project engineering team.

  • Execution Plan Review: Support the review of construction execution planning documents — including lift plans, flush plans, hydro plans, purge plans, and pre-commissioning procedures — developing technical judgment for acceptance criteria.

  • Milestone & Schedule Tracking: Assist with tracking and documenting construction progress against the project schedule and milestones; maintain open items logs, punch list status, and change order tracking.

  • Quality & Workmanship Inspections: Conduct field inspections of contractor workmanship and adherence to project specifications, drawings, and applicable codes; document findings and escalate non-conformances to the senior Construction Engineer.

  • Turnover & Mechanical Completion Packages: Support the development and management of punch lists, mechanical completion packages, and system turnover packages under senior Construction Engineer direction.

  • Commissioning & Startup Support: Assist with commissioning and startup activities, including supporting functional tests, loop checks, and performance verification activities.

  • Field Documentation & As-Builts: Maintain daily field reports, inspection records, and project documentation; capture as-built redlines and field changes for incorporation into the record document set.

  • Permitting & HSE Compliance: Coordinate work permit tracking and support site safety program compliance in collaboration with the site HSE representative.

  • Standards & Process Development: Contribute to the development of engineering, construction, and commissioning standards and procedures as directed.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Educational Foundation: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Chemical, or Construction Engineering, or a related field.

  • Professional Experience: 2+ years of field engineering, construction management, or inspection experience on power generation, oil & gas, or heavy industrial projects.

  • Cross-Discipline Field Knowledge: Developing hands-on knowledge of construction and commissioning activities across mechanical and/or electrical systems in an industrial or power generation environment.

  • Civil & Concrete Foundations: Foundational knowledge of concrete construction, including foundations, rebar placement, and formwork.

  • Structural Steel Construction: Foundational knowledge of structural steel erection, including sequencing, connections, and field inspection.

  • Electrical Power Systems: Foundational knowledge of electrical power systems installation, including conduit, cable tray, pulling, terminations, and grounding.

  • Piping & Mechanical Systems: Foundational knowledge of piping system construction, including pipe supports, welding inspection, pressure testing, and system cleanliness requirements.

  • Power Generation Assets: Foundational knowledge of power generation equipment and systems, including gas turbines, reciprocating engines, generators, switchgear, and auxiliary systems.

  • Codes & Industry Standards: Familiarity with relevant industry codes and standards (e.g., NFPA 70, ASME B31.1/B31.3/B31.8, NEC, ANSI/IEEE) and their practical application in the field.

  • Technical Document Review: Experience supporting the review of contractor submittals, RFIs, and construction execution documents.

  • Project Scheduling: Familiarity with scheduling software (Primavera P6, MS Project, or equivalent); ability to read and interpret project schedules.

  • Documentation & Detail Orientation: Strong organizational skills and attention to detail — able to maintain accurate field documentation, inspection records, and punch list logs in a fast-moving construction environment.

  • Site Assignment & Travel: Ability to perform extended site assignments, including weekly travel to remote project sites or resident assignment during peak construction and commissioning phases.

  • Safety & Compliance: This position is designated safety-sensitive and is located in safety-sensitive facilities. Mandatory participation in company drug, alcohol, and safety programs is required. Candidates must be able to pass a background check.

  • Physical Demands: Ability to traverse uneven terrain and active construction sites, climb ladders, scaffolding, and stairs, lift moderate loads (up to 40 lbs), and work outdoors for extended periods in varying weather conditions (including high heat, cold, rain, and snow) while wearing appropriate PPE.

Bonus Points:

  • Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification or actively pursuing professional engineering licensure (FE/PE).

  • Prior experience supporting data center power infrastructure or modular substation execution.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $100,000 - $115,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDDIG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Compute Cloud
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

As the Director of Engineering - Cloud Compute, you will play a pivotal role in building our foundational IaaS offerings and accelerate the development of our carbon-reducing, AI focused cloud platform. Leveraging your extensive experience in cloud computing, you will lead complex engineering initiatives, mentor engineers, and collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to deliver scalable and reliable cloud compute solutions. Our customers include rapidly growing AI companies and enterprise AI teams who use our high performance GPU compute products with VPC and cluster networking technology. We’re now adding broad new compute and virtualization capabilities to meet the needs of our growing customer base.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Serve as a team lead for cloud compute engineering at Crusoe Cloud, collaborating with leadership to define and implement the long-term road map and strategy for the team

  • Guide the engineering team through architecture decisions, design processes, design reviews, code reviews, and implementation tasks

  • Scale the team, including managing engineer onboarding, growing or hiring managers, and implementing team and org processes.

  • Stay aware of the latest trends and techniques in cloud software, incorporating these insights to maintain Crusoe’s market-leading offerings

  • Drive the hiring process to attract top talent, and implement strategies to retain and develop these professionals

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 7+ years of engineering management experience, 10+ years of experience working in software engineering

  • In-depth understanding of Compute products (CPU, GPU, ASIC accelerators) and how customers consume them

  • Understanding of key hypervisors and virtualization technologies (eg KVM, VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V) and how they enable cloud computing.

  • Familiarity with AI/ML workloads and how they drive compute requirements for the cloud data center.

  • Proven experience in building and maintaining scalable and highly available fault-tolerant distributed systems and application architectures

  • Knowledge of professional software engineering practices and best practices for the full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills

 

Bonus Points

  • Proven track record of operating production infrastructure to strict SLOs and SLAs, leveraging fleet-wide observability and monitoring to drive reliability, optimization, and capacity planning

  • Deep expertise in Linux environments, configuration management, and modern deployment automation to ensure safe, scalable rollouts across large-scale compute fleets

  • Demonstrated leadership in ambiguous, fast-moving environments,bringing structure, clarity, and cross-functional alignment during periods of rapid organizational growth

  • Active open-source or upstream contributions to cloud infrastructure, containerization, or virtualization technologies (e.g., KVM, QEMU, containerd, Kubernetes)

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $285,000 - 335,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.title: Senior Workplace Manager, Colocation & Spark
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We're looking for a Senior Workplace Manager to own the site and employee experience across our growing network of Spark and colocation data center sites. These are remote workplaces without a coordinator on the ground, so you'll build the standards, systems, and vendor relationships that keep sites running and employees supported without daily physical presence.

This role partners closely with the broader workplace team, Construction, Facilities, Operations, and Security.

This is a full-time role requiring candidates to work onsite in our offices in Dallas, TX or Denver, CO. It also involves regular travel (up to 50%, including international) for site mobilizations and quality control visits.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Lead the buildout of the Colocation & Spark workplace program, partnering on standards, service levels, and mobilization playbooks so each new site opens ready and on a repeatable model, rather than one at a time from scratch

  • Own day-to-day workplace operations across the portfolio, establishing the systems, reporting, and remote-monitoring cadence that keep sites functional and issues visible without a coordinator physically on-site

  • Manage vendor and, for colocation sites, landlord relationships, serving as the primary point of contact for facilities, maintenance, service issues, and contract performance, with clear escalation paths for emergencies

  • Own the workplace budget across the portfolio, including forecasting, vendor spend, and cost optimization that doesn't compromise the employee experience

  • Deliver a strong site and employee experience for dispersed teams at each location, including planning your own travel around mobilizations, executive visits, and periodic quality checks

  • Bring Crusoe's broader People and Workplace strategy to a distributed footprint, adapting programs and communications built for large single offices to remote teams

  • Ensure a hospitality-caliber visitor experience at every site: even without being there day-to-day, make sure executive visits, guests, and new hires are met with the same warmth and polish as any Crusoe office, orchestrated through site vendors, advance planning, and clear on-the-ground points of contact

  • Own food, beverage, and office amenities programs across the portfolio, managing snack and catering vendors remotely and building events and moments of connection for distributed teams

  • Hire, manage, and develop the Colocation & Spark Workplace Coordinator team as it grows both domestically and internationally, setting priorities and a consistent standard of service across sites

  • Travel to sites to support executive, VIP, and prospective client visits, coordinating logistics and on-the-ground details in advance so tours run smoothly and reflect well on Crusoe

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 7+ years of experience in workplace, facilities, or site operations, spanning multiple locations rather than a single office, and ideally at a fast-growing company

  • Experience building a program, standard, or playbook without an established precedent to follow

  • Proven experience managing budgets, vendor contracts, and landlord or building-management relationships

  • Experience managing and developing direct reports, with a focus on accountability and service, including comfort managing a team spread across multiple countries and time zones

  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, comfortable partnering across People, Construction, Facilities, Operations, IT, and Security

  • Comfortable substituting systems and remote monitoring for daily physical presence, with sound judgment on when a problem needs a site visit

  • Highly organized and comfortable operating independently, solving problems, and building structure in an environment without established playbooks

  • A hands-on operator who takes ownership and is motivated by building something from the ground up

  • Willing and able to travel regularly for mobilizations and site visits

 

Bonus Points

  • Experience in data center environments

  • Familiarity with remote-monitoring or ticketing systems for facilities and workplace operations

  • Experience scaling a function during a period of fast geographic growth

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

     

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $140,000 - $170,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

 

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Network Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Network Engineer to support the design, deployment, and ongoing operation of our corporate network infrastructure across offices, warehouses, and data centers. This role is ideal for an engineer who has moved beyond foundational networking and is ready to take ownership of medium-to-large network projects while continuing to grow toward an intermediate or advanced-level role.

You'll work closely with IT Operations, Systems Engineering, Security, and Project Management teams to ensure reliable, secure, and scalable network solutions across all corporate locations, with a clear path toward Senior Network Engineer responsibilities as you grow in the role.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Design, implement, and support network infrastructure across offices, warehouses, and datacenters: full site-build lifecycle (topology, IP/VLAN/subnet design, wireless planning, redundancy/failover), BOMs, expansions, migrations, and refreshes.

  • Administer, monitor, and troubleshoot the full network stack (firewalls, switches, wireless), serving as an escalation point for complex issues, driving root cause analysis, and participating in on-call/after-hours support.

  • Ensure configurations align with security policies, support audits and vulnerability remediation, and assist with security system integrations (cameras, access control).

  • Configure SaaS integrations (SSO, SCIM, OIDC, OAuth — primarily Okta) and build automations/workflows using low-code/API tools like Workato and Postman, in partnership with IT and Security.

  • Bring an automation-first mindset: proactively identifying ways to reduce manual work and staying current on AI-assisted tools for IT infrastructure and ops.

  • Maintain network documentation (diagrams, IP schemas, VLAN assignments, rack elevations, port maps) and contribute to standardizing designs and deployment patterns.

  • Collaborate with Senior Network Architect and Engineers on complex initiatives, liaise with vendors/ISPs/carriers on circuit turn-ups, and mentor Network Analysts.

  • Travel up to 20% may be required to support site deployments.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience as a Network Engineer in office, warehouse, or datacenter environments.

  • Strong understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, and routing.

  • Solid knowledge of Layer 2 and Layer 3 networking protocols.

  • Experience with wired and wireless enterprise networks.

  • Practical experience with circuit provisioning and carrier management.

  • Ability to analyze and troubleshoot network connectivity issues efficiently using Wireshark.

  • Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, and technical documentation skills.

  • Comfortable owning network components or projects end-to-end.

  • Ability to work effectively across IT, Security, and Operations teams and explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences.

  • A growth mindset: eager to learn new platforms and progress toward senior-level responsibilities.

  • Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.

Bonus Points

  • Cisco Meraki experience (firewall, switching, wireless).

  • CCNA or equivalent certification.

  • Experience with WAN technologies (MPLS, DIA, SD-WAN), VPNs, and monitoring tools.

  • Familiarity with Lucid, Jira, IAM platforms (e.g., Okta, including SSO/SCIM/OIDC), low-code automation tools (e.g., Workato, Postman), and AI-assisted workflows.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $125,000 -$147,500 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Join our team as the Manager of Power Distribution Programs and take ownership of the project management function for our entire Switchboards & Switchgear sector — low voltage, medium voltage, skid integration, and custom switchboard assemblies. You will own portfolio delivery performance, margin, and the development of the project management team beneath you.

Power Distribution is the highest-volume manufacturing sector in the business and the one under the most acute growth pressure. Hyperscale demand for switchgear and PDC-mounted distribution is outrunning conventional lead times, and the sector is simultaneously expanding into medium voltage. This role must deliver current commitments while building the management structure to absorb what is coming.

This is a working leadership role. You'll manage project managers, own the portfolio, and personally carry the most sensitive customer programs. Your work directly impacts our ability to energize compute from sustainable, renewable and/or stranded energy sources.

We are seeking an experienced people leader with a proven background in electrical equipment or comparable ETO manufacturing, a strategic mindset, and the operational discipline to scale through rapid growth. This is a full-time position. (#INDMFG)

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Power Distribution Portfolio Ownership: Own the consolidated schedule across LV switchboard, MV switchgear, MV PDC, and skid integration programs.

  • Team Leadership and Mentorship: Lead and develop a team of project managers, setting the standard for schedule discipline, submittal management, change capture, cost accuracy, and customer communication.

  • Customer and Stakeholder Management: Serve as senior escalation for Power Distribution customers, including executive-level schedule impact, change negotiation, and recovery planning.

  • Capacity and Production Planning: Partner with plant leadership on capacity and line loading across switchboard and switchgear assembly areas; drive resolution of throughput constraints.

  • Program Economics and Target Accountability: Set the margin and cost targets for each Power Distribution program at baseline, and own delivery against them through close-out. Partner with Project Controls in a standing monthly economics review where you jointly validate the cost-to-complete position — Project Controls owns the model, you own the operational assumptions inside it: labor hours remaining, change order capture, submittal and schedule position, and long-lead material exposure. Sign the forecast you submit. When a program drifts off target, bring the variance, the root cause, and a recovery plan to the same review rather than waiting for it to surface in the roll-up.

  • Submittal Performance Governance: Govern submittal and drawing approval performance sector-wide. This is the dominant schedule risk in electrical equipment and must be managed as a tracked metric, not an anecdote.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Supply Chain leadership on long-lead component strategy for breakers, bus, transformers, and MV components across the full order book. Support Sales and Estimating on pursuit strategy, lead time commitments, and manufacturability review before award.

  • Process Improvement: Drive standardization of schedule templates, Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs), test documentation, and close-out packages across product lines.

  • Executive Reporting and Dashboard Ownership: Own the Power Distribution executive dashboard — throughput, on-time delivery, backlog, and margin across LV switchboard, MV switchgear, MV PDC, and skid integration. Your project managers complete the project-level inputs; you own the dashboard’s accuracy, its cadence, and the story it tells to leadership. Represent Power Distribution in PMO governance including stage gates and post-mortem review.

  • Schedule Quality Assurance: Perform logic checks, float analysis, critical path validation, and baseline change control on program schedules — audit and correct, not merely report.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Industry Experience — Electrical Equipment Manufacturing: Deep technical knowledge of low-voltage and medium-voltage power distribution equipment, including applicable listing and testing standards.

  • Project Management Experience: Minimum of 8+ years managing projects within the electrical equipment, construction, engineering and/or manufacturing industry.

  • People Leadership: 3+ years of direct leadership of project managers or technical professionals, with a track record of developing them.

  • Engineering & Constructability Competency: Ability to interpret single-line diagrams, schematics, and equipment layouts, and to lead a team that challenges designs on buildability. We are looking for a leader who can give our engineering group productive, risk-based feedback from a “we have to build this” perspective before release.

  • Bachelor of Science: BS in Business, Engineering, Construction Management. Closely related fields will be considered.

  • Portfolio Accountability: Demonstrated ownership of a multi-program manufacturing portfolio with accountability for on-time delivery and margin.

  • Complex Change Leadership & Process Ownership: Proven experience serving hyperscale, utility, or mission-critical customers with rigorous documentation and change requirements.

  • Capacity Planning: Strong command of manufacturing capacity planning and ERP-based production management.

  • Schedule Development & Management: Proficient with programs such as Smartsheet, MS Project, Monday.com or Primavera P6.

  • Technical Proficiency: Proficiency in Google Suite and Microsoft Office. Experience with manufacturing ERP systems like SAP or Visual; experience with Acumatica is preferred.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience scaling an electrical equipment manufacturing operation through significant volume growth.

  • Direct experience with UL 891, UL 1558, and ANSI C37.20 series equipment.

  • Experience introducing medium-voltage manufacturing capability into an existing facility.

  • Data Center Construction Experience.

  • PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $140,000 -$160,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

Crusoe is seeking a detail-oriented, organized, and proactive Workplace Coordinator to create exceptional workplace experiences for our San Francisco office. As the first point of contact for employees, guests, and vendors, you will deliver a warm, professional front desk experience while supporting the day-to-day operations of a fast-growing workplace.

This is a full-time, in-office position based in our San Francisco office, requiring on-site presence five days per week. In this hands-on role, you will partner closely with the Workplace Manager to ensure smooth daily operations, support employee engagement initiatives, and help foster a welcoming, productive, and inclusive office environment.

As Crusoe continues to scale, your adaptability, attention to detail, and dedication to operational excellence will play a key role in shaping our San Francisco office into a thriving hub for our team.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Serve as the face of the San Francisco office, providing a friendly, professional, and consistent front desk experience for employees, visitors, and vendors

  • Manage visitor check-ins using the visitor management system and ensure adherence to security protocols.

  • Support daily front desk and office operations, acting as the primary point of contact for general workplace inquiries.

  • Conduct regular walkthroughs to ensure conference rooms, shared spaces, and office areas are clean, organized, stocked, and fully functional. Address any discrepancies as necessary.

  • Coordinate with vendors and facilities partners as needed to address office needs

  • Assist with planning and executing office events, including setup, breakdown, and catering coordination.

  • Support employee engagement initiatives, team events, and company-wide activities.

  • Assist with new hire onboarding logistics and setup for visiting employees,

  • Contribute to a positive, inclusive, and well-run office environment that reflects Crusoe’s values and culture.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Have 3+ years of experience in workplace coordination, front desk, office management, or operations roles within a fast-paced environment.

  • Are comfortable being fully on-site five days per week and supporting a front desk–focused role.

  • Enjoy supporting day-to-day office operations and taking ownership of a physical workplace.

  • Take pride in delivering a polished, welcoming, and high-quality front desk experience.

  • Are highly organized, proactive, and detail-oriented, with strong multitasking and prioritization skills

  • Communicate clearly and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

  • Are resourceful and solution-oriented, able to anticipate needs and address issues before they escalate.

  • Are passionate about creating engaging, well-run workplace experiences that support employee success.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location
