About the Role

Crusoe is seeking a talented and motivated attorney to join our Legal team as Director, Legal Counsel, Corporate & Securities. This role is essential for building a best-in-class corporate legal function to support Crusoe's rapid growth and increasing complexity.

Reporting to the VP & Assistant General Counsel, Securities, you will be the primary legal point of contact for Crusoe's corporate governance, securities law compliance, and investor and regulatory reporting. This position offers a unique opportunity to have a direct impact on our company's trajectory, helping to build the governance and compliance infrastructure required for the next stages of our growth.

This role works in close partnership with our Director, Legal Counsel, Capital Markets. The two positions are designed to provide seamless cross-coverage for one another across the full corporate and securities mandate, and the ideal candidate is comfortable stepping into capital markets transactions when needed. The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented and pragmatic legal professional with significant law firm training and a desire to apply their expertise in a dynamic, in-house environment.

Corporate Governance & Board Support (Primary Focus)

  • Lead the preparation of materials for the Board of Directors and its committees, including agendas, presentations, minutes, and resolutions.

  • Manage the preparation and distribution of stockholder consents and notices, including vote threshold analysis.

  • Support the planning and execution of the annual stockholder meeting, including preparation of the notice and meeting materials, proxy and voting logistics, and coordination of meeting minutes and resolutions.

  • Advise on company governing and investor documents, including charter, bylaws, voting agreements, investor rights agreements, and right of first refusal agreements.

  • Help build and scale corporate policies, controls, and processes that mature with the company as it grows in size and complexity.

  • Maintain organized internal deal files and corporate records. Develop standardized templates, checklists, and playbooks to improve team efficiency and transaction consistency.

Securities Compliance & Regulatory Reporting (Primary Focus)

  • Lead the development and review of the company's securities-related disclosures and reporting materials, including periodic and event-driven reporting to investors and other stakeholders.

  • Develop and maintain disclosure controls, information governance, and communications protocols appropriate for a sophisticated, well-capitalized organization.

  • Advise on insider trading policies, equity transaction reporting, and related compliance processes for directors, officers, and other key stakeholders.

  • Monitor regulatory developments and ensure ongoing compliance with applicable securities laws.

Capital Markets & Financings (Cross-Coverage)

  • Provide backup and surge support on capital markets transactions — including equity and debt securities offerings— from diligence through closing.

  • Assist with disclosure schedules, ancillary documents, and KYC requests, and coordinate document flow with investors, banks, and initial purchasers during active deals.

  • Step in on transaction execution and post-closing covenant and reporting compliance as needed.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Serve as a key legal advisor on corporate and securities matters to partners across the company, including Finance, Accounting, Investor Relations, and HR.

  • Translate complex legal and regulatory requirements into clear, practical guidance for business stakeholders.

What You'll Bring

  • Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar.

  • A minimum of 4-7 years of corporate and securities experience at a top-tier law firm, with a primary concentration in corporate governance, securities compliance, and regulatory reporting.

  • Deep subject matter expertise in board and stockholder governance, securities disclosure obligations, and insider trading compliance.

  • Working knowledge of capital markets transactions, including Rule 144A and other private placements, sufficient to provide cross-coverage for the Capital Markets function.

  • Proven track record of advising companies on complex corporate and transactional matters.

  • Exceptional attention to detail with strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent business judgment and strong communication skills, with the ability to effectively advise and influence stakeholders at all levels.

  • Demonstrated ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with extreme professionalism.

  • A proactive, team-oriented mindset with the ability to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.

  • Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, and AI tools (Claude, Gemini).

  • In-house experience at a technology or high-growth company is a plus.

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

About This Role:

Join our team as a Project Manager II taking ownership of manufacturing execution for custom low-voltage Switchboard Programs — the highest-volume, highest-throughput line in our Power Distribution sector. These are UL 891 listed, Engineered to Order assemblies built to hyperscale customer standards, with tight delivery windows and unforgiving long-lead component exposure.

This role is about throughput and material discipline. Switchboard programs live or die on breaker and bus availability, drawing approval turnaround, and clean work packet release to the assembly line. You'll own the full production path from customer submittal approval through factory acceptance testing and shipment, across a portfolio of concurrent orders.

You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with production supervisors, test technicians, and the materials team on the floor every day. Your work directly impacts our ability to energize compute from sustainable, renewable and/or stranded energy sources.

We are seeking an experienced professional with a proven background in electrical equipment or industrial manufacturing, a strategic mindset, and the persistence to drive submittal cycles and supplier commitments to closure. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Switchboard Manufacturing Execution: Own assigned switchboard orders end to end — submittal approval, engineering release, material readiness, assembly, wiring, test, and shipment.

  • Submittal and Approval Cycle Ownership: Drive the customer submittal and drawing approval cycle to closure. This is the single most common source of schedule loss in electrical equipment and must be actively managed, not passively tracked.

  • Long-Lead Material Management: Manage exposure on breakers, bus, metering, instrument transformers, and enclosures with Supply Chain against firm production start dates.

  • Project Planning and Execution: Maintain the production schedule at work-order level in alignment with assembly line loading and plant capacity.

  • Strategic Change & Risk Management: Process engineering changes and customer-driven revisions through impact analysis, pricing, and approval before floor implementation; ensure BOM and routing updates follow. Maintain risk logs, action logs, RFIs, submittals and change orders.

  • Quality and Test Coordination: Partner with Quality leaders to ensure the Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) is executed on time and to the applicable standards and specifications, including production testing, non-conformance closure, and customer witness testing where required.

  • Budget Reporting and Forecasting: Manage order cost performance — labor hours against estimate, material variance, and change order capture — and report against baseline. You own the accuracy of your order cost model, maintain it to the PMO reporting standard and cadence, and sign the monthly cost-to-complete position that feeds the program economics review.

  • Logistics and Delivery: Coordinate shipment readiness: final inspection, documentation package, crating, and logistics alignment with customer receiving windows.

  • Customer and Stakeholder Management: Serve as the day-to-day customer contact for assigned orders, including schedule reporting and change communication.

  • Executive Dashboard Inputs: Complete the project-level portions of the sector executive dashboard on the published cadence — schedule position, milestone status, cost and margin position, and open risk. Your inputs are what gets reported upward, so their accuracy and timeliness are yours to own.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Industry Experience — Electrical Equipment Manufacturing: Experience with low-voltage power distribution equipment: switchboards, panelboards, bus systems, protective devices, and metering.

  • Building Code & Electrical Code Knowledge: Competent in electrical code knowledge for collaboration with the in-house engineering department, manufacturing technicians, and customer engineers of record.

  • Project Management Experience: Minimum of 3+ years managing projects within the electrical equipment, construction, engineering and/or manufacturing industry.

  • Bachelor of Science: BS in Engineering, Industrial Technology, Construction Management or a closely related field.

  • Engineering & Constructability Competency: Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, elevation drawings, schematics, and wiring diagrams, weigh in on aspects of designs, and advise on risks associated with design decisions. We are looking for someone to add value from an “I have to build this” perspective to provide productive feedback to our engineering group.

  • Submittal Cycle Management: Demonstrated experience managing customer submittal and approval cycles as a controlled schedule activity with aging and escalation.

  • Supply Chain Judgment: Experience managing long-lead material risk in a constrained supply environment.

  • Schedule Development & Management: Proficient with programs such as Smartsheet, MS Project, Monday.com or Primavera P6.

  • Technical Proficiency: Proficiency in Google Suite and Microsoft Office. Experience with manufacturing ERP systems like SAP or Visual; experience with Acumatica is preferred.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Direct experience with UL 891 switchboard manufacturing or UL 1558 switchgear.

  • Familiarity with NFPA 70, NFPA 70E, and applicable ANSI/IEEE standards for LV distribution equipment.

  • Experience supplying hyperscale data center or mission-critical customers.

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) or Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification.

  • Lean or continuous improvement experience on an assembly line.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $100,000 -$110,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Network Production Engineer, Deployment
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Crusoe Cloud is seeking a high-energy, detail-oriented Senior Network Production Engineer to support the physical and logical implementation of our global network. As we rapidly expand our footprint of high-performance compute (HPC) and GPU-based AI infrastructure, this role plays a key part in bringing new data centers and edge sites online, directly enabling the scale and reliability our AI cloud customers depend on.

This is a technical, hands-on, full-time role that sits at the intersection of Network Engineering, Data Center Operations, and Project Management. The ideal candidate is comfortable both on-site and remote, follows and helps refine deployment standards, and takes ownership of ensuring every switch, router, and fiber optic link is deployed to spec, validated, and seamlessly handed off to our Operations team.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Network Deployment Execution: Execute on-site and remote network deployments for new data center and edge site builds, from rack-and-stack through final cutover.

  • Implementation Planning: Implement architecture designs into concrete deployment steps: cable maps, port assignments, device configs, and site-specific runbooks.

  • Automation Development: Write and maintain Python/Ansible automation and ZTP workflows to stage, configure, and validate batches of switches and routers without manual touch.

  • Acceptance Testing: Support burn-in and site acceptance testing (SAT) on new clusters, chase down failures, and help drive clean handoffs to Operations.

  • Fabric Configuration & Troubleshooting: Configure and troubleshoot Arista, Juniper, and NVIDIA/Mellanox gear in leaf-spine fabrics, including BGP, EVPN-VXLAN, and LLDP issues at the link and fabric level.

  • Vendor & Physical Layer Coordination: Work directly with structured cabling vendors, remote hands, and data center providers on-site to resolve physical layer issues — bad fiber runs, power/cooling deviations, mislabeled patch panels — before they block turn-up.

  • Physical/Link-Layer Diagnostics: Diagnose physical and link-layer problems using OTDRs, light meters, and packet captures when something doesn't come up clean.

  • Inventory & Capacity Tracking: Track hardware inventory and support turn-up of new backbone and edge interconnect capacity against deployment schedules.

  • Cross-Team Collaboration: Collaborate with other engineers on tricky sites or configs, and flag recurring issues back to the team so they get addressed at the process or automation level.

  • On-Call Support: Participate in an on-call rotation, responding to and troubleshooting network incidents affecting production infrastructure.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 5+ years of experience in network engineering with a focus on large-scale data center deployments and infrastructure projects.

  • Strong knowledge of physical layer standards: solid experience with structured cabling (SMF/MMF, MPO/MTP), optical transceivers (400G/800G), and data center power/cooling requirements.

  • Solid routing and switching knowledge: hands-on experience configuring Arista (EOS), Juniper (Junos), and NVIDIA/Mellanox platforms in a leaf-spine architecture.

  • Protocol familiarity: working understanding of BGP, EVPN-VXLAN, and LLDP as they relate to large-scale fabric provisioning.

  • Automation-minded: proficiency in Python and Ansible for automating repetitive deployment tasks and validating configuration state.

  • Logistical skills: ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously across different time zones and physical locations.

  • Troubleshooting skills: ability to diagnose physical layer and link-layer issues using OTDRs, light meters, and packet captures.

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical field or equivalent practical experience in hyperscale or ISP environments.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Experience working in hyperscale, ISP, or large multi-tenant data center environments.

  • Familiarity with GPU cluster networking (e.g., RDMA/RoCE, InfiniBand, or NVIDIA NCCL-aware fabric design).

  • Exposure to network monitoring and observability tooling (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, telemetry-based fabric health checks).

  • Vendor certifications such as CCNP, JNCIP, or Arista ACE.

  • Prior experience mentoring junior engineers or contributing to deployment standards/documentation.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $170,000 - $205,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

 - Protocol familiarity: working understanding of BGP, EVPN-VXLAN, and LLDP as they relate to large-scale fabric provisioning.

 - Automation-minded: proficiency in Python and Ansible for automating repetitive deployment tasks and validating configuration state.

 - Logistical skills: ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously across different time zones and physical locations.

 - Troubleshooting skills: ability to diagnose physical layer and link-layer issues using OTDRs, light meters, and packet captures.

 - Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical field or equivalent practical experience in hyperscale or ISP environments.

 

Bonus Points:

 - Experience working in hyperscale, ISP, or large multi-tenant data center environments.

 - Familiarity with GPU cluster networking (e.g., RDMA/RoCE, InfiniBand, or NVIDIA NCCL-aware fabric design).

 - Exposure to network monitoring and observability tooling (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, telemetry-based fabric health checks).

 - Vendor certifications such as CCNP, JNCIP, or Arista ACE.

 - Prior experience mentoring junior engineers or contributing to deployment standards/documentation.

About This Role:

Join our team as a Senior Project Manager of Modular Building Programs for HAC (Hot/Cold) Aisle Containment and Spark™ Modular Data Center products. Take ownership of planning, organizing, and executing ETO (Engineered to Order) programs with precision and efficiency. HAC is high-volume, fast-turn, and configuration-driven — it demands a project manager who can run repeatable work at speed while holding cost and quality discipline.

This role sits at the intersection of estimating accuracy and production reality. HAC programs are won and lost on material cost, scope delineation, and the ability to release clean packages to the floor quickly. You'll manage multiple concurrent HAC programs across design variants while carrying supporting scope on Spark™ MDC (Modular Data Center) builds.

Your work directly impacts our ability to deploy modular data center infrastructure that computes from sustainable, renewable and/or stranded energy sources. This is a strong growth role for a project manager ready to take on greater customer ownership within the modular sector.

We are seeking a motivated professional with a background in construction, engineering, and/or manufacturing, strong cost instincts, and a bias toward getting clean packages to the floor fast. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Hot/Cold Aisle Containment Programs: Manage concurrent HAC programs from award through fabrication, kitting, and shipment — owning schedule, cost, scope, and delivery commitment for each.

  • Configuration Control: Manage HAC design variants and ensure the correct released design, BOM, and material takeoff drive each production release.

  • Budget Reporting and Forecasting: Own material-driven cost performance. Track quoted versus actual material cost, drive takeoff accuracy, and escalate variance with root cause — not just a number. You own the accuracy of your project cost model, maintain it to the PMO reporting standard and cadence, and sign the monthly cost-to-complete position that feeds the program economics review.

  • Customer and Stakeholder Management: Coordinate scope delineation with customers and installing contractors. Clarify what ships, what is field-installed, and where responsibility transfers, and get it in writing.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Estimating on pricing support, quantity validation, and competitive positioning inputs for HAC pursuits.

  • Production Release Readiness: Drive drawing release, BOM completeness, kitting plan, and shop packet quality before work orders open.

  • Logistics and Delivery: Manage shipment sequencing to match customer install schedules, including staged and partial releases.

  • Spark™ Program Support: Support Spark™ MDC programs with schedule maintenance, change tracking, and documentation as assigned.

  • Strategic Change & Risk Management: Maintain change logs, risk logs, RFIs and submittals, and produce customer-facing schedule impact reporting for assigned programs.

  • Process Improvement: Contribute to standardization of HAC estimating templates, BOM structures, and production packets to reduce cycle time per program.

  • Executive Dashboard Inputs: Complete the project-level portions of the sector executive dashboard on the published cadence — schedule position, milestone status, cost and margin position, and open risk. Your inputs are what gets reported upward, so their accuracy and timeliness are yours to own.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Industry Experience: Experience in construction, prefabrication, or manufacturing product delivery with exposure to multi-disciplinary products.

  • Project Management Experience: Minimum of 5+ years managing projects within the electrical equipment, construction, engineering and/or manufacturing industry.

  • Bachelor of Science: BS in Business, Engineering, Construction Management. Closely related fields will be considered.

  • Cost Management: Demonstrated ownership of material cost performance, including takeoffs, BOM accuracy, and variance analysis.

  • Engineering & Constructability Competency: Ability to read and interpret fabrication drawings, layouts, and structural/sheet metal detail, and to advise on risks associated with design decisions. We are looking for someone to add value from an “I have to build this” perspective to provide productive feedback to our engineering group.

  • Concurrent Program Execution: Proven ability to manage multiple fast-turn programs simultaneously without loss of schedule or cost control.

  • Schedule Development & Management: Proficient with programs such as Smartsheet, MS Project, Monday.com or Primavera P6.

  • Technical Proficiency: Proficiency in Google Suite and Microsoft Office. Experience with manufacturing ERP systems like SAP or Visual; experience with Acumatica is preferred.

  • Team Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to foster teamwork and influence peers, ensuring collaborative project execution.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Data center construction experience

  • Direct experience with data center containment, raised floor, cable management, or similar white-space infrastructure products.

  • Exposure to modular data center or prefabricated electrical building manufacturing.

  • Estimating or takeoff experience in a competitive bid environment.

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) or Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification.

  • Lean manufacturing or continuous improvement training.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $130,000 -$150,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Join our team as the New Product Project Manager for Low and Medium Voltage products and take ownership of New Product Introduction (NPI) across our power distribution offerings — moving new switchboard, switchgear, and skid-integrated designs from concept through prototype, listing, first article, and full production release.

This role exists because ETO manufacturers scale by turning custom one-offs into repeatable, manufacturable products. You'll own the industrialization path: design for manufacturability, tooling and fixture requirements, routing and work instruction development, listing and certification coordination, supply chain qualification, and the pilot build that proves the line can produce it at rate.

This is a builder's role. You'll work across Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain with no direct reporting line over any of them, and you'll be measured on whether new products reach stable production — not on whether a prototype worked once. Your work directly impacts how fast we can energize compute from sustainable, renewable and/or stranded energy sources.

We are seeking a deeply technical professional with a proven background in product industrialization and manufacturing engineering, and a comfort operating where no process yet exists. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • New Product Introduction Programs: Own NPI program plans for new LV and MV product introductions, including stage gates, deliverables, and go/no-go criteria for production release.

  • Design for Manufacturability: Drive DFM reviews with Engineering — challenge designs on labor content, part count, standardization, and line compatibility before release.

  • Certification and Listing: Coordinate UL, ANSI/IEEE, seismic and arc-resistant certification activities, including test lab scheduling, sample builds, and documentation.

  • Production Readiness Package: Develop routings, work instructions, station layouts, tooling and fixture requirements, test procedures, and quality inspection criteria.

  • Prototype and First Article Builds: Lead pilot builds on the floor, capturing build issues, cycle times, and rework drivers, and driving corrective action into both the design and the process.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Supply Chain to qualify new components and suppliers, establish sourcing for new BOM content, and validate lead times against target production rates.

  • Cost Standards: Establish target cost and labor standards for new products and validate them against actual pilot build performance. You own the accuracy of your program cost model, maintain it to the PMO reporting standard and cadence, and sign the monthly cost-to-complete position that feeds the program economics review.

  • Production Handoff: Coordinate the transition to production project management — no new product transitions until the receiving team has a complete, validated build package.

  • Strategic Change & Risk Management: Maintain the NPI portfolio schedule and report status, risk, and gate position to Power Distribution and PMO leadership.

  • Process Improvement: Feed field and factory performance data back into product improvement cycles after launch.

  • Executive Dashboard Inputs: Complete the project-level portions of the sector executive dashboard on the published cadence — schedule position, milestone status, cost and margin position, and open risk. Your inputs are what gets reported upward, so their accuracy and timeliness are yours to own.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Electrical Equipment Manufacturing Industry Experience: Working technical knowledge of low-voltage and medium-voltage power distribution equipment and the standards that govern them.

  • Project Management Experience: Minimum of 5+ years managing projects or programs in manufacturing, including direct new product introduction or product industrialization ownership.

  • Bachelor of Science: BS in Electrical, Mechanical, or Manufacturing Engineering. Closely related technical fields will be considered.

  • Manufacturing Process Documentation: Demonstrated experience developing production routings, work instructions, and manufacturing process documentation.

  • Certification Coordination: Experience coordinating product certification or third-party listing activities with external test labs.

  • Team Collaboration: Proven cross-functional leadership across engineering, operations, quality, and supply chain without direct authority.

  • Comfort with Ambiguity: Ability to define scope, structure, and process where none currently exists.

  • Technical Proficiency: Proficiency in Google Suite and Microsoft Office. Experience with manufacturing ERP systems like SAP or Visual; experience with Acumatica is preferred.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Hands-on experience with UL 891, UL 1558, or ANSI C37.20 series equipment development.

  • Experience introducing medium-voltage products into a facility with a primarily low-voltage manufacturing history.

  • Skid integration or packaged power system experience.

  • DFMEA, APQP/PPAP, or equivalent methodology training.

  • Lean or Six Sigma certification.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $100,000 -$110,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

Your work directly impacts our ability to energize compute from sustainable, renewable and/or stranded energy sources at a scale the current facility cannot yet support. This role suits a project manager who is comfortable being handed a problem with no template, no precedent inside the building, and a hard date.

We are seeking an experienced professional with a proven background spanning capital projects and manufacturing operations, a strategic mindset, and the self-direction to build structure where none exists.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Medium Voltage Manufacturing Expansion: Own capability expansion programs including scope definition, budget, schedule, and cross-functional execution.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Join our team as the Senior Project Controls Manager and take ownership of the cost and schedule integrity of every Engineered to Order (ETO) manufacturing program we run. You will build and enforce the baseline discipline that lets the PMO forecast credibly — a common WBS, a common schedule structure, a common cost taxonomy, and a reporting layer that ties production reality back to the numbers we quoted.

This is the analytical backbone of the PMO. You will not run projects; you will make the people who run projects measurably better at it. You'll own the estimate-to-baseline handoff, the cost-to-complete reporting layer, and the monthly program economics review that keeps both manufacturing sectors honest about where their programs actually stand.

The role is deliberately cross-sector. You'll work across Spark MDC, PDC buildings, low- and medium-voltage switchgear, and switchboard lines — and you will be the person who can say, with evidence, where a program actually stands. Your work directly impacts our ability to deploy infrastructure that computes from sustainable, renewable and/or stranded energy sources.

We are seeking a deeply analytical professional with a proven background in cost engineering, project controls, or manufacturing finance, and the credibility to hold project managers and operations leaders to a standard. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Baseline Standards and Governance: Establish and maintain PMO-wide standards for cost and schedule baselining, including a common WBS and cost code structure across both manufacturing sectors.

  • Baseline Change Control Standard: Define the cross-sector standard for how a cost or schedule baseline may be revised — what triggers a re-baseline, who approves it, and how the original commitment stays visible after the change. Audit compliance across both sectors; the sector managers run quality assurance on their own schedules, you own the rule they run it against.

  • Estimate-to-Baseline Handoff: Validate that awarded scope, quoted hours, material costs, and margin assumptions are correctly loaded before a program starts — this is where most margin is won or lost.

  • Budget Reporting and Forecasting: Build the cost-to-complete and estimate-at-completion tooling that project managers run their projects on, and make it good enough that keeping it current is the easy path. PMs own their project numbers — committed cost, earned production, and forecast at completion — and you partner with them on the standard and cadence that keeps those numbers trustworthy, coaching where the model is confusing and flagging where it’s drifting. At the portfolio level you’re the consumer: roll the data up, work variances through with the responsible PM, and bring leadership a forecast the whole team stands behind.

  • Monthly Program Economics Review: Own the standing monthly economics review across both sectors — you set the calendar, publish the pre-read, run the meeting, and hold the drumbeat month over month so it survives busy quarters. Each sector manager brings a signed cost-to-complete position for every active program; you validate the model, challenge the operational assumptions behind it, and drive variance and recovery items to a documented owner and date. Track closure of prior-month actions so the review compounds rather than resets.

  • SOP and Tooling Ownership: Own the SOPs and tooling that make the review executable — the forecast submission artifact and its sign-off, the variance and recovery log, the pre-read package, and the reporting templates PMs work in. Write the procedures, version them, train the PMs on them, and revise them when the process outgrows the tool. If a control only exists in someone’s spreadsheet, it is not yet a control.

  • Reporting and Dashboard Tooling: Build and maintain the data layer and reporting tooling behind the sector executive dashboards. The sector managers own their dashboards and the story they tell; you own the pipeline underneath — the source-of-truth queries, the refresh automation, and the reconciliation that makes both sectors’ numbers comparable.

  • Data Integrity and ERP Governance: Own cost data hygiene across the PMO — cost code discipline, work order structure, WIP accuracy, and BOM-to-job-cost alignment. Audit for drift, drive correction with the responsible team, and keep bad inputs from reaching the forecast.

  • Portfolio Risk and Contingency Management: Track contingency and risk allowance across the active portfolio — what was carried at baseline, what has been drawn, and what remains against known exposure. Give leadership a defensible view of how much cushion is actually left.

  • PM Enablement and Training: Onboard every new project manager onto the controls toolset and reporting standard, run refreshers as the tooling changes, and build the cost and schedule competency of the PM population over time. Adoption is a deliverable, not a hope.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Finance and Accounting on revenue recognition inputs, work-in-process valuation, and variance explanation. Support Estimating with actualized cost feedback so future bids reflect real production performance.

  • Post-Mortem Analysis: Lead financial and schedule post-mortem analysis at project close-out, and publish trend findings back into estimating and operations.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Project Controls Experience: Minimum of 6+ years in project controls, cost engineering, or manufacturing finance, including work in an ETO or make-to-order production environment.

  • Bachelor of Science: BS in Engineering, Construction Management, Finance, Accounting, or a closely related quantitative field.

  • Cost Management: Demonstrated ownership of cost baselines, earned value or equivalent progress measurement, and estimate-at-completion forecasting.

  • Advanced Modeling Capability: Advanced Google Sheets modeling including dynamic cost structures, sensitivity analysis, and large-scale data reconciliation.

  • Technical Proficiency: Hands-on ERP experience for job costing, work orders, and BOM-level cost roll-up. Proficiency in Google Suite and Microsoft Office.

  • Schedule Development & Management: Strong scheduling literacy across Smartsheet, MS Project, Monday.com or Primavera P6 — with the ability to audit and correct schedule logic.

  • Team Collaboration: Proven ability to influence project managers and operations leaders without direct authority.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with Acumatica

  • Experience supporting both discrete manufacturing and construction-style project accounting.

  • Power BI, Looker Studio, or Python-based reporting automation.

  • Experience using AI-assisted analytics to accelerate project controls work — forecast modeling, schedule risk and float analysis, anomaly detection in cost data, or automating reconciliation and reporting.

  • AACE certification (CCP, EVP, PSP) or equivalent.

  • Prior experience standing up a project controls function from scratch.

  • Data Center Construction Experience.

  • MBA in Business, Accounting or Engineering/Project Management is preferred.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $130,000 -$150,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

As the Principal Product Manager, Bare Metal, you'll own the strategy and outcomes for a brand-new initiative at Crusoe: our bare metal offering, giving AI-native companies direct GPU and CPU access to power the world's most demanding training and inference workloads. This is a role at the intersection of hardware and software, spanning compute, networking, observability, and management. You will be defining the problem space as much as solving it. You should be genuinely comfortable operating in ambiguity, though you won't be doing it alone: you'll have support from senior leadership to help clean up open questions as the initiative takes shape.

This role blends Product Management, Solutions Architecture and Process Design. You will need technical depth spanning across the hardware, firmware and operating system layers (e.g. BMC — Baseboard Management Controller, secure boot) as well as the process rigor to design how the product behaves operationally.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Roadmap Ownership: Drive the vision for bare metal compute, encompassing GPU/CPU offerings, rapid provisioning systems, and full lifecycle management.

  • Process & Operational Design: Define the end-to-end customer experience when something goes wrong — the ticketing workflow, escalation paths, and process behind it — in close partnership with Infrastructure Operations and Customer Support.

  • Outcome Management: Ensure tight alignment between hardware and software layers to deliver a differentiated bare metal experience.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Lead initiatives across engineering and infra-ops to deliver provisioning, enhanced observability, and customer self-service capabilities.

  • Customer & Market Synthesis: Partner with Sales and GTM teams to transform customer feedback into roadmap priorities, ensuring deep product-market fit.

  • Executive Representation: Represent the bare metal strategy to partners and internal executives, framing technical infrastructure decisions within a clear business context and treating this portfolio like a business you're accountable for.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Infrastructure Leadership: 10+ years of experience in cloud and computing technology, including 4+ years in product management focused on infrastructure or platform products, with a track record of leading complex, cross-functional initiatives through ambiguity.

  • Hardware Depth: Direct experience at the hardware and firmware level, you don't need to be an engineer, but you need to have worked at that layer.

  • Process Orientation: A demonstrated ability to design and formalize operational processes (support workflows, ticketing, incident handling) for a technical product

  • Deep Compute & Operational Expertise: Comprehensive knowledge of server hardware, bare metal provisioning, distributed systems, networking, and large-scale fleet operations.

  • Strategic Decision Making: Proven ability to navigate ambiguous, ill-defined problem spaces and drive long-term vision while balancing technical constraints and business outcomes

  • Communication Mastery: The ability to articulate deep technical complexity to executive audiences and translate business goals into clear product direction.

Bonus Points

  • Hyperscale/Cloud Operations: Experience with large-scale GPU/CPU AI infrastructure platforms or clouds.

  • Technical Tooling: Familiarity with IPMI/BMC protocols, infrastructure automation tools, or bare metal provisioning frameworks.

  • AI/ML Domain Knowledge: An understanding of GPU-based AI workloads and their specific demands on compute and network infrastructure.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

About This Role:

Crusoe is building the world's favorite AI-first cloud infrastructure company, pioneering vertically integrated, purpose-built AI infrastructure solutions trusted by Fortune 500 companies. As a Senior Staff Instrumentation and Controls Engineer, you'll independently lead end-to-end I&C vendor oversight for Crusoe's most complex, multi-system Power Generation programs, serving as the primary technical owner from design through operational handoff. You'll oversee the entire project lifecycle for power generation controls, from initial design and installation to optimization, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), commissioning, and initial operations support. Your expertise in instrumentation, controls systems, data analysis, and energy optimization will be vital in delivering scalable and sustainable solutions that ensure the reliable and efficient operation of our facilities, accelerating abundance of energy and intelligence. This is a full-time position.

Role Scope: This position functions as Owner’s Engineer for assigned programs. Professional Engineer (PE) licensure is desired but not required.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Technical Problem-Solving: Provide high-level expertise, strategic direction and technical support and knowledge for complex problem-solving related to the design and operation of Crusoe Power Generation Plant control systems.

  • System Integration: Provide Owner's Engineer oversight of the systems integrator's work, coordinating with electrical and mechanical engineering teams to ensure control systems are seamlessly integrated with other critical plant systems.

  • Installation Oversight: Oversee the installation of control systems, ensuring they meet precise design specifications and adhere to stringent industry standards.

  • System Testing and Coordination: Oversee comprehensive testing of control systems to verify correct and safe operation, including Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT).

  • Commissioning Leadership: Lead the commissioning process, working hand-in-hand with the project team to bring power plants online, efficiently troubleshoot issues, and ensure smooth startup operations.

  • Operational Support: Provide essential technical support during the initial operation phase, directing resolution of any control system-related issues that may arise.

  • Training & Documentation: Oversee the training of operations staff on the effective use of control systems and oversee development of clear, comprehensive documentation, training materials, and operational procedures.

  • Safety & Regulatory Compliance: Ensure that all control systems strictly comply with relevant safety standards and regulations, promoting a secure operational environment.

  • Fail-Safe & Redundancy Implementation: Review and enforce fail-safe and redundancy design requirements across vendor deliverables, ensuring proactive prevention of accidents and reliability of plant operations.

  • Quality Assurance Leadership: Drive continuous improvement by establishing and rigorously enforcing Crusoe Instrumentation & Controls standards across all projects, ensuring maximum operational integrity and reliability.

  • Project Planning & Resource Allocation: Actively participate in project planning, scheduling, and strategic resource allocation for all control systems-related tasks.

  • Technology Advancement: Stay continuously updated on the latest technologies and advancements in control systems and power generation, applying new insights to our operations.

  • Mentorship & Development: Train and develop junior I&C engineers, building technical judgment and vendor-oversight capability across the team.

  • Standards Development: Lead the creation of engineering design, construction, and commissioning standards for vendors, establishing repeatable frameworks that raise deliverable quality and consistency across programs.

  • Vendor Oversight & Coordination: Lead end-to-end I&C vendor oversight for complex, multi-system programs, coordinating and aligning multiple vendors' DCS design, SCADA implementation, power control system integration, and field instrumentation scope into one coherent program architecture.

  • Cross-Vendor Conflict Resolution: Independently resolve cross-vendor design conflicts within assigned programs without escalation, directing vendors to the aligned technical solution.

  • Vendor Deliverable Review: Review vendor deliverables for engineering adequacy, directly challenging a vendor's technical basis when non-conformances or design risks are identified.

  • Standards Currency: Maintain current working knowledge of applicable ISA standards (e.g., ISA-5.1, ISA-18.2) and ensure project designs and vendor deliverables reflect the latest published guidance.

  • Technical Judgment: Evaluates complex, multi-layered I&C challenges—control system integration failures, DCS programming issues for non-standard equipment, and field instrumentation anomalies—developing well-reasoned technical solutions without waiting for perfect information, and operates effectively in novel technical environments where specifications are incomplete.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Educational Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Controls/Automation Engineering, or a related field, is required.

  • Power Systems Experience: Professional experience in a power systems environment, demonstrating practical knowledge of power generation operations.

  • Controls System Expertise: 20+ years of experience in control systems, electrical power management systems, controls engineering, or a closely related field.Experience with Power Plant DCS (Distributed Control Systems) or PLC-based Control Systems.

  • Technical Understanding: Strong understanding of mechanical systems, electrical systems, PLCs, and industrial control systems.

  • Collaboration Skills: Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across departments to meet challenging organizational goals.

  • Communication Proficiency: Excellent communication skills, with the ability to clearly present complex technical information to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Data-Driven Passion: A strong passion for leveraging data to continuously improve system performance and enhance operational efficiency.

  • Professional Licensure: Professional Engineer (PE) license is desired but not required. This role serves as Owner’s Engineer; Engineer of Record responsibility sits with the EPC firm.

  • ISA Standards Fluency: Maintains awareness of evolving industry standards and stays current as new guidance is published, ensuring vendor and project deliverables reflect the latest requirements.

  • Vendor & Stakeholder Relationships: Demonstrated ability to build and maintain working relationships with key equipment vendors and commissioning agents, and to directly influence project scheduling, commissioning readiness criteria, and equipment procurement decisions.

  • AI-Forward: Actively champions AI-enabled tools and new ways of operating, driving adoption across engineering workflows to improve efficiency and design quality.

Bonus Points:

  • Relevant certifications (e.g., Professional Engineer (PE), Certified Automation Professional (CAP)).

  • Specific experience with systems such as SEL PowerMax, SEL RTAC, Ignition SCADA, Canary Historian, GE Mark VIE Turbine Control Systems, Solar Rockwell PLC, AllenBradley PLC’s, ComAp, ESM 2 Waukesha, or similar platforms.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $190,000 -$215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDDIG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Instrumentation & Controls Engineer II - Modular
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role

As an Instrumentation & Controls Engineer II supporting Crusoe's modular data center platform, you will help build the control system that ships inside every module we manufacture. Modular is how Crusoe compresses the timeline from steel to compute, and that speed only holds if the controls package is repeatable, verified in the factory, and correct the first time it lands in the field. You will work alongside senior I&C engineers to develop the point lists, instrument schedules, and control system drawings that define the platform, then prove that work out on the factory floor through factory acceptance testing before a module ever leaves the building.

This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who wants to build depth in industrial controls inside a manufacturing environment rather than one-off site design. You will move between the design desk and the factory, translating standards into deliverables and then validating those deliverables against real hardware. Expect close mentorship from experienced engineers, clear ownership of your assigned deliverables, and increasing independence as your judgment develops. Denver is your home base, with estimated travel at 25% to manufacturing partners and deployment sites. This is a full-time position.

What You'll Be Working On

  • Design Deliverable Development: Develop point lists, instrument schedules, I/O assignments, and control system drawings for modular data center systems under the direction of senior I&C engineers.

  • Factory Acceptance Testing: Execute and document FAT protocols on control panels and integrated modules, including point-to-point verification, loop checks, and calibration confirmation prior to shipment.

  • Manufacturing Support: Partner with manufacturing on the factory floor to resolve control panel build issues, wiring discrepancies, and instrument installation questions as modules move through production.

  • Platform Standardization: Contribute to the repeatable design packages, drawing templates, and test procedures that let the modular platform scale across successive builds without rework.

  • Vendor and Integrator Coordination: Support technical coordination with control panel fabricators, systems integrators, and instrument suppliers on submittals, specification compliance, and open technical items.

  • Field Verification and Startup Support: Conduct field walks, equipment inspections, and basic calibration verification at manufacturing and deployment sites to confirm as-built accuracy and commissioning readiness.

  • Documentation Integrity: Maintain accurate as-built drawings, test records, and instrument documentation so downstream construction, commissioning, and operations teams work from a reliable source of truth.

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • Instrumentation & Controls Foundation: 2 to 4 years of professional experience in industrial instrumentation and controls, including exposure to point list development, control system drawings, and field instrumentation.

  • PLC Proficiency: Working familiarity with Rockwell and Allen-Bradley platforms, including Studio 5000 and ControlLogix or CompactLogix hardware.

  • SCADA Exposure: Hands-on experience with Ignition SCADA or a comparable platform, including tag configuration, screen navigation, and basic troubleshooting.

  • Testing and Verification Discipline: Demonstrated ability to execute structured test procedures, document results accurately, and identify discrepancies before they propagate into downstream deliverables.

  • Field and Factory Readiness: Comfort working in active manufacturing and construction environments, including field walks, panel inspections, and instrument verification alongside technicians and trades.

  • Collaborative Judgment: A track record of applying established engineering standards independently while escalating technical ambiguity to more experienced engineers early and clearly.

  • Mandatory Education: A Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Control Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

Bonus Points

  • Data Center or Mission-Critical Experience: Prior work on data center mechanical or electrical control systems, or in another high-availability industrial environment.

  • Modular or Prefabricated Delivery: Experience supporting a productized or prefabricated equipment platform where design repeatability and factory verification drive schedule.

  • Protocol Depth: Practical familiarity with Modbus TCP, BACnet, or OPC UA in a multi-vendor integration context.

  • Industry Certifications: Relevant credentials such as network certifications, Rockwell or Inductive Automation certifications.

  • OT Cybersecurity Awareness: Understanding of industrial network segmentation and OT security practices as applied to control system deployments.

  • Mission Alignment: A genuine interest in energy and AI infrastructure, and in the engineering rigor required to build it at speed.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $110,000 -$120,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

Crusoe is building the infrastructure layer that powers the most demanding AI workloads on the planet. Our storage stack is what keeps tens of thousands of GPUs fed with data, whether that means block volumes for fast bootups, a shared file system for a training cluster, or the object storage tier a physical AI customer depends on.

The Cloud Storage team at Crusoe is seeking a Staff TPM to serve as the main execution driver for our most impactful, cross-team programs. You will be a multiplier, responsible for executing the Product and Engineering strategy, create scalable processes, and allow the team to execute predictably.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • End-to-end program delivery for Storage Engineering, spanning multi-quarter release planning, dependency governance, and executive communication.

  • Complex, high-risk programs including feature rollouts, new Storage deployments, and platform resiliency.

  • Cross-functional alignment across IaaS, Cloud Foundations, Data Center Operations, and external storage providers.

  • Proactive risk identification across programs and vendor timelines.

  • Lightweight, scalable TPM frameworks suited to Crusoe's pace; real-time execution dashboards and crisp, data-driven executive updates.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Technical Foundation

  • In-depth understanding of cloud technologies, platforms, and services (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS).

  • Experience building and launching storage products, such as block volumes, file-systems, or object storage.

  • Direct technical experience working with storage hardware, protocols, or file systems.

  • Ability to engage credibly with engineering on technical topics and tradeoffs.

  • Proven ability to help define, scope, and document ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives with minimal guidance.

  • Analytical mindset with the ability to use data to inform decision-making.

Program Leadership

  • 7+ years as a Technical Program Manager in fast-paced technical environments, with a track record of owning complex programs end-to-end across engineering and product organizations.

  • Proven ability to drive alignment across engineering, product, and infrastructure leadership without direct authority.

  • Experience building execution models in low-structure environments where the process did not yet exist.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication for delivering clear, data-driven updates to executive stakeholders.

  • Active, daily use of AI tools to improve program execution, risk detection, and communication.

Bonus Points

  • Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field;

  • 5+ years experience working with execution teams building Storage platforms/services

  • Experience coaching or mentoring junior TPMs in a high-growth technical environment.

  • Exposure to multi-site or globally distributed engineering teams.

  • Background at a Series D to Series F company or a high-performing team within a hyperscaler focused on AI infrastructure.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $200,000-$240,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

As a Project Manager on Crusoe’s Cloud Deployment Operations team, you will drive the physical expansion and operational readiness of our sustainable data center infrastructure. In this full-time role, you will lead complex, high-impact infrastructure deployment projects across our data center environments. You will be the orchestrator ensuring sites are ready, structured cabling and physical layer infrastructure are installed to exact specifications, and our cutting-edge cloud infrastructure is brought online efficiently and reliably to power the future of compute.

The ideal candidate is a self-directed, highly organized technical project manager who thrives in fast-paced, dynamic environments. You bring a deep understanding of physical infrastructure deployments, data center operations, and cloud readiness, paired with the exceptional collaboration skills required to align cross-functional engineering teams and external vendors. By bridging the gap between physical deployment and operational reality, you will directly accelerate Crusoe's mission to build the most climate-aligned digital infrastructure on earth.

 

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Ensure Site Readiness: Oversee all aspects of site readiness, proactively coordinating with diverse stakeholders to guarantee facilities are fully prepared for seamless equipment installation and operational deployment.

  • Own Deployment Execution: Lead end-to-end project management for physical layer and cable infrastructure rollouts, driving vendor execution from initial planning phases through final testing and handoff.

  • Manage Physical Infrastructure: Partner closely with internal deployment engineers to oversee the installation of structured cabling (backbone fiber, copper, pathways, and containment), ensuring third-party vendors execute strictly according to engineering designs and timelines.

  • Drive Cross-Functional Collaboration: Align project goals, key dependencies, and deliverables by working hand-in-hand with our Digital Infrastructure Group (DIG), Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), and external partners.

  • Build Project Plans & Schedules: Develop, maintain, and manage highly detailed project plans—utilizing Gantt charts and tracking tools—to map critical milestones, track dependencies, and ensure on-time project delivery.

  • Mitigate Risks: Proactively identify project risks, physical constraints, and resource blockers, establishing robust mitigation strategies to maintain continuous project momentum.

  • Engage Stakeholders: Deliver clear, concise, and proactive updates regarding project progress, risks, and milestones to engineering, operations, and leadership teams to ensure total organizational alignment.

  • Continuous Process Improvement: Standardize and optimize deployment methodologies, contributing new processes and documentation to elevate the efficiency of the Cloud Deployment Operations team.

 

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Proven Technical PM Experience: 7+ years of experience in technical project or program management, with a dedicated focus on infrastructure deployments, data center operations, hardware rollouts, or large-scale technical infrastructure projects.

  • Technical Infrastructure Acumen: A solid, foundational understanding of data center site readiness, networking, server deployments, and cloud readiness concepts.

  • Data Center Execution Knowledge: Demonstrated experience supporting hardware deployments, rack and stack operations, or physical layer infrastructure rollouts within complex data center environments.

  • Project Management Expertise: A proven track record of successfully managing complex technical projects from initial inception to completion, demonstrating meticulous organizational skills and attention to detail.

  • Mastery of PM Tools: Exceptional proficiency in using advanced project management tools, including Gantt charts, for planning, scheduling, and tracking project progress.

  • Stellar Communication Skills: Exceptional written and verbal communication abilities, with a natural tendency to anticipate stakeholder information needs and keep cross-functional leadership and engineering teams aligned.

  • Adaptable Problem-Solving: Strong analytical abilities and a resilient mindset, capable of navigating unforeseen physical constraints, resolving conflict, and adapting to changing priorities.

  • Travel Flexibility: Ability and willingness to travel to physical data center sites as needed to provide hands-on project oversight and support deployment activities.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Advanced Degrees: A preferred degree or field of study in Engineering, Computer Science, Construction Management, or a related technical field.

  • Industry Certifications: Active Project Management Professional (PMP) or Certified Data Center Design Professional (CDCDP) certifications.

  • Extended Experience: 10+ years managing large-scale, hyper-scale, or modular data center build-outs and physical layer installations.

  • Sustainable Infrastructure Passion: Experience or interest in working with alternative energy systems, stranded energy resources, or climate-aligned computing technologies.

 

Benefits:

Crusoe also offers a competitive benefits package designed to support financial security, health, and overall well-being, including pension contributions, private health and dental insurance, income protection, life assurance, and more.

 

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid as a salary or hourly. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.
