We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About this Role:

Crusoe Cloud is seeking a Senior Manager Engineering, Network Operations to own production reliability for our global network infrastructure, spanning edge, backbone, data center fabric, and GPU cluster interconnects. As our footprint of high-performance compute (HPC) and GPU-based AI infrastructure scales, you will build and lead the team responsible for incident response, root cause analysis, and operational excellence across a growing, 24x7, multi-region network.

You're accountable for the org's operational output: uptime, mean-time-to-resolution, and the rigor of every postmortem. You build and scale the operations team, set the standards for how incidents are handled and prevented, and are a trusted voice in planning conversations with sister Network Operations, Network Deployment, Architecture, and Site Reliability leadership.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Build and Lead the Organization: Own the operations org's structure and growth. Hire and develop Senior and Staff Network Production Operations Engineers across multiple sites and time zones, and build the management layer beneath you as the on-call footprint and device fleet scale.

  • Own Production Reliability: Be accountable for uptime across Crusoe's global edge, backbone, data center, and GPU cluster network, directly supporting AI workloads running across thousands of GPUs worldwide.

  • Own Incident Response: Set the org's incident command structure, escalation paths, and on-call model. Serve as an executive escalation point during high-severity network events, and ensure stakeholder communication is fast, clear, and accurate.

  • Own Root Cause Analysis and Remediation: Hold the org accountable for rigorous RCAs and for tracking remediation plans through to closure. Run cross-team post-incident reviews and drive systemic fixes in partnership with Architecture and Deployment.

  • Drive Operational Automation: Champion the shift from manual triage to automated detection, diagnosis, and remediation. Direct investment in tooling built on top of Crusoe's observability stack (streaming telemetry, SNMP, NetFlow, Kentik, Grafana, Prometheus, ThousandEyes) to reduce toil and accelerate MTTR.

  • Own SLIs/SLOs: Partner with Architecture and SRE to define, track, and report on network reliability metrics. Hold the org to those targets and escalate when they're at risk.

  • Run Executive-Level Cadence: Own operational reporting and risk escalation to Deployment, Architecture, and Site Reliability leadership. Represent the operations org in cross-functional and executive planning.

  • Champion Operational Standards: Ensure runbooks, escalation playbooks, and SOPs are current, followed, and continuously improved, with an eye toward what can be scripted or automated rather than performed manually.

  • Develop the Next Layer of Leaders: Coach engineers and emerging leads into stronger technical and operational leaders, and build the org's bench strength for future scale.

  • Partner Across the Network Organization: Work closely with Deployment leadership on handoff quality from build to production, and with Architecture on feedback from the field that should shape reference designs and standards.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 10+ years of experience in network engineering or network operations, including 4+ years managing engineers or engineering managers in a large-scale, 24x7 infrastructure environment.

  • Proven People and Org Leadership: Track record of building, scaling, and retaining high-performing operations teams. Experience managing managers or team leads is strongly preferred.

  • Incident and Reliability Ownership at Scale: Demonstrated ability to own production reliability across large, multi-region device fleets, with the reporting and risk management to match at an executive level.

  • Strong Technical Fluency: Expert working knowledge of BGP, EVPN-VXLAN, IS-IS, OSPF, MPLS, QoS, and TCP/IP in production data center environments; familiarity with RDMA/RoCE lossless fabrics (PFC, ECN, DCQCN) for GPU/HPC workloads; comfort with Arista (EOS) and Juniper (Junos) platforms in leaf-spine CLOS architectures, enough to credibly challenge your own team and partner teams without needing to be the org's deepest technical expert.

  • Automation Fluency: Working understanding of Python-based tooling, observability automation, and auto-remediation practices, sufficient to guide investment decisions and evaluate tooling proposals.

  • Executive Communication: Comfortable setting context, managing expectations, and delivering hard news to senior stakeholders across Deployment, Architecture, and Supply Chain, especially during and after high-severity incidents.

  • Operational and Strategic Judgment: Able to balance near-term incident pressure against longer-term org health, reliability standards, and team sustainability.

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience in hyperscale or ISP environments.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with NVIDIA/Mellanox networking platforms in GPU cluster environments.

  • Familiarity with Kentik or Arbor for traffic analysis and DDoS visibility.

  • Experience defining SLIs/SLOs in partnership with SRE or product teams.

  • Exposure to operating 10K+ device fleets across hyperscale or cloud environments.

  • Background building or scaling post-incident learning programs org-wide.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $230,000 - $280,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

As a Principal Organizational Development Strategist, you will serve as a high-impact individual contributor driving the health, design, and effectiveness of Crusoe’s organization as we rapidly scale. This role is ideal for a senior OD practitioner who thrives in fast-moving, ambiguous environments and blends strategic thinking with pragmatic execution.

Working as an internal consultant, you will independently diagnose organizational needs, challenge assumptions, and design interventions that improve team dynamics, strategic alignment, and leadership capabilities. Partnering closely with People Analytics, Talent Management, and executive leadership, you will turn data-driven insights into scalable solutions across our engineering, data center, manufacturing, and corporate teams. You will also develop and oversee Crusoe's enterprise coaching strategy.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Organizational Design & Effectiveness: Diagnose org health issues and support structural design initiatives—including role clarity, team operating models, decision-making frameworks, and change management.

  • Talent Strategy & Performance Alignment: Partner with the Performance & Talent Management (PTM) team to translate talent reviews and succession data into actionable development frameworks, capability building, and targeted interventions.

  • Engagement Insights & Action Planning: Analyze quantitative and qualitative engagement data alongside People Analytics to surface critical organizational insights, leading executive debriefs and targeted team action planning.

  • High-Stakes Facilitation & Advisory: Design, coordinate, and facilitate strategic offsites, leadership alignment sessions, and team effectiveness workshops; serve as a trusted, candid sounding board for business leaders.

  • Performance & Manager Enablement Tools: Build scalable, lightweight toolkits and resources that empower managers to set clear expectations, differentiate performance, deliver constructive feedback, and build psychological safety.

  • Executive Partnership & High EQ: Demonstrated ability to counsel senior leaders on leadership strategy and organizational health, combined with sound discretion when managing sensitive coaching situations.

  • Systemic Program Architecture: Design repeatably scalable tools and OD frameworks rather than one-off fixes, ensuring solutions adapt seamlessly to Crusoe’s evolving footprint.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 10-15+ Years of OD / Talent Experience: Deep experience in organizational development, talent management, industrial/organizational psychology, or internal/external management consulting, ideally within high-growth, technical, or industrial sectors.

  • Org Design & Diagnostic Expertise: Proven track record of diagnosing organizational friction, facilitating org design frameworks, and driving complex change initiatives without an established playbook.

  • Consultative & Executive Influence: Exceptional communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills; comfortable challenging senior executives respectfully and bringing structure to open-ended problems.

  • Data & Analytics Translation: Ability to synthesize complex people data, engagement trends, and operational metrics into compelling narratives and targeted interventions.

  • Agility & Resourcefulness: Proven ability to manage multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously, moving seamlessly from high-level strategy to hands-on execution.

 

Bonus Points

  • Advanced Degree: Master’s or Ph.D. in Organizational Development, I/O Psychology, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • Certifications: Formal training or certifications in executive coaching, change management (e.g., Prosci), org design, or assessment frameworks (e.g., Hogan, Birkman, DiSC).

  • Infrastructure Tech Context: Curiosity about AI, hardware manufacturing, and the physical data center infrastructure powering future technologies.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

     

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $195,000 - $230,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

 

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

As a Principal Organizational Development Strategist, you will serve as a high-impact individual contributor driving the health, design, and effectiveness of Crusoe’s organization as we rapidly scale. This role is ideal for a senior OD practitioner who thrives in fast-moving, ambiguous environments and blends strategic thinking with pragmatic execution.

Working as an internal consultant, you will independently diagnose organizational needs, challenge assumptions, and design interventions that improve team dynamics, strategic alignment, and leadership capabilities. Partnering closely with People Analytics, Talent Management, and executive leadership, you will turn data-driven insights into scalable solutions across our engineering, data center, manufacturing, and corporate teams. You will also develop and oversee Crusoe's enterprise coaching strategy.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Organizational Design & Effectiveness: Diagnose org health issues and support structural design initiatives—including role clarity, team operating models, decision-making frameworks, and change management.

  • Talent Strategy & Performance Alignment: Partner with the Performance & Talent Management (PTM) team to translate talent reviews and succession data into actionable development frameworks, capability building, and targeted interventions.

  • Engagement Insights & Action Planning: Analyze quantitative and qualitative engagement data alongside People Analytics to surface critical organizational insights, leading executive debriefs and targeted team action planning.

  • High-Stakes Facilitation & Advisory: Design, coordinate, and facilitate strategic offsites, leadership alignment sessions, and team effectiveness workshops; serve as a trusted, candid sounding board for business leaders.

  • Performance & Manager Enablement Tools: Build scalable, lightweight toolkits and resources that empower managers to set clear expectations, differentiate performance, deliver constructive feedback, and build psychological safety.

  • Executive Partnership & High EQ: Demonstrated ability to counsel senior leaders on leadership strategy and organizational health, combined with sound discretion when managing sensitive coaching situations.

  • Systemic Program Architecture: Design repeatably scalable tools and OD frameworks rather than one-off fixes, ensuring solutions adapt seamlessly to Crusoe’s evolving footprint.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 10-15+ Years of OD / Talent Experience: Deep experience in organizational development, talent management, industrial/organizational psychology, or internal/external management consulting, ideally within high-growth, technical, or industrial sectors.

  • Org Design & Diagnostic Expertise: Proven track record of diagnosing organizational friction, facilitating org design frameworks, and driving complex change initiatives without an established playbook.

  • Consultative & Executive Influence: Exceptional communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills; comfortable challenging senior executives respectfully and bringing structure to open-ended problems.

  • Data & Analytics Translation: Ability to synthesize complex people data, engagement trends, and operational metrics into compelling narratives and targeted interventions.

  • Agility & Resourcefulness: Proven ability to manage multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously, moving seamlessly from high-level strategy to hands-on execution.

 

Bonus Points

  • Advanced Degree: Master’s or Ph.D. in Organizational Development, I/O Psychology, Business Administration, or a related field.

  • Certifications: Formal training or certifications in executive coaching, change management (e.g., Prosci), org design, or assessment frameworks (e.g., Hogan, Birkman, DiSC).

  • Infrastructure Tech Context: Curiosity about AI, hardware manufacturing, and the physical data center infrastructure powering future technologies.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

     

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $175,000 - $205,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

 

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Accountant, Lease Accounting
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

As the Senior Accountant, Lease Accounting, you’ll own lease accounting operations at Crusoe from end to end. Our lease portfolio reflects a vertically integrated data center business: land, powered shell, build-to-suit, colocation, ground leases, equipment, and energy-related arrangements. Very few look alike, and no template will do the work for you. You’ll read each agreement, understand the deal behind it, work out how the terms translate under ASC 842, and build a repeatable monthly process around it.

In a typical month, you’ll abstract new leases and process modifications in LeaseQuery, post lease journal entries, reconcile LeaseQuery activity to the general ledger and AP, and partner with Legal, Real Estate, Data Center Development, Procurement, FP&A, and Tax to know about new deals and amendments before they are signed. You’ll thrive in this role if you’re detail-oriented, energized by non-standard problems, and driven to make the process better every month. You’ll also support quarterly disclosures, SOX controls, and external audit requests, with guidance from Technical Accounting on judgment-heavy items.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • LeaseQuery ownership: Own input of new leases and maintain schedules, including modifications, remeasurements, extensions, terminations, and reassessments

  • Lease inventory: Keep a complete inventory of executed agreements and amendments

  • ASC 842 application: Apply the standard to non-standard arrangements, including lease vs. non-lease components, embedded leases, build-to-suit, variable payments, and option assessments

  • Accounting memos: Work with manager to prepare lease abstracts and memos for new and modified leases, with Technical Accounting guidance on judgment-heavy items

  • Month-end close: Prepare and post lease journal entries for expense, interest, ROU amortization, and liability entries

  • Reconciliations: Reconcile LeaseQuery activity and lease liability and ROU asset balances to the general ledger and AP, and clear variances

  • Cross-functional partnership: Work with Legal, Real Estate, Data Center Development, Procurement, FP&A, Treasury, and Tax on lease intake, forecasts, and structuring

  • Process improvement: Document procedures and build intake workflows and automation that scale with the business

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • 4-7 years of accounting experience, including at least 1-2 years of hands-on ASC 842 lease accounting

  • Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Accounting, Finance, or a related field,

  • Experience with complex or non-standard lease agreements, not only standard real estate leases

  • Working knowledge of lease classification, modifications, remeasurement, and discount rate concepts

  • Experience with a lease accounting system (LeaseQuery preferred; LeaseAccelerator, CoStar, or similar)

  • Strong month-end close and reconciliation discipline in a public or public-ready environment

  • Advanced Excel skills and comfort with large data sets

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining accounting to non-accountants

Bonus Points:

  • CPA or CPA-eligible

  • Big 4 or public accounting experience, or experience at a high-growth technology or infrastructure company

  • Exposure to data center, energy, real estate development, or other capital-intensive industries

  • Experience with build-to-suit, powered shell, colocation, or ground lease structures

  • Familiarity with an ERP such as NetSuite or Sage Intacct, FloQast, and SOX controls

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $90,000.00 - $110,000.00. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Network Production Engineer, Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:
Crusoe Cloud is seeking a Senior Network Production Operations Engineer to support production reliability across our global network infrastructure, including edge, backbone, data center fabric, and GPU cluster interconnects. This is a hands-on production role focused on incident response, root cause analysis, and automation-driven operational execution that keeps our hyperscale AI infrastructure running at scale. Your work will directly affect the availability of AI workloads running across thousands of GPUs worldwide.

The ideal candidate is an experienced network engineer with solid operational experience in large-scale environments who thrives in high-pressure situations and takes pride in keeping systems healthy. You'll build automation to reduce operational toil, execute on established SLIs and SLOs, contribute to observability tooling, and serve as a responder during high-severity network events.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Production Reliability: Support uptime across Crusoe's global edge, backbone, data center, and GPU cluster network, directly supporting AI workloads at scale.

  • Operational Automation: Write and maintain Python-based tooling to reduce toil, automate common remediation workflows, and speed up mean time to resolution across the operations org.

  • Incident Response: Participate in high-severity network events — detection, triage, mitigation — and contribute to stakeholder communication and postmortem documentation.

  • Root Cause Analysis: Perform RCAs using existing and newly built tooling, and help drive remediation items to closure.

  • Observability: Build automation on top of Crusoe's monitoring stack (streaming telemetry, SNMP, NetFlow, Kentik, Grafana, Prometheus, ThousandEyes) to reduce manual triage and surface actionable signal faster.

  • Operational Standards: Maintain and improve runbooks, escalation playbooks, and SOPs, flagging opportunities for scripting or automation.

  • SLI/SLO Execution: Help build and maintain the automated dashboards and alerting that back reliability metrics, in partnership with Architecture and SRE teams.

  • Collaboration: Work closely with Architecture and SRE teams to execute on operational excellence initiatives and improve day-to-day practices.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 5+ years of production network engineering experience with a focus on operations, incident response, and reliability in large-scale or internet-scale environments.

  • Strong Python and scripting proficiency: comfortable writing diagnostic tooling and automation scripts, and extending existing automation pipelines.

  • Hands-on experience with observability and monitoring tools including streaming telemetry, SNMP, NetFlow/sFlow, Grafana, Prometheus, and ThousandEyes, and the ability to script against their APIs.

  • Experience operating RDMA/RoCE lossless fabrics for GPU or HPC workloads, including familiarity with PFC, ECN, and DCQCN tuning.

  • Solid hands-on knowledge of BGP, EVPN-VXLAN, IS-IS, OSPF, MPLS, QoS, and TCP/IP in production data center environments.

  • Proficiency with Arista (EOS) and Juniper (Junos) platforms in leaf-spine CLOS architectures across multi-vendor environments.

  • Comfort operating large device fleets across multi-region environments with on-call responsibility.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with NVIDIA/Mellanox networking platforms in GPU cluster environments.

  • Familiarity with Kentik or Arbor for traffic analysis and DDoS visibility.

  • Exposure to contributing to SLIs and SLOs alongside SRE or product teams.

  • Exposure to operating 10K+ device fleets across hyperscale or cloud environments.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off & paid holidays

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

Compensation Range:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $230,000 - $280,000 plus Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

We're looking for a Commercial Strategy & Pricing Manager to own our deal desk function and lead the implementation, management, and ongoing optimization of our CPQ. This role sits at the intersection of pricing strategy, sales enablement, and systems ownership. You’ll be the Revenue Operations partner for Account Executives navigating complex, technical deals, while also building the infrastructure that lets the sales org quote and close faster.

We're specifically looking for someone who has experience setting defensible prices with novel deal structures with limited comps in a dynamic market. Our is a technical, consultative sale, where deal complexity, competitive dynamics, dynamic pricing make "one price fits all" impossible.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Deal Desk & Pricing Strategy

    • Advise AEs on deal structuring, negotiation tactics, and creative packaging to protect margin while removing friction to close. Serve as the primary point of contact for AEs on non-standard deals, terms, pricing, and discounting.

    • Set and continuously adjust pricing in response to a dynamic market, translating fast-moving conditions into clear, real-time pricing guidance for the GTM , product, and Finance teams.

    • Conduct ongoing market rate analysis leveraging any competitor pricing intelligence, internal win/loss data, and segment-level price sensitivity to recalibrate price points, discounts, and approval thresholds

    • Own the deal approval workflow, ensuring the deals get the right level of scrutiny without becoming a bottleneck. Partner with Sales Leadership, Finance, and Legal on exception approvals, non-standard terms, and contract structuring

    • Track deal desk metrics: discount trends, approval cycle time, win rates by deal type, price realization. Build dashboards and reporting to give leadership visibility into pricing trends and deal desk throughput.

    CPQ Ownership

    • Own end-to-end implementation, configuration, and maintenance of the CPQ system

    • Build and maintain product bundles, pricing rules, discount schedules, approval matrices, and quote templates. Continuously audit CPQ data integrity (product catalog, price books, rules logic) to ensure quotes reflect our latest pricing strategy.

    • Partner with Sales, Finance, and Product on new product launches, packaging changes, and price book updates, translating them into CPQ configuration

    • Identify and eliminate friction in the quote-to-cash process. Reduce quote turnaround time and manual workarounds

    • Train, enable, and support AEs and sales managers on CPQ best practices.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 4-7 years of experience in Revenue Operations focusing on running a deal desk function, advising AEs on deal structuring, pricing strategy, and contract negotiations, preferably within a high growth, B2B technology environment.

  • Proven track record setting and adjusting prices in a dynamic, fast-moving market. Strong understanding of market rate benchmarking and competitive pricing analysis. Experience pricing usage-based and consumption-based products

  • Hands-on CPQ implementation and administration experience (Salesforce CPQ, DealHub, PandaDoc, Zuora, or similar)

  • Strong Excel/Sheets modeling skills for pricing analysis; SQL or reporting tool experience a plus

  • Experience at a growth-stage company where you've had to build or rebuild processes from scratch

Bonus Points

  • Experience with hyperscalers, GPU clouds, or high-performance compute environments.

  • Familiarity with large-scale AI training and inference architectures.

  • Strong network in the AI/ML and enterprise technology ecosystem.

  • Track record of working with Fortune 500 enterprises and digitally native businesses on transformative infrastructure deals.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $155,000 to $185,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.title: Staff Integrated Capacity Planner
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

At Crusoe, the Capacity Planning & Efficiency team operates at the critical intersection of all Crusoe products, services, and underlying physical infrastructure. This role owns the integrated planning system itself - the connective tissue that turns long-range strategy into a committed, buildable, fundable plan. You will run the end-to-end planning rhythm across every resource class: GPU and accelerated AI fabrics, compute, storage (File, Object, and Block), network, and the data center power and space that gates all of it. You will own long-range planning, the integrated business planning cycle, allocation and constraints planning, the operating calendar, and the supply chain and financial commitments that flow out of them.

This is a single pane of glass role. Where domain planners go deep on one resource, you go wide across all of them and arbitrate - reconciling demand signals against supply commitments, hardware lead times, site readiness, and capital and operating budgets into one defensible plan the company runs on. You will not own any single resource domain; you own the system that reconciles them all, and the calls that fall out of it when supply is short. You will partner directly with Finance to translate the capacity plan into demand capex and opex forecasts, and you will be the person leadership turns to when a constraint, a slip, or a demand surprise forces a re-plan. This role is uniquely positioned to maximize fleet utilization with company-wide impact, directly supporting Crusoe's mission to align the future of computing with environmental sustainability.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Long-Range Capacity Planning: Own the multi-year outlook across GPU, compute, storage, network, and the power and site energization schedules that gate all of it, and build the scenario models - demand cases, technology transitions, refresh and decommission waves - that inform where Crusoe commits capital and builds next.

  • Integrated Business Planning: Run the IBP/S&OP cycle end to end - demand review, supply review, reconciliation, and the executive decision forum. Maintain both the unconstrained demand signal and the constrained committed plan; the gap between them is how Crusoe sizes what it is leaving on the table.

  • Constraints & Bottleneck Planning: Maintain a live model of what is actually binding - silicon allocation, supplier lead times, power energization, rack and network availability, deployment labor - quantify the impact of each, and drive every mitigation to a decision.

  • Allocation & Arbitration: Own the framework that decides which demand gets which capacity when supply is short - prioritization rules, trade-off analysis, and a clean escalation path when the call has to go to leadership.

  • Plan of Record & Operating Calendar: Design and run the planning calendar that synchronizes Cloud Engineering, Supply Chain, Data Center Operations, Product, and Finance. Govern the plan of record - commitment time fences, what is frozen versus still movable, and what triggers a re-plan.

  • Demand & Bookings Translation: Convert contracted commitments, backlog, ramp schedules, and on-demand growth into resource-level forecasts, including the attach ratios that link GPU capacity to storage, network, and compute. Manage forecast accuracy and bias as owned metrics.

  • Supply Chain Integration: Translate the plan into supplier commitments, purchase timing, and buffer strategy, navigating global lead times and allocation constraints with Supply Chain and Server Hardware Engineering.

  • Financial Integration: Interface directly with Finance and Product to drive demand capex and opex forecasts off the capacity plan, own the linkage to unit economics, depreciation schedules, and utilization targets, and explain the variances when plan and actuals diverge.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Proven Integrated Planning Expertise: 8+ years in infrastructure capacity planning, IBP/S&OP, supply and demand planning, systems engineering, or technical program management, including end-to-end ownership of a recurring planning cycle. Strong candidates come from either deep infrastructure or formal planning backgrounds - we expect to teach the other half.

  • Breadth Across Resource Classes: Technical fluency across compute, storage (File, Object, and Block), network, and accelerated computing, plus the power, space, and cooling constraints that govern deployment. Deep expertise in one domain is not required; holding your own with the people who have it is.

  • Supply Chain Fluency: Practical experience with lead times, supplier allocation, buffer strategy, and converting a plan into committed purchase orders and delivered hardware.

  • Financial Acumen: Comfort operating in capex and opex terms - building demand-driven capital forecasts and defending the numbers in front of Finance and leadership.

  • Modeling Craft: Expert-level Excel or Google Sheets. You build models other people can inherit, audit, and run without you - clear structure, documented assumptions, versioned, and still trustworthy several quarters after they were built.

  • Hyper-Growth Experience: Planning inside high-growth public cloud environments or massively distributed systems, where the plan changes and the rhythm still has to hold.

  • Exceptional Influence & Communication: Structured narrative delivery, crisp documentation, and executive-grade presentations that turn a complex plan into a decision leadership can make in the room. You will run a planning cycle spanning five organizations without managing any of them, and escalate cleanly when alignment is not reachable.

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Mathematics, Data Science, or an equivalent technical field.

Bonus Points

  • Experience standing up an S&OP or integrated business planning function from scratch, including the cadence, data model, and decision forums.

  • Experience building or defining foundational product requirements for custom in-house planning, provisioning, or capacity modeling software.

  • Hands-on quantitative modeling skill - SQL, Python, or optimization and simulation methods applied to constrained allocation problems.

  • Direct experience planning GPU clusters and accelerated AI computing fabrics at scale.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $200,000-$240,000+ Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Principal Hardware Product Manager - Spark
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the role:

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI Factory company accelerating the abundance of energy and intelligence through modular infrastructure. We are seeking a Principal Hardware Product Manager to own the multi-year Hardware roadmap and Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) for Crusoe Spark™, our modular datacenter.

 

In this role, “hardware” and “product” refers to the physical infrastructure of the Spark module: structural steel modules, RPPs, DLC cooling loops, CDUs, chillers, piping headers, electrical and mechanical systems, and power distribution gear. Compute hardware (servers, GPUs, storage, networking, and rack specifications) is owned by Cloud Product. Cloud Product defines the compute needs; you define the Hardware that houses and powers it.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

I. Physical Module Roadmap & Design Requirements

  • Hardware Roadmap Ownership: Own and maintain the multi-year Spark hardware roadmap.

  • Hardware PRD Authorship: Author precise Spark PRDs for physical modules, translating compute needs into concrete structural, thermal, and electrical specifications.

  • Compute-to-Hardware Translation: Receive Cloud Product’s GPU, server, and rack requirements and translate them into modular physical configurations - power envelopes/distribution, rack weights, fluid specs. Partner with Cloud Product leads and own the facility-side interface: power distribution to racks, fluid flow, rack weight and floor loadings etc.

  • Physical Version Management: Manage hardware generation transitions. Define cut-in criteria, retrofit rules, module-side accommodation of rack footprint, loading, and cooling interface per Cloud Product’s rack specifications., and documentation required for manufacturing release.

II. Requirements Ownership & Engineering Partnership

  • Spark Hardware TPM Alignment: Work in lockstep with Spark Hardware TPMs and engineering discipline leads (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural, Thermal) to guide physical development from concept to build.

  • Requirements Discipline: Set clear product hardware requirements (module power distribution capacity, thermal capacity, transportability) and hold hardware engineering teams accountable without prescribing detailed sub-component implementation.

  • Design Partner Leadership: Serve as the primary design contact for external architecture, engineering, and modular design firms.

  • Requirements intake from Cloud Product: Collaborate with Cloud Product teams to ensure that the physical Spark module hardware supports the GPU & rack-level architecture needs. Translate GPU/rack compute needs directly into physical facility capabilities (fluid flow rates, power specs, structural building and frame requirements).

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Physical Infrastructure Roadmap Expertise: 10-15 years owning multi-year physical product roadmaps, with a proven track record shipping complex hardware or heavy mechanical/electrical infrastructure.

  • Disciplined Hardware PRD Management: Expertise in writing clear hardware product requirements (PRDs) for physical systems and requisite sub-systems separating product requirements from engineering requirements, and designing to requirements supplied by an upstream customer or platform team.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Track record driving alignment across mechanical, electrical, structural, thermal, and manufacturing teams during first-of-a-kind builds.

  • Clear Technical Communication: Exceptional written communication with emphasis on precise engineering trade-off documentation and executive-level clarity.

 

Education

  • Required: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Systems, or a related physical engineering discipline.

  • Strongly Preferred: Master’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical or Electrical) and/or an active Professional Engineer (PE) license in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

 

Bonus Points

  • DLC & Advanced Thermal Design: Experience specifying liquid cooling loops, CDUs, or secondary fluid loops for high-density compute environments.

  • Data Center Infrastructure: Product experience in physical data center infrastructure, high-voltage distribution, industrial cooling, or heavy modular/prefab hardware.

  • Advanced Power Distribution: Experience specifying 800V DC or medium-to-low voltage data center power topologies.

  • Modular Construction / Offsite Fabrication: Hands-on experience with modular/prefab construction, containerized enclosures, or advanced offsite manufacturing.

  • Tooling Fluency: Familiarity with CAD/BIM platforms (Revit, SolidWorks), electrical single-line diagrams (SLDs), or CFD/thermal simulation workflows.

 

This Role Is Not a Good Fit If:

  • You’ve owned physical infrastructure products end to end: You have defined, built, and shipped complex mechanical enclosures, power distribution products, or industrial systems, and you’re energized by designing steel, piping, pumps, and power distribution where next-gen compute runs inside.

  • You turn upstream requirements into buildable design: You’re comfortable receiving requirements from a platform or customer team and translating them into precise structural, thermal, and electrical specifications, with clear trade-offs documented.

  • You’d rather define the design than run the schedule: You want to set physical design requirements and make the trade-offs that shape the module, and you partner with TPMs and engineering leads who run the schedule and program logistics.

 

How This Role Works with Cloud Product:

About the role:

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI Factory company accelerating the abundance of energy and intelligence through modular infrastructure. We are seeking a Principal Hardware Product Manager to own the multi-year Hardware roadmap and Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) for Crusoe Spark™, our modular datacenter.

 

In this role, “hardware” and “product” refers to the physical infrastructure of the Spark module: structural steel modules, RPPs, DLC cooling loops, CDUs, chillers, piping headers, electrical and mechanical systems, and power distribution gear. Compute hardware (servers, GPUs, storage, networking, and rack specifications) is owned by Cloud Product. Cloud Product defines the compute needs; you define the Hardware that houses and powers it.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

I. Physical Module Roadmap & Design Requirements

 - Hardware Roadmap Ownership: Own and maintain the multi-year Spark hardware roadmap.

 - Hardware PRD Authorship: Author precise Spark PRDs for physical modules, translating compute needs into concrete structural, thermal, and electrical specifications.

 - Compute-to-Hardware Translation: Receive Cloud Product’s GPU, server, and rack requirements and translate them into modular physical configurations - power envelopes/distribution, rack weights, fluid specs. Partner with Cloud Product leads and own the facility-side interface: power distribution to racks, fluid flow, rack weight and floor loadings etc.

 - Physical Version Management: Manage hardware generation transitions. Define cut-in criteria, retrofit rules, module-side accommodation of rack footprint, loading, and cooling interface per Cloud Product’s rack specifications., and documentation required for manufacturing release.

 - Spark Hardware TPM Alignment: Work in lockstep with Spark Hardware TPMs and engineering discipline leads (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural, Thermal) to guide physical development from concept to build.

 - Design Partner Leadership: Serve as the primary design contact for external architecture, engineering, and modular design firms.

 - Requirements intake from Cloud Product: Collaborate with Cloud Product teams to ensure that the physical Spark module hardware supports the GPU & rack-level architecture needs. About the Role:

We are seeking a highly skilled, hands-on Senior level performance engineer who thrives on deep technical challenges. The ideal candidate possesses a mastery of Linux kernel systems and low-level optimization, with a collaborative mindset to drive cross-functional projects. This is a full-time position where you will roll up your sleeves to perform direct performance benchmarking and system tuning, making a tangible impact on Crusoe’s global compute operations.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • System Performance Benchmarking: Design and execute rigorous benchmarks to analyze system behavior, identifying bottlenecks and opportunities for performance enhancement.

  • Kernel Optimization: Develop and implement low-level optimizations within the Linux kernel to maximize efficiency and system throughput.

  • Hands-on Development: Write and maintain high-performance code using Go, C, C++, or Rust to drive infrastructure improvements.

  • Data Plane Tuning: Focus on data plane performance, ensuring our cloud architecture meets the high-speed requirements of modern AI workloads.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with Software Infrastructure, Product, and other engineering teams to align performance initiatives with broader organizational goals.

  • Technical Problem-Solving: Actively troubleshoot complex system issues, applying an analytical approach to ensure reliability and scalability.

  • Strategic Knowledge Sharing: Contribute to team documentation and best practices, fostering a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement.

     

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Linux Kernel Mastery: Deep expertise in Linux system internals and kernel-level programming is essential for this role.

  • Programming Proficiency: Expert-level skills in Go, C, and C++ (Rust is also a strong asset).

  • Systems Performance Mindset: A proven track record of hands-on performance tuning, benchmarking, and optimization in complex environments.

  • Educational Foundation: A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

  • Collaborative Spirit: Ability to work effectively within cross-functional teams, communicating complex technical concepts clearly to stakeholders.

  • AI Ecosystem Familiarity: Experience or exposure to the Artificial Intelligence/Cloud ecosystem and standard industry tooling.

     

Bonus Points:

  • Hands-on experience with Rust development.

  • Prior experience working in high-scale cloud or infrastructure engineering environments

  • Deep familiarity with performance-critical infrastructure components beyond the kernel layer.

  • Experience with specific low-level performance analysis and tracing tools.

     

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $170,000 - $205,000. + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

About the Role:

The Crusoe Cloud Software Development team is seeking a passionate and experienced Senior Staff Software Engineer specializing in Linux Kernel Security. This critical role is essential in strengthening the security posture of our core Linux kernel and operating system components, which underpin our cutting-edge hardware and software solutions for the AI cloud. A deep understanding of Linux kernel internals, security vulnerabilities, mitigation techniques, and secure development practices is paramount for developing reliable, high-assurance systems. This is a full-time position.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Kernel Hardening & CVE Triage: Implement kernel security enhancements, manage configuration hardening, and triage incoming CVEs to assess severity and exploitability.

  • Access Control, Boot Security & Guardrails: Enforce mandatory access controls, secure the boot path, and establish CI guardrails and fuzzing coverage to prevent regressions.

  • Vulnerability Research & Analysis: Research vulnerabilities across kernel, driver, and OS components to build proactive mitigations and backport non-trivial upstream fixes to production.

  • Secure Development Practices: Establish and advocate for secure coding standards and best practices for kernel-level development. Conduct security-focused code reviews to identify and eliminate potential vulnerabilities early in the development lifecycle.

  • Security Auditing & Tools: Utilize and develop specialized tools for kernel security auditing, fuzzing, static analysis, and dynamic analysis to uncover hidden vulnerabilities and ensure compliance with security policies.

  • Incident Response Support: Provide expert support during security incidents involving kernel or OS-level compromises, assisting with root-cause analysis, containment, and recovery efforts.

  • Performance and Security Balance: Work to ensure that security enhancements do not unduly impact system performance, especially critical for our high-performance AI infrastructure.

  • First 90 days: Own kernel CVE triage end to end and have shipped at least one backported fix through our full release path. You have an independent read on where our kernel configuration is weakest.

  • First year: Kernel security response has a defined SLA by severity and we consistently hit it. A hardening baseline is defined, enforced in CI, and rolled out across supported SKUs. Cloud Hypervisor has been audited and the highest-value isolation gaps are closed or scheduled.

  • Cloud Hypervisor & Isolation: Audit, harden, and reduce privilege across Cloud Hypervisor device models and vhost-user datapaths, contributing upstream security fixes and advancing confidential computing primitives (AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX).

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate closely with other engineering teams (hardware, hypervisor, OS development, cloud infrastructure, and security operations) to integrate security best practices and ensure a comprehensive security strategy across the stack.

  • Technical Leadership: Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers on kernel security best practices, fostering a culture of security awareness and excellence.

  • Debugging and Root-Cause Analysis: Debug and root-cause a variety of complex security-related issues at the kernel level.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Linux Kernel Security Expertise: Proven deep knowledge of Linux kernel internals (e.g., memory management, process scheduling, system calls, I/O subsystems) with a strong focus on security aspects.

  • Vulnerability & Exploitation Knowledge: Solid understanding of common kernel vulnerabilities (e.g., privilege escalation, information disclosure, denial of service) and associated exploitation techniques.

  • Security Mitigations: Experience with existing Linux kernel security mitigations (e.g., ASLR, DEP/NX, SMEP/SMAP, KASLR, namespaces, cgroups, LSMs like SELinux/AppArmor).

  • Secure Coding: Strong background in secure coding principles and experience conducting security-focused code reviews, particularly in C.

  • Debugging & Analysis Tools: Proficiency with kernel debugging tools (e.g., GDB, crash, kgdb) and security analysis tools (e.g., valgrind, address sanitizers, fuzzers).

  • Hardware Security Concepts: Familiarity with hardware-assisted security features (e.g., Intel SGX, AMD SEV, ARM TrustZone) and their relevance to kernel security.

  • Education & Experience: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, and a minimum of 5 years of relevant industry experience with at least 3 years focused on low-level operating systems or kernel security.

  • Safety and Compliance: Must be able to pass a background check.

  • Company Values: Embody the Company values.

  • Experience dealing with CVE Remediation and automation

  • First 90 days: You own kernel CVE triage end to end and have shipped at least one backported fix through our full release path. You have an independent read on where our kernel configuration is weakest.

  • First year: Kernel security response has a defined SLA by severity and we consistently hit it. A hardening baseline is defined, enforced in CI, and rolled out across supported SKUs. Cloud Hypervisor has been audited and the highest-value isolation gaps are closed or scheduled.

 

Bonus Points

  • Experience with specific kernel security projects or contributions to open-source kernel security initiatives.

  • Familiarity with hypervisor security and the interaction between the hypervisor and the guest kernel's security.

  • Experience with hardware security modules (HSMs) or Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs).

  • Background in offensive security or penetration testing at the kernel level.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $250,000 - $300,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI Factory accelerating energy and compute infrastructure. We are seeking a New Product Introduction (NPI) Engineering Leader in the Spark Business Unit to bridge Spark Hardware Design with enterprise execution.

In this role, “hardware” and “product” refers to the physical infrastructure of the Spark module: structural steel modules, RPPs, DLC cooling loops, CDUs, chillers, piping headers, electrical and mechanical systems, and power distribution gear. Compute hardware (servers, GPUs, storage, networking, and rack specifications) is owned by Cloud Product. Sitting on the Spark Hardware product team, you are the single-threaded owner ensuring the physical module is fully verified for handoff to manufacturing. You gather and lead everything needed to introduce Spark hardware modules into the Crusoe ecosystem, orchestrating the NPI phase-gate process to turn the design team’s output into one complete NPI packet. You don’t run manufacturing. You equip and support Manufacturing and Supply Chain with clean design baselines, complete documentation, and qualified inputs to build at scale.

What You'll Be Working On:
I. Gate Framework & Hardware Release Authority

  • Framework Ownership: Own the Spark hardware NPI framework (Concept to Launch) within the Spark BU to align design engineering progress with enterprise release readiness.

  • Release Authority: Define design release readiness for physical Spark modules. Ensure design freeze and production gates clear only when product specs, subsystem verification tests, and manufacturing handoff criteria are fully met.

  • Design Package Quality: Enforce gate discipline to resolve design, thermal interface, and electrical interference issues in engineering well before drawings and BOMs reach manufacturing, such that manufacturing receives a clean and complete NPI packet.

  • Product Readiness Scorecard: Maintain an objective hardware readiness scorecard (modeled on MRL/PRR standards) providing clear product maturity visibility to leadership and manufacturing.

  • Design Baseline & Change Control: Manage engineering baseline transitions into production. Support ECO/ECN workflows in PLM so Supply Chain and Manufacturing operate against clear, unambiguous release states.

  • Handoff Package Completeness: Deliver complete hardware release packages to downstream teams, including CAD models, structural drawings, electrical single-lines, fluid schematics, multi-level BOMs, and factory acceptance test (FAT) criteria.

II. Enterprise Enablement & Subsystem Integration

  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Translate Spark hardware roadmaps into actionable handoff schedules for Supply Chain, Quality, Manufacturing, and Construction well ahead of production builds.

  • Validation Campaigns: Plan and orchestrate first-of-a-kind (FOAK) prototype builds. Participate on the shop floor during validation runs to feed design-for-manufacturability (DFM) insights back to engineering.

  • Manufacturing Enablement: Partner directly with Manufacturing, ensuring their engineering team has the documentation, assembly instructions, tooling access, and test specs for a smooth line setup.

  • Supply Chain Synchronization: Partner with Supply Chain early to identify long-lead electrical and thermal components, ensuring supplier vetting before design freeze.

  • Subsystem Hardware Integration: Ensure core physical elements (mechanical shells, structural frames, Direct-to-Chip cooling loops, 800V DC distribution, and rack interfaces) are validated as a cohesive package prior to release.

  • Downstream Deployment Handoff: Ensure released packages include clear interface control documents (ICDs) usable by site engineering, civil construction, and commissioning teams.

III. Launch & Continuous Improvement

  • Ramp Support: Partner closely with Manufacturing during initial production ramps to resolve design friction or supply exceptions and protect schedules.

  • Single Source of Truth: Provide executive stakeholders and Spark BU leadership unified visibility into release readiness, subsystem risks, and manufacturing enablement.

  • Closed-Loop Feedback: Lead post-launch reviews following build campaigns to capture field and factory feedback, continually refining release standards for future hardware generations.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Education

  • Required: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial, or Systems Engineering, or a related physical engineering discipline.

Experience

  • 10 to 15 years in hardware NPI, technical program management, or systems engineering within a physical hardware organization.

  • Direct experience holding release authority and guiding complex hardware programs from concept through transfer-to-manufacturing.

  • Fluent in Level of Development (LOD) frameworks (i.e. LOD 100–400).

  • Proven track record equipping manufacturing, supply chain, and field teams with high-quality release packages.

Technical Depth
NPI & Handoff Methodology: Mastery of phase-gate frameworks, hardware verification, and formal transfer-to-manufacturing processes.

  • PLM & Configuration Management: Expertise in PLM systems, multi-level hardware BOMs, revision control, and structured ECO/ECN workflows.

  • Design for Excellence (DFX): Practical knowledge of DFM, DFA, and DFT principles to optimize design packages for assembly and testing prior to release.

  • Quality & Validation: FMEA, First Article Inspection (FAI), hydrostatic leak testing, and electrical high-pot testing standards.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with modular, containerized, or prefabricated infrastructure product lines.

  • Familiarity with high-density data center physical requirements (fluid manifolds, heat exchangers, heavy electrical equipment).

  • A collaborative approach combining rigorous design package standards with a commitment to cross-functional empowerment.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $225,000 - $255,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About This Role:

Crusoe is seeking a Staff Electrical Engineer to join our Power Systems organization. This role is a high-level technical position responsible for the design, construction, commissioning, and long-term operational success of our power plant facilities across the USA. You will serve as the primary subject matter expert for power generation assets, bridging the gap between front-end design and field execution.

 

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Engineering & Design: Lead front-end engineering for capital projects, including the layout and sizing of power systems. Review one-lines, wiring diagrams, schematics, electrical studies, and control narratives to ensure they meet company design specifications.

  • QA/QC Oversight: Review vendor drawings, check wiring diagrams against schematics, and ensure all design deliverables from consultants meet project specifications.

  • Project Execution: Provide technical guidance during the construction and commissioning of power plant assets. Support and provide input to field teams and third-party consultants on complex electrical issues.

  • Operational Support: Partner with Field Operations to troubleshoot electrical failures, perform root-cause analysis, and optimize existing power infrastructure for maximum uptime.

  • Technical System Integration: Apply deep technical expertise across power generation assets, including generator physics and operations. Specify and integrate high and medium voltage equipment such as 34.5 kV GIS (Gas Insulated Switchgear) indoor units, GSU (Generator Step-Up) Transformers, and MV/LV Switchgear and MCCs (Motor Control Centers).

  • Advanced Controls: Utilize working knowledge of Governor and AVR (Automatic Voltage Regulator) controls.

  • Modern Protocols & Studies: Implement the IEC 61850 standard, including GOOSE & MMS protocols. Conduct Protection & Control coordination studies and fault analysis.

 

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education & Experience: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering (BSEE) and a minimum of 6+ years in industrial electrical engineering.

  • Standards & Compliance: Expert working knowledge of NEC application to industrial installations.

  • Communication Skills: Ability to work effectively with both engineers and operations personnel.

  • Travel: Ability to travel approximately 20% to project sites.

  • Technical Expertise: Comprehensive understanding of generator physics and operations. Proficiency in Protection & Control coordination studies and fault analysis. Knowledge of the IEC 61850 standard.

  • Company Values: Embody the Company values.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with Simple and Combined Cycle Turbine Generators (10 MW – 600 MW) and Reciprocating Engines (3 MW – 20 MW).

  • Experience in implementation and management of Microgrid Controllers.

  • Knowledge of best practices for the synchronization of islanded electrical systems.

  • Experience with Hardware-in-the-Loop testing and Electromagnetic Transient (EMT) studies.

  • Professional Engineering (PE) license in Texas or Colorado.

  • Experience with power modeling software (e.g., ETAP or SKM).

  • Previous experience managing utility-scale interconnects.

  • Power Generation or Oil & Gas industry experience.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

     

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000 -$180,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDCORP)
