As a Senior Staff Commissioning Engineer on the Spark team, you will own commissioning for these modules. That covers factory testing in Brighton, site integration, integrated systems testing, and formal turnover to operations. Spark moves much of commissioning into the factory. You will build the test standards, procedures, and quality gates that let every module ship ready to energize and come online quickly at the site. You will be the technical authority for mechanical and controls commissioning across the Spark fleet, and you will turn lessons from each deployment into improvements in module design, manufacturing, and the commissioning program itself. This is a full-time role.

What You'll Be Working On

  • Commissioning Program Ownership: Own the Spark commissioning program end to end. Define how L1–L5 activities split between the factory and the site, and build standardized Cx plans, test scripts, and turnover packages that scale across a fleet of modules.

  • Factory Testing: Lead factory acceptance and integration testing of mechanical, cooling, and controls systems at the Brighton factory so every module meets specification before it ships.

  • Quality Gates: Set first-article inspection, in-process quality checks, and ship-readiness criteria with manufacturing and quality teams. Hold shipment when a module does not meet them.

  • Site Integration and IST: Oversee installation validation, startup, and integrated systems testing at deployment sites. Verify that modules connect correctly to site power, cooling, and network infrastructure.

  • Design and Manufacturing Feedback: Track commissioning issues across builds, identify root causes, and drive fixes into module design, supplier quality, and factory processes.

  • Vendor and CxA Management: Manage third-party commissioning agents and equipment suppliers, including scope, schedule, deliverables, and factory witness testing of purchased components.

  • Technical Escalation: Serve as the primary escalation point for mechanical and controls issues in the factory and in the field, from troubleshooting through formal closure.

  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Align engineering, manufacturing, construction, controls, and operations teams on commissioning scope, roles, and readiness milestones.

  • Operations Handover: Deliver complete, accurate turnover documentation. Support the transition to operations through training coordination and post-handover support.

  • Safety and Compliance: Enforce safety, compliance, and regulatory requirements across factory and site commissioning activities.

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • Experience: 8+ years in data center commissioning, construction, or critical infrastructure delivery, including ownership of commissioning programs across multiple projects.

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field; equivalent commissioning experience considered.

  • Commissioning Depth: Expert knowledge of L1–L5 commissioning and the documentation and testing requirements at each level.

  • Cooling and Controls Systems: Hands-on commissioning experience with data center cooling infrastructure, including liquid cooling such as CDUs and direct-to-chip systems, and BMS and controls systems.

  • Factory Testing: Experience developing and running factory acceptance or factory witness testing for prefabricated, skid-mounted, or modular equipment.

  • Technical Documentation: Ability to review and interpret construction drawings, P&IDs, single-line diagrams, sequences of operation, submittals, and test procedures.

  • Vendor Accountability: Track record managing third-party commissioning agents and holding suppliers accountable to scope, schedule, and quality.

  • Travel: Willingness to travel to the Brighton factory and deployment sites as required (up to 75%).

Bonus Points

  • CxA, CCP, or equivalent commissioning certification.

  • Experience commissioning in a manufacturing or production-line environment, or scaling a commissioning process from first article to volume production.

  • Experience with high-density AI and GPU compute deployments.

  • Experience building digital commissioning tools, test automation, or systems for tracking test results across a fleet.

  • Working knowledge of electrical distribution (switchgear, UPS, PDUs) where it interfaces with mechanical and controls systems.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $175,000 -$215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

About the Role: We are seeking a highly motivated Electrical Design Engineer to act as the primary technical bridge between internal stakeholders, construction partners, design firms, and our customers. This role focuses on the design phase of Crusoe’s data center campus projects. You will ensure that large-scale power distribution systems are designed for safety, compliance, reliability, constructability, and speed of execution.

This position requires an electrical professional with a strong mix of electrical construction and design methodologies, power distribution equipment specification, and a strong background in fast paced design and project management.

The role is in office with options to be located in San Francisco, Denver, or Dallas. Travel will vary, but is anticipated to be 25%.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Advance design for large-scale data center campuses from conceptual sketches to construction ready sets.

  • The position may support various initiatives in support of Crusoe’s mission to accelerate intelligence in addition to campus design.

  • Design and specify electrical equipment for critical power path - including power transformers, LV/MV switchgear, UPS, data center building power distribution, protection and controls, auto transfer, switchboards, cabling, busway, panels, etc

  • Perform critical technical calculations and system studies, including short-circuit, protection, arc-flash, load flow, harmonics, dynamic transient analysis studies

  • Review drawings, specifications, and shop drawings prepared by external consultants to ensure strict compliance with the project’s Basis of Design.

  • Support the Field Engineering team by aiding rapid resolution of RFIs, reviewing submittals, and providing design clarifications during the construction phase.

  • Participate in factory witness testing (FWT) for engineered or complex electrical equipment.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering.

  • 10+ years of electrical engineering design experience, with a heavy emphasis on data centers or mission-critical industrial facilities.

  • Expert-level knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC) and relevant NFPA/IEEE standards.

  • Proficiency with engineering software (AutoCAD, Revit, ETAP, SKM)

  • Proven track record of successfully taking complex electrical designs from schematic phases through to construction execution.

  • Excellent communication skills to coordinate closely with mechanical, real estate, and power engineering teams.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Active Professional Engineer (PE) License.

  • Experience modeling systems with alternative energy inputs and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS).

  • Familiarity with SCADA and Emergency Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS).

  • Mega Project in-field construction experience for data centers or similar mission critical facilities.

  • Experience working with hyperscale clients in a fast paced design/build environment.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $195,000 -$225,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.title: Senior Escalation Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe Cloud runs some of the most demanding AI workloads in the world on large-scale GPU infrastructure. When something goes wrong for a customer, the path from first report to root cause often crosses several teams: Support Engineering, Product Engineering, SRE, Networking, Storage, and Data Center Operations. As Escalation Manager, you'll own that path.

Reporting to the Director, Customer Support Engineering, within Cloud Go-To-Market, you'll be the bridge between Customer Support and Engineering. You'll track every escalation and customer-impacting incident from start to finish, make sure the right engineers are engaged and moving, and keep customers and stakeholders informed. Then you'll look across all of it to find the patterns, turn them into supportability requests the Product team can act on, and drive the escalation rate down over time.

You'll work side by side with the Senior Manager, Customer Support, who leads and develops the Support Engineering team. They build the team's technical depth; you make sure the path from Support to Engineering is fast, visible, and needed less often. Together, you'll help support engineers take more ownership of their cases, both before and after they escalate.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Define and maintain escalation criteria, severity definitions, and handoff standards so support engineers know when to escalate, how to escalate, and what an escalation-ready case looks like

  • Build and publish reporting on escalation volume and rate, time to engage, time to resolve, aging, and top drivers by product area and customer, for Support, Engineering, and Product leadership to use in their decisions

  • Improve the tooling and workflows between the support platform and engineering trackers, such as Zendesk and Jira, so escalations move faster with less manual work

  • Own the end-to-end lifecycle of every escalation from Support to Engineering: intake, triage, routing, follow-through, and closure

  • Keep a single source of truth for all active escalations and customer-impacting incidents, each with a clear owner, next step, and ETA, so nothing ages without someone noticing

  • Own the supportability backlog with Product, track requests through to delivery, and close the loop with the support team on what shipped

  • Own escalation rate as a core KPI, set reduction targets with the Director, and lead the initiatives that bring escalation rate and time to resolve down quarter over quarter

  • Act as the primary bridge between Support Engineers and Engineering teams, unblocking stalled issues and escalating further when needed

  • Run recurring escalation reviews with Engineering to keep aging issues moving

  • Join incident response for customer-impacting events: coordinate support-side communication, track affected customers, and make sure follow-ups land after resolution

  • Give clear, timely status updates to customers, account teams, and leadership on high-severity and high-visibility issues

  • File, prioritize, and advocate for supportability requests with Product, including better logging, diagnostics, observability, error messages, self-service tooling, and internal admin capabilities that let Support resolve issues without Engineering

  • Bring the customer's voice into product planning with data, not anecdotes

  • Review escalations regularly to identify recurring issues, product gaps, knowledge gaps, and process breakdowns

  • Feed findings into postmortems, runbooks, and knowledge base articles, and partner with the Senior Manager, Customer Support on training that closes the gaps the escalation data reveals

  • Coach support engineers to troubleshoot further, own cases end to end, and actively drive their escalations instead of handing them off

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 5+ years in technical support, support engineering, escalation management, incident management, or SRE/operations in a cloud, infrastructure, or SaaS environment

  • 2+ years owning escalations or incidents that span multiple engineering teams

  • A solid technical foundation in cloud infrastructure, including Linux, networking, virtualization, and Kubernetes: enough to read logs, follow a technical investigation, and hold your own with engineers

  • A track record of reducing escalation volume or resolution time through process, tooling, or product changes

  • Comfort with data: building dashboards and reports (SQL, Looker, Tableau, Sheets, or similar) and turning them into clear recommendations

  • Hands-on experience with tools such as Zendesk, Jira or incident.io, and Slack

  • Calm, clear communication under pressure, in writing and live, with customers, engineers, and executives

  • The ability to influence without authority and hold cross-functional teams to their commitments

  • Experience in a fast-paced organization going through rapid growth

Bonus Points

  • Experience with GPU compute, HPC, InfiniBand or RoCE networking, or AI/ML training and inference infrastructure

  • A background as a support engineer or SRE before moving into escalation management

  • Experience standing up an escalation or problem management function from scratch

  • Scripting or automation skills (Python, Bash) to streamline workflows

  • ITIL or other incident and problem management certification

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $145,000 - $175,000 base + bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

As Senior L&D Program Manager - Manager Programs, you will continue to develop and operate a best-in-class global Manager Development Program for Crusoe’s global manager population. This role is ideal for an experienced L&D strategist who moves quickly, thrives in fast-paced environments, and brings instructional precision, big-picture thinking, and operational excellence.

You will balance high-level strategy with hands-on execution—designing and facilitating manager experiences, curating learning journeys, and establishing data-driven feedback loops. Partnering directly with senior leaders across engineering, data center operations, manufacturing, and corporate teams, you will ensure our leaders are equipped to scale with Crusoe’s rapid growth.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Manager Program Facilitation & Iteration: Facilitate and continuously evolve Crusoe’s Manager Program (“Manager Bootcamp”), aligning content with company strategy, culture, and operational priorities.

  • Manager Journey Curation: Build a cohesive, end-to-end development journey that connects managers to Crusoe’s mission, business model, and organizational impact.

  • Modular & Functional Tracks: Partner with internal teams (HR / People, Talent Development, senior leadership) to build modular and team-specific development tracks tailored to technical, manufacturing, and data center operational teams.

  • Program Operations & Metrics: Build robust measurement frameworks and feedback loops to evaluate program effectiveness, track leadership performance metrics, and optimize operational delivery.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with People, IT, Workplace, and business leaders to create seamless, high-touch manager experiences.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 8–10+ Years of L&D Leadership: Proven track record in Learning & Development, Organizational Development, or Instructional Design, with explicit experience scaling manager programs inside technical, engineering, or industrial organizations.

  • Technical Org Fluency: Deep understanding of how engineering, technical operations, and manufacturing leads operate, what motivates them, and how to build credibility in highly technical cultures.

  • Data-Driven Approach: Expertise using workforce analytics and learning metrics to evaluate program ROI, identify performance risks, and justify strategic interventions.

  • Program Execution: Equal parts strategic architect and hands-on builder; comfortable designing frameworks from scratch in ambiguous, fast-growing environments.

  • Enthusiasm for Travel: Willingness and ability to travel to global offices, manufacturing sites, and data centers as needed (approx. 25% travel).

 

Bonus Points

  • Organizational Development Background: Advanced grounding in adult learning theory or organizational effectiveness.

  • Modern L&D Tech Stack: Hands-on familiarity with tools such as WorkRamp, Lattice, Confluence, or modern LMS/knowledge platforms.

  • Infrastructure Tech Context: Genuine curiosity about AI systems, hardware manufacturing, and the physical data center infrastructure powering future technologies.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

     

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000 - $195,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. About the Role:

Crusoe's Finance team is looking for a Senior Manager to own headcount and operating expense (OpEx) finance across the company. This role is the single source of truth for how many people we have, how many we're planning to hire, and what we're spending outside of capital projects — and it's responsible for the planning, budgeting, forecasting, and actuals reporting that keeps leadership and the business aligned on both. You'll partner with People, Recruiting, and department leaders on headcount planning, own the OpEx budget process end-to-end, and make sure monthly actuals tell an accurate, timely story against plan. This is a highly visible role for someone who wants to bring structure and rigor to how a scaling company manages its people and operating costs.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Headcount Planning & Tracking: own the headcount plan and forecast across the company, partnering with People and department leaders to track open reqs, hiring pace, and attrition against plan

  • OpEx Budgeting/forecasting: lead the annual budgeting and in-year OpEx forecasting process across departments, working with budget owners to build defensible, well-documented plans

  • Actuals Reporting & Variance Analysis: own monthly and quarterly actuals reporting for headcount and OpEx, identifying variances to plan and partnering with budget owners on root cause and corrective action

  • Forecast Management: maintain rolling headcount and OpEx forecasts, updating for approved changes, hiring plan shifts, and in-year business decisions

  • Business Partnering: serve as the go-to finance contact for department leaders on headcount and OpEx questions, helping them understand their budgets and make informed trade-offs. Partner with HR on new or changing benefit ideas to improve employee’s experience. Additionally, partner with Marketing and other leaders on OPEX budgets / plans and associated ROI

  • Process & Systems Improvement: improve the tools and processes used to plan, track, and report on headcount and OpEx, reducing manual reconciliation and increasing self-serve visibility for stakeholders

  • Executive & Board Reporting: prepare clear, accurate headcount and OpEx reporting packages for executive leadership and the board

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 6+ years of progressive finance experience, including meaningful ownership of headcount and/or OpEx planning and reporting

  • Strong financial modeling skills, with advanced proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets and experience with planning tools (e.g., Anaplan, Adaptive, Workday, or similar)

  • Demonstrated ability to partner with People/Recruiting teams and translate hiring plans into financial impact

  • Track record of owning a budgeting and actuals reporting process end-to-end, including variance analysis and stakeholder communication

  • Excellent attention to detail and a strong sense of ownership over data accuracy — headcount and OpEx numbers get scrutinized by leadership every month

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain budget and variance drivers clearly to non-finance stakeholders

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; MBA a plus

About the Role:

Crusoe's Finance team is looking for a Senior Manager to own headcount and operating expense (OpEx) finance across the company. This role is the single source of truth for how many people we have, how many we're planning to hire, and what we're spending outside of capital projects — and it's responsible for the planning, budgeting, forecasting, and actuals reporting that keeps leadership and the business aligned on both. You'll partner with People, Recruiting, and department leaders on headcount planning, own the OpEx budget process end-to-end, and make sure monthly actuals tell an accurate, timely story against plan. This is a highly visible role for someone who wants to bring structure and rigor to how a scaling company manages its people and operating costs.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

 - Headcount Planning & Tracking: own the headcount plan and forecast across the company, partnering with People and department leaders to track open reqs, hiring pace, and attrition against plan

 - OpEx Budgeting/forecasting: lead the annual budgeting and in-year OpEx forecasting process across departments, working with budget owners to build defensible, well-documented plans

 - Actuals Reporting & Variance Analysis: own monthly and quarterly actuals reporting for headcount and OpEx, identifying variances to plan and partnering with budget owners on root cause and corrective action

 - Forecast Management: maintain rolling headcount and OpEx forecasts, updating for approved changes, hiring plan shifts, and in-year business decisions

 - Business Partnering: serve as the go-to finance contact for department leaders on headcount and OpEx questions, helping them understand their budgets and make informed trade-offs.  Partner with HR on new or changing benefit ideas to improve employee’s experience.  Additionally, partner with Marketing and other leaders on OPEX budgets / plans and associated ROI

 - Process & Systems Improvement: improve the tools and processes used to plan, track, and report on headcount and OpEx, reducing manual reconciliation and increasing self-serve visibility for stakeholders

 - Executive & Board Reporting: prepare clear, accurate headcount and OpEx reporting packages for executive leadership and the board

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - 6+ years of progressive finance experience, including meaningful ownership of headcount and/or OpEx planning and reporting

 - Strong financial modeling skills, with advanced proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets and experience with planning tools (e.g., Anaplan, Adaptive, Workday, or similar)

 - Demonstrated ability to partner with People/Recruiting teams and translate hiring plans into financial impact

 - Track record of owning a budgeting and actuals reporting process end-to-end, including variance analysis and stakeholder communication

 - Excellent attention to detail and a strong sense of ownership over data accuracy — headcount and OpEx numbers get scrutinized by leadership every month

 - Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain budget and variance drivers clearly to non-finance stakeholders

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; MBA a plus

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $195,000-$235,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

About the Role:

Crusoe is looking for an organized, proactive, and execution-driven Workplace Project Manager, Real Estate to lead workplace design and construction projects across our growing global portfolio.

This role will manage projects from initial planning and scoping through design, construction, occupancy, and closeout. The Project Manager will be responsible for driving project schedules, budgets, design coordination, vendor performance, and cross-functional workstreams while ensuring projects align with Crusoe’s workplace standards, operational needs, and employee experience goals.

Projects may include new office buildouts, expansions, relocations, renovations, space reconfigurations, workplace refreshes, and furniture installations. The Project Manager will independently lead assigned projects and work closely with internal stakeholders, architects, contractors, consultants, landlords, and vendors to deliver projects on time and within budget.

The Project Manager will also partner with teams responsible for Crusoe’s colocation, data center, and manufacturing sites, providing workplace planning and design expertise for the office and employee-facing portions of these projects. This includes programming, space planning, workplace standards, employee experience, and FF&E procurement, while the broader project remains under the ownership of the respective business or project team.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Project Management & Delivery

    • Lead assigned workplace design and construction projects from initial scoping and programming through design, construction, occupancy, and closeout

    • Establish and manage project scope, budget, schedule, milestones, risks, dependencies, and key decision points

    • Drive day-to-day project execution and maintain accountability across architects, contractors, consultants, vendors, landlords, and internal stakeholders

    • Lead project meetings, communicate status and decisions, identify risks early, and drive issues to resolution

    • Manage project decisions within established scope and budget while escalating material changes, risks, and strategic decisions as appropriate

    • Manage design development, permitting, construction, installations, inspections, punch lists, occupancy readiness, turnover, and project closeout

    • Lead cross-functional coordination across Workplace, IT, AV, Security, Brand & Creative, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and other business partners

    • Develop project delivery strategies, phasing plans, and sequencing approaches that minimize business disruption while maintaining project objectives

    • Manage external project managers and consultants where applicable and ensure clear ownership, accountability, and performance

    • Support portfolio-level initiatives and larger strategic projects as part of the broader Workplace Design & Construction team

  • Workplace Planning & Cross-Business Partnership

    • Lead programming and requirements gathering and translate business, employee, and operational needs into practical workplace solutions

    • Review and provide direction on test fits, architectural plans, furniture layouts, finish selections, and design packages

    • Ensure projects align with Crusoe’s workplace design standards while appropriately adapting solutions to local conditions, operational requirements, budgets, and schedules

    • Partner with teams responsible for colocation, data center, and manufacturing projects to define and deliver the workplace and office components of these environments

    • Serve as the Workplace Design & Construction representative for assigned cross-business projects, providing guidance on programming, space planning, workplace design, employee experience, and FF&E

    • Identify opportunities to improve space efficiency, functionality, employee experience, and consistency across locations

    • Partner with Workplace and Brand & Creative to create a cohesive and recognizable Crusoe experience across the portfolio

  • Budget, Procurement & FF&E

    • Develop and manage project budgets, forecasts, commitments, invoices, contingencies, and change-order logs

    • Monitor project financial performance and proactively identify potential budget impacts, savings opportunities, and forecast changes

    • Lead or support competitive bidding, proposal evaluation, vendor selection, contracting, purchase orders, and vendor onboarding

    • Review vendor proposals and change orders for scope, cost, schedule, and alignment with project requirements

    • Manage FF&E planning, specifications, pricing, procurement, delivery, installation, and punch-list coordination

    • Track long-lead items and procurement milestones and proactively address risks that could impact project delivery

    • Coordinate with Finance and Procurement to maintain accurate project forecasts, commitments, and financial reporting

    • Ensure complete and organized project documentation, including drawings, contracts, approvals, specifications, warranties, as-builts, and closeout materials

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 5+ years of experience in workplace design and construction, commercial real estate, architecture, interior design, construction management, or a related field

  • Demonstrated experience independently managing office buildouts, tenant improvements, renovations, expansions, relocations, or similar workplace projects

  • Strong understanding of the design and construction process from programming and test fits through design development, permitting, construction, occupancy, and closeout

  • Experience managing project budgets, schedules, consultants, contractors, vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders

  • Ability to review and provide meaningful feedback on architectural drawings, furniture plans, specifications, and design packages

  • Working knowledge of construction terminology, project delivery processes, procurement, and FF&E

  • Strong judgment and ability to independently resolve project issues while recognizing when escalation or leadership alignment is required

  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to clearly communicate project status, risks, decisions, and recommendations

  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and shifting priorities in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

  • Proficiency in Google Workspace and familiarity with Asana, Smartsheet, Monday.com, or similar project-management tools

  • Bachelor’s degree in architecture, interior design, construction management, real estate, engineering, or a related field preferred

  • PMP, LEED, or another relevant professional certification is a plus

     

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

     

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $130,000 - $160,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

 

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Fleet Management
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We’re looking for a seasoned engineering leader to own and scale the GPU and data center infrastructure that powers our neocloud platform. This hands-on leadership role sits at the intersection of software and hardware. You’ll lead the teams building validation platforms, lifecycle automation, and orchestration services that keep our fleet healthy, while also owning firmware qualification, hardware security, deployments, and data center operations across a fleet growing roughly 10x year over year. Our fleet runs under a 99.5% monthly availability SLA, so your reliability and automation work is directly tied to revenue.

You’ll set the technical charter for fleet reliability and operational excellence, defining north-star availability metrics and building automation that replaces today’s manual processes. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Product, Finance, and the executive team. The ideal candidate scales through systems rather than headcount, reasons from first principles, and leads from the front by digging into root causes. This is a full-time, senior leadership position.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Infrastructure Deployment & Fleet Management: Lead day-to-day fleet operations and greenfield deployments across co-location and owned facilities, from rack landing to customer availability. Own core fleet-health metrics and drive toward a 30-day time-to-sellable target.

  • Firmware Lifecycle Management: Build the pipeline to qualify and track every firmware release across 10+ SKUs and multiple OEMs/ODMs. Eliminate the qualification backlog (e.g., the ~66-day NVIDIA firmware lag), hold partners accountable, and evaluate in-house BMC development (OpenBMC).

  • Validation Framework & Platform: Consolidate siloed hardware automation pipelines and validation scripts into a single platform built on a proper workflow engine. Own bare-metal and multi-node burn-in/stress testing, define pass/fail criteria, deliver performance baselines (such as MFU) at cluster handover, and make stack-validation results a required approval criterion for production changes.

  • Data Center Infrastructure Engineering (DCIE): Own power, cooling, networking fabrics, and physical security. Prioritize RMAs ahead of warranty expiry, reduce manual node recoveries through lifecycle automation, and make that automation the source of truth for site deployments. Lead asset-visibility initiatives such as fleet-wide RFID and advanced DCIM tooling.

  • Hardware Security & Attestation: Own the strategy for trusted, tamper-evident hardware. Lead the design and rollout of firmware and OS integrity attestation (TPM-based identity, secure boot gating, remote attestation) that can quarantine compromised hardware, with no impact on customer training or inference workloads.

  • Reliability & Incident Operations: Define operational KPIs (uptime, PUE, MTTR, MTTD, MTBF), and establish runbooks, a tiered on-call model, and single-owner incident closure.

  • Procurement, CapEx & Budget Ownership: Partner with Procurement, Hardware, and Supply Chain on GPU and hardware sourcing, including pricing, supply commitments, and SLAs. Work with the Hardware leader on fleet capital and operating budgets, and report on fleet health, spend, and forecast to executive leadership.

  • Team Leadership & Outcome Alignment: Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of fleet engineers, DC infrastructure professionals, and platform/automation software engineers. Translate engineering targets into clear business outcomes and define SLOs with Product across compute, storage, networking, and inference.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 18+ years of experience in infrastructure, data center operations, or fleet management, including 6+ years in a senior leadership role

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

  • Deep hands-on expertise with GPU infrastructure, including NVIDIA or AMD accelerator platforms

  • A genuine blend of software and hardware leadership, with equal credibility driving platform/automation software (workflow engines, orchestration, validation pipelines) and physical-layer DC operations

  • Experience operating or scaling data center infrastructure in a high-growth environment such as a neocloud, hyperscaler, or large enterprise

  • Strong command of DC fundamentals: power distribution, cooling systems, networking fabrics, and physical security

  • Proven ability to manage vendor relationships and negotiate large-scale infrastructure contracts ($50M+), and to own large CapEx budgets in partnership with Finance and Procurement

  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex infrastructure topics for executive and non-technical audiences

Bonus Points

  • Prior experience at a neocloud or AI infrastructure company, and familiarity with GPU failure modes and auto-remediation techniques

  • Hands-on experience with firmware qualification, BMC/OpenBMC development, or hardware attestation (TPM, secure boot, remote attestation)

  • Familiarity with InfiniBand, RoCE, or other high-performance networking fabrics at scale

  • Experience building validation/burn-in platforms and multi-node performance benchmarking (e.g., MFU, collective communication tests)

  • Exposure to DCIM, asset management/RFID, or lifecycle automation and fleet orchestration tools (e.g., NetBox, Temporal), or a background in sustainability initiatives such as renewable energy procurement

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $325,000 - $370,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

As a Senior Deployment Automation Engineer for the Compute Team, you will be responsible for deployment and testing automation of large-scale, multi-node GPU clusters. You will develop the CI/CD infrastructure, including both deployment and integration testing, for a rapidly scaling fleet of virtualized GPU and CPU hosts across our AI Cloud. Your role is critical in ensuring the stability of the low-level infrastructure and enabling teams across our Cloud Infrastructure organization to quickly and reliably release, test, and deploy their artifacts across our datacenters.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Deployment and Integration Testing: Develop applications and systems for deployment and integration testing on bare-metal, on-premise systems across Crusoe’s AI Cloud Stack.

  • CI/CD Automation and Tooling: Build CI/CD platforms that enable developers to quickly test, iterate, and deploy critical, low-level systems and applications.

  • Multi-Node Scaling Validation: Design and execute large-scale validation tests across multi-node virtualized clusters to ensure linear scaling and stability of GPU workloads.

  • Configuration Management and Observability: Maintain and scale bare-metal Linux configurations using a mix of custom and off the shelf tooling such as Gitlab, Ansible, osquery, etc.

  • Deployment Orchestration: Create control applications to coordinate canary deployments on live production systems, run Blue/Green testing, and perform automatic rollback where necessary.

  • Cluster Orchestration: Develop and maintain automation frameworks in Python or Go to dynamically provision, configure, and stress-test multi-node virtualized environments.

  • Create automated test suites leveraging tools like fio, stress-ng, and iperf to ensure performance and multi-tenant isolation of CPU and GPU hosts.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Education & Experience: 5+ YOE demonstrated ability to competently and independently perform responsibilities plus Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.

  • Experience building and deploying automated integration testing, ranging from low-level Linux Systems up to Distributed Control Planes.

  • Proven track record of designing and deploying microservice applications end to end in a distributed Cloud Environment.

  • A strong understanding of how cloud resources (Compute, Network, Storage) are abstracted and managed in an IaaS environment.

  • Working knowledge of the modern infrastructure stack, including Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, and Postgres.

  • CI/CD & Gitlab: Intimate knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and Gitlab Tooling to enable stable infrastructure releases across multiple datacenters.

  • Configuration Management: Previous experience with at least 1-2 configuration management systems, including Ansible, Puppet, Chef, or SaltStack.

  • System Internals: Knowledge of Linux kernel internals, specifically PCIe topology, VFIO, and memory management (HugePages, IOMMU).

Bonus Points

  • Distributed GPU Ecosystems: Familiarity with NVIDIA (CUDA/NCCL) and/or AMD (ROCm/RCCL) stacks in a multi-node context.

  • Networking Knowledge: Understanding of RDMA, RoCE, and InfiniBand protocols and their implementation in virtualized systems.

  • Experience with MNNVL (Multi-Node NVLink) or specialized AI fabric architectures.

  • Familiarity with hardware-level debugging tools and performance profilers (e.g., NVIDIA Nsight, AMD Omniperf).

  • Knowledge of containerized orchestration for GPUs (e.g., Kubernetes with specialized device plugins).

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $170,000 -$205,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

About the Role:

Crusoe is looking for an organized, proactive, and execution-driven Workplace Design & Construction Project Manager to lead workplace design and construction projects across our growing global portfolio.

This role will manage projects from initial planning and scoping through design, construction, occupancy, and closeout. The Project Manager will be responsible for driving project schedules, budgets, design coordination, vendor performance, and cross-functional workstreams while ensuring projects align with Crusoe’s workplace standards, operational needs, and employee experience goals.

Projects may include new office buildouts, expansions, relocations, renovations, space reconfigurations, workplace refreshes, and furniture installations. The Project Manager will independently lead assigned projects and work closely with internal stakeholders, architects, contractors, consultants, landlords, and vendors to deliver projects on time and within budget.

The Project Manager will also partner with teams responsible for Crusoe’s colocation, data center, and manufacturing sites, providing workplace planning and design expertise for the office and employee-facing portions of these projects. This includes programming, space planning, workplace standards, employee experience, and FF&E procurement, while the broader project remains under the ownership of the respective business or project team.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Project Management & Delivery

    • Lead assigned workplace design and construction projects from initial scoping and programming through design, construction, occupancy, and closeout

    • Establish and manage project scope, budget, schedule, milestones, risks, dependencies, and key decision points

    • Drive day-to-day project execution and maintain accountability across architects, contractors, consultants, vendors, landlords, and internal stakeholders

    • Lead project meetings, communicate status and decisions, identify risks early, and drive issues to resolution

    • Manage project decisions within established scope and budget while escalating material changes, risks, and strategic decisions as appropriate

    • Manage design development, permitting, construction, installations, inspections, punch lists, occupancy readiness, turnover, and project closeout

    • Lead cross-functional coordination across Workplace, IT, AV, Security, Brand & Creative, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and other business partners

    • Develop project delivery strategies, phasing plans, and sequencing approaches that minimize business disruption while maintaining project objectives

    • Manage external project managers and consultants where applicable and ensure clear ownership, accountability, and performance

    • Support portfolio-level initiatives and larger strategic projects as part of the broader Workplace Design & Construction team

  • Workplace Planning & Cross-Business Partnership

    • Lead programming and requirements gathering and translate business, employee, and operational needs into practical workplace solutions

    • Review and provide direction on test fits, architectural plans, furniture layouts, finish selections, and design packages

    • Ensure projects align with Crusoe’s workplace design standards while appropriately adapting solutions to local conditions, operational requirements, budgets, and schedules

    • Partner with teams responsible for colocation, data center, and manufacturing projects to define and deliver the workplace and office components of these environments

    • Serve as the Workplace Design & Construction representative for assigned cross-business projects, providing guidance on programming, space planning, workplace design, employee experience, and FF&E

    • Identify opportunities to improve space efficiency, functionality, employee experience, and consistency across locations

    • Partner with Workplace and Brand & Creative to create a cohesive and recognizable Crusoe experience across the portfolio

  • Budget, Procurement & FF&E

    • Develop and manage project budgets, forecasts, commitments, invoices, contingencies, and change-order logs

    • Monitor project financial performance and proactively identify potential budget impacts, savings opportunities, and forecast changes

    • Lead or support competitive bidding, proposal evaluation, vendor selection, contracting, purchase orders, and vendor onboarding

    • Review vendor proposals and change orders for scope, cost, schedule, and alignment with project requirements

    • Manage FF&E planning, specifications, pricing, procurement, delivery, installation, and punch-list coordination

    • Track long-lead items and procurement milestones and proactively address risks that could impact project delivery

    • Coordinate with Finance and Procurement to maintain accurate project forecasts, commitments, and financial reporting

    • Ensure complete and organized project documentation, including drawings, contracts, approvals, specifications, warranties, as-builts, and closeout materials

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 5+ years of experience in workplace design and construction, commercial real estate, architecture, interior design, construction management, or a related field

  • Demonstrated experience independently managing office buildouts, tenant improvements, renovations, expansions, relocations, or similar workplace projects

  • Strong understanding of the design and construction process from programming and test fits through design development, permitting, construction, occupancy, and closeout

  • Experience managing project budgets, schedules, consultants, contractors, vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders

  • Ability to review and provide meaningful feedback on architectural drawings, furniture plans, specifications, and design packages

  • Working knowledge of construction terminology, project delivery processes, procurement, and FF&E

  • Strong judgment and ability to independently resolve project issues while recognizing when escalation or leadership alignment is required

  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to clearly communicate project status, risks, decisions, and recommendations

  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and shifting priorities in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

  • Proficiency in Google Workspace and familiarity with Asana, Smartsheet, Monday.com, or similar project-management tools

  • Bachelor’s degree in architecture, interior design, construction management, real estate, engineering, or a related field preferred

  • PMP, LEED, or another relevant professional certification is a plus

     

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

     

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $110,000 - $135,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

The Crusoe Cloud Software Development team is seeking a passionate and experienced Staff Software Engineer specializing in Linux Kernel Security. This critical role is essential in strengthening the security posture of our core Linux kernel and operating system components, which underpin our cutting-edge hardware and software solutions for the AI cloud. A deep understanding of Linux kernel internals, security vulnerabilities, mitigation techniques, and secure development practices is paramount for developing reliable, high-assurance systems. This is a full-time position.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Kernel Hardening & CVE Triage: Implement kernel security enhancements, manage configuration hardening, and triage incoming CVEs to assess severity and exploitability.

  • Access Control, Boot Security & Guardrails: Enforce mandatory access controls, secure the boot path, and establish CI guardrails and fuzzing coverage to prevent regressions.

  • Vulnerability Research & Analysis: Research vulnerabilities across kernel, driver, and OS components to build proactive mitigations and backport non-trivial upstream fixes to production.

  • Secure Development Practices: Establish and advocate for secure coding standards and best practices for kernel-level development. Conduct security-focused code reviews to identify and eliminate potential vulnerabilities early in the development lifecycle.

  • Security Auditing & Tools: Utilize and develop specialized tools for kernel security auditing, fuzzing, static analysis, and dynamic analysis to uncover hidden vulnerabilities and ensure compliance with security policies.

  • Incident Response Support: Provide expert support during security incidents involving kernel or OS-level compromises, assisting with root-cause analysis, containment, and recovery efforts.

  • Performance and Security Balance: Work to ensure that security enhancements do not unduly impact system performance, especially critical for our high-performance AI infrastructure.

  • First 90 days: Own kernel CVE triage end to end and have shipped at least one backported fix through our full release path. You have an independent read on where our kernel configuration is weakest.

  • First year: Kernel security response has a defined SLA by severity and we consistently hit it. A hardening baseline is defined, enforced in CI, and rolled out across supported SKUs. Cloud Hypervisor has been audited and the highest-value isolation gaps are closed or scheduled.

  • Cloud Hypervisor & Isolation: Audit, harden, and reduce privilege across Cloud Hypervisor device models and vhost-user datapaths, contributing upstream security fixes and advancing confidential computing primitives (AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX).

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Collaborate closely with other engineering teams (hardware, hypervisor, OS development, cloud infrastructure, and security operations) to integrate security best practices and ensure a comprehensive security strategy across the stack.

  • Technical Leadership: Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers on kernel security best practices, fostering a culture of security awareness and excellence.

  • Debugging and Root-Cause Analysis: Debug and root-cause a variety of complex security-related issues at the kernel level.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Linux Kernel Security Expertise: Proven deep knowledge of Linux kernel internals (e.g., memory management, process scheduling, system calls, I/O subsystems) with a strong focus on security aspects.

  • Vulnerability & Exploitation Knowledge: Solid understanding of common kernel vulnerabilities (e.g., privilege escalation, information disclosure, denial of service) and associated exploitation techniques.

  • Security Mitigations: Experience with existing Linux kernel security mitigations (e.g., ASLR, DEP/NX, SMEP/SMAP, KASLR, namespaces, cgroups, LSMs like SELinux/AppArmor).

  • Secure Coding: Strong background in secure coding principles and experience conducting security-focused code reviews, particularly in C.

  • Debugging & Analysis Tools: Proficiency with kernel debugging tools (e.g., GDB, crash, kgdb) and security analysis tools (e.g., valgrind, address sanitizers, fuzzers).

  • Hardware Security Concepts: Familiarity with hardware-assisted security features (e.g., Intel SGX, AMD SEV, ARM TrustZone) and their relevance to kernel security.

  • Education & Experience: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, and a minimum of 5 years of relevant industry experience with at least 3 years focused on low-level operating systems or kernel security.

  • Safety and Compliance: Must be able to pass a background check.

  • Company Values: Embody the Company values.

  • Experience dealing with CVE Remediation and automation

  • First 90 days: You own kernel CVE triage end to end and have shipped at least one backported fix through our full release path. You have an independent read on where our kernel configuration is weakest.

  • First year: Kernel security response has a defined SLA by severity and we consistently hit it. A hardening baseline is defined, enforced in CI, and rolled out across supported SKUs. Cloud Hypervisor has been audited and the highest-value isolation gaps are closed or scheduled.

 

Bonus Points

  • Experience with specific kernel security projects or contributions to open-source kernel security initiatives.

  • Familiarity with hypervisor security and the interaction between the hypervisor and the guest kernel's security.

  • Experience with hardware security modules (HSMs) or Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs).

  • Background in offensive security or penetration testing at the kernel level.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 -$260,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. About This Role

As a Senior Commissioning Engineer, you will lead commissioning execution for assigned systems and scopes within Crusoe's data center projects. You will independently oversee test procedures, support documentation review, and serve as a go-to resource for field-level troubleshooting and issue resolution. This role bridges hands-on execution with emerging project leadership, and is designed for an engineer ready to take on broader responsibility and move toward full project ownership. (#INDDIG)

 
 

What You'll Be Working On

  • Lead the execution of commissioning test procedures across assigned systems including pre-functional checklists, functional performance tests, and integrated systems tests.

  • Review and provide input on commissioning test scripts, MOPs, punch lists, and turnover documentation.

  • Serve as a field-level technical resource for troubleshooting and resolving commissioning deficiencies across mechanical or controls disciplines.

  • Coordinate with trade contractors and subcontractors to schedule, sequence, and support commissioning activities on-site.

  • Verify installation conditions against approved drawings, submittals, and specifications to confirm readiness for testing.

  • Track and drive closure of open deficiencies, ensuring accurate documentation and timely resolution.

  • Support integrated systems testing and reliability demonstrations for critical MEP, and BMS/EPMS infrastructure.

  • Participate in factory witness testing and startup validation activities as assigned.

  • Maintain complete and accurate commissioning records, field reports, and turnover packages.

  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to Junior CxE team members in the field.

  • Ensure adherence to Crusoe commission requirements and collect feedback from the field to improve the commissioning program.

  • Communicate progress, risks, and technical issues clearly to the management team.

  • Adhere to and help enforce site safety protocols and compliance requirements throughout all commissioning phases.

 
 

What You'll Bring

  • 4+ years of experience in data center commissioning, building systems, or critical infrastructure construction.

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field; equivalent field experience considered (CxA certification a plus).

  • Solid understanding of data center systems including cooling infrastructure, and BMS systems.

  • Working knowledge of commissioning levels L1 through L5 and associated documentation and testing requirements.

  • Ability to independently execute and troubleshoot functional and integrated system tests.

  • Proficient in reading and interpreting construction drawings, single-line diagrams, submittals, and equipment specifications.

  • Strong documentation habits with the ability to manage multiple open items accurately in a fast-paced field environment.

  • Effective communicator with the ability to coordinate across trades, contractors, and internal project teams.

  • Willingness to travel to project sites as required (75% travel).

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $115,000 -$140,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Integrated Capacity Planner
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

At Crusoe, the Capacity Planning & Efficiency team operates at the critical intersection of all Crusoe products, services, and underlying physical infrastructure. This role sets the strategy that everything else plans against. You will decide what Crusoe's capacity posture should be over a multi-year horizon - where to build, what to buy versus lease versus partner for, which technology transitions to bet on and when, and how much risk to carry against demand that has not been signed yet. Those answers become the targets the rest of the planning function executes toward.

This is the most senior individual contributor role in capacity planning at Crusoe. Where planners run cycles and reconcile plans, you own the questions underneath them: what the plan is optimizing for, what the company should commit to years before demand arrives, and what to do when the answer is genuinely unknown. You will be the technical authority the exec staff, the board, and Crusoe's capital partners rely on for the capacity story, and the person who raises the bar across every planner in the function. This role is uniquely positioned to shape Crusoe's infrastructure strategy at its foundation, directly supporting the mission to align the future of computing with environmental sustainability.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Capacity Strategy: Set the multi-year capacity posture Crusoe plans against - build versus lease versus partner, regional siting, technology transition timing, fleet refresh economics, and how much speculative capacity to carry ahead of contracted demand.

  • Capital Deployment Recommendations: Own the analysis behind Crusoe's largest infrastructure commitments. Frame the options, quantify the downside, and make the recommendation the exec staff acts on - then own whether it was right.

  • Allocation Policy: Own the policy governing how scarce capacity is allocated across customers, products, and regions, and make the contested calls that cannot be resolved inside the planning cycle.

  • Planning Methodology & Standards: Define how planning is done across the function - models, taxonomy, horizons, accuracy standards, review bar - and hold the GPU, compute and storage, hardware and supply chain, and integrated planners to it.

  • Executive, Board & Capital Partner Narrative: Own the capacity story told to the exec staff, the board, and Crusoe's lenders and investors. Translate a physically constrained build plan into the numbers and confidence intervals those audiences need.

  • Supply Strategy: Co-own Crusoe's strategic supply posture with Supply Chain - allocation negotiations with silicon and system vendors, multi-sourcing strategy, and the commitments made years ahead of the demand that justifies them.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
