About This Role:

Crusoe Cloud is revolutionizing high-performance computing by offering sustainable, low-cost GPU compute power. As a Cloud Support Engineer, you'll play a crucial role in empowering our customers to leverage this technology for groundbreaking advancements in fields like AI/ML, physics simulations, and computational biology. You will be the primary point of contact for technical support, ensuring our customers can seamlessly utilize Crusoe Cloud to achieve their goals. This role directly impacts Crusoe's mission by enabling our customers to accelerate their research and development, contributing to a more sustainable future. You will be involved in exciting projects, working with cutting-edge technologies and collaborating with a talented team to solve complex challenges. The ideal candidate is a highly motivated and experienced technical professional with a passion for customer success, a deep understanding of cloud technologies, and a commitment to Crusoe's values. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Customer Support: Provide exceptional technical support to customers via Zendesk, meeting SLAs and maintaining high CSAT (95%+).

  • On-Call Rotation: Participate in a 24/7 on-call rotation to ensure timely resolution of critical issues.

  • Troubleshooting: Diagnose and resolve issues related to VMs, hardware failures, and scaling tests using CLI and internal tools.

  • Alert Triage and Maintenance: Manage alert triage, prepare for maintenance windows, and conduct node delivery testing.

  • Collaboration: Work closely with SRE, Networking, and Storage teams from initial triage to root cause analysis (RCA) delivery.

  • Global Teamwork: Adhere to global team collaboration and handoff processes for ticketing and on-call procedures.

  • Knowledge Sharing: Develop onboarding/training materials, knowledge base documentation, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education/Experience: Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or 2+ years of equivalent technical experience.

  • Linux Proficiency: Strong command-line interface (CLI) skills in Linux environments.

  • Version Control: Proficiency with Git for code management and collaboration.

  • Customer Support Experience: 2+ years of experience in a customer support role, ideally within cloud, storage, or networking environments.

  • Cloud Technologies: Experience with container orchestration (e.g., Kubernetes), workload management (e.g., Slurm, Terraform), and monitoring tools (e.g., Grafana).

  • Public Cloud Knowledge: Familiarity with other public cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP).

  • Communication Skills: Excellent communication and customer service skills, including the ability to prioritize competing escalations.

Bonus Points:

  • Cloud Expertise: Deep understanding of specific cloud platforms and services.

  • Automation Skills: Experience with automation tools and scripting languages.

  • Problem-Solving Abilities: Demonstrated ability to analyze complex technical issues and develop effective solutions.

  • Passion for Sustainability: A strong interest in contributing to a more sustainable future through technology.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $125,000 - $150,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

About the Role:

We’re seeking a Senior Enterprise AI Automation Engineer to play a key role in executing Crusoe’s 2026 Enterprise AI Strategy. In this role, you will design and build agentic AI systems that move the organization from simple information retrieval to orchestrated, multi-system automation.

You’ll operate at the intersection of AI, enterprise systems, and integration platforms—building scalable agent workflows, enabling a citizen developer ecosystem, and establishing the technical foundations for an AI-powered operating model.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Designing and implementing agentic AI workflows using a modular, API-first architecture across platforms such as Workato ONE, Anthropic Claude, and Gemini.

  • Building autonomous agents that orchestrate workflows across enterprise systems (e.g., Salesforce, Coupa, Slack, Google Workspace)

  • Architecting and integrating a unified data layer that enables AI agents to access and act on data across siloed systems

  • Developing integrations, APIs, and custom connectors that enable scalable AI orchestration across business platforms

  • Implementing MCP (Model Context Protocol) connectors and model-agnostic orchestration patterns

  • Designing deployment pipelines and lifecycle management systems for AI agents in production environments

  • Embedding security, data privacy, and compliance guardrails into all AI implementations

  • Creating reusable templates, frameworks, and tooling to support a Citizen Developer Program

  • Mentoring internal teams through code reviews, training, and technical enablement programs

  • Evaluating emerging AI technologies and prototyping next-generation capabilities to advance agentic maturity

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including 2+ years in AI/ML or AI application development

  • Strong proficiency in Python and API development (REST, GraphQL, webhooks)

  • Hands-on experience with enterprise integration platforms (e.g., Workato, MuleSoft, Zapier)

  • Experience working with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, or similar)

  • Deep understanding of agentic architectures, RAG patterns, and prompt engineering

  • Experience designing scalable, distributed systems in cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure)

  • Strong knowledge of microservices, event-driven architecture, and integration design patterns

  • Experience with CI/CD, infrastructure as code, and DevOps practices

  • Understanding of data security, privacy, and compliance considerations (SOC 2, GDPR)

Bonus Points

  • Experience deploying agentic AI systems in production environments

  • Familiarity with iPaaS platforms (Workato preferred) and enterprise automation ecosystems

  • Experience with Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 automation and extensibility

  • Knowledge of Model Context Protocol (MCP) or similar interoperability standards

  • Experience implementing AI governance frameworks in enterprise settings

  • Background in infrastructure, energy, or high-performance computing environments

  • Contributions to open-source AI projects or technical thought leadership

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $145,000-$170,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Leadership & Strategy

Cost Accounting & Inventory

 - Own the cost accounting framework, including standard cost methodology, the annual standard-setting process, overhead absorption and labor rates.

Close, Reporting & Controls

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

As a Senior Manager on the Strategic Initiatives team, you'll work directly with the President/CSO and other leaders to help Crusoe make big decisions quickly, then make them happen. Our executives face questions like: What’s the right ownership structure for any given asset? How much of our data center supply chain should we build ourselves? How should we enter a new country? You'll take these questions, gather the facts and the right people, write a clear recommendation, and push for a decision. When the answer is "go," you'll often lead the work yourself until it has a permanent owner. The job is a blend of high-level strategic thinking, analysis, and writing, cultivating relationships with internal and external partners, and running mission critical projects. We’re looking for the rare candidate that’s as comfortable on a job site or factory floor as they are in the boardroom. Crusoe Spark, our modular data center business, started as a program on this team.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Recommendations to executives: Define each decision up front: who makes it, what the options are, and what has to be true for each option to work. Work with stakeholders across product, engineering, and finance to write short memos that cover the background, financial analysis, options, tradeoffs, and your recommendation, backed by a model with unit economics, scenarios, and capacity plans.

  • Launching new programs: turn approved recommendations into programs with goals, milestones, a budget, an executive sponsor, and a working team. Run pilots that test the riskiest assumptions, and at each checkpoint recommend whether to scale up, change course, or stop. Coordinate engineering, finance, legal, real estate, and outside partners until the program is ready to hand to a business unit leader, along with a written plan, metrics, and a list of open risks.

  • Special projects for the President's office: Lead projects that no single team owns or that cross business units, Support the President on leadership meetings, board and investor materials, international expansion, and deal evaluations, and screen incoming requests to the office. Pitch in wherever needed

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 7–10 years in management consulting, corporate strategy, investment banking, private equity, or a strategy or chief of staff role at a fast-growing infrastructure, energy, or technology company. That should include meaningful time at an operating company, not only in advisory work.

  • Strong writing for senior leaders, such as investment memos, board materials, or strategy recommendations backed by numbers. We'll ask for a writing sample and give you a case exercise.

  • Experience taking a program from approved idea to day-to-day operation, including changing course along the way and handing it off to a permanent owner.

  • The ability to build financial models from scratch, including scenarios. You're comfortable with capital-heavy businesses: megawatts, cost per kilowatt, capex, and lead times.

  • Experience in at least one of these areas: data centers, power and energy, AI compute and cloud, or manufacturing.

  • Daily use of AI tools like Claude or Gemini for research, analysis, and writing, along with the judgment to check what they give you.

Behavioral Traits:

  • Clear writer: You can explain a complex problem in one page.

  • Ownership mentality: When a project is yours, you own all of it: the analysis, the people, the recommendation, and the result.

  • Organizational fluency: Busy teams make time for you because you make their work easier, not harder.

  • Range: in a single week, you might visit a factory floor, review a contract, and build board slides.

  • Intellectual curiosity: You want to know how a substation works and how a delay in cooling equipment changes a revenue forecast.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience preparing board or investor materials at a late-stage private company.

  • Experience launching a new product, business line, or venture, either inside a larger company or at a startup.

  • Experience with international market entry or cross-border deals, especially in Latin America or Europe. Spanish or Portuguese is a plus.

  • Experience scaling manufacturing or with lean operations.

  • An MBA or a quantitative graduate degree.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $175,000 - 215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. About This Role:

As the General Ledger Senior Accountant, you'll be the go-to person for everything related to Prepaid Expenses and Leases. On a typical day, you'll review new lease agreements to determine accounting implications, reconcile monthly lease journal entries back to Lease Query, and collaborate closely with Project Managers, Finance, Procurement, and Operations to identify when leases are expected to commence. You'll also own the reconciliation of the prepaid expenses sub-ledger to the general ledger, prepare Prepaids waterfalls across Crusoe's consolidated entities, and manual prepaid reconciliations to keep everything accurate and audit-ready.

Beyond the day-to-day mechanics, you'll play a key role in the monthly close process, preparing journal entries, supporting fluctuation analysis, and partnering with the Cloud Operations, Data Infrastructure teams and various Accounting functions on new leases, modifications and prepaids. You'll thrive in this role if you're detail-oriented, comfortable working with large volumes of data, and energized by finding smarter, more efficient ways to get things done. This position is ideal for someone who can work independently, take ownership of their responsibilities, and stay a step ahead in a fast-paced, rapidly evolving environment while also lending support on audits, due diligence, and other projects as they arise.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Review new lease agreements and lease modifications and input them into LeaseQuery

  • Track and reconcile lease activity on a month-to-month basis

  • Project Managers, Finance, Procurement, and Operations to identify when leases are expected to commence

  • Reconcile Lease Liabilities and ROU Asset balances from LeaseQuery to general ledger

  • Reconcile the prepaid expenses sub-ledger to the general ledger

  • Prepare and reconcile monthly and year-to-date Prepaid asset waterfalls across Crusoe's consolidated legal entities

  • Prepare and record monthly close journal entries

  • Support monthly reporting and fluctuation analysis

  • Collaborate with the Cloud Operations, Data Infrastructure teams and various Accounting functions on leases and prepaid expenses

  • Support audit and due diligence requests as needed

  • Perform other duties as assigned

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • 4-6 years of general ledger accounting experience

  • Experience with leases accounting

  • Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field

  • Solid understanding of GAAP

  • Working knowledge of internal controls and accounting best practices

  • Understanding of consolidations, joint ventures, and intercompany transactions

  • Exposure to and understanding of month-end financial reporting processes

Bonus Points:

  • A knack for working smarter- always looking for ways to improve processes and drive efficiency

  • Keen attention to detail, even when moving quickly

  • Ability to work with and manipulate large volumes of data

  • Comfort working independently, taking ownership, and adapting in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment

  • A forward-thinking mindset- able to anticipate issues before they arise and proactively identify solutions

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Paid parental leave

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe’s Finance team is looking for a Senior Financial Analyst to own headcount and operating expense (OpEx) finance across the company. This role is the single source of truth for how many people we have, how many we’re planning to hire, and what we’re spending outside of capital projects — and is responsible for the planning, budgeting, forecasting, and actuals reporting that keeps leadership and the business aligned on both. You’ll partner with People, Recruiting, and department leaders on headcount planning, own the OpEx budget process end-to-end, and make sure monthly actuals tell an accurate, timely story against plan.

This is a highly visible role for someone who wants to bring structure and rigor to how a scaling company manages its people and operating costs. This is a full-time, exempt position.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Headcount Planning & Tracking — Own the headcount plan and forecast across the company, partnering with People and department leaders to track open reqs, hiring pace, and attrition against plan.

  • OpEx Budgeting & Forecasting — Lead the annual budgeting and in-year OpEx forecasting process across departments, working with budget owners to build defensible, well-documented plans.

  • Actuals Reporting & Variance Analysis — Own monthly and quarterly actuals reporting for headcount and OpEx, identifying variances to plan and partnering with budget owners on root cause and corrective action.

  • Forecast Management — Maintain rolling headcount and OpEx forecasts, updating for approved changes, hiring plan shifts, and in-year business decisions.

  • Business Partnering — Serve as the go-to finance contact for department leaders on headcount and OpEx questions, helping them understand their budgets and make informed trade-offs. Partner with HR on new or changing benefit ideas to improve employee experience, and with Marketing and other leaders on OpEx budgets/plans and associated ROI.

  • Process & Systems Improvement — Improve the tools and processes used to plan, track, and report on headcount and OpEx, reducing manual reconciliation and increasing self-serve visibility for stakeholders.

  • Executive & Board Reporting — Prepare clear, accurate headcount and OpEx reporting packages for executive leadership and the board.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.

  • 3+ years of progressive finance experience, including meaningful ownership of headcount and/or OpEx planning and reporting.

  • Strong financial modeling skills, with advanced proficiency in Excel/Google Sheets and experience with planning tools (e.g., Anaplan, Adaptive, Workday, or similar).

  • Demonstrated ability to partner with People/Recruiting teams and translate hiring plans into financial impact.

  • Track record of owning a budgeting and actuals reporting process end-to-end, including variance analysis and stakeholder communication.

  • Excellent attention to detail and a strong sense of ownership over data accuracy — headcount and OpEx numbers get scrutinized by leadership every month.

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain budget and variance drivers clearly to non-finance stakeholders.

Bonus Points

  • MBA.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Protective Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is building the infrastructure that powers the AI revolution. As our global footprint expands across data centers, power generation, manufacturing, construction sites, and corporate offices — and as the visibility of our executives and the stakes of our operations continue to rise — the ability to protect our people wherever the business takes them is increasingly critical.

The Senior Manager, Protective Operations will lead Crusoe's executive protection and protective operations programs globally, providing risk-based protection for executives, employees, travelers, and company operations. You will serve as the company's subject matter expert for executive protection, travel risk, protective intelligence, threat management, and sensitive security investigations.

This role will join Crusoe's growing Physical Security organization at a formative moment. You will shape the standards, protocols, vendor network, and operating rhythm that supports Crusoe's expanding global footprint — working closely with the GSOC, the Senior Physical Security Intelligence Analyst, People, Legal, Communications, Information Security, Facilities, and business leaders to identify risk and translate intelligence into effective protective measures.

The ideal candidate brings experience from U.S. Secret Service, Diplomatic Security Service, high-end executive protection, special operations, or protective details at the national or diplomatic level, and has translated that tradecraft into corporate Protective Operations leadership. You know how to protect people without unnecessarily disrupting the business, and you know how to lead a program that scales.

What You'll Be Working On:

Executive Protection Program Leadership

  • Lead Crusoe's global Executive Protection program, including executive travel, residential considerations, ground transportation, advance work, event coverage, and protective operations

  • Develop risk-based protection strategies based on threat, exposure, location, activity, and other relevant factors rather than title alone

  • Lead security planning for executive appearances, media engagements, conferences, town halls, board activities, major company events, and other high-profile engagements

  • Establish and maintain the standards, protocols, and tradecraft discipline expected of a world-class corporate protection program

Travel Risk Management

  • Own the Travel Risk Management program, establishing processes for pre-travel risk assessment, traveler briefings, high-risk travel, escalation, emergency support, and traveler assistance

  • Conduct advance work and security assessments for domestic and international travel, including hotels, venues, transportation, routes, medical capabilities, and contingency planning

  • Build the duty-of-care framework and escalation procedures that protect Crusoe travelers wherever the business sends them

Protective Intelligence Partnership

  • Partner closely with the Senior Physical Security Intelligence Analyst and the GSOC to translate protective intelligence into protective action — movement planning, principal protection decisions, advance planning, and threat response

  • Shape the intelligence requirements and collection priorities that support protective operations

  • Operationalize protective intelligence products into daily decisions, travel decisions, and event planning

Threat Assessment and Management

  • Establish and support threat assessment and management processes for workplace violence, threatening communications, stalking, harassment, fixated individuals, concerning behavior, and other potential threats

  • Partner with HR, Employee Relations, Legal, and the Intelligence Analyst on threat cases requiring coordinated response and protective action

  • Apply structured behavioral threat assessment methodologies to differentiate legitimate threats from noise

Sensitive Security Investigations

  • Lead or support sensitive security investigations involving threats, theft, misconduct, unauthorized access, insider risk, security incidents, and suspected fraud in partnership with Legal, People, Internal Audit, Information Security, and other stakeholders

  • Support elevated-risk employee matters, including sensitive terminations, credible threats, domestic violence concerns affecting the workplace, and other situations requiring additional protective measures

  • Maintain investigative discipline, chain of custody, and reporting standards appropriate to the sensitivity of each matter

Site and Geographic Risk Assessment

  • Conduct geographic and site security risk assessments in support of new markets, potential company locations, major projects, and business expansion

  • Evaluate country, city, neighborhood, and site-level risks including crime, political instability, civil unrest, terrorism, emergency response, medical capabilities, transportation, natural hazards, and other relevant threats

  • Produce assessments that inform executive travel, site selection, event planning, and business expansion decisions

Program Development and Vendor Management

  • Develop protective operations plans, standards, protocols, and escalation procedures that scale across a growing global organization

  • Select, manage, and evaluate executive protection, secure transportation, travel security, investigative, and other specialized security vendors globally

  • Grow the vendor network — domestic and international — required to extend Crusoe's protective capabilities wherever the business operates

  • Support budget development, forecasting, and financial management for protective operations programs and vendors

Operational Partnership

  • Coordinate closely with the GSOC during executive travel, elevated-risk events, emerging threats, and critical incidents

  • Establish relationships with law enforcement, government agencies, security partners, and other external organizations relevant to protective operations

  • Support crisis and incident response involving executives, employees, travelers, threats, or other security events

Program Measurement and Maturity

  • Develop metrics and reporting to measure program effectiveness, emerging risks, protective activity, and opportunities for improvement

  • Help mature the Protective Operations function as Crusoe's global footprint and risk profile continue to evolve

  • Maintain discretion and sound judgment when handling highly sensitive executive, employee, investigative, and company information

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 10+ years of experience in executive protection, corporate security, protective intelligence, law enforcement, military protective operations, diplomatic security, or a related field

  • 5+ years leading complex executive protection, protective operations, or corporate security programs

  • Demonstrated experience protecting senior executives and supporting domestic and international travel

  • Strong experience conducting advances, threat assessments, security risk assessments, and protective planning

  • Experience developing and managing executive protection programs in a corporate environment strongly preferred

  • Knowledge of protective intelligence, behavioral threat assessment, workplace violence prevention, and threat management principles

  • Experience conducting or managing sensitive corporate or security investigations

  • Understanding of travel risk management, including international security environments, traveler risk assessment, emergency response, and duty-of-care considerations

  • Experience planning security for media engagements, executive appearances, major events, and other high-profile activities

  • Ability to assess rapidly evolving situations, make sound risk-based decisions, and operate effectively with incomplete information

  • Demonstrated ability to work with senior executives while maintaining discretion, professionalism, adaptability, and confidentiality

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to clearly communicate risk and recommendations to executives and business leaders

  • Experience managing specialized security vendors, executive protection providers, secure transportation providers, and other external partners

  • Ability to collaborate effectively across Legal, People, Communications, Information Security, Facilities, Operations, and other business functions

  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally approximately 30–50%, with periods of increased travel based on operational requirements

  • Ability to respond outside normal business hours when significant protective or security situations require support

Bonus Points

  • Prior service with U.S. Secret Service, Diplomatic Security Service, FBI, DEA, U.S. Marshals Service, or an equivalent federal protective agency

  • Military special operations background with protective detail experience (SOF, MARSOC, Naval Special Warfare, Air Force Special Tactics, or equivalent)

  • Prior corporate executive protection leadership experience within technology, critical infrastructure, data centers, energy, manufacturing, or another rapidly growing global organization

  • Experience leading principal-level protective details for Fortune 500 CEOs, founders, or high-net-worth principals

  • Experience developing enterprise Travel Risk Management or Workplace Violence Prevention programs

  • Experience conducting protective intelligence and open-source threat research

  • Experience supporting international operations and higher-risk travel environments, including gray and amber travel zones

  • Experience working with law enforcement, intelligence, diplomatic, or government security organizations

  • Familiarity with intelligence, case management, mass notification, travel risk, and security operations platforms (Ontic, Dataminr, Everbridge, International SOS, Crisis24, or peer tools)

  • CPP, PSP, PCI, Certified Threat Manager (CTM), ATAP certifications, or other relevant professional credentials

  • Multilingual capability, particularly in languages supporting Crusoe's international footprint


Operating Conditions:

  • San Francisco or Denver on-site, with domestic and international travel of approximately 30–50% to support executive protection, advance work, high-risk travel, site assessments, and major events

  • On-call availability for executive travel windows, elevated-risk events, emerging threats, and critical incidents

  • Response outside normal business hours when significant protective or security situations require support

  • Occasional nights, weekends, and holidays as the operational tempo demands

  • Handling of sensitive, confidential, and executive-protection information with appropriate discretion is a core expectation of the role

What Success Looks Like:

Success in this role means Crusoe has a proactive, intelligence-led, and risk-based protective operations program capable of supporting executives and employees wherever the business operates.

You will lead a program that identifies threats early, provides executives and travelers with appropriate protection without unnecessarily disrupting business, responds effectively to sensitive incidents, and scales as Crusoe expands into new markets and operating environments.

You will also establish a close operating partnership with the GSOC and the Intelligence Analyst: the GSOC maintains global situational awareness and enterprise threat monitoring, the Intelligence Analyst produces protective intelligence assessments, and Protective Operations owns the translation of intelligence into protective action.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 - $260,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About This Role:

Reporting to the Director of Quality, the Senior Supervisor, Quality Engineering is responsible for developing and leading a robust contract manufacturing and supplier quality management program. This role ensures that all sourced products, materials, and components meet Crusoe’s stringent quality standards while supporting the organization's growing strategic supplier requirements.

As a critical leader, you will drive continuous improvement across the contract manufacturing supply base, mitigate risks, and ensure compliance with industry regulations. You will serve as a key partner to the Senior Director of Program Management, the Director of Engineering, and executive stakeholders to maintain product integrity and operational efficiency.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Execution & Coordination: Define and execute a supplier quality vision and long-term strategy aligned with organizational goals and risk mitigation.

  • Supplier Management: Establish and maintain robust programs for supplier selection, development, monitoring, and performance scorecards.

  • Quality Systems: Implement incoming material reviews, CAPA processes, and traceability protocols to enable effective root cause analysis.

  • Standards & Compliance: Establish supplier quality systems consistent with ISO 9001 or similar standards and maintain compliance with regulatory requirements (such as UL 891).

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Procurement, Technology, R&D, and Operations to ensure suppliers meet specifications during volume ramps and resolve systemic process breakdowns.

  • Performance Tracking: Define and track KPIs for supplier quality, presenting data-driven insights and risk assessments to senior leadership.

  • Continuous Improvement: Promote a culture of quality and provide training to employees on process improvement and quality matters.

  • Risk Mitigation: Conduct assessments for critical suppliers and develop contingency strategies for quality-related supply chain disruptions.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or Industrial Engineering.

  • 5+ years experience in quality within a manufacturing/industrial environment.

  • 2+ years experience in leadership roles managing team performance and development.

  • Supplier Management: Understanding of Supplier Quality best practices, contract manufacturing management, and the ability to evaluate technical supplier capabilities.

  • System Knowledge: Experience developing and implementing supplier scorecards, performance dashboards, and quality improvement roadmaps.

  • Soft Skills: Exceptional communication and negotiation skills with a proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive alignment across functions.

  • Operational Attributes: Demonstrated ability to lead through ambiguity, manage conflict, and approve/disqualify vendors based on data-driven criteria.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required. Must be able to pass a background check.

  • Expertise in ISO 9001, UL 891, and Lean Six Sigma tools.

  • Direct experience developing and administering a full Quality Management System (QMS).

About the Role:

Crusoe is seeking a Sr. GRC Analyst to own and drive the day-to-day execution of our Governance, Risk, and Compliance program. Reporting to the Head of GRC, this role is responsible for running core compliance operations across our security and privacy frameworks, from user access reviews and audit evidence to customer trust support and vendor risk, while also bringing SOX expertise to the IT controls that underpin our internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR), from gap identification through remediation.

You'll be the engine behind our continuous compliance posture: keeping audits on track, maintaining policies and standards, responding to customer security inquiries, and driving improvements across our GRC platform. As a senior member of the team, you'll be expected to operate independently, take ownership of full audit cycles, and partner confidently with stakeholders across IT, Security, Finance, and Engineering. The ideal candidate is proactive, detail-oriented, and brings a mindset for efficiency, leveraging AI tools and automation to reduce manual effort and scale their impact across the program.

What You'll Be Working On:

Audit & Controls

  • Applying expertise in SOX audit requirements to support the design, operation, and testing of IT general controls (ITGCs), including access management, change management, and computer operations, and maintaining the related control documentation, process narratives, and risk-control matrices

  • Evaluating in-scope systems and processes to identify SOX control gaps, and partnering closely with control owners across IT, Finance, and Engineering to design and drive remediation plans with clear ownership and timelines through to closure

  • Collecting, organizing, and delivering audit evidence for SOX, SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and other framework requirements

  • Partnering with internal control owners to ensure evidence is accurate, current, and audit-ready

  • Acting as a day-to-day point of contact for internal and external auditors, managing requests and facilitating walkthroughs

  • Responding to evidence and documentation requests for various strategic initiatives

Compliance Operations

  • Owning the coordination and completion of User Access Reviews (UARs) across in-scope systems and applications on a recurring schedule, including those supporting financial reporting

  • Maintaining and updating organizational security policies and standards to reflect current regulatory and business requirements

  • Conducting third-party security assessments and supporting review of vendor contracts for compliance with security requirements

Customer Trust

  • Responding to customer security questionnaires and due diligence requests within established SLAs

  • Maintaining and updating the Security Diligence Playbook to ensure responses are consistent, accurate, and efficient


GRC Platform & Automation

  • Driving enhancements within our GRC tool, including asset management, integrations, test configurations, control mapping, review workflows, and risk objects

  • Identifying opportunities to streamline and automate repetitive GRC workflows, including continuous control monitoring

  • Applying AI and LLM-based tools to improve productivity across compliance operations, such as accelerating questionnaire responses, summarizing audit evidence, or drafting policy updates

  • Tracking and reporting on compliance metrics and control health to GRC leadership

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 5–7 years of experience in GRC, information security, IT audit, or a related compliance role, with demonstrated ownership of end-to-end audit cycles

  • Practical knowledge of compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and NIST CSF

  • Solid understanding of SOX 404 audit requirements and IT general controls, with hands-on experience identifying control gaps and working with stakeholders to remediate them

  • Hands-on experience with GRC platforms (Vanta preferred; Drata, AuditBoard, or similar also valued)

  • Experience conducting user access reviews, vendor risk assessments, and internal audits

  • Familiarity with responding to customer security questionnaires and managing trust center content

  • Comfort using AI tools (e.g., Gemini, Claude, Copilot) to accelerate day-to-day work and improve operational efficiency

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate compliance requirements for both technical and non-technical audiences; skilled at influencing control owners without direct authority

  • Highly organized, self-directed, and able to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders independently

  • Detail-oriented with strong follow-through on recurring operational tasks

Bonus Points

  • Certifications such as CISA, CRISC, CISSP, Security+, or ISO 27001 Lead Auditor

  • Background from public accounting and/or high-growth technology companies navigating SOX compliance

  • Experience with cloud environments (GCP preferred; AWS/Azure exposure helpful)

  • Familiarity with financial systems (ERP, billing, or revenue recognition platforms)

  • Experience with policy management and security awareness training platforms

  • Familiarity with AI risk assessment frameworks and emerging AI governance practices

  • Experience mentoring junior analysts or leading cross-functional compliance initiatives

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $130,000 - $155,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Lead Financial Analyst, Manufacturing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe’s Manufacturing business is ramping quickly, with a limited history of controllership and financial planning that is still largely top-down. The Lead Analyst, FP&A is the hands-on owner of the financial engine for the MFG business: the integrated model, the planning cycles, and the KPIs leadership uses to run the business. You will work with the MFG Finance managers covering the Data centre and Spark products, and with BI, Field Services and BizOps. You will move planning from top-down to bottoms-up, tied to real business inputs and execution.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with a lot of room to shape how Manufacturing Finance operates. You will be the hands-on builder and day-to-day owner of the MFG financial model, planning cycles, and reporting, which means you’ll do the work yourself rather than direct it. At the same time, you’ll set the standards for how the team plans, models, and reports, including model architecture, data definitions, templates, and review cadence. Because MFG Finance is early in its build-out, much of what you create will become the team’s default way of working.

You’ll be the central analytical hub of the team. The DC and Spark finance leads, the MFG BI team, Field Services, BizOps Data Analytics, and Accounting will all rely on your model and your numbers, so you’ll need to be as comfortable aligning stakeholders and defending assumptions as you are in a spreadsheet. You’ll have regular visibility with Finance leadership and business executives through the MBR and other forums, and your analysis will directly inform decisions on supplier and CM engagements, cost and margin targets, and cash planning.

What You'll Be Working On:

Financial model and planning

  • Build and run the consolidated MFG business unit financial model covering close support, forecast, long-range plan (LRP), budget, and scenario analysis.

  • Own variance analysis models and templates such as volume/rate/mix variances

  • Drive bottoms-up planning by translating inputs from Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering and Field Services into financial outcomes.

  • Build scenario and sensitivity models for volume, supplier pricing, schedule shifts, and cost and margin targets.

  • Support cash flow planning and liquidity analysis for the MFG business.

Reporting and KPIs

  • Own the financial content of the Monthly Business Review (MBR), including variance analysis, commentary, and executive-ready materials.

  • Define, track, and report key business and finance KPIs (such as cost, margin, headcount, Opex, and utilization), and drive accountability for them with business & finance owners.

  • Automate reporting and keep data definitions and sources consistent.

Business & Finance partnership

  • Partner with broader FP&A team to drive end to end planning, timelines & R&Rs for Rhythm of Business (Close, Forecast, Budget and LRP)

  • Partner with the DC and Spark finance leads to give them a consistent planning and reporting foundation.

  • Build the business-case evaluation template for supplier and contract manufacturer (CM) engagements, and support analysis of sourcing and CM decisions.

  • Provide finance support to Field Services and New Product Introduction (NPI), including cost tracking and program-level analysis.

  • Work with Accounting on close, accruals, inventory and cost accounting questions, and help strengthen controllership as the business scales.

Tools and process

  • Own the finance tools roadmap for MFG, including model architecture, data pipelines, and dashboards.

  • Document processes and train partners on tools and planning calendars.

  • Help set up the planning infrastructure for Phase 2 (integrated supply planning and S&OP) as the team grows.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, or another quantitative field.

  • 7+ years in FP&A, corporate finance, business finance, or consulting, with a track record of owning planning cycles (budget, forecast, LRP) end to end.

  • Advanced financial modeling skills, including building large, multi-driver models from scratch.

  • Experience supporting hardware, manufacturing, supply chain or tech businesses, with working knowledge of COGS, BOM cost, inventory, and CM or supplier economics.

  • Strong data skills: advanced Excel or Google Sheets and SQL, plus experience with BI and visualization tools (such as Looker or Tableau).

  • Ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations for senior, non-finance leaders.

  • Comfort working in ambiguity in a fast-growth environment, with a bias to build and iterate.

Preferred

  • Experience in data center, AI infrastructure, semiconductor, or other capital-intensive technology companies.

  • Experience with planning systems (such as Adaptive, Anaplan, or Hyperion) and ERP data (such as NetSuite or SAP).

  • Exposure to cash flow forecasting, capital planning, or S&OP processes.

  • Working knowledge of NPI and field or service operations economics.

  • MBA, CPA, or CFA.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000-$195,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role

As a Principal Software Engineer for Infrastructure, you will partner with teams across the company to help shape the technical direction of the compute, storage, and networking platforms that power Crusoe’s AI-first cloud. This is a high-leverage leadership role that spans the full infrastructure stack: you will work alongside engineers and stakeholders on the systems that help massive GPU clusters run AI and HPC workloads at extreme throughput, low latency, and high reliability. Your work spans the Linux kernel, hypervisors and virtualization, distributed storage, network fabrics, and the control planes that tie them together.

You will be a trusted technical partner across the infrastructure stack, helping guide architecture decisions and mentoring engineers to raise our collective technical bar. You will look at the whole system alongside the teams who own each layer: how a storage tier, a scheduler, and a network fabric interact under a multi-node training job, and where the real bottleneck sits. You will collaborate closely with Product, Hardware, and Infrastructure teams to build a reliable, scalable platform together that aligns with Crusoe’s mission to innovate sustainably. This is a full-time position.

What You’ll Be Working On

  • Infrastructure Strategy: Partner with engineering, product, and leadership to help shape the long-term direction for compute, storage, and networking, and to turn that direction into practical plans and milestones.

  • Architecture & Design: Collaborate with teams on architecture reviews, design documents, and code reviews for critical infrastructure components and services across all three domains.

  • Compute & Virtualization: Work with compute teams on the virtualization and orchestration layers that deliver bare-metal-class performance to GPU workloads, including hypervisor tuning, SR-IOV, vDPA, virtio, device passthrough, and NUMA- and topology-aware scheduling.

  • Storage Systems: Work with storage teams on high-throughput, low-latency storage for training and inference pipelines, including distributed block, file, and object storage, NVMe and NVMe-oF, RDMA-based data paths, and checkpointing and data-loading performance.

  • Networking & Fabric: Partner with networking teams on architectures for GPU-to-GPU fabrics, high-speed Ethernet, and specialized AI clusters, using technologies such as XDP, eBPF, DPDK, OVS/OVN, BGP, EVPN, and VXLAN.

  • Kernel & Driver Work: Contribute to Linux kernel modules and high-performance drivers across the network, storage, and device stack.

  • Hardware Integration: Work with Hardware teams on accelerators and offload devices, including GPUs, SmartNICs, DPUs, IPUs, and NVMe, from qualification through bring-up of new platforms.

  • Cross-Stack Performance & Reliability: Team up with on-call, SRE, and domain engineers to troubleshoot complex production issues that cross compute, storage, and network boundaries, and to improve performance, observability, capacity planning, and failure-domain design.

  • Technology Evaluation: Explore emerging infrastructure technologies with the team, contribute to open-source projects where strategically relevant, and share learnings with the broader organization.

  • Mentorship & Collaboration: Partner with internal stakeholders on end-to-end features, and mentor and support engineers across teams to foster a culture of engineering excellence.

What You’ll Bring to the Team

  • Large-Scale Infrastructure Mastery: 10+ years of experience building and operating large-scale infrastructure systems in production, ideally within cloud or hyperscale data center environments.

  • Cross-Domain Breadth: Hands-on experience across compute, storage, and networking, and a track record of solving problems that cross domain boundaries.

  • Systems Programming Excellence: Strong systems programming skills in C, C++, Rust, or Go, with experience working on performance-critical services and control planes.

  • Linux Internals Depth: Extensive knowledge of the Linux kernel architecture, memory management, scheduler, I/O and network stacks, and device driver development.

  • Virtualization & Compute Literacy: Experience with KVM/QEMU or similar hypervisors, container runtimes, and orchestration platforms such as Kubernetes, plus an understanding of GPU, CPU, and NUMA topology and its effect on workload performance.

  • Storage Literacy: Familiarity with distributed storage architectures (block, file, or object), NVMe/NVMe-oF, RDMA, and the consistency, durability, and performance tradeoffs involved.

  • Network & Fabric Literacy: Familiarity with data center fabrics (e.g., Spine-Leaf, BGP, EVPN, VXLAN), network virtualization tools such as OVS or OVN, and high-speed packet processing technologies such as XDP, eBPF, or DPDK.

  • Accelerator Knowledge: Familiarity with SmartNICs, DPUs, and accelerators, such as NVIDIA ConnectX-6/7 and BlueField-3 or Intel IPUs.

  • Production Debugging: Experience working with others to diagnose complex issues across the full stack, from hardware and firmware through the kernel to control-plane software.

  • Strategic Influence: A proven track record of leading through influence, with excellent written communication skills and a strong mentoring mindset.

  • Education: A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related analytical field (or equivalent professional experience).

Bonus Points

  • Open-Source Contributions: Active contributions to projects such as the Linux kernel, KVM/QEMU, Kubernetes, Ceph, OVS, OVN, Cilium, or Multus.

  • Orchestration & Automation Expertise: Experience with infrastructure automation, fleet management, or complex orchestration tooling.

  • GPU Training at Scale: Prior experience building compute, storage, or networking stacks for multi-node GPU training at scale.

  • Hardware Co-Design: Experience working with hardware teams on platform design, qualification, and firmware-to-software integration.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $285,000 - $335,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Talent Acquisition Program Manager II
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is growing rapidly, and the way we recruit has to keep up. Many of the practices that carried us this far, such as workflows patched together with one-off configurations, tooling choices made vendor by vendor, and process knowledge that lives with a few individuals, will not hold as hiring volume rises and we open in new countries.

We are hiring a senior owner to build what comes next.

You will be responsible for the product side of Talent Acquisition: advising on the road map for our recruiting tech stack (Ashby, sourcing tools, Metaview), the design of hiring workflows from requisition intake to onboarding handoff, and the programs that make our processes work globally. Right now, improvements tend to happen when someone feels enough pain to raise them. In this role, you make improvement a steady, planned part of how TA works.

The right person is a program manager who designs durable systems rather than one-time fixes, is comfortable with workflow automation and AI-enabled tools, and can keep recruiters, hiring managers, and vendors on track without having them report to you.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Recruiting technology and vendor strategy

    • Advise TA leadership on the roadmap for the recruiting tech stack. Identify where automation, AI, integrations, and self-service can reduce manual work across Ashby, our sourcing tools, and Metaview.

    • Partner with vendors and internal partners on how AI and agentic tools can make recruiters more effective, and confirm that each technology choice is sustainable to maintain.

    • Create a lightweight framework for evaluating and approving new tools, since none exists today.

  • Workflow analysis and process redesign

    • Map the full candidate and hiring lifecycle, from requisition intake through offer and onboarding handoff, and surface friction and duplicated effort proactively.

    • Redesign processes with methods such as Lean, Six Sigma, and the 5 Whys, weighing system configuration, user experience, and policy changes against the outcome you want.

    • Maintain current process documentation and workflow maps so that Recruiting, People Technology, and Legal can self-serve instead of submitting requests.

  • Business cases, metrics, and prioritization

    • Write business cases that put numbers on operational impact, experience gains, and ROI, then use them to rank initiatives by impact, scalability, and strategic fit.

    • Work with Recruiting leadership and Analytics to define and report on core recruiting metrics, and investigate the underlying cause when a target is missed.

    • Support preparation of the regular metrics reviews and executive summaries TA leadership shares with the business.

    • Track adoption and realized ROI against each business case after launch.

  • Global expansion enablement

    • Build recruiting processes and tooling that scale and meet local requirements as we enter new regions, working closely with Legal, Compliance, and regional partners.

    • Build local hiring regulations, data privacy, and AI compliance into designs from the start rather than adding them later.

    • Develop a reusable launch playbook for hiring at each new site.

  • Program and portfolio management

    • Lead transformation and technology initiatives from start to finish: scoping, requirements, project plans, user acceptance testing, launch readiness, and post-launch review.

    • Run pilots and phased rollouts with success criteria agreed in advance, and use the results to expand, refine, or retire the initiative.

    • Balance the full portfolio of work against competing priorities, capacity, and timelines.

  • Change management and adoption

    • Manage risks, dependencies, and stakeholders across Recruiting, People Technology, Legal, Compliance, and the business, and clear blockers early.

    • Plan the communications, training, and feedback loops for every rollout. A launch only counts once people are using the new way of working.

  • Systems and automation

    • Treat repeated manual follow-up as a signal that something needs to be automated, and replace it with a form, workflow, dashboard, or scheduled alert.

    • Keep the configuration, documentation, and structure of the tools and files these programs depend on in good order, and move work into proper systems wherever they exist.

    • Produce a playbook that any recruiter, coordinator, or program manager can follow without your involvement.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 8+ years in recruiting operations, including TA program management, or product management, with experience in a fast-growing company and a history of taking on broader scope and influence.

  • A record of leading complex, cross-functional transformation programs from business case through launch, including UAT, communications, launch planning, and broad adoption.

  • Deep experience analyzing and redesigning processes with Lean, service design, or comparable methods.

  • Hands-on experience with ATS platforms (Ashby preferred) and the wider recruiting stack, plus experience selecting and implementing AI and workflow automation with vendors and technical partners. You have automated work you once did manually.

  • Strong analytical ability: defining metrics, finding root causes, building business cases, and quantifying ROI to guide investment.

  • The ability to hold senior stakeholders to commitments while keeping their trust. People respond to you because you are clear about what you need, the reason, and the deadline.

  • Excellent written communication for technical and non-technical readers alike. You can write one clear update that gets a large group moving in the same direction without a meeting.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and high volume, including taking over active programs where documentation is incomplete.

  • Humility and drive: you will happily run the pilot, and you will also fix the process that made the pilot necessary.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Human Resources, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Bonus Points

  • Experience in a high-growth cloud, AI infrastructure, or deep tech company where hiring volume and process demands scale fast.

  • Familiarity with AI-native or agentic recruiting platforms, including configuring them or working with engineers on custom internal tools.

  • Skill with interview intelligence tools (such as Metaview) and recruiting analytics or BI platforms.

  • Experience supporting recruiting expansion into international markets, including work with local employment counsel or regional hiring partners.

  • Change management experience in which a new operating model reached measurable adoption.

  • PMP, Lean Six Sigma, or a similar certification.

  • Interest in building and leading a small team as the function grows.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $130,000 - $160,000+ Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

As the Onboarding Operations Specialist, you will be the operational heartbeat of Crusoe’s new hire experience. Sitting at the intersection of logistics, systems administration, and physical employee welcome experiences, you will ensure that every new hire receives a seamless, flawless, and memorable introduction to Crusoe from the moment they accept their offer through their first week.

This is a high-touch, detail-oriented, onsite role based in our San Francisco headquarters. You will manage complex onboarding logistics across our global footprint, administer core data workflows in our HRIS (Rippling, Workday) and ticketing platforms (Jira), and help bring our San Francisco in-person orientation experience to life every week.

 
 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • HRIS Data & Lifecycle Management: Own the Jira onboarding queue for new hire offer acceptances. Launch and review new hire profiles in HRIS, ensuring precise data entry for segment allocation, EEOC tracking, IT department mappings, and state payroll registrations.

  • Data Changes & Cross-Functional Coordination: Manage data change tickets (start date shifts, manager/department updates) in Jira and HRIS. Proactively notify cross-functional partners in IT, Workplace, Travel, and Payroll when changes impact logistics.

  • New Hire & Manager Communications: Own the global onboarding inbox, delivering prompt, accurate answers to new hires. Maintain automated pre-hire HRIS workflows, email templates, and Slack communications to keep new hires and managers informed and prepared.

  • New Hire Travel Coordination: Oversee new hire travel procedures and ensure effective internal and external communications related to travel needs.

  • I-9 & Compliance Operations: Execute complete I-9 verification checks for new cohorts, manage E-Verify processing (including image checks), and follow up on outstanding documentation to maintain 100% legal compliance.

 
 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Operational Rigor & Attention to Detail: Meticulous execution skills with a track record of handling high-volume operational tasks, logistics, and data entry without dropping details.

  • HRIS & Ticketing Systems Experience: Direct hands-on experience using modern HRIS platforms (e.g., Rippling, Workday) and task management tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence).

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to communicate clearly and coordinate effectively across IT, Workplace, Travel, Payroll, and hiring managers.

  • Problem-Solving & Agility: Strong troubleshooting instincts when start dates shift, virtual stream links mismatch, or last-minute schedule changes arise.

  • High-Touch Hospitality Mindset: A passion for creating warm, memorable, and welcoming candidate and employee experiences.

 

Bonus Points

  • Experience supporting multi-site or hybrid in-person and remote onboarding programs.

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $50.00 - $60.00 per hour. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

 

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Manager, Logistics & Asset Management
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads.
