We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role

Crusoe Cloud is standing up a dedicated logistics and asset management function to support rapid growth across our global production footprint. The Manager, Logistics & Asset Management will own the design and standardization of logistics, spares, inventory and asset-tracking processes across every Crusoe Cloud site, from initial deployment through hardware decommission, and will build the cross-site operating model that keeps parts and assets moving reliably to support 24/7 white-space operations.

This is a builder role, you will define how logistics and asset management should work across a fast-growing, geographically distributed fleet, and you will be the connective tissue between site-level execution and factory/supply-chain operations.

Reporting Structure

This role reports to the Director, Cloud Site Operations and holds a dotted-line, functional relationship to each site's Logistics Coordinator; setting shared processes, tools, and performance standards for logistics and asset management across Crusoe Cloud Data Centers across the world.. Each Site Logistics Coordinator retains a solid-line reporting relationship to their local Site Manager for day-to-day direction and performance management. In short: this role sets the playbook, while site managers continue to run day-to-day site operations and people management.

What You'll Do

  • Define and standardize logistics, spares, and asset-management processes across all Crusoe Cloud production sites, including current colo sites and upcoming builds as the footprint expands

  • Own the functional (dotted-line) relationship with each site's Logistics Coordinator — setting shared processes, tools, and performance standards while site managers retain day-to-day direction of those coordinators

  • Govern the on-site parts depot / sparing model, including per-site sizing and scope, in partnership with site teams and vendor/sourcing partners

  • Partner with Crusoe's Spark factory logistics and inventory teams (Brighton, CO) to align site-level logistics practices with upstream manufacturing and fulfillment processes

  • Build and maintain asset-tracking standards and processes across sites, including physical inventory accuracy, reconciliation cadence, auditing, and system-of-record integrity

  • Develop onboarding, training, and documentation so Site Logistics Coordinators can execute consistently regardless of site or region

  • Establish KPIs and reporting for logistics and asset-management health across the site portfolio, and surface risks (stockouts, reconciliation gaps, process drift) to site and SiteOps leadership

  • Support new-site standups by scoping logistics and asset-management requirements as part of site launch planning

  • Travel to production sites as needed to assess local conditions, support coordinators directly, and validate that standardized processes are working in practice

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Experience designing or running logistics, inventory, or asset-management programs across multiple physical sites or facilities

  • Comfort operating in a dotted-line/matrixed structure; influencing and setting standards for people you don't directly manage

  • Background in data center, manufacturing, warehouse, or supply-chain operations

  • Experience building processes from scratch in a fast-growing or scaling environment, rather than optimizing an already-mature program

  • Strong systems/process orientation, comfortable defining standards, documentation, and KPIs that others will execute against daily

  • Willingness to travel regularly to global production sites

Preferred

  • Data center or GPU/compute hardware operations experience

  • Experience partnering with manufacturing or factory logistics teams on upstream supply chain alignment

  • Experience supporting new data center standups in a multi-site organization

Location

This role is based out of Bellevue, Washington; San Francisco, California; or Denver, Colorado, with regular travel to Crusoe Cloud production sites globally.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000 -$195,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role

Crusoe’s Service Desk team plays a critical role in troubleshooting, configuring, and resolving issues across servers, networks, infrastructure, SaaS applications, and file shares. You’ll partner closely with teams across the company and external vendors to elevate the user experience and keep operations running smoothly. We’re looking for someone self-motivated and customer-obsessed, who thrives in a fast-paced environment, takes pride in solving complex technical problems, and is energized by continuous learning and opportunities to grow.

What You’ll Be Working On

  • Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues across networks, infrastructure, and SaaS applications in a fast-paced environment.

  • Partner with cross-functional teams and external vendors to improve system performance and deliver seamless user support.

  • Own complex issues end to end, from initial report through resolution, documenting outcomes and driving system improvements.

  • Administer and configure cloud identity platforms, MDM automation, and MDR/XDR tools to keep the IT ecosystem secure and efficient.

  • Lead technology rollouts and system upgrades as part of company-wide infrastructure initiatives.

What You’ll Bring to the Team

  • Strong background in cloud identity management platforms (SSO, SAML 2.0, and MFA).

  • Hands-on experience with MDM automation tools such as Google MDM, Kandji, or Intune.

  • Experience administering and troubleshooting Windows, macOS, and Linux systems.

  • Familiarity with MDR/XDR platforms such as Sophos XDR, CrowdStrike, or Huntress.

  • Proficiency with ticketing systems, IT documentation platforms, and SaaS management.

  • Experience working as a project-oriented engineer, comfortable leading initiatives end to end.

  • Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to self-start, collaborate, and problem-solve effectively.

  • Ability to pass a background check.

Bonus Points

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience with 6+ years of IT systems experience.

  • Prior experience working in large enterprises with significant user bases.

  • Previous NOC/SOC experience.

Benefits:

Crusoe also offers a competitive benefits package designed to support financial security, health, and overall well-being. Our benefits are tailored to local market standards and include core offerings such as pension contributions and additional perks to support work-life balance.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join the Admin Tooling team within Cloud Customer Experience (CCX). The CCX organization is at the forefront of delivering a best-in-class user experience for both internal and external users of our AI-focused cloud platform.

The Admin Tooling team owns the foundations of internal tooling to provide a secure, reliable, self-service platform that enables internal teams to move fast without giving up the governance and auditing our customers expect.

Crusoe's internal tooling requirements continue to evolve rapidly alongside the growth of the business. As a founding member of the Admin Tooling team you will be responsible for contributing to the product and technical vision for internal tooling across the company.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Partner Cross-Functionally: Work closely with Product and Design, Developer Experience, Security and Customer Success teams to understand bottlenecks across the company and propose new processes and software solutions to address them.

  • Drive Architectural Vision & Strategy: Own the end-to-end technical roadmap for the admin tooling stack. This includes AuthN and AuthZ systems, API and microservice design, and client interfaces including Web, CLI and MCP.

  • Own Critical Systems: Maintain and extend existing internal tools that enable customer interactions, complex datacenter operations and other business-critical functions.

  • Mentor and Lead: Set team engineering practices, drive design reviews, and mentor junior and mid-level engineers to build a high-performing engineering culture.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Professional Experience: 5+ years of software development experience, including programming with modern compiled languages such as Go, Rust, Java, or C++. Our services are primarily written in Go.

  • Communication Skills: Exceptional ability to talk directly with end users, empathize with their problems and align on a solution that is technically sound and solves those problems.

  • Bias to Action: A proven track record of quickly and efficiently understanding problems and delivering software to address those problems.

  • System Design: Proven ability to design and scale fault-tolerant distributed systems and develop managed cloud services.

  • Observability and Reliability: Experience defining SLOs, instrumenting services with metrics, logs, and traces, and using that signal to debug production issues.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with RBAC/Permissioning systems

  • Experience with TypeScript/React

  • Experience with internal tooling/developer platforms such as Retool or Backstage

Benefits:

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

Crusoe's internal tooling requirements continue to evolve rapidly alongside the growth of the business. As a founding member of the Admin Tooling team you will be responsible for contributing to the product and technical vision for internal tooling across the company.



What You'll Be Working On:

 - Partner Cross-Functionally: Work closely with Product and Design, Developer Experience, Security and Customer Success teams to understand bottlenecks across the company and propose new processes and software solutions to address them.

 - Drive Architectural Vision & Strategy: Own the end-to-end technical roadmap for the admin tooling stack. This includes AuthN and AuthZ systems, API and microservice design, and client interfaces including Web, CLI and MCP.

 - Own Critical Systems: Maintain and extend existing internal tools that enable customer interactions, complex datacenter operations and other business-critical functions.

 - Mentor and Lead: Set team engineering practices, drive design reviews, and mentor junior and mid-level engineers to build a high-performing engineering culture.



What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - Professional Experience: 5+ years of software development experience, including programming with modern compiled languages such as Go, Rust, Java, or C++. Our services are primarily written in Go.

 - Communication Skills: Exceptional ability to talk directly with end users, empathize with their problems and align on a solution that is technically sound and solves those problems.

 - Bias to Action: A proven track record of quickly and efficiently understanding problems and delivering software to address those problems.

 - System Design: Proven ability to design and scale fault-tolerant distributed systems and develop managed cloud services.

 - Observability and Reliability: Experience defining SLOs, instrumenting services with metrics, logs, and traces, and using that signal to debug production issues.
   
   

Bonus Points

 - Experience with RBAC/Permissioning systems

 - Experience with TypeScript/React

 - Experience with internal tooling/developer platforms such as Retool or Backstage

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

About the Role:

Crusoe is building the infrastructure that powers the AI revolution — data centers, power generation, manufacturing, construction, and corporate offices expanding across North America. The physical security technology stack protecting those sites has to perform at SLA at all times.

The Senior Physical Security Systems Engineer owns the standards, SLAs, and ongoing performance of that stack. You set the standards our Design and Construction team deploys against, validate deployed systems at acceptance, and own the configuration, integration health, and lifecycle management of the stack once sites go live. You will work closely with the GSOC, Senior Physical Security Intelligence Analyst, Protective Operations, Design and Construction, IT, and Network Engineering.

The ideal candidate brings hands-on operator experience from a hyperscale, data center, critical infrastructure, or technology environment and knows how to run a multi-site stack without breaking it.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Set and own the physical security systems standards that the Design and Construction team deploys against; validate systems at acceptance and own the operational handoff into production

  • Define and own SLAs for platform availability, camera uptime, access control responsiveness, alarm quality, and integration health

  • Operate access control, video management, intrusion detection, visitor management, and incident platforms at configuration depth

  • Build and maintain integrations across the stack and with Ontic, Active Directory, and mass notification; script automation for health monitoring, SLA reporting, and lifecycle tasks

  • Partner with Network Engineering, IT, and OT on VLAN segmentation, bandwidth, cert management, Active Directory integration, and device hardening

  • Own firmware strategy, patch management, device lifecycle, tech refresh, and health monitoring dashboards across the footprint

  • Ensure systems generate the audit evidence supporting SOC 2, ISO 27001, NERC CIP, and customer contractual requirements; partner with GRC on audit cycles

  • Coordinate with the GSOC on system health and operator tooling; partner with the Intelligence Analyst on Ontic deployment; support Protective Operations on executive protection and event systems; support crisis and incident response involving physical

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 7+ years operating enterprise physical security systems at operator depth

  • Hands-on fluency with access control platforms (Lenel, Genetec, Genea, or similar system) and video management systems (Genetec, Milestone, Ambient, or similar system)

  • Strong IT and networking fluency — VLAN segmentation, bandwidth planning, cert management, Active Directory integration, firmware and patch strategy, device hardening

  • Experience setting operational standards and SLAs and holding systems accountable to them across distributed, multi-site operations

  • Strong written and verbal communication across technical and executive audiences

  • Ability to collaborate across the GSOC, Protective Operations, Intelligence, Design and Construction, IT, and Network Engineering

  • Ability to travel domestically approximately 20–35% and respond outside normal business hours when significant situations require support

  • Strong IT and networking fluency — VLAN segmentation, bandwidth planning, cert management, Active Directory integration, firmware and patch strategy, device hardening

  • Experience setting operational standards and SLAs and holding systems accountable to them across distributed, multi-site operations

  • Strong written and verbal communication across technical and executive audiences

  • Ability to collaborate across the GSOC, Protective Operations, Intelligence, Design and Construction, IT, and Network Engineering

  • Ability to travel domestically approximately 20–35% and respond outside normal business hours when significant situations require support

Bonus Points

  • Hyperscale data center, critical infrastructure, power generation, or technology environment experience

  • NERC CIP compliance experience

  • Advanced scripting, API, or automation experience applied to physical security systems

  • Prior experience at Meta, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, CyrusOne, Vantage, Tesla, SpaceX, Apple, or a peer organization

  • Vendor-side or integrator-side senior engineering experience with a desire to move to a client-side operator role

  • Military signals, communications, OT engineering, or physical security MOS translation

  • Certifications: PSP, CPP, platform-specific (Genetec, Lenel, Milestone, Verkada, Ambient), network (CCNA, Security+, or peer)

Operating Conditions:

  • Dallas on-site, with domestic travel of approximately 20–35%

  • On-call availability for critical systems events, SLA breaches, and major incidents

  • Occasional nights, weekends, and holidays as the operational tempo demands

  • Handling of sensitive security systems, access data, video content, and company information with discretion is a core expectation

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $150,000 -$180,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.title: Associate / Senior Associate, Corporate Development
jobs.descriptionHtml:

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly motivated and analytical professional to join our Corporate Finance team as an Associate, Corporate Development.

This role requires a unique blend of financial structuring expertise, capital allocation discipline, and world-class relationship management to secure and optimize the financing essential for our high-growth initiatives.

What You'll Be Working On:

Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) and Divestitures

  • Market Mapping and Origination: Work across the organization’s business units and functions to identify acquisition targets from a sector-first perspective. Focus areas include AI / Digital infrastructure, Technology & Software, Industrials, Energy and Real Estate. This includes creating and maintaining market maps, running thematic research projects and reaching out directly to targets.

  • Transaction Execution: Support the end-to-end M&A process, including target identification, strategic rationale development, due diligence, valuation, negotiation and closing.

  • Financial Modeling & Valuation: Build and maintain complex financial models (valuation and merger models, accretion/dilution analyses and precedent transaction analyses) to evaluate potential acquisitions.

  • Due Diligence: Coordinate and manage cross-functional due diligence teams (Legal, Finance, Operations, etc.), synthesizing key findings and developing risk mitigation strategies. Work closely with third-party providers.

  • Market Analysis: Conduct industry and competitive landscape analysis within the AI / Digital Infrastructure, Technology & Software, Industrials, Energy and Real Estate sectors. Examples include data centers, compute, power and cooling, connectivity, and AI and infrastructure software. The goal is to identify strategic market gaps and attractive investment opportunities.

  • Prepare and present transaction rationale to the Executive Leadership Team and possibly the Board of Directors.

Strategic Investments & Partnerships

  • Sourcing and Evaluation: Evaluate strategic investment and partnership opportunities that align with the company’s long-term growth objectives.

  • Deal Structuring: Assist in structuring and negotiating terms for joint ventures, strategic alliances and minority investments.

  • Business Case Development: Create compelling investment memorandums and presentations for Senior Leadership, outlining strategic fit, financial implications and execution plans.

General Corporate Development

  • Pipeline Management: Help manage and maintain a robust pipeline of potential M&A and investment targets.

  • Commercial-facing Activities: Attend conferences and travel to industry events to support origination and market intelligence.

  • Reporting: Prepare detailed analytical reports and presentations on key market trends, portfolio performance and deal progress for internal stakeholders.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely with internal business unit leaders to assess strategic needs and integration plans.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 1–3+ years of experience in Investment Banking (Analyst or Associate level), Corporate Development, Private Equity or Transaction Advisory Services.

  • Direct experience on M&A transactions, including a core role in structuring and modeling different scenarios and preparing transaction screening memos.

  • Strong coverage experience or deep sector knowledge within AI / Digital Infrastructure, Technology & Software, Industrials, Energy and/or Real Estate is highly preferred.

  • Exceptional financial modeling and valuation skills, with advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.

  • Outstanding analytical and problem-solving abilities, with the ability to turn complex financial and strategic analysis into clear, concise and actionable recommendations.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and comfort presenting to senior executives and external partners.

  • A high degree of professionalism and intellectual curiosity, and the ability to manage multiple projects and work well under tight deadlines.

  • A proactive, self-starter mentality, with the ability to work independently while being a strong team player.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting or a related quantitative field.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $130,000 - $160,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is built on vertical integration, and our advantage depends on how well our business units work together. This role sits at the center of that. You’ll strategize and build the Crusoe Operating System: the software, processes, and AI that connect our business units and make vertical integration a real operating advantage.

You’ll work side by side with the CTO and senior leaders to keep teams aligned, initiatives moving, and priorities clear as the company grows quickly. You’ll support the CTO and a direct staff of about six, work closely with Crusoe Cloud Engineering and Product, and have direct access to the people making the biggest decisions.

This is a high-agency role. This is not merely tracking and directing others; you will roll up your sleeves and complete nebulous projects yourself. You spot what needs attention before anyone asks, and you step in without waiting for direction. The problems are real and high-impact: coordination gaps between teams, initiatives that stall without an owner, and processes that work at one stage and break at the next. You’ll build the structure and clarity that let a fast-scaling company run as one organization.

This is not a calendar-and-slide-deck chief of staff role, and it isn’t a program manager scoped to a single initiative. You’ll need enough technical depth to engage credibly with engineering leaders and enough organizational instinct to work in the seams between teams.

If you like getting your hands dirty, do your best work in fast-moving environments, and want a tangible impact on how a high-growth company at the junction of the world’s most important industries operates, we’d like to meet you.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Build the Crusoe Operating System. Strategize and build the combination of software, processes, and AI that ties our business units together.

  • Lead internal AI and IT strategy. Weave modern technology into every business process at Crusoe.

  • Support the CTO and the CTO’s staff. Partner with the CTO and a staff of about six to keep priorities clear and work moving.

  • Be the connective tissue across leadership. Build real relationships with executives, senior leaders and tech leads. Know what’s actually going on in their orgs, and help them see the things they’re too close to notice.

  • Keep the health of the org strong. Chase down open items and keep processes streamlined.

  • Build and own the KPI infrastructure. Give leadership real visibility through dashboards, operational metrics, and initiative trackers. Data should tell the story before anyone has to ask.

  • Keep the org close. Identify redundant processes and gaps, and suggest ways to close and collapse them.

  • Push back with technical credibility. Go deep on the topics that matter, don’t accept surface-level answers, and hold yourself and others accountable to commitments.

  • Be the face of the CTO’s office in cross-functional forums. Represent priorities and constraints clearly so individual teams aren’t pulled in ten directions by people who aren’t in the room.

  • Own the cross-cutting programs that don’t have a natural single owner. Technology adoption, tooling decisions, org-wide comms, and similar work. If nobody owns it, you do.

  • Coordinate headcount planning and org design. Handle the operational logistics of scaling across multiple sites and countries.

  • Use AI tooling and agentic systems aggressively. Aggregate information across a large, globally distributed org, and build systems and workflows that scale.

  • Tighten the connective tissue between our operational tools. Operational data should flow cleanly into reporting and decisions without manual stitching.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Engineering or computer science background strongly preferred, with 8+ years in software engineering and operations.

  • The ability to operate independently with little direction.

  • People skills to talk to every executive as a peer, and to represent engineering and IT credibly to every team at Crusoe.

  • A solutions-oriented approach, with strong documentation and organization.

  • Experience in a high-growth technology environment where things break and processes are still being built. Ambiguity doesn’t paralyze you; it’s where you do your best work.

  • Experience helping scale an organization through a significant growth phase. You know which processes to formalize and which to leave lightweight.

  • Strong opinions about operational excellence, and the willingness to push back on leaders when follow-through slips. Diplomacy matters, but so does directness.

  • The ability to work across teams without formal authority. People trust you because you come prepared, follow up, and make their lives easier.

  • The ability to take messy, inconsistent data from multiple sources and turn it into a clear picture of organizational health.

  • A scrappy mindset. When the automation doesn’t exist yet, you build it or do it manually until it does.

  • Low ego, high drive. You care about the outcome more than the credit.

Bonus Points

  • Previous founder, or early stage engineer

  • Cloud experience, close to the physical infrastructure

  • Experience standing up or running an operations or chief of staff function from scratch

  • Experience driving quarterly or annual planning for organizations of 200+ people

  • Background in AI/ML infrastructure

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $230,000 - $280,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Strategic Initiatives and Government Operations Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI infrastructure company. Crusoe sources power, manufactures modular data centers, builds hyperscale campuses, and operates its own cloud. Our ability to execute across this stack of capabilities requires Crusoe to coordinate closely with a diverse set of stakeholders: governments, utilities, customers, communities, and other local stakeholders. Every development requires Crusoe to navigate a unique set of permitting, energy, tax, workforce, logistics, environmental and other considerations that collectively earn the local and commercial trust needed to move forward. Our approach to navigating these considerations shapes both our cost structure and our differentiation vis-a-vis competitors. Our ability to treat and understand each of these stakeholders as unique collaborators, while operating at increasing scale is critical to Crusoe’s ongoing growth and approach.

As policy and regulation related to AI-infrastructure continues to evolve, our approach must constantly adapt with it. A county, state or country may rewrite its incentives or regulations, a utility commission may change tariff structures, a federal agency may issue a new program, or a community may raise new concerns about AI-infrastructure. Our team has to see these changes, understand what they mean for the business, develop an approach that addresses the problem, and help the broader organization act.

The Strategic Initiatives and Government Operations role will turn policy, regulatory, and community realities into business decisions and policies that improve the communities in which we operate, while making Crusoe the preferred AI-infrastructure provider for our partners, customers, communities, and regulators. We ensure Crusoe's growth is both profitable and differentiated, and that our business delivers real social and environmental value wherever possible.

Your Mission

This role will have two core functions:

  • Help Crusoe scope, analyze, and execute on big, strategic bets with a clear view of the government, community, and commercial forces that decide whether they succeed.

  • Enable the broader Government Affairs team’s operations by connecting the dots; creating cross-functional workflows, products, and reports that bring insight to light and allow team members and executives to improve decision-making; and embedding AI across the team’s day-to-day operations

Across these two core functions, you will build quantitative and qualitative analysis, run initiatives, and turn ambiguous problems into structured plans and recommendations for leadership. You will work closely with the Senior Manager of Strategic Initiatives and the VP of Government Affairs while partnering closely with the commercial, energy, development, finance, and sustainability teams to ensure our initiatives support and are integrated into the company’s broader operations.

This will be a fast–paced, ambiguous role, requiring strong communication and prioritization of competing initiatives and responsibilities. Success in this role will entail a mixture of robust analysis, communication, and organization as well as pragmatic execution. It will be measured by whether your work helps Crusoe win the right projects, make better decisions, and build a business that is both profitable and good for the communities it serves.

What You'll Be Working On

Strategic bets: scope, analyze, and execute

  • Scope and frame high-priority strategic initiatives with the Senior Manager of Strategic Initiatives, from early hypothesis through execution and handoff to a permanent owner.

  • Analyze the government, regulatory, and community forces behind new markets, campuses, facilities, and initiatives: permitting, entitlements, interconnection, incentives, tax policy, housing, environment, and workforce programs, across states and countries.

  • Translate those forces into commercial implications: initiative / site economics, project timelines, incentive value, risk, and differentiation versus competitors.

  • Build models and scenario analyses to size opportunities, compare jurisdictions or programs, and test the assumptions behind strategic decisions.

  • Write memos and build decks for the VP of Government Affairs and the President & CSO's organization that lead with the recommendation, lay out the evidence, and name key uncertainties.

  • Help shape how Crusoe's business model stays profitable and differentiated, including how energy-first / sustainable development, community benefits, and environmental performance create commercial advantage.

Government Affairs operations: connect the dots

  • Design and run the cross-functional workflows that link Government Affairs with commercial, energy, development, finance, and sustainability teams, so policy and community insight reaches the people who need it, and visa-versa.

  • Build and maintain trackers and datasets of jurisdictions, regulations, programs, stakeholders, commitments, and milestones, giving the team and executives a current view of where Crusoe stands.

  • Create recurring internal reports and intelligence products that flag the policy and community developments that matter most and cut through the noise.

  • Prepare briefing materials, talking points, decks, and background memos for meetings with officials, utilities, community leaders, and partners.

  • Coordinate the operational side of engagement: timelines, deliverables, community commitments, and follow-through, so each community is treated as a unique collaborator even as Crusoe scales.

  • Help define, measure, and report the social, economic, and environmental value Crusoe creates, such as local jobs, tax base, grid support, and emissions outcomes.

Embedding AI across the team

  • Identify where AI can make the Government Affairs team faster and better, and build the workflows, templates, and tools to do it.

  • Use AI for research, policy monitoring, drafting, and synthesis, while verifying outputs against primary sources and applying sound judgment about where they fall short.

  • Document and train teammates on these workflows so they are adopted and reused, not one-off experiments.

  • Turn recurring research and intelligence needs into repeatable workflows using AI research tools, agents, APIs, data sources and light scripting.

  • Build systems that can monitor markets and companies at a scale that would be impossible through manual research alone.

  • Design AI workflows with trust and verification in mind. Maintain traceability to primary sources, test outputs for accuracy and understand where automated systems are likely to fail.

  • Build tools that augment judgment rather than replace it: systems that make analysts faster while preserving clear ownership of conclusions and recommendations.

  • Document and share workflows so they can be reused and improved across the GA team.

What You'll Bring to the Team

Background

  • 2 to 5 years in strategy or management consulting, government relations or public affairs, policy analysis, corporate strategy, market research, project finance, energy or infrastructure development, or a similarly analytical environment. A strong body of independent work can substitute.

  • Strong Excel skills. You build clean, well-structured models and trackers, and you can walk us through one you built.

  • Fluency in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

  • Hands-on AI fluency. You use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or similar tools for real research, analysis, and drafting. You know how to guide them, interpret their outputs, and catch where they are wrong. You have built or improved a workflow with them and can show us.

  • Strong written and verbal communication. You write conclusion-first and can brief senior executives, technical teams, and external stakeholders with equal clarity.

  • Commercial judgment. You can reason about customers, costs, incentives, business models, and unit economics, and get up to speed quickly in an unfamiliar market, jurisdiction, or policy area.

  • Operational rigor. You have built processes, trackers, or reporting that other people relied on, and kept them accurate over time.

  • Analytical rigor. You evaluate sources, check your math, separate facts from assumptions, and can defend your reasoning.

  • 25-50% variable travel to Crusoe locations

Traits

  • Comfort with ambiguity. You thrive in fast-paced, vague environments and decide what matters most without waiting for a fully defined brief.

  • Prioritization. You juggle competing initiatives and requests, make clear trade-offs, and communicate them.

  • Structured thinking. You break messy problems into clear questions, options, and next steps.

  • Pragmatic execution. You balance robust analysis with getting things done, and know when an answer is good enough to act on.

  • Executive presence. You are comfortable presenting to senior leaders, and pushing back when the evidence supports it.

  • Judgment. You can distinguish what is interesting from what is important, and you use AI and other tools with sound judgment rather than blind trust.

  • Connector mindset. You see how work in one team affects another and build the bridges between them.

  • Mission orientation. You care about social and environmental impact and believe it strengthens, rather than competes with, a profitable business.

  • Collaboration and discretion. You work well across technical, commercial, and external stakeholders, and you handle sensitive information with care.

  • Ownership. You follow through on commitments and keep multiple workstreams moving at once.

  • Low ego, next person-up, and team-based approach. You lean into problems and eagerly take on the challenges that need to be solved, even when “it’s not in the job description”.

Bonus Points

  • Experience in government relations, public policy, or regulatory affairs, especially energy, utilities, land use, or economic development.

  • Domain exposure to AI compute, data centers, power and energy markets, or infrastructure development.

  • International policy or market experience.

  • Experience with community engagement, ESG or sustainability programs, or impact measurement.

  • Experience building dashboards, automations, or AI agents; Python, SQL, or AI coding tools are a plus.

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI infrastructure company. Crusoe sources power, manufactures modular data centers, builds hyperscale campuses, and operates its own cloud. Our ability to execute across this stack of capabilities requires Crusoe to coordinate closely with a diverse set of stakeholders: governments, utilities, customers, communities, and other local stakeholders. Every development requires Crusoe to navigate a unique set of permitting, energy, tax, workforce, logistics, environmental and other considerations that collectively earn the local and commercial trust needed to move forward. Our approach to navigating these considerations shapes both our cost structure and our differentiation vis-a-vis competitors. Our ability to treat and understand each of these stakeholders as unique collaborators, while operating at increasing scale is critical to Crusoe’s ongoing growth and approach.



As policy and regulation related to AI-infrastructure continues to evolve, our approach must constantly adapt with it. A county, state or country may rewrite its incentives or regulations, a utility commission may change tariff structures, a federal agency may issue a new program, or a community may raise new concerns about AI-infrastructure. Our team has to see these changes, understand what they mean for the business, develop an approach that addresses the problem, and help the broader organization act.



The Strategic Initiatives and Government Operations role will turn policy, regulatory, and community realities into business decisions and policies that improve the communities in which we operate, while making Crusoe the preferred AI-infrastructure provider for our partners, customers, communities, and regulators. We ensure Crusoe's growth is both profitable and differentiated, and that our business delivers real social and environmental value wherever possible.




YOUR MISSION

This role will have two core functions:

 - Help Crusoe scope, analyze, and execute on big, strategic bets with a clear view of the government, community, and commercial forces that decide whether they succeed.

 - Enable the broader Government Affairs team’s operations by connecting the dots; creating cross-functional workflows, products, and reports that bring insight to light and allow team members and executives to improve decision-making; and embedding AI across the team’s day-to-day operations



Across these two core functions, you will build quantitative and qualitative analysis, run initiatives, and turn ambiguous problems into structured plans and recommendations for leadership. You will work closely with the Senior Manager of Strategic Initiatives and the VP of Government Affairs while partnering closely with the commercial, energy, development, finance, and sustainability teams to ensure our initiatives support and are integrated into the company’s broader operations.



This will be a fast–paced, ambiguous role, requiring strong communication and prioritization of competing initiatives and responsibilities. Success in this role will entail a mixture of robust analysis, communication, and organization as well as pragmatic execution. It will be measured by whether your work helps Crusoe win the right projects, make better decisions, and build a business that is both profitable and good for the communities it serves.




WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING ON

Strategic bets: scope, analyze, and execute

 - Scope and frame high-priority strategic initiatives with the Senior Manager of Strategic Initiatives, from early hypothesis through execution and handoff to a permanent owner.

 - Analyze the government, regulatory, and community forces behind new markets, campuses, facilities, and initiatives: permitting, entitlements, interconnection, incentives, tax policy, housing, environment, and workforce programs, across states and countries.

 - Translate those forces into commercial implications: initiative / site economics, project timelines, incentive value, risk, and differentiation versus competitors.

 - Build models and scenario analyses to size opportunities, compare jurisdictions or programs, and test the assumptions behind strategic decisions.

 - Write memos and build decks for the VP of Government Affairs and the President & CSO's organization that lead with the recommendation, lay out the evidence, and name key uncertainties.

 - Help shape how Crusoe's business model stays profitable and differentiated, including how energy-first / sustainable development, community benefits, and environmental performance create commercial advantage.




GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS OPERATIONS: CONNECT THE DOTS

 - Design and run the cross-functional workflows that link Government Affairs with commercial, energy, development, finance, and sustainability teams, so policy and community insight reaches the people who need it, and visa-versa.

 - Build and maintain trackers and datasets of jurisdictions, regulations, programs, stakeholders, commitments, and milestones, giving the team and executives a current view of where Crusoe stands.

 - Create recurring internal reports and intelligence products that flag the policy and community developments that matter most and cut through the noise.

 - Prepare briefing materials, talking points, decks, and background memos for meetings with officials, utilities, community leaders, and partners.

 - Coordinate the operational side of engagement: timelines, deliverables, community commitments, and follow-through, so each community is treated as a unique collaborator even as Crusoe scales.

 - Help define, measure, and report the social, economic, and environmental value Crusoe creates, such as local jobs, tax base, grid support, and emissions outcomes.




EMBEDDING AI ACROSS THE TEAM

 - Identify where AI can make the Government Affairs team faster and better, and build the workflows, templates, and tools to do it.

 - Use AI for research, policy monitoring, drafting, and synthesis, while verifying outputs against primary sources and applying sound judgment about where they fall short.

 - Document and train teammates on these workflows so they are adopted and reused, not one-off experiments.

 - Turn recurring research and intelligence needs into repeatable workflows using AI research tools, agents, APIs, data sources and light scripting.

 - Build systems that can monitor markets and companies at a scale that would be impossible through manual research alone.

 - Design AI workflows with trust and verification in mind. Maintain traceability to primary sources, test outputs for accuracy and understand where automated systems are likely to fail.

 - Build tools that augment judgment rather than replace it: systems that make analysts faster while preserving clear ownership of conclusions and recommendations.

 - Document and share workflows so they can be reused and improved across the GA team.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TEAM

Background

 - 2 to 5 years in strategy or management consulting, government relations or public affairs, policy analysis, corporate strategy, market research, project finance, energy or infrastructure development, or a similarly analytical environment. A strong body of independent work can substitute.

 - Strong Excel skills. You build clean, well-structured models and trackers, and you can walk us through one you built.

 - Fluency in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).

 - Hands-on AI fluency. You use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, or similar tools for real research, analysis, and drafting. You know how to guide them, interpret their outputs, and catch where they are wrong. You have built or improved a workflow with them and can show us.

 - Strong written and verbal communication. You write conclusion-first and can brief senior executives, technical teams, and external stakeholders with equal clarity.

 - Commercial judgment. You can reason about customers, costs, incentives, business models, and unit economics, and get up to speed quickly in an unfamiliar market, jurisdiction, or policy area.

 - Operational rigor. You have built processes, trackers, or reporting that other people relied on, and kept them accurate over time.

 - Analytical rigor. You evaluate sources, check your math, separate facts from assumptions, and can defend your reasoning.

 - 25-50% variable travel to Crusoe locations




TRAITS

 - Comfort with ambiguity. You thrive in fast-paced, vague environments and decide what matters most without waiting for a fully defined brief.

 - Prioritization. You juggle competing initiatives and requests, make clear trade-offs, and communicate them.

 - Structured thinking. You break messy problems into clear questions, options, and next steps.

 - Pragmatic execution. You balance robust analysis with getting things done, and know when an answer is good enough to act on.

 - Executive presence. You are comfortable presenting to senior leaders, and pushing back when the evidence supports it.

 - Judgment. You can distinguish what is interesting from what is important, and you use AI and other tools with sound judgment rather than blind trust.

 - Connector mindset. You see how work in one team affects another and build the bridges between them.

 - Mission orientation. You care about social and environmental impact and believe it strengthens, rather than competes with, a profitable business.

 - Collaboration and discretion. You work well across technical, commercial, and external stakeholders, and you handle sensitive information with care.

 - Ownership. You follow through on commitments and keep multiple workstreams moving at once.

 - Low ego, next person-up, and team-based approach. You lean into problems and eagerly take on the challenges that need to be solved, even when “it’s not in the job description”.




BONUS POINTS

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is seeking a seasoned Control Room Operator (CRO) to coordinate all on-shift operations at our power facility. This senior-level role is primarily responsible for the safe operation of all plant equipment across a variety of scenarios, ranging from cold plant startups to emergency operations during plant upsets. You will serve as an individual contributor within the Operations & Maintenance Department, making critical decisions on non-routine or escalated technical issues with limited supervision.

The ideal candidate possesses excellent troubleshooting, diagnosis, and leadership skills, with a proven track record of using Distributive Control Systems (DCS) to monitor and adjust operating parameters. This role is vital for ensuring compliance with all local, State, and Federal regulations while driving plant efficiency and safety. (#INDMFG)

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Operational Coordination: Lead the coordination of all on-shift operations, ensuring the safe operation of plant equipment during normal and emergency scenarios.

  • System Monitoring & Control: Use Distributive Control System (DCS) computers to operate equipment and monitor parameters, making necessary adjustments to maintain optimal performance.

  • Compliance & Safety Oversight: Ensure strict adherence to all local, State, and Federal regulations, as well as internal plant procedures.

  • Hazardous Materials & Security: Maintain plant security, handle and transfer bulk chemicals, and ensure safe storage and transport of waste materials.

  • Chemical Analysis: Perform chemical analysis and control on steam, cooling, and condensate systems, while meticulously maintaining chemistry logs.

  • Lockout Tagout (LOTO): Utilize RedTag PRO and other specialized software for the professional issuance of Lockout Tagouts to ensure personnel safety during maintenance.

  • Technical Troubleshooting: Resolve the most complex technical issues and independently prioritize responsibilities for specific functional areas.

  • Process Improvement: Assist in the development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and provide strategic input to enhance plant efficiency, reliability, and safety.

  • Training & Mentorship: Provide advanced on-the-job skills training to others in complex technical areas and guide team members in task completion.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: Generally 10+ years of directly related experience in a power plant environment.

  • Specialized Knowledge: Deep understanding of health and safety regulations, including working around hazardous energy, chemicals, and waste materials.

  • Technical Skills: Previous experience using test equipment, calibration appliances, and machinery repair/control systems.

  • Aptitude: Strong mechanical aptitude with a basic understanding of chemistry, physics, electricity, and mathematics.

  • Decision Making: Proven ability to make competent decisions regarding non-routine technical issues and emergency operations.

  • Computer Proficiency: Skilled in using PC computers, Microsoft Office products, and specialized plant control software.

  • Physical Capabilities: Ability to perform walking, reaching, climbing, stooping, and lifting up to 50 pounds.

  • Authorization: Must be authorized to work in the USA.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Advanced Education: Degree from a technical or vocational school, or relevant military service.

  • Certifications: Possession of advanced certifications or licensures relevant to power plant operations.

  • Equipment Operation: Experience operating heavy equipment such as manlifts and forklifts.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $50 -$58/HR + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About This Role:

Reporting to the Treasury Senior Manager, the Treasury Manager will serve as a senior leader within the Treasury function, owning critical work streams across investment portfolio management, interest rate risk, debt compliance, and liquidity — while managing relationships with external investment advisors and supporting the broader Treasury team. This role is ideal for a deeply analytical finance professional who brings hands-on expertise in investment oversight and interest rate hedging, and who can operate both strategically and tactically in a fast-growing, complex environment. As a high-visibility member of the Treasury leadership team, you will drive process discipline, cross-functional collaboration, and data-driven decision-making across the organization.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Drive the build-out and oversight of banking and investment infrastructure required to support the execution of multi-billion-dollar projects

  • Oversee the company's investment portfolio, including day-to-day monitoring and management of external investment advisor relationships; ensure alignment with the Investment Policy Statement (IPS)

  • Analyze interest rate market conditions and risk exposure to inform hedging strategy; support the evaluation, recommendation, and execution of derivative transactions, and ensure strict compliance with lender-mandated hedging requirements.

  • Own lender debt covenant compliance across multiple SPVs and legal entities—including monitoring, reporting, and lender communications—and proactively manage covenant headroom across the company's growing credit facility portfolio.

  • Design and implement a robust reporting and monitoring framework for all existing and future debt facilities, ensuring operational feasibility and risk mitigation as the debt portfolio expands.

  • Support liquidity forecasting efforts in partnership with Finance and key business stakeholders, ensuring capital allocation decisions are informed by rigorous and forward-looking analysis

  • Lead strategic analytical support for key initiatives across the organization, ensuring capital is deployed efficiently and risk is managed proactively

  • Support Treasury cash management team activities, ensuring optimal positioning of global cash balances and the seamless execution of high-value transactions

  • Build and maintain executive-level reporting packages, dashboards, and ad-hoc analyses for senior leadership using Excel and PowerPoint

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • 7+ years’ experience in Treasury, Corporate Finance, or Investment Management in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Economics, or a related field

  • Highly advanced quantitative and analytical skills

  • Exceptional Excel modeling skills, with the ability to create detailed and complex financial models from scratch for a variety of purposes

  • Strong command of financial theory (economics, capital structure, WACC, derivatives, portfolio management, company valuations, etc.) and its practical applications

  • Detail-oriented, with a focus on accuracy and precision in financial analysis and reporting

  • Ability to analyze legal documents and understand the technical and accounting implications of complex transactions

  • Demonstrated experience overseeing investment portfolios and managing external investment advisor relationships, with strong working knowledge of fixed income

  • Hands-on experience with interest rate derivatives, hedging strategy development and execution, and ongoing effectiveness monitoring

  • Track record of successfully leading complex, cross-functional workstreams and delivering results through direct management and organizational influence

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to distill complex topics into manageable recommendations

  • Self-starter who can multitask and deliver in a dynamic environment under tight timelines, iterative fact-sets, and changing priorities; must be “hands-on"

  • Positive attitude and a solutions-focused approach

Bonus Points:

  • CFA Charterholder, or progress toward

  • MBA, Master of Finance, or equivalent experience

  • Knowledge of Bloomberg modeling tools and API syntax

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $135,000 - $195,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role

We are seeking an Electrical Design Engineer to join the electrical design team for Crusoe's modular data centers and to stay with each deployment from design through construction and commissioning. You will be the technical link between Crusoe's design team, Crusoe Industries (which manufactures our modular data centers), construction partners, and Cloud customers. You will adapt modular designs to each site and carry field lessons back into the next design iteration.

This position requires an electrical professional who thrives at the intersection of facility engineering and product design, and who is comfortable in both the design office and the field.

The role is in-office in Denver. Travel is anticipated at 40% to support factory acceptance testing, supplier visits, and site deployments.

What You'll Be Working On

  • Design and specify the electrical systems for modular data center deployments, including MV/LV distribution, UPS, generators, switchboards, and RPPs, with high-availability requirements.

  • Take site-specific designs from schematic through construction-ready sets, and review drawings, submittals, and shop drawings from design partners against the Basis of Design.

  • Audit short-circuit, protection, arc-flash, and load flow studies.

  • Develop and maintain installation details for modular electrical systems, and support the roadmap with R&D as new technologies and configurations are explored.

  • Resolve RFIs and Field Engineering Directives during construction, and support installation quality checks and factory witness testing.

  • Support commissioning (Levels 1-5) with Crusoe's Cx team, reviewing procedures and results for technical accuracy.

  • Capture lessons learned from the field and feed them back into design templates.

  • Be an electrical safety champion with Crusoe's construction partners.

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical field.

  • 7+ years of electrical design experience in data centers or other mission-critical facilities, with exposure to construction or commissioning.

  • Working knowledge of the NEC and relevant NFPA/IEEE standards.

  • Proficiency with AutoCAD or Revit and a power systems analysis tool (ETAP or SKM).

  • A track record of taking designs through construction and troubleshooting field issues with practical, code-compliant solutions.

  • Ability to manage ambiguity and move between customer discussions and detailed engineering.

  • Strong communication skills for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Bonus Points

  • Active Professional Engineer (PE) license.

  • Experience designing or installing modular, prefabricated, or edge data centers.

  • Understanding of how AI compute loads affect power distribution, from the utility transformer to the server rack.

  • Experience with BESS or alternative energy inputs, or with SCADA and EPMS.

  • Experience in a fast-paced design/build environment.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $170,000 -$180,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

As the Senior Accountant, Lease Accounting, you’ll own lease accounting operations at Crusoe from end to end. Our lease portfolio reflects a vertically integrated data center business: land, powered shell, build-to-suit, colocation, ground leases, equipment, and energy-related arrangements. Very few look alike, and no template will do the work for you. You’ll read each agreement, understand the deal behind it, work out how the terms translate under ASC 842, and build a repeatable monthly process around it.

In a typical month, you’ll abstract new leases and process modifications in LeaseQuery, post lease journal entries, reconcile LeaseQuery activity to the general ledger and AP, and partner with Legal, Real Estate, Data Center Development, Procurement, FP&A, and Tax to know about new deals and amendments before they are signed. You’ll thrive in this role if you’re detail-oriented, energized by non-standard problems, and driven to make the process better every month. You’ll also support quarterly disclosures, SOX controls, and external audit requests, with guidance from Technical Accounting on judgment-heavy items.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • LeaseQuery ownership: Own input of new leases and maintain schedules, including modifications, remeasurements, extensions, terminations, and reassessments

  • Lease inventory: Keep a complete inventory of executed agreements and amendments

  • ASC 842 application: Apply the standard to non-standard arrangements, including lease vs. non-lease components, embedded leases, build-to-suit, variable payments, and option assessments

  • Accounting memos: Work with manager to prepare lease abstracts and memos for new and modified leases, with Technical Accounting guidance on judgment-heavy items

  • Month-end close: Prepare and post lease journal entries for expense, interest, ROU amortization, and liability entries

  • Reconciliations: Reconcile LeaseQuery activity and lease liability and ROU asset balances to the general ledger and AP, and clear variances

  • Cross-functional partnership: Work with Legal, Real Estate, Data Center Development, Procurement, FP&A, Treasury, and Tax on lease intake, forecasts, and structuring

  • Process improvement: Document procedures and build intake workflows and automation that scale with the business

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • 4-7 years of accounting experience, including at least 1-2 years of hands-on ASC 842 lease accounting

  • Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Accounting, Finance, or a related field,

  • Experience with complex or non-standard lease agreements, not only standard real estate leases

  • Working knowledge of lease classification, modifications, remeasurement, and discount rate concepts

  • Experience with a lease accounting system (LeaseQuery preferred; LeaseAccelerator, CoStar, or similar)

  • Strong month-end close and reconciliation discipline in a public or public-ready environment

  • Advanced Excel skills and comfort with large data sets

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining accounting to non-accountants

Bonus Points:

  • CPA or CPA-eligible

  • Big 4 or public accounting experience, or experience at a high-growth technology or infrastructure company

  • Exposure to data center, energy, real estate development, or other capital-intensive industries

  • Experience with build-to-suit, powered shell, colocation, or ground lease structures

  • Familiarity with an ERP such as NetSuite or Sage Intacct, FloQast, and SOX controls

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $105,000-$155,000 + Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
