If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

As the Accounting Manager, Leases, you’ll own lease accounting at Crusoe: the technical conclusions, the monthly operation, the controls, and the audit relationship. Our lease portfolio reflects a vertically integrated data center business: land, powered shell, build-to-suit, colocation, ground leases, equipment, and energy-related arrangements. Very few look alike. You’ll set the standard for how this non-standard portfolio is accounted for under ASC 842 and make sure it runs cleanly every month as the business scales.

This is a player-coach role. You’ll personally work the most complex agreements and judgments, review the work of a Senior Accountant (and future team members) who handles day-to-day lease administration and reconciliations. You’ll partner closely with the Senior Manager, General Ledger, Technical Accounting, Legal, Real Estate, Data Center Development, Treasury, Tax, and FP&A, and you’ll be the primary lease contact for external auditors. You’ll thrive in this role if you’re a strong technical accountant who can also build process, develop people, and influence the business.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Technical accounting: Own ASC 842 conclusions for complex arrangements, including embedded leases, variable payments, option assessments, classification, modifications, and terminations

  • Memos and policy: Draft and review lease memos, own the lease policy and ensure consistent application across lease portfolio

  • LeaseQuery governance: Own the lease subledger, including reviewing new leases, modifications, remeasurements ensuring appropriate supporting documentation

  • Month-end close: Own the lease close end to end, including journal entries, liability and ROU roll-forwards, and GL and AP reconciliations, delivered on the close calendar

  • Review and escalations: Review Senior Accountant entries, reconciliations, and variance analysis, and resolve escalations

  • Reporting and disclosures: Partner heavily with financial reporting team on lease disclosures, including maturity analysis, weighted-average term and discount rate, and lease cost components

  • Cross-functional partnership: Work with Legal, Real Estate, Data Center Development, Procurement, FP&A, Treasury, and Tax on lease intake and portfolio management

  • Controls and audit: Own SOX controls and audit support for the leases

  • Team leadership: Coach and develop the Senior Accountant, and build the lease function as it grows, including roles, documentation, and backup coverage

  • Process improvement: Build intake workflows, standard procedures, and automation that scale with the business

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • 7-10 years of accounting experience, including at least 4 years of hands-on ASC 842 experience and deep familiarity with non-standard lease structures

  • Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Accounting, Finance, or a related field and CPA

  • Demonstrated ability to reach technical accounting conclusions

  • Experience leading or mentoring senior and staff accountants (people management experience preferred)

  • Experience with a lease accounting system (LeaseQuery preferred; CoStar, or similar)

  • Strong month-end close, reconciliation, and controls discipline in a public or public-ready environment

  • Advanced Excel skills and comfort with large data sets

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to influence business partners

Bonus Points:

  • Big 4 or public accounting experience, plus experience at a high-growth technology or infrastructure company

  • Exposure to data center, energy, real estate development, or other capital-intensive industries

  • Hands-on experience with build-to-suit, powered shell, colocation, or ground lease structures

  • SOX 404 experience, managing external audit relationships, and building process and teams in a fast-scaling environment

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $115,000 - $140,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Engineering, Core-backend
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Core Backend team in our Cloud Customer Experience (CCX) organization. Core Backend builds the shared services that every Crusoe Cloud product depends on: quota management, customer notifications, organization onboarding and KYC, and the API framework that sits in front of our backend services. Customers rely on these systems to sign up, get access to the capacity they are entitled to, and hear from us when something changes on their account. Product teams rely on them so they can launch on Crusoe Cloud without building their own quota, notification or onboarding systems.

You will lead a team of backend engineers, partner with the team's product manager, and set technical direction for services that sit on the path of every customer request. This is a full-time, hands-on management role for someone who has led backend or platform teams, can go deep on distributed systems design, and can weigh requests from many internal teams against one roadmap.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Shared services for product teams: Own the services other Crusoe Cloud teams build on, including quota management, the notification service and the API framework, so a new product can launch without building its own versions of them.

  • Quota management: Run the system of record for what each organization and project can consume across GPU, compute, storage and networking, along with the request and approval workflows that change those limits.

  • Customer onboarding: Lead self-serve onboarding, organization state management and automated KYC, and work with risk and security partners on fraud prevention for self-serve customers.

  • Customer notifications: Own the service that sends email, in-console, webhook and Slack notifications to Crusoe Cloud customers.

  • Reliability and operations: Set and meet SLOs for the team's services, run on-call and incident reviews, and move long-running operations onto durable workflows.

  • Technical direction: Guide architecture decisions with the team, including API standardization across services and breaking apart monolithic services, and make the tradeoffs between new features and platform work.

  • Cross-functional partnership: Work with Product, Customer Success, Security and the other CCX teams (Billing, Identity and Access Management, Client Interfaces and Admin Tooling) to set one roadmap from many requests.

  • Team building: Hire, mentor and grow engineers, including filling open roles on the team.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • People leadership: 2+ years managing software engineering teams, including hiring, performance management and career development for engineers at different levels.

  • Backend engineering: 6+ years of professional software engineering experience building backend services in Go or another compiled language (Rust, Java or C++). Our services are primarily written in Go.

  • Distributed systems: Experience designing and running distributed systems or cloud platform services, including versioned APIs (gRPC or REST), relational databases such as PostgreSQL, and message queues such as Kafka, NATS or Pub/Sub.

  • Operations: Experience owning customer-facing production systems, including SLOs, monitoring and alerting, on-call and incident response.

  • Platform mindset: A track record of leading a team that serves other engineering teams, and of setting priorities when several teams need something at once.

  • Communication: Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining technical tradeoffs to engineers, product managers and non-technical partners.

  • Education: Bachelor's degree minimum.

Bonus Points

  • Quota and entitlement systems: Experience building quota, rate limiting or entitlement systems for a cloud provider or multi-tenant platform.

  • Onboarding and risk: Experience with customer onboarding, KYC or fraud prevention systems.

  • Workflow engines: Experience with Temporal or similar workflow engines, or with state machines and reconciliation loops for long-running operations.

  • API platforms: Experience building API gateways or API frameworks used by many engineering teams.

  • AI infrastructure: Familiarity with GPU cloud platforms or AI infrastructure.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $215,000 -$260,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Software Engineer to join Crusoe’s Data Center Infrastructure Engineering team. This position is focused on the development of software for the management of a fleet of GPU servers as well as the data centers that house those systems. The role focuses on the developing and implementing advanced diagnostic, observability, automation and repair tooling for high-performance GPU compute clusters.

The ideal new team member will be a hands-on problem solver who is comfortable working independently. The new team member will play a critical role in maintaining the health and scalability of Crusoe’s rapidly growing GPU fleet.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Developing and implementing deep-level diagnostics and troubleshooting of hardware faults within GPU racks and high-density compute systems.

  • Developing troubleshooting and automation tooling for GPU platforms including NVIDIA A100, H200, GB200, B200 and AMD 350X / 355X.

  • Developing automation and AI agents for executing component-level diagnosis and remediation for failed or degraded hardware.

  • In conjunction with data center operations develop innovative tooling and AI agents for managing the critical environment.

  • Developing tooling for post-repair validation and testing tools such as burn-in, Pytorch, and NVIDIA NCCL to ensure system stability and performance.

  • Own the deployment, monitoring, and operational support of developed tooling, ensuring solutions maximize GPU fleet availability and performance to drive customer success.

  • Developing automation and operational tooling for facilities management power as well as direct liquid cooling hardware systems

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • 4-6 years of software engineering experience.

  • The ability to identify a problem, rapidly develop a scalable solution and ship it.

  • Ability to lean in and assist team members working on critical or complex technical initiatives.

  • Ability to set the technical direction for a specific project and execute.

  • Expertise in distributed systems, reliability, and cloud platforms (Kubernetes, IaC, GCP etc.)

  • Strength in at least one programming language - Go, Python, Java, Rust.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

  • Ability to work independently and within a team

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with Temporal and Kubernetes.

  • Experience working directly with hardware vendors.

  • Background in large-scale GPU fleet operations or hyperscale data center environments.

Benefits:

  • Industry competitive pay

  • Restricted Stock Units in a fast-growing, well-funded technology company

  • Health insurance package options that include HDHP and PPO, vision, and dental for you and your dependents

  • Employer contributions to HSA accounts

  • Paid Parental Leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Teladoc

  • 401(k) with a 100% match up to 4% of salary

  • Generous paid time off and holiday schedule

  • Cell phone reimbursement

  • Tuition reimbursement

  • Subscription to the Calm app

  • MetLife Legal

  • Company paid commuter benefit; $50 per pay period

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $170,000 - $205,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

jobs.descriptionHtml:

About This Role:

As the Accounting Manager, Leases, you’ll own lease accounting at Crusoe: the technical conclusions, the monthly operation, the controls, and the audit relationship. Our lease portfolio reflects a vertically integrated data center business: land, powered shell, build-to-suit, colocation, ground leases, equipment, and energy-related arrangements. Very few look alike. You’ll set the standard for how this non-standard portfolio is accounted for under ASC 842 and make sure it runs cleanly every month as the business scales.

This is a player-coach role. You’ll personally work the most complex agreements and judgments, review the work of a Senior Accountant (and future team members) who handles day-to-day lease administration and reconciliations. You’ll partner closely with the Senior Manager, General Ledger, Technical Accounting, Legal, Real Estate, Data Center Development, Treasury, Tax, and FP&A, and you’ll be the primary lease contact for external auditors. You’ll thrive in this role if you’re a strong technical accountant who can also build process, develop people, and influence the business.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Technical accounting: Own ASC 842 conclusions for complex arrangements, including embedded leases, variable payments, option assessments, classification, modifications, and terminations

  • Memos and policy: Draft and review lease memos, own the lease policy and ensure consistent application across lease portfolio

  • LeaseQuery governance: Own the lease subledger, including reviewing new leases, modifications, remeasurements ensuring appropriate supporting documentation

  • Month-end close: Own the lease close end to end, including journal entries, liability and ROU roll-forwards, and GL and AP reconciliations, delivered on the close calendar

  • Review and escalations: Review Senior Accountant entries, reconciliations, and variance analysis, and resolve escalations

  • Reporting and disclosures: Partner heavily with financial reporting team on lease disclosures, including maturity analysis, weighted-average term and discount rate, and lease cost components

  • Cross-functional partnership: Work with Legal, Real Estate, Data Center Development, Procurement, FP&A, Treasury, and Tax on lease intake and portfolio management

  • Controls and audit: Own SOX controls and audit support for the leases

  • Team leadership: Coach and develop the Senior Accountant, and build the lease function as it grows, including roles, documentation, and backup coverage

  • Process improvement: Build intake workflows, standard procedures, and automation that scale with the business

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • 7-10 years of accounting experience, including at least 4 years of hands-on ASC 842 experience and deep familiarity with non-standard lease structures

  • Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Accounting, Finance, or a related field and CPA

  • Demonstrated ability to reach technical accounting conclusions

  • Experience leading or mentoring senior and staff accountants (people management experience preferred)

  • Experience with a lease accounting system (LeaseQuery preferred; CoStar, or similar)

  • Strong month-end close, reconciliation, and controls discipline in a public or public-ready environment

  • Advanced Excel skills and comfort with large data sets

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to influence business partners

Bonus Points:

  • Big 4 or public accounting experience, plus experience at a high-growth technology or infrastructure company

  • Exposure to data center, energy, real estate development, or other capital-intensive industries

  • Hands-on experience with build-to-suit, powered shell, colocation, or ground lease structures

  • SOX 404 experience, managing external audit relationships, and building process and teams in a fast-scaling environment

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $135,000 - $165,000. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

Crusoe is looking for a Senior Financial Analyst, Central Finance to support a variety of corporate finance initiatives, solving critical finance, strategy, and operations-related problems across the organization. This role offers a unique opportunity to work across teams and see firsthand how a fast-growing business operates — a great platform for learning how to operationalize change at scale. This is a highly visible role that interacts regularly with executive management, and requires someone comfortable moving fluidly across Finance, Corporate Development, Treasury, and business groups.

The ideal candidate is highly analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable multi-tasking in a results-oriented, fast-paced environment. This is a full-time, exempt position.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Financial Modeling & Analysis — Build and maintain robust financial models for corporate planning, budgeting, and cash flow forecasting; perform sensitivity, scenario, and variance analysis to evaluate performance and inform decision-making.

  • Planning & Forecasting — Drive the monthly forecasting and annual budgeting processes by partnering with business unit finance teams to gather inputs, consolidate actuals and forecast data, and deliver accurate, timely financial plans aligned with corporate targets.

  • Performance Management Reporting — Create and support monthly executive team reports, board materials, and ad-hoc analyses, building clear, actionable performance narratives for leadership.

  • Systems & Data Management — Own and manage the company’s planning platform, ensuring data integrity, availability, and accuracy for financial reporting and analysis; identify opportunities to integrate AI and automation to enhance forecasting and reporting capabilities.

  • Cross-Functional Partnership — Collaborate with Cloud, Digital Infrastructure, Accounting, and other teams to ensure Finance model assumptions reflect the latest business inputs and meet reporting and control standards.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 2-4 years of experience in financial planning & analysis, investment banking, treasury, or corporate finance required.

  • Excellent skills in financial modeling and forecasting.

  • Strong interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills.

  • Team player who can work well independently and with limited direction.

  • Working knowledge of accounting principles and financial statements.

  • Detail-orientation with a focus on accuracy and precision.

Bonus Points

  • MBA or CFA designation.

  • Client or industry experience in Technology, Data Center Infrastructure, Cloud, or Energy.

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

Crusoe is looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager to own program execution for cloud availability — the maintenance windows, host patching, network switch upgrades, and incident management work that keeps our GPU infrastructure running reliably for customers. This role sits with an engineering team that manages system uptime and infrastructure SLAs and has not historically worked with a TPM function, so the right candidate earns credibility through technical depth and execution rigor rather than process alone. You'll drive planning and execution of maintenance windows that balance minimal customer disruption against critical hardware and firmware updates, coordinate cross-functional response during major incidents, and build the lightweight frameworks that bring predictability to an operationally complex environment. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone who wants to be personally in the room for incident calls and switch upgrade planning, not managing from a dashboard

 

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Maintenance Window Planning & Execution: Own the planning and execution of maintenance windows/production changes for high-availability cloud infrastructure, balancing minimal customer workload disruption against the need for host patching and hardware updates.

  • Incident Management: Coordinate cross-functional response during major incidents or unplanned outages — driving communications, leading post-incident reviews (PIRs), and tracking remediation items through to closure without compromising SLA commitments.

  • Network Switch Upgrades: Support planning for major network switch upgrades and migrations, tracking the hardest dependencies and flagging what's most likely to break before it does.

  • Technical Risk Identification: Catch technical risks in cloud availability programs before the engineering team surfaces them, and know when to solve it directly versus escalate.

  • Vendor & Partner Coordination: Engage directly with hardware/network vendors and Customer Success on high-stakes infrastructure upgrades, keeping customer-facing teams informed through the process.

About the Role:

Crusoe is seeking a dedicated Operations & Maintenance Technician (OMT) to ensure the proper operation and maintenance of our power facility. This role is essential for maintaining plant reliability, safety, and environmental compliance, whether assigned to a shift or the maintenance team. You will be responsible for operating, troubleshooting, and repairing a wide range of mechanical, electrical, and instrumentation equipment critical to our mission.

The ideal candidate is a skilled technician capable of managing complex systems such as gas and steam turbines, generators, and water treatment equipment while strictly adhering to safety and environmental regulations. This is a full-time position that requires an individual contributor who is authorized to work in the USA.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Plant Operations & Maintenance: Operate and maintain a simple cycle power generating facility and its auxiliary equipment, including heat recovery steam generators, air compressors, and fire suppression systems with minimal guidance.

  • Technical Troubleshooting & Repair: Identify and resolve CEMS problems, perform Root Cause Analysis of failures, and repair defective plant equipment such as pumps, valves, and gearboxes.

  • System Inspections & Data Recording: Conduct "Inspection of Watch" on all plant systems and read meters or automatic devices to record temperatures, vibrations, fluid levels, and water chemistry to verify operating conditions.

  • Water Chemistry Management: Perform analysis on HRSG, auxiliary boiler, and cooling tower systems; control chemical feed and blowdown rates to maintain proper control ranges.

  • Electrical & Mechanical Tasks: Open and close circuit breakers for system operation or electrical isolation, and perform piping and conduit installation for plant upgrades.

  • Documentation & Systems: Utilize the facility’s computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) and assist with the development of Operations and Maintenance procedures.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with vendors for chemical ordering and equipment repair, work with Plant Management on capital projects, and assist in administering the Operator training program.

  • Facility Upkeep: Perform general housekeeping, painting, and continuous improvement tasks to maintain the appearance and cleanliness of the plant and control room.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Education: High School diploma or equivalent is required.

  • Power Plant Expertise: Demonstrable knowledge of all facets of power plant operations and the ability to make competent decisions in emergency situations.

  • Technical Literacy: Ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical one-lines, logic drawings, technical manuals, and P&IDs.

  • Maintenance Skills: Proficiency in troubleshooting mechanical, instrumentation, and electrical equipment, as well as operating welding and cutting equipment.

  • Communication & Software: Good verbal and written communication skills and proficiency in Microsoft Office, specifically Excel and Word.

  • Physical Requirements: Ability to walk, reach, climb, and lift up to 50 pounds.

  • Work Flexibility: Willingness to work 12-hour rotating shifts and availability for call-ins or work overload as needed.

  • Authorization: Must be authorized to work in the USA.

  • Safety and Compliance: This position is designated a safety-sensitive position and/or is located in a safety-sensitive facility. Drug and alcohol program participation is required.

Bonus Points:

  • Associates Degree (AA) or equivalent from a two-year college or technical school.

  • Two to four years of related power plant experience and/or training.

  • Experience operating heavy equipment such as man lifts and forklifts.

  • Advanced proficiency in Water Chemistry and demineralized water system operations.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $41 -$47 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. (#INDMFG)

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Staff Engineer, Crusoe Managed Data Transfer (Distributed Systems)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We are looking for a Staff Engineer to be the technical lead and systems architect for Crusoe's Managed Data Transfer (MDT) service, the person who owns how its parts fit together and how MDT fits into Crusoe Cloud. MDT moves petabyte-scale training data between hyperscaler storage and Crusoe storage as a managed service, so AI labs and Physical AI companies can train on Crusoe GPUs without building their own transfer pipelines. You will design the control plane, the transfer worker fleet and the integration with Crusoe's storage and network, and set the path for adding other clouds and Crusoe-internal transfers.

This is an engineering leadership role on a new team. Managed Data Transfer starts from a working prototype that already serves customers in production, so your first decisions are about what to keep, harden or replace, and how to sequence that work without disrupting the customers who depend on it. You will lead the design through Crusoe's architecture review, mentor the engineers who build it, and report to the Engineering Manager of Managed Data Transfer within Managed platform services.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Architecture Ownership: Own the end-to-end design of MDT: the job API and scheduler, the transfer workers on Kubernetes, storage integration and network paths. You decide what the system looks like and explain why.

  • Prototype Assessment and Migration: Evaluate the production prototype, decide what gets refactored, extended or replaced, and move its current users onto the managed service without interruption.

  • Throughput and Correctness: Set the data-plane strategy (sharding, concurrency, straggler handling, checksum verification) and the benchmarks that prove it, aiming for line-rate transfers over dedicated interconnects.

  • Cross-Team Contracts: Own the interfaces between MDT and Storage, Network, Kubernetes, IAM, Console, Billing and Monitoring. You define what partner teams build to and hold the line on it.

  • Extensibility and Build-versus-Buy: Design for new clouds and Crusoe-internal transfers with a pluggable transfer engine and regional worker pools, and evaluate open-source and vendor options before the team builds.

  • Operational Excellence: Set the bar for reliability, observability and on-call for every system the team ships.

  • Product Partnership: Work with Product on scope, pricing trade-offs and milestones, and surface edge cases early enough to change the plan.

  • Technical Mentorship: Raise the team's level through design reviews, RFC feedback and direct coaching, so the team runs well without depending on you.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • Distributed Systems Depth: Hands-on experience designing and operating data-intensive distributed systems at scale, including the failure modes that only appear in production.

About the Role:

As Senior Manager, Corporate Recruiting, you will lead and scale Crusoe's corporate recruiting function during a pivotal period of growth. Reporting to the Director of Talent Acquisition, you'll oversee recruiting across all non-technical organizations.

This is a hands-on leadership role for a highly analytical, resourceful, and execution-oriented recruiting leader who thrives in a fast-paced, evolving environment. You'll be responsible for building and developing a high-performing team of recruiters and sourcers while establishing the structure, processes, and operational discipline needed to deliver predictable hiring outcomes at scale.

You'll partner closely with senior business leaders on workforce planning, hiring forecasts, recruiting capacity modeling, and talent strategy, using data to anticipate hiring needs, identify risks, optimize resources, and drive informed business decisions.

Success in this role requires someone who can operate with a high degree of autonomy, navigate ambiguity, prioritize competing business needs, and move seamlessly between strategic planning and hands-on problem-solving. You'll bring a strong sense of ownership, sound judgment, and the ability to turn complex recruiting challenges into actionable solutions.

As a key partner to Recruiting Operations, Talent Intelligence, and business leadership, you'll help build a recruiting organization recognized for its operational excellence, data-driven decision-making, hiring velocity, and exceptional candidate experience.

 
 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Recruiting Strategy & Execution: Develop and execute corporate recruiting strategies across multiple functions, aligning hiring priorities, resources, and execution plans with business growth objectives.

  • Team Leadership & Development: Build, coach, and develop a high-performing team of recruiters and sourcers, fostering a culture of accountability, ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

  • Workforce Planning & Capacity Modeling: Partner with business leaders and Finance to develop hiring forecasts, assess recruiter capacity, model hiring demand, and proactively identify resource gaps to ensure the team can deliver against hiring commitments.

  • Data-Driven Recruiting Performance: Own recruiting KPIs, including hiring attainment, time-to-fill, pipeline conversion, recruiter productivity, and forecast accuracy. Translate recruiting data into actionable insights, recommendations, and measurable improvements.

  • Operational Excellence & Scalability: Identify process inefficiencies, remove bottlenecks, and implement scalable recruiting practices that improve hiring velocity, predictability, quality, and overall team effectiveness.

  • Independent Leadership & Problem-Solving: Operate effectively with minimal oversight in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. Navigate ambiguity, make sound decisions, manage competing priorities, and proactively resolve challenges before they impact hiring outcomes.

  • Technology, AI & Automation: Partner with Recruiting Operations to identify and implement AI-enabled tools, automation, and workflow improvements that increase recruiter productivity and operational efficiency while maintaining quality and compliance.

  • Talent Intelligence & Market Insights: Leverage external market data, competitive intelligence, and talent availability to inform recruiting strategies, workforce planning, and business decisions.

As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About the Role:

As Senior Manager, Corporate Recruiting, you will lead and scale Crusoe's corporate recruiting function during a pivotal period of growth. Reporting to the Director of Talent Acquisition, you'll oversee recruiting across all non-technical organizations.

This is a hands-on leadership role for a highly analytical, resourceful, and execution-oriented recruiting leader who thrives in a fast-paced, evolving environment. You'll be responsible for building and developing a high-performing team of recruiters and sourcers while establishing the structure, processes, and operational discipline needed to deliver predictable hiring outcomes at scale.

You'll partner closely with senior business leaders on workforce planning, hiring forecasts, recruiting capacity modeling, and talent strategy, using data to anticipate hiring needs, identify risks, optimize resources, and drive informed business decisions.

Success in this role requires someone who can operate with a high degree of autonomy, navigate ambiguity, prioritize competing business needs, and move seamlessly between strategic planning and hands-on problem-solving. You'll bring a strong sense of ownership, sound judgment, and the ability to turn complex recruiting challenges into actionable solutions.

As a key partner to Recruiting Operations, Talent Intelligence, and business leadership, you'll help build a recruiting organization recognized for its operational excellence, data-driven decision-making, hiring velocity, and exceptional candidate experience.

 
 

What You'll Be Working On:

 - Recruiting Strategy & Execution: Develop and execute corporate recruiting strategies across multiple functions, aligning hiring priorities, resources, and execution plans with business growth objectives.

 - Team Leadership & Development: Build, coach, and develop a high-performing team of recruiters and sourcers, fostering a culture of accountability, ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

 - Workforce Planning & Capacity Modeling: Partner with business leaders and Finance to develop hiring forecasts, assess recruiter capacity, model hiring demand, and proactively identify resource gaps to ensure the team can deliver against hiring commitments.

 - Data-Driven Recruiting Performance: Own recruiting KPIs, including hiring attainment, time-to-fill, pipeline conversion, recruiter productivity, and forecast accuracy. Translate recruiting data into actionable insights, recommendations, and measurable improvements.

 - Strategic Business Partnership: Serve as a trusted talent advisor to Director- and VP-level stakeholders, influencing hiring strategies, organizational planning, prioritization, and talent decisions through data and market intelligence.

 - Operational Excellence & Scalability: Identify process inefficiencies, remove bottlenecks, and implement scalable recruiting practices that improve hiring velocity, predictability, quality, and overall team effectiveness.

 - Independent Leadership & Problem-Solving: Operate effectively with minimal oversight in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. Navigate ambiguity, make sound decisions, manage competing priorities, and proactively resolve challenges before they impact hiring outcomes.

 - Technology, AI & Automation: Partner with Recruiting Operations to identify and implement AI-enabled tools, automation, and workflow improvements that increase recruiter productivity and operational efficiency while maintaining quality and compliance.

 - Talent Intelligence & Market Insights: Leverage external market data, competitive intelligence, and talent availability to inform recruiting strategies, workforce planning, and business decisions.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

 - Relevant Industry Experience: Experience leading corporate recruiting within hyperscalers, neocloud providers, cloud computing, AI/ML, AI infrastructure, data center, energy, hardware, or advanced manufacturing organizations. Strong understanding of the talent landscape, competitive hiring dynamics, and organizational complexity associated with scaling infrastructure-intensive businesses.

 - High-Growth & Scaling Experience: Proven success building and scaling corporate recruiting teams in fast-paced, high-growth environments, ideally within organizations experiencing rapid headcount expansion, evolving business priorities, and increasing operational complexity.

 

Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location
   
    

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $155,000 - $185,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

 

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About this Role:

Crusoe Cloud is seeking a Senior Manager Engineering, Network Operations to own production reliability for our global network infrastructure, spanning edge, backbone, data center fabric, and GPU cluster interconnects. As our footprint of high-performance compute (HPC) and GPU-based AI infrastructure scales, you will build and lead the team responsible for incident response, root cause analysis, and operational excellence across a growing, 24x7, multi-region network.

 

You're accountable for the org's operational output: uptime, mean-time-to-resolution, and the rigor of every postmortem. You build and scale the operations team, set the standards for how incidents are handled and prevented, and are a trusted voice in planning conversations with sister Network Operations, Network Deployment, Architecture, and Site Reliability leadership.

 

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Build and Lead the Organization: Own the operations org's structure and growth. Hire and develop Senior and Staff Network Production Operations Engineers across multiple sites and time zones, and build the management layer beneath you as the on-call footprint and device fleet scale.

  • Own Production Reliability: Be accountable for uptime across Crusoe's global edge, backbone, data center, and GPU cluster network, directly supporting AI workloads running across thousands of GPUs worldwide.

  • Own Incident Response: Set the org's incident command structure, escalation paths, and on-call model. Serve as an executive escalation point during high-severity network events, and ensure stakeholder communication is fast, clear, and accurate.

  • Own Root Cause Analysis and Remediation: Hold the org accountable for rigorous RCAs and for tracking remediation plans through to closure. Run cross-team post-incident reviews and drive systemic fixes in partnership with Architecture and Deployment.

  • Drive Operational Automation: Champion the shift from manual triage to automated detection, diagnosis, and remediation. Direct investment in tooling built on top of Crusoe's observability stack (streaming telemetry, SNMP, NetFlow, Kentik, Grafana, Prometheus, ThousandEyes) to reduce toil and accelerate MTTR.

  • Own SLIs/SLOs: Partner with Architecture and SRE to define, track, and report on network reliability metrics. Hold the org to those targets and escalate when they're at risk.

  • Run Executive-Level Cadence: Own operational reporting and risk escalation to Deployment, Architecture, and Site Reliability leadership. Represent the operations org in cross-functional and executive planning.

  • Champion Operational Standards: Ensure runbooks, escalation playbooks, and SOPs are current, followed, and continuously improved, with an eye toward what can be scripted or automated rather than performed manually.

  • Develop the Next Layer of Leaders: Coach engineers and emerging leads into stronger technical and operational leaders, and build the org's bench strength for future scale.

  • Partner Across the Network Organization: Work closely with Deployment leadership on handoff quality from build to production, and with Architecture on feedback from the field that should shape reference designs and standards.

 

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 10+ years of experience in network engineering or network operations, including 4+ years managing engineers or engineering managers in a large-scale, 24x7 infrastructure environment.

  • Proven People and Org Leadership: Track record of building, scaling, and retaining high-performing operations teams. Experience managing managers or team leads is strongly preferred.

  • Incident and Reliability Ownership at Scale: Demonstrated ability to own production reliability across large, multi-region device fleets, with the reporting and risk management to match at an executive level.

  • Strong Technical Fluency: Expert working knowledge of BGP, EVPN-VXLAN, IS-IS, OSPF, MPLS, QoS, and TCP/IP in production data center environments; familiarity with RDMA/RoCE lossless fabrics (PFC, ECN, DCQCN) for GPU/HPC workloads; comfort with Arista (EOS) and Juniper (Junos) platforms in leaf-spine CLOS architectures, enough to credibly challenge your own team and partner teams without needing to be the org's deepest technical expert.

  • Automation Fluency: Working understanding of Python-based tooling, observability automation, and auto-remediation practices, sufficient to guide investment decisions and evaluate tooling proposals.

  • Executive Communication: Comfortable setting context, managing expectations, and delivering hard news to senior stakeholders across Deployment, Architecture, and Supply Chain, especially during and after high-severity incidents.

  • Operational and Strategic Judgment: Able to balance near-term incident pressure against longer-term org health, reliability standards, and team sustainability.

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience in hyperscale or ISP environments.

 

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with NVIDIA/Mellanox networking platforms in GPU cluster environments.

  • Familiarity with Kentik or Arbor for traffic analysis and DDoS visibility.

  • Experience defining SLIs/SLOs in partnership with SRE or product teams.

  • Exposure to operating 10K+ device fleets across hyperscale or cloud environments.

  • Background building or scaling post-incident learning programs org-wide.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

 

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $220,000 - $265,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Senior Category Manager, Metals & Raw Materials
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

The Senior Category Manager, Metals & Raw Materials owns Crusoe’s foundational spend categories end-to-end at the strategic layer. In this role, your primary focal point is establishing upstream control over raw material inputs and metal fabrication—including structural carbon and stainless steel, sheet metal, aluminum extrusion, copper busbars, and specialized modular enclosures—while integrating critical electrical balance-of-plant components (switchgear, Power Distribution Centers [PDCs], transformers, and cable/wire).

Operating across Crusoe’s key manufacturing and deployment hubs (including Arvada, Brighton, Tulsa, and Ponchatoula), you will bridge the gap between global commodity markets and finished sub-assemblies. Because these categories sit at the intersection of volatile commodity cycles, strategic custom fabrications, and bottleneck electrical components, you will combine financial hedging acumen and technical vetting (welding standards, metal forming, metallurgical certs, tolerances, and NEC/UL compliance) with commercial rigor.

This role will be onsite at our Arvada, Colorado location.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Raw Material & Commodity Intelligence: Track global indices and cost drivers across base and refined metals (Hot-Rolled Coil/HRC, cold-rolled sheet, structural shapes, aluminum, and copper). Implement should-cost models, scrap-clawback clauses, and index-based pricing mechanisms to optimize mill and metal service center spend.

  • Upstream Supply Chain & AVL Vetting: Own the Approved Vendor List (AVL) across raw material distributors, metal service centers, and custom contract fabricators. Conduct rigorous shop-floor capability audits—evaluating laser cutting, CNC forming, robotic welding (AWS compliance), stamping, powder coating, and dimensional tolerances against engineering specifications.

  • Integrated Category Strategy (Metals & Balance of Plant): Apply framework methodologies (e.g., Kraljic Matrix) to govern a 12–24 month category roadmap that links structural enclosures and frames directly to long-lead electrical equipment (switchgear, breakers, busway, and industrial cable). Balance strategic supply resilience with aggressive commercial leverage.

  • Make vs. Buy & Tolling Strategies: Formulate forward-looking make/buy/toll strategies. Evaluate the commercial feasibility of purchasing mill-direct steel and copper for consigned "toll" processing by external fabricators vs. buying turnkey assemblies, maximizing margin capture and schedule predictability.

  • Commercial Negotiations & Buyer-Favorable Contracting: Draft, structure, and negotiate Master Supply Agreements (MSAs), Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and long-term reservation agreements. Redline buyer-adverse clauses around raw material surcharges, delivery milestones, liquidated damages, liability caps, and force majeure.

  • Proactive Risk Mitigation & Multi-Sourcing: Maintain an active Category Risk Register mapping single-source exposures, geopolitical/tariff risks, mill outage liabilities, and extended lead-time bottlenecks (particularly on high-grade electrical steels and long-lead switchgear). Execute qualifying dual-sourcing roadmaps across domestic and nearshore suppliers.

  • Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) & Value Engineering: Partner closely with Mechanical, Electrical, and Systems Engineering & Production to evaluate material substitutions (e.g., aluminum vs. copper, structural tube vs. open channel, alternative sheet gauges) to reduce unit cost and scrap rates without compromising structural integrity or thermal/electrical performance.

  • Cross-Functional Execution Frameworks: Develop clean standing commercial pricing schedules, rebate tiers, and lead-time matrices that empower Material Planners and Tactical Buyers to execute release orders smoothly in the ERP.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • Experience: 5–8+ years of dedicated strategic sourcing, supply chain, or category management experience with a primary emphasis on raw metals, structural steel, sheet metal fabrication, or heavy mechanical equipment, accompanied by exposure to industrial electrical systems.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Business, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Commodity & Metallurgical Knowledge: Working understanding of metal alloy specifications, mill test reports (MTRs), metal forming processes, welding/finishing standards, and the cost breakdown of raw material vs. conversion cost vs. logistics.

  • Technical Breadth: Ability to interpret engineering drawings, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), structural weld symbols, and electrical balance-of-plant schematics (including baseline familiarity with NEC and UL standards).

  • Contract Structuring & Redlining: Proven hands-on experience structuring comprehensive MSAs, raw material indexation agreements (e.g., CRU, LME, Fastmarkets), and redlining complex commercial terms.

  • Strategic Methodologies: Advanced proficiency in total cost of ownership (TCO) modeling, make/buy trade studies, supplier scorecarding, and formal RFP/RFQ execution.

Bonus Points:

  • Direct experience managing raw metal service center agreements, mill-direct reservation programs, or toll-processing arrangements.

  • Background auditing metal fabrication shops, CNC machining cells, or switchgear manufacturing plants.

  • Hands-on ERP/MRP experience (Acumatica, NetSuite, SAP) and expertise structuring complex multi-level Bills of Materials (BOMs).

  • Direct domain background in data center infrastructure, modular enclosures, energy generation, or high-power industrial assets.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the range of $120,000 - $145,000 + Bonus + Restricted Stock Units included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role:

We’re seeking a Staff Enterprise Technology Administrator to join our Enterprise Technology team, a specialized group within IT responsible for the financial and operational systems that power the business.

In this role, you will serve as the primary subject matter expert and dedicated system owner for Procure-to-Pay (P2P) and Order-to-Cash (O2C) processes, owning both sides of the workflow stack as equally weighted responsibilities. You’ll own the configuration, maintenance, and optimization of key financial platforms including Coupa, Sage Intacct, and Acumatica, while supporting an ecosystem of connected tools such as Stripe, LeaseQuery, Asset4000, FloQast, and Workiva. At this level, you will also set the governance model, access framework, and technical roadmap these platforms operate under going forward.

Working at the intersection of finance and technology, you will partner closely with Procurement, Sourcing, Finance, Accounting, and Sales Operations leadership to ensure systems run reliably while proactively driving improvements to financial workflows and integrations, rather than only responding to requests as they arrive.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Administering, configuring, and optimizing financial platforms including Coupa, Sage Intacct, and Acumatica to ensure system stability, data integrity, and performance, and establishing the governance standards these platforms are run against

  • Owning Procure-to-Pay workflows end to end, including purchase requisitions, purchase orders, supplier onboarding, and accounts payable processes

  • Owning Order-to-Cash operations end to end, including invoicing automation, accounts receivable workflows, and revenue recognition configurations

  • Partnering with Finance and Sales Operations leadership to troubleshoot billing, collections, and system integration issues, and shaping multi-quarter enhancement roadmaps rather than handling issues one at a time

  • Setting strategy and governance for the finance-related service desk function, including SLAs, recurring issue identification, and automation or self-service improvements that structurally reduce support volume over time

  • Maintaining and troubleshooting integrations between Coupa, Sage Intacct, Stripe, and CRM systems to ensure reliable data flow

  • Owning the periodic access review and audit program to maintain SOX compliance, and setting the least-privilege access model and control framework other stakeholders are expected to follow

What You'll Bring to the Team:

  • 8+ years of hands-on experience as a Systems Administrator, Financial Systems Analyst, or similar role directly administering financial platforms, not adjacent business, sourcing, or project-controller roles

  • Deep, current hands-on administration experience with at least one of Coupa, Sage Intacct, or Acumatica, meaning direct configuration and system ownership rather than end-user familiarity or implementation-only exposure, with demonstrated ability to ramp quickly on the others

  • Demonstrated, hands-on ownership of both Procure-to-Pay workflows (procurement, supplier management, accounts payable) and Order-to-Cash workflows (billing, accounts receivable, revenue recognition) as equally required competencies, not a primary-plus-nice-to-have pairing

  • A track record of proactive process improvement and governance ownership, having served as the primary or sole subject matter expert for a financial system rather than operating in a purely reactive, ticket-driven capacity

  • Experience supporting integrations between financial systems, including API-based integrations, and demonstrated experience implementing financial software or delivering major system enhancements

  • Confirmed, hands-on experience with SOX compliance, periodic access reviews, and audit support, meaning personal ownership of controls work rather than operating within an environment someone else governed

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to partner with Finance and Accounting leadership, translate ambiguous business requirements into system solutions, and manage competing priorities across multiple stakeholder groups

Bonus Points

  • Experience supporting financial platform ecosystems including Stripe, LeaseQuery, Asset4000, FloQast, and Workiva

  • Familiarity with finance system integration architecture or middleware platforms

  • Experience supporting financial systems in high-growth technology organizations

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $155,000 -$180,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicant's knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. About This Role:

We are seeking a highly motivated and results-driven Contract Recruiter to support our Finance and Strategic Finance functions at Crusoe. You’ll recruit across a variety of Finance related roles like Investment Banking, Private Equity, and Strategic Finance.

This role is designed for a highly autonomous recruiter who can run complex, high-bar hiring end-to-end, manage senior stakeholders, and operate as a true talent partner. You will inherit an active, high-impact requisition load and play a critical role in enabling the recruiting team to scale by taking ownership of execution while leadership focuses on strategy, planning, and org design.

This is a six month contract with potential to extend or become a full-time role based on business need.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for Finance, Business Operations and Strategic Finance roles across Investment Banking, Private Equity, and Strategic Finance, from mid-level through director

  • Partner closely with hiring managers and senior leaders as a strategic advisor, not just an executor

  • Build and maintain strong pipelines through proactive sourcing and outreach into various talent pools

  • Run intake sessions, structure interview processes, and design role-appropriate technical and customer-facing assessments

  • Screen for the blend of technical depth and customer-facing skill these roles require, and calibrate the bar with hiring managers early

  • Conduct candidate interviews, provide timely updates, and lead compensation negotiations

  • Manage a high-volume, high-complexity req load independently with minimal oversight

  • Keep pipeline data, notes, and status current in the ATS so leadership can see progress without asking

What You’ll Bring to the Team:

  • 7+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, mostly in Finance and Strategic Finance, across several functions such as Investment Banking, Private Equity, and Strategic Finance

  • Track record of hiring quota-carrying and customer-facing roles, plus a good grasp of how Finance and Strategic Finance teams are structured and measured

  • Proven ability to run senior and hard-to-fill searches from start to finish with limited support

  • Strong sourcing skills, including passive candidate outreach through LinkedIn and other tools

  • Ability to assess what makes someone successful in different Finance and Strategic Finance functions, from commercial acumen to technical fluency to customer empathy

  • Experience partnering with and influencing senior stakeholders, including hiring managers at director level and above

  • Skilled in salary and equity negotiation

  • Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills

  • Highly organized, with strong attention to detail and time management

  • Data-driven: you use recruiting metrics and market trends to guide hiring strategy

Bonus Points:

  • Experience recruiting in fast-paced, high-growth startup environments

  • Proven ability to consistently meet or exceed hiring goals

  • Experience keeping detailed documentation in an ATS

Compensation:

Compensation will be paid in the hourly range of $70.00 - $80.00 Compensation to be determined by the applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

About the Role

Crusoe's Platform Engineering team builds the services that automate how we manage our cloud fleet. As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll design and ship modular microservices on top of our underlying infrastructure, turning stakeholder requirements into platform capabilities that directly drive feature delivery and revenue.

What You'll Be Working On

  • Design, build, and operate microservices that automate fleet provisioning, lifecycle, and capacity management

  • Extend existing platform services with new features that directly drive customer-facing delivery

  • Turn ambiguous stakeholder requirements into clear, modular designs and drive them to production

  • Build on GCP and managed Kubernetes, working closely with infrastructure and cross-functional teams

  • Own the reliability and observability of the services you ship

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend or platform services

  • Strong proficiency in at least one backend language such as Go, Python, Java, or C#

  • Experience designing microservices and APIs (gRPC/REST) in distributed systems

  • Hands-on experience with Postgres and event-driven systems such as Kafka

  • A track record of leading projects end-to-end and raising the bar for engineers around you

Bonus Points

  • Experience building on GCP, AWS, or managed Kubernetes

  • Capacity management or fleet/hardware lifecycle experience

  • Neocloud or GPU cloud infrastructure experience

  • Experience with Go

  • Observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana)

Benefits

  • Industry competitive pay

  • Restricted Stock Units in a fast growing, well-funded technology company

  • Health insurance package options that include HDHP and PPO, vision, and dental for you and your dependents

  • Employer contributions to HSA accounts

  • Paid Parental Leave

  • Teladoc

About the Role:

Crusoe is hiring an AI Engineer for our Developer Relations Engineering team: an engineer who builds agentic AI systems and enjoys showing other developers how they work. You will build reference agents, open-source integrations, and sample applications on Crusoe Cloud and Crusoe Managed Inference.

In this role, you will lead technical content creation, community engagement, and developer outreach across AI infrastructure and managed services workloads. You will produce documentation, tutorials, white papers, sample applications, and video guides.

You will partner with the Product, Engineering, Research, and GTM/Solutions Engineering teams and work across the open-source agent ecosystem.

You will spend most of your time building and then sharing what you build.

What You'll Be Working On:

  • Agentic Reference Systems: Architect and ship end-to-end reference agents and starter kits on Crusoe that developers can use as a starting point for production, covering tool use, MCP, multi-agent orchestration, RAG, structured outputs, memory, and evals.

  • Examples & Documentation: Own the code examples, tutorials, and documentation that help developers go from first API call to working agent, and keep them tested and up to date as the ecosystem changes.

  • Open Source & GitHub: Own Crusoe's developer-facing GitHub presence, including examples, cookbooks, and integrations. Contribute upstream to agent frameworks, inference engines, and developer tooling (for example LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP, vLLM, and SGLang) so they work well with Crusoe.

  • Technical Content & Video: Turn the systems you build into content developers rely on: deep-dive blog posts, notebooks, YouTube videos, livestreams, and short technical clips.

  • Building in Public: Share your work on X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Discord, Reddit, Hacker News, etc. Answer technical questions, review community projects, and become a trusted technical voice in the agent and open-source community.
